generated_text: …and honestly, the sheer volume of glitter on Amelia after that craft session was unbelievable. I’m  still  finding it. It’s like a sparkly plague. Oh, you know how it is. They thrive on the chaos, don’t they? Little glitter bombs. Is Leo coping alright without you being super-mum all weekend? He’s fine. Actually, he’s been quite independent. Made his own breakfast this morning – a mountain of toast and jam, predictably – and insisted on choosing his own outfit. Which resulted in mismatched socks and a dinosaur t-shirt with striped shorts. Bless him. It’s good for him, though. I sometimes think I smother him a bit. You don’t. You’re a brilliant mum, Sarah. But it's nice he gets a bit of space, too. Especially with your work being so busy lately. How’s the proofreading going? Still drowning in legal documents? Sadly, yes. Mrs. Abernathy is on a roll with her property law revisions. It's…detailed. Pays the bills, though. And it’s better than chasing clients for marketing fees, which feels like a full-time job in itself. What about you? Anything interesting happening? Still keeping busy? Relatively. Mostly just…life. Trying to navigate this whole new ‘mum’ thing again. It feels so different the second time around. Ethan’s surprisingly good, though. He’s been trying to help with little Ben, which is sweet. Though mostly it involves offering him his building blocks, regardless of whether Ben wants them or not. That's Ethan, all over. Always trying to  fix  things. Remember when he tried to 'help' Grandma with her knitting? The yarn ended up everywhere. Oh, don’t remind me! Grandma was remarkably patient. Speaking of family, have you thought any more about coming down to Mum and Dad’s for their anniversary next month? I have. It’s just…with work, and everything…and trying to find someone to look after Leo… it’s a bit of a logistical nightmare. And honestly, Mum’s been hinting about wanting a ‘proper’ birthday celebration for  Ben  too. Feels like it'll be a juggling act. She does tend to do that, doesn’t she? Always managing to combine everyone’s celebrations into one huge, chaotic event. I’ve already warned Dad to prepare for a bombardment of baby photos. I'm thinking of suggesting we take them all out for a meal, somewhere nice.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of paperwork just to get the van across the Dutch border was unbelievable. I mean, pre-Brexit it was just…drive. Now it's declarations, customs codes, proving the origin of every single bit of kit, even the camping stove! Right? It’s madness, isn't it? I was talking to Ben at the department yesterday, he's trying to get funding for fieldwork in Germany, and he's having the same nightmare. The admin alone is almost enough to make it not worth the hassle. Though, Germany’s a bit better organised than the Netherlands, supposedly? Organised, maybe. Still a faff. And expensive! We budgeted for petrol, tolls, campsites…didn't factor in needing a translator to decipher some of the forms. Luckily, some bloke at the border spoke Geordie, believe it or not. Saved my life, he did. No way! A Geordie at the Dutch border? Cambridge really does warp your sense of what’s normal. You’d think you’d find more Dutch speakers, wouldn't you? You would! He said he used to work on the ferries, Sunderland to Rotterdam. Small world. Anyway, it got me thinking…remember when we backpacked around Italy back in uni? Just rocked up at borders with our passports, didn’t even think twice. God, yes! Florence, Rome, Venice…that was amazing. And so easy. We spent more time worrying about getting pickpocketed than filling out customs forms. Felt truly…free, you know? That interrail pass was the best investment I ever made. Completely. I’m already feeling so much less inclined to just  go  somewhere. It’s not the cost of the trip itself, it’s the pre-trip stress. Planning's gone from ‘what sights do we want to see?’ to ‘what documentation do we need to prove we own this saucepan?!’ It’s actively discouraging travel, isn’t it? And it’s not just the EU. Trying to take research equipment into Switzerland is apparently a whole other level of bureaucracy. I was reading about a guy bringing a spectrometer… it was rejected at the border because the calibration certificate wasn't stamped in triplicate with a specific shade of blue ink. You are joking. Blue ink? That’s…that’s just spiteful. It feels like they're deliberately making it difficult. I was thinking about heading to Portugal next year, maybe do some coastal hikes.

…and honestly, the whole point of rhubarb crumble is the custard. Not a watery, packet custard, mind you. Proper, thick, vanilla bean custard. It needs to  coat  the back of your spoon. Can we have crumble tomorrow, please? After fish fingers? Hmm, maybe. If you both promise to eat your vegetables tonight. And no arguing about which vegetable is the  most  disgusting. We had that with broccoli last week, and it took twenty minutes to settle. Broccoli  is  disgusting! It looks like little trees! And they’re green! They are good for you, Leo. They make you strong. And actually, lots of good things are green – peas, spinach… And money! Money is green! That's… a very good point, Maisie. Though not  all  money is green, is it? What about the gold ones? The £20 ones? Exactly. You’re both very financially aware, aren’t you? Which brings me back to… Monopoly. Oh no. Not Monopoly again! What’s wrong with Monopoly? It’s a classic! And a brilliant way to learn about… property and economics. It’s boring. And it takes  forever . And Maisie always wins. I do  not  always win! Just… most of the time. It’s because I’m good at saving my money. See? A valuable life skill! Leo, you tend to spend all your money on hotels on Mayfair straight away. That’s not a sustainable business strategy. But Mayfair is the best! Everyone wants to land on Mayfair! Yes, but if you’ve got no money left, you can’t afford to stay out of jail, can you? Or pay the rent when someone lands on your street. You need a balanced portfolio. Diversification! Diversi-what-now? It means don’t put all your eggs in one basket. Or all your money in one property. Spread it around. Buy a few cheaper properties, collect rent, and build up slowly. Just like building up to a lovely rhubarb crumble. You need the rhubarb, the sugar,  then  the crumble topping,  then  the custard. You can’t just have the crumble straight away. So, like, buy Old Kent Road and then…what? Then you wait for someone to land on it! And then you charge them rent! It’s a slow burn, Old Kent Road. But it’s a start. And it’s much cheaper than Park Lane. I like buying the pink ones. They’re pretty.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is just  ridiculous . Like, we're talking millions of words, all needing tagging for part-of-speech and semantic roles. It’s not just copy-pasting anymore, you know? They want nuance. They want  layers . Millions? Good grief. Sounds… intense. Still, you always were good with detail. Remember that Lego Millennium Falcon we built when we were kids? You sorted all the tiny pieces before I even opened the instructions. Oh, don’t remind me. You were too busy trying to just  force  things together. That Falcon was structurally unsound for weeks. This is different though, Liam. It’s not satisfyingly tactile. It's just… staring at a screen, endlessly classifying. And the intern keeps mis-tagging 'like' as a verb.  Like , a verb! It’s a filler, a discourse marker! It drives me up the wall. Right, because you’ve explained that to him, what, five times now? Six. Six times. And each time he looks at me like I'm speaking Klingon. He’s a Classics student, which, honestly, explains a lot. All that Latin declension has scrambled his brain. Maybe he's just intimidated. You  are  the corpus queen, after all. Seriously, ‘corpus’ sounds like something out of a sci-fi film. What exactly  is  a corpus anyway, in layman's terms? I know it's something to do with language, but… It's basically a really, really big collection of text and speech. Think newspaper articles, books, transcripts of conversations, everything. And we analyse it to see how language is actually used – not how people  think  it’s used, but how they actually say things. It’s useful for loads of stuff, like improving speech recognition software or understanding how language changes over time. Sounds… useful, I guess. A bit dry for my tastes though. Give me a bridge to design and I’m happy. Something concrete. Something you can  see  working. This feels… abstract. It is abstract. But it  is  important! It's about preserving language, understanding communication… alright, alright, I'm on a soapbox. I just… I need to vent. Work’s been stressful. And Mr. Henderson keeps breathing down my neck about ‘optimizing workflows’. As if I haven't already automated half the process! Henderson sounds like a nightmare. The kind of manager who thinks 'synergy' is a verb. You know him too well. Honestly, sometimes I think he just makes up management jargon to sound important.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the state of Mrs. Higgins’ garden now. Completely overgrown. She used to take such pride in her roses, you know? Crimson Glory, they were. Beautiful things. I offered to give ‘er a hand, but she just waved me away, said her back wasn’t up to watching anyone bendin’ and strechin’ about. Stubborn as a mule, that woman. Aye, she always was. Remember when she refused to let young Timmy use her hedge clippers? Said he’d ruin ‘em. Timmy was only seven! Good lad, though, that Timmy. Turned out alright, didn’t he? Became a proper electrician, I heard. Not like some of the youngsters nowadays, glued to those computers all day. Oh, don’t get me started on computers, Arthur. Honestly, I can barely work the telly remote these days. All these buttons and flashing lights... it's a wonder anyone understands anything. Though, I have to admit, little Emily – my granddaughter – showed me how to video call the other day. Seeing her face appear on that screen… nearly made me cry. So you’re tellin’ me you’re converted then, Doreen? Goin’ to be zoomin’ away with the best of ‘em? I still reckon a good old-fashioned phone call is best. You can  hear  the person, you know? The nuances, the little sighs… you don’t get that with these digital things. He’s right, you know. It’s colder, isn’t it? Like talkin’ to a ghost. I tried it with young Kevin last Christmas. All I could see was the top of his ‘ead and his cat wanderin’ about. Couldn’t even tell if he was listenin’. Well, it's not  ideal , is it? But Emily lives up in Scotland now, since she met that nice David. And it’s not always easy to just… pop up for a cuppa. At least with the video, I can see she’s alright. She's expecting her first, you know. Oh, really? That's wonderful news, Doreen! A great-grandchild for you. Congratulations! What’s the due date? September, she thinks. Though she's being a bit vague. Says she doesn’t want to jinx it. Sensible girl. Honestly, it feels like only yesterday she was a little thing, running around with scraped knees. Time just flies, doesn't it? It does that. Seems like only last week I was teachin’ young Thomas how to ride his bicycle down the lane.

…and honestly, the packaging is  still  giving me grief. I thought sourcing recycled cardboard would be straightforward, but finding boxes that are the right dimensions for the serum bottles  and  look remotely presentable is proving to be a nightmare. I spent hours yesterday measuring everything! Seriously, I'm starting to dream in centimetres. Ugh, packaging. The bane of every small business owner’s existence, isn’t it? I completely get it. I went through hell trying to find decent stickers for the lip balm labels. They either looked cheap, or the adhesive was rubbish and they’d peel off. Did you think about getting something custom made? It's more expensive, obviously, but you get  exactly  what you want. I did, got a quote, and nearly choked on my tea. It was… substantial. I’m trying to keep the initial outlay as low as possible, you know? Especially with Mum constantly reminding me about ‘sensible investments’ and ‘not getting carried away’. She's convinced Honest Skincare will be the next big thing, but simultaneously expects me to run it on a tenner. Sounds like Mum! Mine’s exactly the same. All encouragement and then a detailed spreadsheet of projected costs. But seriously, custom packaging  does  elevate things. People judge a book by its cover, and skincare by its box, unfortunately. Maybe you could compromise? Find a slightly less bespoke option, but still good quality? That’s what I’m leaning towards. I found a company that does pre-made boxes but they'll print our logo on them. The issue is, the internal dividers are a bit… flimsy. I'm worried the bottles will rattle around in transit. I need to protect the product, obviously. What did you do with the lip balms? How did you ensure they weren't getting squashed? I ended up using shredded tissue paper – proper eco-friendly stuff, obviously. And padded envelopes. It added a bit to the postage cost, but less than a full custom packaging overhaul. Have you looked at your shipping costs properly? That’s another thing that can sneak up on you. I’ve had a quick look, but I need to do a full comparison. Royal Mail, Hermes, Evri… it’s all a bit confusing. I was hoping to offer free shipping over a certain amount, but I need to work out the price points. It's all connected, isn't it?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it! Claiming it was a ‘misunderstanding’. A misunderstanding that cost Mrs. Higgins her pension, more like. Honestly, the state of politics these days… it's just appalling. You’re on a roll, Moira. Though I have to say, I largely agree. I saw that story too. The whole thing stinks. Though, knowing how the news cycles, it’ll be forgotten by next week. Something else shiny and awful will grab their attention. Exactly! It’s deliberately engineered to distract, isn’t it? Keeps everyone flitting from one outrage to the next without actually addressing anything substantial. It feels… exhausting. Though, thankfully, being retired means I only have to  witness  the chaos, rather than actively try to explain it to a classroom full of increasingly apathetic teenagers. You still dealing with that then, Arthur? The apathy? Oh, it's… a feature, not a bug, these days, Moira. They’re just so overwhelmed with information, and most of it's terrible. Trying to inspire them to care about anything beyond their phones is a constant battle. Little Timmy Wilkins actually asked me yesterday if the Romans had TikTok. TikTok! Good heavens! That’s… bleak. Though, I suppose if the Romans had TikTok, we’d probably know a lot more about what they were  really  up to. Less sanitized history, perhaps. Probably a lot more gladiatorial death streams. Speaking of which, how are you holding up? It's been a couple of weeks since your last appointment with Dr. Davies. Did he say anything more about... well, you know? Oh, Arthur. It’s… inconclusive, still. He’s running more tests. Apparently, it’s not showing up clearly enough to be certain. He’s put it down to ‘age-related changes’ mostly, but he wants to be thorough. Honestly, it’s the  waiting  that’s the worst. It's like being suspended in amber. I can imagine. That must be dreadful. I wish there was something more I could do. Just… let me know if you need anything, alright? Practical things, emotional support, someone to yell at the television with over the state of the world. I’m here. You always are, aren’t you? That's why I appreciate you popping round so often. It's not easy, you know, being… well, unproductive. Not  having  a purpose, after all those years of shaping young minds. It feels… peculiar.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Brussels sprouts my mother insists on making is criminal. It's like she’s personally offended if anyone  doesn’t  eat all three helpings. Three helpings?! Blimey, you’ve got my sympathy. My mam’s obsessed with parsnips. Roasted, mashed, in soup…parsnip everything. It’s…a lot. Though, to be fair, she does a cracking gravy. Oh, gravy is  essential . My lot go big on the stuffing. My Aunt Carol makes it with chestnuts and apricot, which sounds awful, but is genuinely divine. But sprouts…yeah, that's a commitment. Are we all freezing this year, or is it just me? The house feels glacial, even with the heating on. Freezing’s the word. I’ve barely touched the central heating, trying to be sensible with the bills, but it's grim. Though, to be fair, spending half my day in the workshop keeps me warm enough. I'm building a commission – a ridiculous, ornate birdhouse. Someone wants a miniature Tudor mansion for their budgies. A Tudor mansion for budgies! That’s…commitment of a different kind. Sounds wonderfully bonkers, though. Is it giving you a chance to use all your fancy tools? Oh, absolutely! I’ve been meaning to justify the purchase of that tiny dovetail saw for months. This is its moment. Though, ironically, I'm having trouble finding miniature slate tiles. The local builders' merchants just laughed at me. You need to go online, lad. You can get anything online. Speaking of things I shouldn’t be spending money on, I’ve been looking at those 3D printers. Fancy making your own tools, or bits for your commissions? Tempting, very tempting. But I’m still clinging to the belief that  real  craftsmanship involves actual hand tools. Though, I confess, my back isn't getting any younger. It’s making me think…perhaps I should be planning for…retirement? Mid-life crisis manifesting as practical concerns, I suppose. Don't even  say  the R-word. I'm still trying to finish my PhD! Though, I did overhear my supervisor talking about post-doc funding drying up. It's terrifying. She was saying something about moving to Spain… Spain sounds lovely. Sun, sea…no Brussels sprouts. Although, on the subject of things growing, did anyone manage to get any mulberries this year? I was hoping to make some jam, but the birds got to them all before I did.

… honestly, I still can’t believe you use the good silver  every  day, Mum. It feels so…sacrilegious! We only get it out at Christmas! Sacrilegious? Oh, don’t be daft, love. What’s the point of having it if you don't use it? It’s just sat in that drawer gathering dust otherwise. Your Grandma Elsie would be turning in her grave. She  loved  a good set table. She did have a point, though, Mum. I’m always a bit worried I’ll drop something. It feels like a really formal occasion just eating shepherd’s pie with a silver fork. It's a lovely set, though. Solid silver. Inherited, wasn’t it, Margaret? From… the Worthingtons? I can never quite recall. Yes, dear, from my Aunt Beatrice. The Worthingtons were her husband’s family. Fancy lot, they were. Always sending us slightly disapproving Christmas cards. Still, it feels like a waste. Especially when Uncle George keeps complaining about needing new gardening tools. Wouldn’t the silver fetch a pretty penny? Silver's no good to a gardener, lass. Need steel for the shears. And a good strong spade, that's what. Though I used to polish this silver, back in the day. Hours I spent, me and your grandmother. Before everything… changed. Oh, Dad, don’t start on that now. Everyone's having a nice time. And speaking of things changing, have you lot made any plans for Sarah’s birthday next month? We were thinking a pub quiz? Her and Liam are proper quiz fiends. Though finding a date is proving tricky. He’s got that new project at work, running him ragged. He’s practically living on caffeine. A pub quiz sounds good. Though honestly, after the last one with the Millers, I swore I'd never subject myself to Clive’s “knowledge” again. He thinks he knows everything. It’s exhausting. Clive Miller? That man. He once tried to tell me the battle of Hastings was fought in… Devon. Devon! I have to admit, I nearly choked on my vol-au-vent. Honestly, some people. Right, well, we should probably think about inviting some of our old friends. Doreen and Arthur haven’t been out much since Arthur’s hip replacement. Doreen… lovely woman. Used to bring the best rhubarb crumble. Better than yours, Margaret, if I’m honest. Oh, you old rascal! Don’t you dare!

…and honestly, the meeting could have been an email. An  email , Leo! Three hours of Mr. Henderson waffling on about synergy and ‘thinking outside the box’. It’s exhausting. Honestly, I think he just likes the sound of his own voice. Is synergy like… when you join Lego bricks together? In a very,  very  abstract way, darling, yes. It’s supposed to mean working together to make something better. But usually it just means more meetings. How’s your pasta? Not too hot? It’s yummy! Can I have more peas please? And are we  really  going skiing? Like, actually skiing? Yes, we’re really going skiing! We booked it, remember? Next month. To Austria. Think snowy mountains, hot chocolate, and… well, probably a few tumbles. Will I be good at skiing? Grandma says I’m good at balancing. You’re a natural balancer, you are. And you’ll have lessons, of course. You’ll be zooming down those slopes in no time. Though, maybe not  zooming  at first. More like… carefully gliding. Can I wear my pink helmet? The one with the sparkly bits? Absolutely. The sparkly pink helmet is mandatory. It's the coolest helmet on the mountain. Though, we might need to get you some proper ski goggles. The sun reflecting off the snow is really bright. Oh. Will it be cold? It will be cold, yes. But we’ll wrap you up warm! Hats, scarves, gloves, the whole lot. Lots of layers. Think of a little polar bear. A fluffy polar bear! Can I take Polar Bear cuddly toy with me? Of course you can! Polar Bear is coming on an adventure. He’ll need his own tiny ski suit, maybe. He would! He’d fall over a lot though. Probably. Just like someone else I know. Speaking of falling over… I really need to figure out what I'm doing with Henderson’s project. He expects a full proposal on my desk Monday morning. It's ridiculous. He keeps changing his mind! One minute he wants charts, the next he wants narrative, then he wants… I don’t even know what he wants half the time. Is it like when I’m building a tower and it keeps falling down? Exactly! It’s like building a tower that keeps falling down. Except a tower made of spreadsheets and meetings. And a very grumpy boss. Can’t you just tell him it’s falling down?

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  loves  to hear himself talk about Shakespeare. Like, we get it, it's important, but three hours on the subtext of  one  soliloquy? Seriously? Tell me about it! He did the same with Macbeth last year. I swear, by the end of the term, I was starting to  become  Lady Macbeth, just to feel something different. Are you at least making progress with the Spanish homework? That Ms. Rodriguez actually seems to care about us understanding it, not just reciting verbs. Sort of. I’m really struggling with the subjunctive. It's just… so many rules! And then remembering which ones apply when? It’s giving me a right headache. You’re always so good at languages, how do  you  cope? It's practice, I think. And honestly, Duolingo is my friend. Don't judge. Plus, I think because I know I want to actually  use  it. I was looking at gap year programs – volunteering in Spain, maybe, teaching English. Woah, seriously? That sounds amazing! I haven't even thought that far ahead. I'm still trying to decide what to have for dinner, let alone what I want to  do  with the rest of my life. Mum's making shepherd’s pie, by the way. Though knowing her, there'll be broccoli on the side. Oh, good or bad? Broccoli’s not the worst, but… Bad. Definitely bad. It’s limp and overcooked every time. Last week it was practically translucent. Remember when we tried to convince ourselves we liked it in Year 7, to seem sophisticated? Oh my god, yes! We were so desperate to be grown-up. “Oh yes, broccoli is  divine .” Honestly. What about maths? Have you started on the trigonometry questions? Don't even. It's all sines and cosines and things moving in circles. I just… I don’t  get  it. Mr. Harrison just breezes through it like it’s the most obvious thing in the world. He’s brilliant, but sometimes he forgets not everyone thinks like him. He’s the same with English, actually. He always brings up incredibly obscure poetry and expects us all to know it. I actually had to Google Wordsworth last night –  Wordsworth!  It’s embarrassing. Maybe we should set up a study group, just the two of us? We could tackle the maths and Spanish together. That’s a really good idea! We could meet at the library after school?

…and honestly, darling, the special effects were just  ridiculous . Like, a giant rubber squid attacking Brighton Pier? Honestly! It felt like something out of a 1950s B-movie, not a blockbuster that cost a fortune to make. Oh, Gran, you’re such a cynic! You never like the big, flashy ones, do you? I thought it was pretty fun, actually. A bit silly, yeah, but good escapism. Escapism? I prefer escapism that doesn’t insult my intelligence, thank you very much. Give me a good character study any day. Something like…oh, what was that lovely film with Judi Dench? The one where she played the queen?  The Favourite ? Or  Mrs Brown ? You’ve watched both of those at least five times each. Oh, they’re both good. But I was thinking…the one before that. With Bill Nighy. Oh, bother, it’s on the tip of my tongue. It was about…a vicar.  Their Best Exotic Marigold Hotel ? That one has Judi Dench too, and Bill Nighy is in it, but he’s not  the  main character… No, no, not that one. This was…smaller. More about relationships. Oh, it’s infuriating. Anyway, never mind. This squid film… honestly, I couldn’t take it seriously. It wouldn't even scare a goldfish! Okay, okay, point taken. I get you prefer something a little more…subtle. I was actually thinking of going to see that new one,  Echoes of the Past , next week. The reviews are supposed to be really good. It’s about a woman rediscovering her family history. Oh, that sounds much more my cup of tea. Is it a bit… grim, though? I’m not in the mood for a proper weeper. Apparently, it's sad but hopeful. Lots of flashbacks and beautiful scenery. They filmed some of it in Cornwall. Cornwall! Oh, I do love Cornwall. We went there on our honeymoon, you know. 1972 it was. Rained for a week solid, but we still had a lovely time. Honestly, Gran, you always have a story to tell! That’s why I love talking films with you. It's never just about the film, is it? It's about…everything else. Well, life  is  everything else, isn’t it, dear? Films just remind you of bits and pieces. This squid film reminded me of that awful trip to Southend-on-Sea when I was a little girl.

…and honestly, the traffic was  brutal . Honestly, Mum, I think I aged about ten years in that queue on the M40. Did you see anything on the news about it? Apparently, there was an accident near Oxford. Oh, you poor love. The M40’s always a nightmare, isn't it? Though, I haven’t been on a motorway in…well, since I retired, really. Just little potters around Birmingham now. Are you sure you’re alright? You look a bit flustered. More sugar? I’m fine, really. Just a bit… stressed. It’s just everything piling up. Work’s been manic - prepping for the new curriculum, marking seemingly endless essays on  Hamlet  – honestly, teenagers and Shakespeare. A losing battle – and then that drive. And now I need to figure out Leo’s vet appointment. He’s been scratching again. Poor Leo. He’s always been a sensitive soul, that cat. Probably allergies. Did you get that new hypoallergenic food I told you about? Old Mrs. Higgins swore by it for Winston, and he had terrible skin. I did, and he’s been on it for a week. No improvement, unfortunately. That’s why I need to book the vet. It’s just... money’s a bit tight this month. New tyres on the car ate into the budget, and then the school trip deposit for Lily… Oh, Lily's school trip! Where are they off to this time? France. Paris, actually. She’s so excited, but it's a significant chunk of change. I told her she'd have to contribute, pocket money and maybe doing extra chores. Good for her, learning the value of a pound. Though, Paris is lovely. I went once, years ago, with your father. Before everything… It was raining, naturally, but even the grey Paris was beautiful. He tried to order snails. Nearly choked, he did. Dad and adventurous cuisine rarely mixed. He was a pie and mash man, through and through. Speaking of which, are you still going to Auntie Brenda’s on Sunday? Yes, dear. Brenda's been on at me to come round for ages. She keeps saying she needs help with her crossword. Honestly, she gets them from the paper, they're not  that  hard. But she enjoys the company, I suppose. And she always pushes a plate of biscuits at me. They're a bit dry, but it’s the thought that counts.

…and honestly, the student just kept arguing! He claimed my interpretation of Yeats was “entirely subjective” as if  all  literary criticism isn’t subjective, to some degree! Honestly, the audacity. Sounds like a typical Tuesday, then. You’d think after three years of lecturing, they’d realise there isn't always a ‘right’ answer. Were you teaching ‘Sailing to Byzantium’ again? You always get the most…spirited debates with that one. It was, actually. And yes, “spirited” is a polite way of putting it. It’s just frustrating. I’m trying to encourage critical thinking, not a battle of wills! How was your afternoon? Less Yeats, I presume? Thankfully, no Yeats. Just a lot of database management, which is infinitely less prone to existential crises. Though Professor Chen did corner me about the research grant applications again. He's convinced we should pivot the whole project, and I’m trying to politely explain why that’s… impractical, three weeks before the deadline. Oh,  him . Always wanting to reinvent the wheel. Remember when he wanted us to incorporate competitive origami into the introductory statistics course? How could I forget! He said it would “enhance spatial reasoning.” It was chaos. Listen, are we stopping for groceries? I practically inhaled my lunch and I'm already thinking about dinner. Good thinking. I was going to suggest it. The little market near the noodle shop, yeah? I need to pick up some coriander, and I’m out of ginger. It's getting quite chilly, isn't it? Even for November in Kunming. It is. Feels like a proper English November, actually. Damp and grey. Though I’m not complaining, honestly. Beats the heatwave we had in September. Speaking of needing things, I need new running shoes. Mine are falling apart. Oh, no! The bright blue ones? The very same. They’ve seen better days. There’s that sports shop in the Parkson Mall, isn’t there? We could go on Saturday, after the language exchange? That sounds good. Parkson Mall is a bit of a trek, but they usually have a good selection. Though finding your size can be a nightmare. You have ridiculously large feet, you know. Hey! They’re perfectly proportionate to my height! Anyway, the mall's good for window shopping too. Maybe find you a nice scarf? You've been saying yours is getting a bit threadbare. Oh, stop it. You spoil me.

…and honestly, the buttercream was a disaster. It just…split. I think I added the butter when it was too warm. It looked like scrambled eggs, honestly. Like scrambled eggs? Really? Ewwww! Scrambled egg icing! That sounds yucky. It  was  yucky, darling. That’s why we had apple slices instead. Anyway, that’s why I’m slightly hesitant about attempting a three-tiered masterpiece for Aunt Carol’s birthday. But you're a really good baker, Mummy! You made that chocolate cake for Grandad, and he said it was the best EVER. That’s sweet of you, poppet. Grandad would say that about anything, bless him. Right, focus. Okay, so Sarah wants to know if we’re still on for Saturday night. She’s finally back from her pottery course. Is that when you're taking pictures of me and Lily? The photoshoot? Yes, sweetie, that’s the plan. Sarah’s going to take some photos for my website – you know, for my teaching profile. She's really good with a camera. And yes, we’re still on for Saturday with Sarah. I already said yes. The question is, who looks after you two little monkeys while we’re out? Can Grandma come? Please, can Grandma come? Grandma’s got her bridge club on Saturday, remember? She’s captain this month, it's very important! I’ve already asked her. Hmm… Uncle David said he  might  be free, but he’s a bit… unreliable. Uncle David is always playing on his computer! He does enjoy his games, doesn't he? Right, options. I was thinking maybe Mrs. Henderson? You both like her, she always reads you lovely stories. She reads really fast! And she made us those sparkly bracelets last time. I want her to read the dinosaur book! The one with the really scary T-Rex! Okay, dinosaur book it is. Let me text Mrs. Henderson now. Okay, sent! Fingers crossed. While we wait, how about we have a quick read? I’ve got that new Roald Dahl book. Ooh! The one about the boy who collects smelly socks? That’s the one! Though it’s not  just  smelly socks, is it? It's a whole adventure! But first, let's talk dinner. I was thinking spaghetti bolognese? With lots of cheese! Lots of cheese it is! You’re very demanding, you know that? Speaking of demanding… Lily, your hair is getting very long.

… honestly, the library is a  state  right now. Packed. You can barely find a plug socket, let alone a quiet corner. I swear everyone decided to leave all their revision to the last minute. Tell me about it! I tried to book a study room yesterday, thinking I was being proactive, and they were all gone. All of them! Ended up just hovering, hoping someone would leave. It was like vultures circling a fallen biscuit, innit? Vultures circling a biscuit! That’s brilliant. Honestly, it’s stressing me out. This media law essay is a monster. I just… I don’t get half of it. It’s all ‘implied contracts’ and ‘defamation’ and my brain just short-circuits. Ugh, law stuff is the worst. I'm glad I stuck with psychology. Though, trying to understand the human brain is a different kind of impossible, to be fair. What are you having anyway? That pasta looks alright. It  looks  alright. It tastes…beige. Like, aggressively beige. It's the veggie pasta, but seriously, where's the flavour? Kingston Uni canteen, lowering my standards since September. You got a better choice? I went for the jerk chicken and rice and peas. It's actually surprisingly decent. My mum makes a  way  better version, obviously. Hers is… transcendent. But for canteen food, it’s a solid 7/10. Ooh, that does sound good. Mum’s cooking is always transcendent. Mine makes a mean roast, but even she struggles with canteen-level blandness. Speaking of mums… mine's been on at me to come home for the weekend. Oh yeah? What’s the occasion? Aside from needing a break from beige pasta, of course? Just… general ‘daughter needing a home-cooked meal and a stern talking-to’ vibes. She keeps hinting I need to 'focus' and 'think about my future'. You know the drill. Oh, the classic. Mine’s the same. She thinks I should be doing a placement year. Like, suddenly  now  she’s all about work experience? When I told her I was thinking about backpacking around Southeast Asia next summer, she nearly choked on her adobo. Backpacking?! Now  that  sounds amazing. That’s way more appealing than a placement year filled with photocopying and making coffee. Though, I'm pretty sure my mum would have the same reaction as yours. She’s a planner, that one. It'd be good though, yeah? Proper adventure.

…and honestly, the amount of rain we had in Whitby was biblical. Like, Noah's Ark biblical. You’d think being by the sea it’d be bracing, you know? Fresh air. Instead, it was just… damp. Perpetually damp. Whitby, eh? Bit of a cliché for a Northern getaway, isn’t it? Though, I can picture it. Mum dragged us to the coast every year. Usually Southend.  That  was a disaster waiting to happen. Seagulls the size of small dogs, chip grease everywhere… Southend's a special kind of hell, I agree. I’ve been. Cambridge is alright though, isn’t it? Not the beach, obviously, but at least it doesn’t smell permanently of fried things. So, Anya, Whitby aside, did you actually  enjoy  your holiday? I did, eventually. Once I accepted the fact I was living in a waterproof coat. The Dracula stuff was good, actually. Really leaned into the gothic vibe. And the fish and chips, despite the drizzle, were phenomenal. Proper haddock, not that frozen rubbish you get down south. Hey! We get good fish and chips in Kent! Okay, maybe not  everywhere , but Pembury knows its way around a fryer. We're close enough to the sea, you see. Although, admittedly, it’s not quite the North Sea experience. This is important research. Anya, you’re the North-East expert. Rate the fish and chips in Whitby, out of ten. And then we’ll get Alistair to rate a Kentish establishment. We need data. For… reasons. Honestly? Nine out of ten. The batter was perfect – crispy, but not greasy. And the portion size was obscene. You could feed a family on one serving. Right, okay. Challenge accepted. I’ll find the best chippy in Pembury and put it to the test. Though I make no promises it’ll reach nine. It’s a high bar. Speaking of tests…are we still on for that new series of 'Taskmaster' tonight? I’ve heard Greg Davies is particularly savage this season. Absolutely. I’ve cleared my schedule. It's the only reason I agreed to have dinner here. Your cooking is fantastic, Anya, but 'Taskmaster' is a national treasure. Oh, so my shepherd's pie isn't a national treasure? I spent hours making that! It’s got proper lamb mince, not that cheap stuff. It  was  good, genuinely. But the sheer, unadulterated joy of watching people fail spectacularly at ridiculous tasks… it's unmatched.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the price of a sausage roll in King’s Cross now. Four pound fifty! Four pound fifty for a bit o’ pastry and some sausage meat. Daylight robbery, I tell you. Daylight robbery. Oh, Arthur, you and your sausage rolls. Everything’s gone up, love. You noticed that when we were lookin’ at them little cottages in Norfolk, didn’t you? Even the price of a decent cuppa is scandalous these days. You two are always on about the price of things. Honestly. Though I have to admit, London  is  expensive. I had a meeting there last week, barely touched my lunch. Not worth the money. How was the rest of the trip, though? Did you get to see the horses at Buckingham Palace? The horses were alright. Bit…static, weren’t they? Just standin’ there. Give me a good, honest plough horse any day. Now  they  got muscle. Reminded me of Old Man Hemmings’ Clydesdale. Beautiful animal, that was. Shame what happened. Oh, Arthur, not the story about Hemmings’ horse  again . We’ve heard it a hundred times! It wandered onto the A47, you know. It’s a sad story, but… But it weren’t ‘is fault! That horse was spooked by a lorry. A great big, rumblin’ thing. They shouldn't allow them lorries on them roads, I say. Right. Well, moving swiftly on… have you two thought any more about selling the house? The market’s still quite buoyant, apparently. I was speaking to a colleague - Sarah, she’s an estate agent - and she reckons we could get a good price. I’ve been lookin’ on Rightmove, just for a bit of fun, mind. And the prices are mental. People wanttin’ all sorts for their money. Tiny little gardens, damp patches… and they're askin' a fortune. Sellin’ the house? Now hold on a minute. Where would we go? We’ve got all our memories here. All me collections. You can't just upsticks and move after seventy-odd years in Costessey. No one's suggesting you move to Kazakhstan, Arthur. Just… perhaps downsize. Somewhere easier to manage? Sarah was saying there’s a lovely little bungalow come up near Wymondham. Two bedrooms, level garden. I did see a few bungalows. But they all need doin' up. And that costs money, doesn't it? More money. And then there’s the car.

…and honestly, the amount of unsolicited advice is just  relentless . Like, everyone's a parenting expert the second you announce you're pregnant. Old Mrs. Higgins at the post office was telling me about how she weaned her kids onto mashed parsnips in 1972. Parsnips! Oh god, don't even. My mum's been on a similar trajectory. Apparently, my cousin Sharon's baby thrived on homemade bone broth. Bone broth, Liv! It's like they think we’re living in the Victorian era. How's little Arthur taking to… well, everything? He’s good. Sleep is… patchy. But he’s gaining weight, which is the main thing, apparently. I’m still trying to figure out this whole breastfeeding thing. It's way harder than it looks. Everyone makes it seem so natural, and then you’re just sat there, leaking and in pain, wondering if you’re doing it right. Tell me about it! I remember those first few weeks with Leo. Honestly, I felt like a cow. Constantly tethered to the sofa, just… feeding. And the latch! It took ages to get the latch right, didn’t it? You’re lucky you’ve got the NCT group, at least. I didn't have anything like that. Just Mum hovering and offering opinions. The NCT group is a lifesaver. Though half of them seem to have these perfect, serene breastfeeding journeys that I’m clearly failing at. Sarah’s baby latched immediately and feeds for forty-five minutes on each side, blissfully contented. Mine spends ten minutes having a good suck and then decides he's had enough and stares at the ceiling. Oh, stop comparing yourself! That’s the worst thing you can do. Every baby is different. Leo was a terrible feeder to begin with. He used to just fall asleep mid-feed, and I was convinced he wasn't getting enough. It stressed me out so much. Did you talk to a health visitor? Yeah, she's reassuring, says he's putting on weight so I shouldn’t worry. But she also said I need to ‘relax’ more. As if  that’s  helpful. It’s easier said than done when you’re constantly anxious about a tiny human relying on you for everything. Easier said than done is an understatement. Honestly, the anxiety doesn't really go away, does it? It just… changes form. I'm worrying now about playdates and starting school.

…and honestly, the price of lettuce! It’s beyond a joke, isn’t it? Five pounds for a cos lettuce! Five pounds! What are they thinking? Alright, alright, Brenda, calm down. It's just lettuce. Though I agree, it  is  ridiculous. Everything’s going up, isn’t it? You read something new every day. Apparently, tomato crops are having a rough time in Spain. Explains a lot. Oh, I saw that. It’s the heatwave, really. Crippled everything. Though five pounds for lettuce… that's just opportunistic pricing, Dad. Pure and simple. Morning all. What’s all the fuss about lettuce? Sounds serious. Did someone steal our lettuce? Worse, Pat, far worse. They’re  charging  us a fortune for it. Honestly, I’m thinking of growing my own. Though the slugs will have a field day. You always say that, love. Remember the disastrous courgette attempt last year? The slugs won, hands down. That was different! I didn’t have netting then. This year will be strategic. Anyway, what are your plans for today, Pat? Big shift at the hospital, I presume? Yep. Full on. Ward 7 is currently resembling a battlefield. Flu’s going around like wildfire. I’m shadowing Dr. Henderson today, so hopefully I'll learn some proper triage skills. It’s terrifying how quickly things can escalate, even with relatively healthy patients. You’ll be amazing, Pat. You’ve got a natural head for it. Remember how you dealt with Gran’s fall last Christmas? Calm as you like. That was different. That was  Gran . Any panic I felt was immediately overridden by needing to get her comfortable. Still, hospital’s a different beast. Speaking of Beasts… where’s Winston? Haven’t seen the furry tyrant this morning. He’s under the table, snoring like a lumberjack. Probably dreamed he’d caught the postman again. That cat is convinced he's a security guard. I saw on TikTok yesterday a cat trying to operate a self-checkout. Hilarious! Honestly, they're so strange. TikTok? Honestly, Chloe. Always on that phone. You need to get out more. Dad, I  am  getting out more. I’ve got that meeting with the client this afternoon about the new campaign for the garden centre. It’s actually a really interesting brief. They want something very…rustic. Think hand-painted signs, wildflower meadows, the whole shebang. Oh, lovely! You’re so good at that, Chloe.

…and honestly, Miss Davies just  loves  to make the maths tests ridiculously hard. Like, who needs to know the area of a trapezium in real life, honestly? It's just…pointless. Tell me about it! I spent ages on that yesterday, and I  still  think I got at least half of it wrong. Though, it's not as bad as physics, is it? Mr. Henderson practically speaks another language. I swear, half the symbols look like tiny alien faces. Ugh, physics. Don’t even get me started. At least with maths, if you know the rules, you can get somewhere. Physics feels completely random. Hey, did you finish that art project? The one with the botanical studies? Nearly! I’ve got the initial sketches done, all the leaves and stuff. It’s actually quite relaxing, drawing plants. Gran’s been helping me with identifying them properly. She’s got like, a whole encyclopaedia of gardening stuff. Gran’s amazing at gardening! Remember that massive pumpkin she grew last year? It was practically bigger than you! She always knows the Latin names for everything too. So impressive. She does! She’s been trying to get me into stamp collecting too, apparently it’s a way to learn about different plants and countries. She's got this huge album, all organised. Honestly, it seems a bit…old-fashioned, doesn't it? A little bit! But kinda cool, I guess. It's definitely a different hobby than scrolling through TikTok. Speaking of old-fashioned, have you even  started  thinking about Christmas? Mum’s already making lists. Oh god, Christmas. Don't remind me. It’s going to be chaos. My aunt Susan is coming all the way from…where was it again? Manchester, I think. And she always asks me about school, like I haven’t just spent the last hour moaning about it to  you . Aw, that’s the worst. My Uncle David always asks me what I want to be when I grow up. As if I know! I’m fifteen, not a fully formed adult. He works in Cambridge still, doesn't he? Something to do with…computers? Yeah, he does. He's a software engineer, I think. He keeps trying to convince me coding is the future. He says Cambridge is totally buzzing with tech companies now. It’s not like when  our  mums were at school, apparently. No way.

…and honestly, Doreen, it’s the eyes, innit? They’re goin’ on me, definite’y. I was tryin’ to thread a needle this mornin’, for mendin’ that little waistcoat for Rodney – you know, the rat puppet? – and I couldn’t see the blessed eye to save my life. Rodney! Oh, bless him. You’re still making things for Rodney? That’s sweet, Arthur. Though honestly, a waistcoat? Doesn’t he get warm enough as it is with all that faux fur? He's a sophisticated rat, apparently. Requires tailoring. Arthur, you really should book an eye test. You were squinting at the racing pages last week, didn’t you? Nearly backed the wrong horse. A costly mistake, as I recall. Costly is right, Geoffrey! Lost a good fiver, I did. But it weren't just the horses, see. It was blurry altogether. And the handbell ringing… that’s gettin’ trickier too. I nearly missed a change last Tuesday, and Maisie gave me such a look! Like  I  was the one upsetting the precision. Maisie  is  a stickler for precision. Always has been. She practically runs the whole tower, doesn’t she? Still, an eye test is a good idea, Arthur. I had mine done last year. Makes such a difference. Remember how I used to struggle reading the bus times? Oh, don’t  mention  the bus times! They’re a nightmare at the best of times. They changed the route again, haven't they? Number 26 used to go right past the chemist, now you’ve gotta walk all the way down to the High Street. It’s a trek for an old man like me. They do seem to change them on a whim. I was trying to get to the garden centre last month, ended up three stops further than I needed to be. Thankfully, I had the satnav on my phone. Though, honestly, relying on technology… it’s not the same as a good, clear bus map. No, it isn't. I miss the old days when the bus conductors knew everyone and could tell you exactly where to get off. And they'd help you with your bags! Remember that, Arthur? You used to get the bus into Norwich every Saturday. Ah, Norwich. Used to be a right bustling place. Went to the market every week with Mum. They had the best plums there, truly. I haven't been in years.

…and honestly, the library’s just  packed  with everyone cramming for finals. I thought a proper coffee and a bit of a chinwag was exactly what I needed. This place is lovely, isn't it? Proper old-school. It is, love. Proper lovely. Café Venice hasn’t changed a bit, has it? Apart from the prices, mind you. Used to be you could get a brew and a biscuit for pennies. Remember when Old Man Rossi ran it? He used to slip you an extra biscotti if you batted your eyelashes at him. Oh, Mum! You're terrible! I wasn’t even born when Old Man Rossi was here! But Dad’s told me stories. He said the whole town used to come here after the football. It was buzzing. Buzzing is right. This was  the  place. Everyone knew everyone. Now it’s… well, still nice, but more tourists, isn't it? And students, like you. They’ve probably never even heard of Horwich Loco Works. Probably not. Everything's changed so much. I was reading about Venice back in the Victorian era, its heyday as a mill town. It was booming, wasn’t it? So different from now. Different doesn't even cover it, petal. My grandad used to work at the mills, down by the canal. Said it was hard work, but everyone had a job, everyone knew their place. There was a community spirit you just don’t see anymore. This café was part of that, really. A central point. It feels like that still, in a way. It's got a good atmosphere. Right, so, what are we doing with the day? I was thinking, after this, we could wander down to the market. See if there’s anything good? And maybe a walk along the canal? The market's a good shout. They’ve got that lovely pie stall now, the one with all the different fillings. And a walk along the canal would be nice. It’s still surprisingly peaceful, even with the M61 rumbling away nearby. Although… I'm craving something sweet. Have they still got those profiteroles here? They used to be to  die  for. I think so! I saw something on the menu that looked like them. We definitely need to try the food. Dad said they’ve upped their game since they did the renovations a few years back. He reckons their lasagne is the best in Bolton.

…and honestly, the leg press felt impossible yesterday. Like, genuinely questioning all my life choices during set three. Did you even  go  to the gym yesterday, or were you conveniently ‘recovering’ from Friday night? Hey! Rude. I was recovering, thank you very much. Leo insisted on trying that new cocktail bar, ‘The Alchemist’, and… well, their concoctions are  strong . Plus, it was Sarah’s birthday. I couldn’t exactly bail. How’s the marathon training going, anyway? Still obsessively tracking your pace? Obsessively is a strong word. Meticulously? Dedicated? Look, it’s in six weeks! I need to know if I’m on track. And yes, I went this morning, despite feeling like I’d been hit by a bus. Speaking of needing to be on track… how’s work? Still battling the beige world of Bupa marketing? Beige is a  very  accurate description. It’s… fine. A lot of meetings about target demographics and increasing uptake of health assessments. Exciting, right? Honestly, I'm starting to think about looking for something completely different. Maybe something more creative. Ooh, like what? You were always so good at art in school. Remember that ridiculous portrait you did of Mr. Henderson, the art teacher? Oh god, don't remind me. It looked like he’d been sculpted from potatoes. No, nothing  that  creative. More… social media management, perhaps? Something where I can actually see the impact of my work. What about you? Still enjoying the project coordination chaos? Chaos is my middle name. Actually, it’s Louise. But it  feels  like chaos. It’s a new project, streamlining the university’s research grant application process. It’s… a lot. Honestly, I’m already dreaming of summer holidays. Have you booked anything? Not yet. I was thinking maybe Greece? Somewhere with sunshine, beaches, and minimal responsibility. I really need to switch off. Remember when we went to Barcelona that time, after uni? That was amazing. Barcelona was epic! We got hopelessly lost at least three times a day. And the tapas… oh, the tapas. This Peri-Peri chicken is good, but it's no patatas bravas. Though, maybe I shouldn’t complain, considering I haven’t even started properly on my Nando’s. You’re demolishing yours! I'm stressed-eating. Beige work stresses require spicy chicken. Speaking of stress… have you heard anything from Ben? He messaged me last week, asking about you.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is astonishing. They’ve already sent three different forms asking for the same information about little Leo! It’s like they  want  to make it difficult. Honestly, you’d think after having two children of my own, registering the birth of a grandchild would be straightforward. Paperwork. The bane of modern existence. It’s always been thus, dear. Though, I daresay it wasn’t quite this complicated when  I  was a lad. Still, births abroad complicate things, don’t they? Your daughter, living in Nice…that throws a spanner in the works. It does. Apparently, because he was born in France, it needs registering with both the French authorities  and  the British consulate. It's a nightmare trying to coordinate everything remotely. She says Nice is lovely, though. Beautiful weather, of course. Though she did mention the property prices are…ambitious. Ambitious is a polite word. France. A fascinating country, utterly frustrating. I’ve always said, controlling land is everything there. Always has been. The peasantry had no real ownership for centuries, you see. So much unrest stemmed from that. And don’t get me started on the bureaucracy! Or the anarchists, for that matter. A volatile mix. Had a rather unfortunate incident with some French visitors a few years back, thought they could simply park anywhere in Oval. Fuss, fuss, fuss! Oh, I can imagine! London parking is a battleground at the best of times. It sounds like your book is really taking shape, then? All these anecdotes… it must be brimming with detail. It is. It’s rather sprawling, to be honest. It started as a study of Philip of Spain and Mary Tudor, but it’s…expanded. Went to the Spanish archives, you know? Fascinating stuff. The sheer detail they kept! Their system of record-keeping put ours to shame. Though weeding through it all… stamina is key. It put me in mind of researching that disaster with the Austrian battleship, the  SMS Szent István . The conflicting reports, the misinformation… historians have a devil of a time getting to the truth. It sounds exhausting. Although, a good historian revels in the detail, doesn’t she? Speaking of detail and disasters – did you hear about the Chichester Cathedral spire? Apparently, a section of it just…collapsed. Good heavens! No, I hadn’t. Dreadful. Porden, wasn't it, the architect? A clever fellow, but even the best are fallible.

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  loves  hearing himself talk. Like, we spent twenty minutes today on the symbolism of a chipped teacup in ‘Great Expectations’! A chipped teacup! Who cares?! Sounds about right. Davies is…intense. More intense than this chilli sauce, definitely. Woah, careful with that stuff, Liam. You’ll breathe fire. He’s not wrong though, about the teacup potentially representing Pip’s fractured social standing. It’s… a stretch, but. Fractured? It’s a  chip , Arlo! It’s probably just been dropped. You’re turning into Davies! This sweet and sour sauce is a lifesaver, honestly. Everything tastes better covered in this. You guys are stressing about Dickens? I’m just trying to survive Maths. Mr. Henderson decided  this week  to start on matrices. Matrices! It’s like he’s deliberately trying to destroy our futures. Oh god, matrices. I felt physically ill when he mentioned them. My brother had to do those in uni. He said they’re useful for…something. Computer graphics? Spaceships? I glazed over. My mum keeps going on about how important Maths is for “life skills”. Like, when am I going to need to calculate the determinant of a matrix at the supermarket? She’s probably thinking about budget spreadsheets, Liam. It’s the mum thing to say. Speaking of mums, mine is trying to get me to eat more vegetables. This prawn cracker is a victory. My Nan’s worse. She tries to sneak spinach into everything.  Everything . I swear she put it in my chocolate brownies last week. No way! That's… dedication. Or madness. Probably both. This place is good though, isn’t it? My family’s been coming here for ages. Best Chinese in Slough, easily. Definitely beats the school dinners. Those grey sausages…I’m still traumatised. Remember when Ben accidentally threw his gravy across the hall in Year 8? Oh my god, yes! And it landed on Mrs. Higgins’ new coat! She went absolutely ballistic. He claimed a pigeon flew in and startled him. A pigeon? Honestly, Ben's stories are legendary. He told his parents he got detention for "philosophical debate" with a teacher. He’s a genius, that one. Though, he  did  try to convince me the new Marvel comic ended with Captain America becoming a sentient toaster. Seriously? That’s peak Ben. He’s got a real talent for fabrication. I’m more worried about the History essay.

…and honestly, Jonathan, darling, you wouldn’t BELIEVE the state of the biscuit tin. Absolutely crammed with those ginger nuts you like, but they’re all broken! Honestly, it looks like a demolition site in there. Oh, Nan, you always say that. It’s a biscuit tin, not a structural engineering project. Are we still on for doing the party food shopping tomorrow, then? I was thinking we could hit up Morrison’s. They’ve got a decent selection. Morrison’s is alright, but their sweets are a bit…basic. Can we maybe just go to the corner shop for the pick ‘n’ mix? That's way better. Hold on a minute, everyone. Before we get too bogged down in confectionery logistics, let's just confirm the guest list. Auntie Brenda confirmed she  can  make it, right? Because if she starts on about her dahlias again… Brenda confirmed. She rang me yesterday, complaining about the price of compost, naturally. Said she’s bringing a Victoria sponge. Though, knowing Brenda, it'll be more sponge than Victoria. Oh dear. Well, at least it’s a sponge. I’m still trying to work out what to get Jonathan. He says he doesn’t  need  anything, which, as you know, is a classic male response. He hinted rather strongly about a new Bluetooth speaker. Apparently, the one he has keeps cutting out during his podcasts. He's obsessed with those true crime ones, isn't he? Drives me mad. Yeah, he's always listening to them. Creepy stuff. A speaker’s good. Or maybe a new game? The one he’s playing at the minute, ‘Galactic Frontiers’ or something, he keeps moaning about needing extra power-ups. Galactic Frontiers. Right. Sounds…intense. I was thinking something less digital. Perhaps a nice leather-bound notebook? He’s been talking about wanting to try and write more. A notebook is lovely, dear, but he’s got mountains of those already. Remember that phase he went through collecting fountain pens? The attic is full of them! It’s all this decluttering we’re doing that’s sparked it, I think. Seeing all the 'stuff' making him think about 'stuff' he  doesn't  need. This whole move is going to be a nightmare, isn’t it? All those memories, all those things… It’s not just a house, it’s a life, is what it is. Mum, don’t start.

…and honestly, Miss Davies practically  threatened  us with the consequences of not choosing ‘the right’ options. Like our entire futures depend on picking between History and Geography! Honestly! Ugh, tell me about it. Mr. Harrison was exactly the same. “Think carefully, this will define you!” Define me? I'm fourteen! The only thing defining me right now is my obsession with that vegan brownie recipe I found on YouTube. Oh, speaking of YouTube, have you seen the latest from Emma Chamberlain? She’s in Japan right now. It's so aesthetic. Way better than thinking about… logarithms. Emma’s brilliant. She makes being an influencer look…effortless, you know? Makes you wonder how much they actually  earn . Imagine just, like, filming yourself and getting paid. That's way more appealing than becoming a solicitor, which is what my mum keeps pushing for. Solicitors are…fine. But boring. My dad keeps saying I should be a doctor. A  surgeon  apparently. Can you imagine me, covered in… stuff? No thanks. I’m leaning towards Art, definitely. And maybe Drama. Drama's good! You’re really good at impressions. Remember when you did Mrs. Peterson? She almost choked on her tea. Oh, that was gold. She gave me a right telling off, though. But seriously, Art and Drama. Maybe English Lit too, even though it’s loads of reading. What are you thinking? I’m struggling. I quite like Biology, but it’s so much memorising. And I’m terrible at PE. Utterly terrible. It’s a constant source of humiliation. PE is the worst. Especially netball. I swear, the ball actively avoids me. It's got a personal vendetta. It's more than that! I genuinely can’t coordinate. And Miss Jenkins keeps saying I need to put in more ‘effort’. What effort? I'm trying! I'm just naturally… un-athletic. I'm considering just avoiding it altogether and taking music instead. Music’s a good shout! You’re amazing at clarinet. Remember that solo you did at the school concert? Everyone was proper impressed. That was ages ago. And my embouchure is failing me at the moment. It feels so wobbly. But yeah, maybe. It’s less terrifying than being tackled by Sophie Davies during hockey. Speaking of which, did you see that article about Simone Biles? Oh my gosh, yes! She's incredible. The strength, the dedication… a total legend.

…and honestly, the audacity of it! Leaving the gate open  again . Honestly, Mrs. Patterson's cat, Winston, was having a field day in my prize-winning dahlias. Nearly took my head off when I tried to shoo him. Nasty little thing, all claws and fluff. Winston, eh? Always been a right rogue, that cat. Old man Patterson lets ‘im roam where ‘e pleases. Reminds me o’ young Derek when ‘e was a lad. Couldn’t keep ‘im contained, no matter what we did. Always climbin’ trees, gettin’ into mischief. Oh, children and animals, always testing the boundaries. It’s nature, isn’t it? Though I must say, dahlias  are  lovely. I always preferred roses myself. Less fuss. Though keeping the aphids off…that was a battle. Remember the greenfly plague of ‘87, Arthur? ’87? Good Lord, that feels a lifetime ago. Everything was plagued then. Greenfly, the weather… Mrs. Miggins’ rhubarb crop failed that year. Disaster, it was. She made the best rhubarb crumble you ever did taste. It sounds idyllic, actually. All this talk of village life and garden pests. Quite a contrast to endless marking and student emails. I was trying to explain the Bayesian Network to a group yesterday, and honestly, half of them looked like they were contemplating the meaning of life, rather than probability. Bayesian what-now? Sounds like somethin’ from that computer of yours, doesn’t it, love? All these fancy systems. I still struggle to work the telly remote sometimes. Used to be a simple on/off switch, you know. Now it’s all programmed and needs updating. Makes your head spin. It’s a model for predicting probabilities, Grandad. Used a lot in AI and machine learning. Essentially, it tries to figure out how things are related. It’s… complicated. But useful. AI. Now there’s a scary thought. Machines thinkin’ for themselves. Gives me the shivers. I saw a program on the telly about self-driving cars. Horrendous. Imagine trusting a  machine  to drive you around! Self-driving cars… Now, I saw a right dust-up about those down at the pub last week. Old George swore they’d never replace a proper driver. Said you need to  feel  the road, understand the engine. He’s got a Morris Minor, you know. Absolutely obsessed with it. Spends more time under the bonnet than he does on the road, I reckon.

…and honestly, the state of it! Old Mrs. Higgins used to say Costessey school was a right pickle even  back  in ‘58. Seems some things never change, eh? They’ve painted it again, have they? Still looks like it needs knockin’ down and startin’ afresh, if you ask me. Oh, don't get me started on schools, Arthur. Harrow wasn't much better when my David went. All these fancy computers and tablets… it’s not the same as a good teacher and a bit of discipline, is it? Though, to be fair, David ended up alright. Works with computers  now , ironically. It’s the way of the world, isn’t it, Margaret? I’m a teacher myself, remember? And yes, the tech can be a distraction, but it also opens up doors. It’s about  how  you use it. Although, trying to get teenagers to use it for learning rather than TikTok is a battle. A constant battle! TikTok? Is that one of these… tweetin’ things? I’ve never got me ‘ead around any of it. My granddaughter, bless ‘er, tries to explain it. Says I should ‘get on the socials’. Sounds right exhausting, if you ask me. All that lookin’ at pictures of people’s dinners. Oh, Arthur, you’re a darling. It  is  mostly pictures of dinners, isn't it? David’s wife is addicted to Instagram. Always showing off her baking. Perfectly iced cakes… makes me feel dreadful about my Victoria sponge, I tell you! Speaking of which, I need to make another one for little Emily next week, she’s having a birthday. That’s nice of you, Margaret. Emily’s a lovely girl. Right, but back to schools… apparently, they’re thinking of ending homework. Can you imagine? Endin’ ‘omework?! What’ll they do with all their time? Get up to mischief, that’s what! When I was a lad, homework was character buildin’. Teach you responsibility and all that. Course, back then it was mostly writin’ lines. "I must not talk in class"… hundreds of times. Oh, the lines! I remember those! Mr. Peterson used to give me lines for everything. Apparently, my ‘chatting’ disrupted the whole class. Though, in my defence, Sarah next to me had a  very  funny story to tell. Actually, reminds me of a joke… Oh, go on, Margaret, let’s have it. We could all do with a good laugh.

… honestly, I’m just baffled. How did it go from a light dusting to  this  in, like, an hour? It's proper coming down now. Cambridge does love a dramatic snowfall, doesn’t it? Remember that one year, back when we first moved here? Everything shut down for a week. Aye, I remember. We were practically living on beans on toast. Speaking of things shutting down, I was hoping to get out to the allotment this weekend. All these seedlings need potting on. Now that’s looking unlikely. Oh, the poor little things. Maybe we can build a mini-greenhouse in the living room? I'm only half-joking. We  do  have space…ish. Don't you even think about it! The living room is already a disaster zone with your piles of research papers. Though, you know, I did see that 'Come Dine With Me' is doing a winter special. Maybe we should apply? Imagine the chaos. Oh god, no. Absolutely not. Remember when your Auntie Brenda was on it? The passive-aggressive commentary? The suspiciously perfect profiteroles? I'd rather face a blizzard in the allotment. Fair enough, fair enough. Brenda's a force of nature. Though, she  did  win. Speaking of forces of nature, Mark's stag do is looming. Have you even thought about what you’re doing? It's only a month away. I’ve been vaguely avoiding thinking about it, to be honest. He wants something…intense. Like, white water rafting and then karaoke dressed as Elvis. I’m currently lobbying for a quiet pub crawl. Slightly less terrifying. What about you and Sarah’s hen? Any progress? It's…complicated. Her mum wants a full-on spa weekend, complete with mud baths and chakra alignment. Sarah just wants to go to a brewery and drink beer. Trying to navigate that diplomatic minefield. It’s going to require serious negotiation skills. And possibly a bottle of wine. Sounds about right. Mothers and hens… a potent combination. We should maybe plan a joint pre-wedding sanity session. Plenty of tea and biscuits. No talk of chakras or Elvis impersonations. Definitely. Right after I’ve mentally prepared for the onslaught of feedback on Mark’s stag do ideas. Oh! And have we actually finalised anything for our summer holiday? Remember we talked about Cornwall? Cornwall is still on the cards, I think. I was looking at a little cottage near St Ives.

…and honestly, Doreen, you always did make the best roast potatoes. None of this air fryer nonsense, proper roasted in dripping, that's the ticket. This is nice, mind, lovely gravy, but… it's just not  quite  the same. Oh, Arthur, you’ll say that every time, won't you? I haven’t made a roast in… well, years now. My hands aren’t what they were. And honestly, this is delicious, Sarah and Ben have done a grand job. Don’t go undermining them now. Thanks, Doreen. It’s good to hear you like it. We tried to follow your recipe for the Yorkshire puddings, actually. Though I think Dad was giving Ben some…  interesting  advice on the batter consistency. Interesting is one word for it. He was very insistent about needing a “good dollop” of something. I think it was bicarbonate of soda? I ended up ignoring him. Good lad! A good dollop is a scientific measurement, you know. My mother used to say that. Though she probably meant butter, to be fair. Speaking of butter, is this salted butter? It tastes a bit…mild. Pretty sure it is, Dad. Maybe your taste buds are just…adjusting. It's a local Norfolk butter, actually, from a farm near Dereham. Dereham, eh? Used to be a proper market town, Dereham. They had a lovely greengrocer’s. Proper fruit and veg, none of this plastic-wrapped stuff. You could get a proper bargain on sprouts back then. Though my mother would boil ‘em to within an inch of their lives. Oh, don’t get me started on overcooked sprouts! I always said, a little bit of bite is essential. People don’t want mush, Arthur. They want something  with  character. We deliberately blanched these for just a few minutes, Doreen. Trying to maintain that character. And we added a bit of pancetta, hoping to elevate them slightly. Pancetta, is it? Fancy. Bit foreign for my liking, pancetta. We just had bacon rinds back in my day. Salted to perfection. You could munch on them for hours. Though I suppose they weren't very good for you... didn't worry about that sort of thing then. Things have changed a bit, Dad. We're slightly more conscious of cardiovascular health now. These days, it's all about balance. Balance! Hmph. When I was a lad, balance meant being able to walk a straight line after a pint down the pub.

…and honestly, the amount of washing up after making a soufflé is  criminal . It's just not worth it for a slightly puffed-up egg mixture, is it? You tried a soufflé? Brave move, Alice. I barely attempt anything beyond pasta. Though, Mum’s roast dinners are legendary. Seriously, no one can make Yorkshire puddings like she can. Oh, don’t I know it! I’ve tried replicating them for years. Never quite get the rise. It’s the lard, you know. People are too scared of lard these days. Everything’s gotta be olive oil and ‘healthy fats’. Pah! Lard is the answer. My mother used to say, “If in doubt, add lard.” Sorted everything. Though, speaking of houses… young Thomas next door is putting in one of those American-style fridges, the ones with the ice dispenser. Waste of money, that is. Fridges weren’t even a twinkle in anyone’s eye when  I  was a lad. We had a… a larder. Cold larder. Dug into the earth, it was. Kept things lovely and cool. None of this electric nonsense. A cold larder? Wow, Grandad, that sounds… archaic. But probably more reliable than my fridge, actually. It keeps making this weird whirring noise. I think it’s dying. Which, considering I just moved into that tiny flat, is fantastic news. Tiny flat? Still settling in then? How's Wegberg treating you? It must be a bit different from Peterborough, eh? It's… different. Very German, unsurprisingly. And quiet.  Very  quiet. Which is nice sometimes, after London. But I miss having a proper bakery on every corner. And pubs that aren’t all wood panelling and oompah bands. Oompah bands? Wegberg sounds a bit… lively, then? I thought Germany was all efficiency and sausages. There’s definitely efficiency. And lots of sausages. But it also has a surprising number of themed pubs. It's a bit of a student town. I'm working at the university, in administration. It's… fine. A bit dull, honestly. Hence the soufflé attempt. I needed some excitement. Dull work is the worst. I remember when I was working, in accounts. Numbers, numbers, numbers all day. Drove me mad. Glad to be retired. Though, this house needs constant attention. Damp's getting into the back bedroom again. Damp! That's the bane of all houses. Had it in our old place in Salford. We tried everything.

…and honestly, the whole thing just spiralled. Apparently, Brenda from accounts thought it was a passive-aggressive comment about her biscuit choices. A  biscuit , Sarah! It was about workflow efficiency! Honestly, people. Oh, you and office politics. Still battling those demons even from the sun-drenched shores of Australia, I see. It’s good to be house-sitting, isn't it? A bit of distance. Though, honestly, this house needs a serious declutter. Have you seen the Tupperware collection? It’s…ambitious. Ambitious is a polite word. It’s a monument to forgotten leftovers. But yes, blissful distance. It’s given me headspace to actually  think  about the uni project. I was mulling over that idea we chatted about – the ‘micro-credential’ system. The one for postgraduate research skills? I think it's brilliant. So much better than just throwing students in at the deep end with a thesis proposal and hoping they don't drown. But how do we make it…sticky? Universities are  so  resistant to change. Sticky is the key word. I was thinking – gamification. Little badges for mastering research methodologies, collaborative online workshops with real-time feedback, even a leaderboard. A bit nerdy, admittedly, but think of the engagement. We could call it “Research Quest.” “Research Quest”? Oh, Alistair, you’re terrible! But…it  has  a ring to it. It wouldn't be my first choice, but it’s memorable. It needs to feel professional, though. Maybe something more… academic-sounding, then layered with the gamification elements. Like, a ‘Research Accelerator’ programme with levels and rewards? Accelerator’s good. I like that. We could leverage TikTok - short, snappy explainer videos on things like literature reviews or ethical considerations. You know, target the students where they already are. I saw this absolutely bonkers video the other day – a bloke building a functional trebuchet in his garden using only IKEA parts. It got 20 million views. Imagine the reach! A trebuchet…right. And how does that relate to postgraduate research? It’s about grabbing attention! It proves people will watch seemingly obscure content if it’s presented well. We need to make research skills  less  intimidating. We’re battling years of ingrained fear of failure. Think about the start-up world – fail fast, learn faster. We need to instil that mentality. That’s a good point. The perfectionism is crippling for so many. I see it with my students constantly.

…and honestly, the spreadsheets nearly defeated me. Three different departments all wanting slightly different data, and Mr. Henderson breathing down my neck. It was  chaos . How was your shift? Please tell me it involved less passive-aggressive emailing. Oh, you have  no  idea how good it is to hear you complain about spreadsheets. Mine involved… a gentleman convinced he was being followed by pigeons. Very persistent pigeons. At least spreadsheets don’t coo. Pigeons? Seriously? Right, spreadsheets are winning today. I’m making a shepherd’s pie, by the way. Comfort food is essential after a week like this. You in? Definitely in! Smells amazing already. Shepherds pie is perfect. It’s going to be a proper autumnal weekend, isn't it? I was thinking we could actually  do  something. Not just collapse into a Netflix-induced coma. I’m up for it. I was looking at going to Rye. Have you ever been? It’s supposed to be really pretty, all cobbled streets and historic buildings. Apparently, it’s got this amazing mermaid street. Bit touristy, maybe, but…a change of scenery. Rye! Oh, I’ve heard of it. Isn’t it in East Sussex? My grandma used to talk about going there on day trips. She loved all those little Sussex towns – Arundel, Chichester… said they had the best cream teas. That’s the one! Cream teas sound excellent, actually. Okay, Rye is potentially on the cards. Alternatively, I heard there's a massive Halloween party happening in Brighton. A friend of a friend is organising it. Brighton, huh? A Halloween party… That  does  sound fun. Depending on my rota, of course. It's a nightmare building one for October, everyone wants the weekend off. Speaking of which, five years from now, do you see yourself still battling spreadsheets, or have you escaped to a tropical island? A tropical island funded by… what, exactly? My shrewd investment in novelty staplers? No, honestly, five years… I'd like to be managing larger projects, maybe even leading a team. Less detail, more strategy. And potentially… living somewhere a bit less grey. Maybe closer to the coast. Devon, maybe? Devon is lovely. Proper countryside. I’m aiming for a more specialist role in mental health, possibly working with eating disorders. I’m thinking of going back and doing a course in family therapy. It's scary thinking that far ahead, isn’t it?

…and honestly, the audacity of it! Leaving the milk out  again . You’d think after sixty-odd years, a person would grasp the concept of refrigeration, wouldn’t you? Honestly, it's like living with a particularly forgetful teenager, not a grown man. Gran, you’re on a roll. Dad just forgets, it’s not malicious. He’s got a lot on his mind with the garden club and… well, everything. Everything? Everything is usually finding the remote control or complaining about the price of tomatoes. It’s not exactly running a multinational corporation, dear. No, it’s just… irritating. You know I like a cuppa with proper milk, not something lukewarm and threatening. I know, I know. I’ll say something, honestly. Though you know what he’s like – he’ll just say he was ‘airing’ it. He thinks that makes it better. ‘Airing’ it! Good Lord. Next he’ll be airing the butter. Speaking of which, did you manage to get the forms sorted for the council tax? They’ve sent me another threatening letter. Yeah, I did them online last night. Should be all sorted. They’re such a pain, though. Honestly, the website is designed to confuse people. Trying to navigate it felt like a full-time job.
