We can still do laser quest, maybe next weekend when he's better. We'll have to adjust slightly. It’s a bit odd having birthdays so close together, isn’t it? March 17th and March 21st… almost twins! It’s cool! More cake! You’re absolutely right. More cake. Although, Nana's requested we have that Monet-themed cake she saw online. The water lilies. Monet? Like the painter? That's… boring. I want a dinosaur cake! Or a spaceship! We can discuss the cake further. First, let's focus on dinner. I'm making roasted chicken and… …and I thought we could try some radishes with butter? Radishes?! No way! They taste like… dirt! I like radishes! They’re crunchy. See? Someone appreciates a little bit of earthiness. Honestly, you two. Speaking of earthy things, your Maths homework looked a bit… patchy.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of emails I had waiting for me when I got back was criminal. Like, who sends that many emails over a long weekend? It’s just…rude. Oof, tell me about it. Even checking my work emails felt like a full-time job just dealing with the backlog. Luckily, it wasn't too bad, mostly just updates from the team. Though Mrs. Henderson  did  manage to swallow her dentures again. Seriously. Second time this month. Oh, bless her. You’re always dealing with the most… interesting cases. It's a far cry from writing catchy slogans for toilet cleaner, isn't it? Though, to be fair, "Sparkling Fresh! For a Throne You Can Trust!"  is  pretty good. You and your copywriting brilliance. It's needed, honestly. I was starting to forget what a normal conversation even  is . Everything's ‘can you swallow?’ or ‘point to where it hurts.’ How’s the new flat treating you, by the way? Settled in alright? I still can’t believe you actually moved out of Mum and Dad’s. Relatively settled. It’s small, obviously. But small is good. Small means less to clean. Speaking of which, I’ve discovered the joy of a robot vacuum. Honestly, Reginald is the best investment I’ve ever made. Though he does have a vendetta against the sofa legs. Reginald? You  named  your robot vacuum? Classic you. I considered getting one, but then I remembered Winston and thought the ensuing chaos wouldn't be worth it. He’d probably try to ride it. Oh god, you’re right. Absolute carnage. Winston's a menace, a beautiful, fluffy menace. How  is  the little beast? Still obsessed with stealing socks? Worse. He’s graduated to underwear. And slippers. I came downstairs this morning to find him proudly parading around with my favourite pair of fluffy pink ones. I’m starting to think he’s deliberately doing it for the Instagram likes. He's a superstar. You've created a monster! So, are you and Ben still talking about… you know… the big move? To the Cotswolds? It's still on the cards, I think. Ben’s found a few potential jobs. It’s just…leaving Mum and Dad feels awful. And finding a practice that'll take me, with the right specialism, is proving tricky. Adult acute speech therapy isn’t exactly booming in rural areas.

…and honestly, the hills around Almondsbury were  brutal . But Dad insisted. Said it built character. Every Saturday, rain or shine, we’d be out on those bikes. I was always trailing behind, desperately trying to keep up with my brother. He was a natural. I was… less so. Though, looking back, it was good for me. Probably why my knees are shot now, but good for me! Sounds familiar, Margaret. My father had me doing paper rounds in Ramsgate from the age of ten. Built character, he said. More like built resentment! Though, it did teach me resourcefulness, I suppose. Speaking of building things, Arthur, you were saying about the solar farm application last night? What was the final verdict? They approved it. Despite the objections. A lot of local fury, naturally. Old Man Hemmings was incandescent. Said it’ll ruin the view across the valley. I argued that we need to be realistic about renewable energy, but… well, he wasn’t listening. Feels like a lost cause sometimes, fighting these battles. Lost causes are a speciality of mine, I’m afraid. Remember my early days as a dentist? The NHS… it was a different world then. We had ‘perks’ you wouldn’t believe. Sailing trips even! Annual conferences… “lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon,” as old Dr. Pritchard used to say. Honestly, it sounds ridiculous now, doesn't it? Sailing trips! Goodness me, Ronald, you’re spoiling us with tales of luxury! We just had lukewarm tea in the staff room. Though, I did manage to snag a rather good deal on a trip to Prague a few years back. Absolutely stunning city. Have you been? Prague? No, never. Keep meaning to. Everything seems so expensive these days, though. But bargains  are  still out there, aren't they? I saw an offer for a weekend in Budapest… tempting. Getting into things is the problem, though. Everything’s booked solid. I tried to get tickets for the Matisse exhibition at the Tate, impossible! That’s where knowing people helps, Derek. A friend of mine worked there for years. He knows a few… back doors. Honestly, you'd be surprised how many empty seats there are even when everything's "sold out." It's all about timing and a friendly face. Speaking of events, are we still on for that jive night? Absolutely! I’ve been brushing up on my swing.

…so, the thing is, TikTok’s reach with that age group is undeniable. Even my niece, who’s barely ten, is all over it. But how do we leverage that for something…  educational ? It feels like swimming upstream, honestly. Everyone's so focused on entertainment. It  is  a challenge, isn’t it? But think about it – where did kids learn about history before documentaries? Stories! TikTok is just a new storytelling medium. It’s short-form, visual… we need to think about how to distill concepts down to those digestible bites. You were talking about case studies, right? Film analysis? Exactly! I’ve been mulling over building a series based on moving image techniques – how filmmakers use framing, editing, sound – to  tell  a story, to evoke emotion, to persuade. We could use clips from iconic movies, documentaries… even TV commercials. Showing  how  it’s done, not just saying "this is good filmmaking." I like that. Very practical. And we could tie it to specific curriculum areas, couldn't we? Like, a clip from 'Citizen Kane' and a discussion about narrative structure for English Literature. Or a propaganda film segment for History – discussing manipulative techniques. Precisely! And it doesn’t have to be high-brow. Think about advertising - kids are bombarded with it. Deconstructing an ad is brilliant media literacy. But… the platform. TikTok feels… transient. Is that the right place to build something with long-term educational value? Hmm, good point. Maybe TikTok as a  teaser , a way to drive traffic to a more robust platform? Like a dedicated website with the full case studies, supplementary material, downloadable worksheets… maybe even a forum for discussion. That’s… smarter. Keep the short, punchy stuff for TikTok, but have a ‘home base’ for the real learning. We'd need to invest in web design, of course. And content creation. Lots of it. Remember that disastrous attempt at YouTube tutorials I did for that tech startup? Oh,  please . The lighting was atrocious, and you kept saying “um” every other word! But you learned from it. We’ll be better organised this time. I've been thinking about the learning materials – maybe we could produce transcripts of the analyses, interactive quizzes… things teachers can actually use in the classroom. You’re brilliant at that – anticipating the teacher’s needs. I'm good at the ‘big picture’, the conceptual stuff. You’re the detail person. Makes us a decent team, I suppose.

…and honestly, the tide was  miles  out. You could walk for ages and still be nowhere near the water. It felt… alien, almost. Not like the sea I remember from Cromer, all crashing waves and bracing wind. Miles out, you say? Sounds like the kind of low tide Old Man Hemmings used to wax lyrical about. He swore, down at Seaford, you could find Roman pottery if you timed it right. Though knowing Hemmings, half his ‘pottery’ was probably just unusually shaped rocks. Probably! Though that does sound rather exciting. Did you hear back from David about his trip to Cornwall? He was going to try and do some proper coastal path hiking, wasn't he? I did, actually. Just this morning. Said it was…challenging. Apparently, the South West Coast Path is not messing around. Blisters the size of 50p pieces, near-vertical climbs, and weather that changed every five minutes. He sent a picture of himself looking utterly defeated, clinging to a gorse bush. Oh, poor David! He's always been a bit of a city boy at heart, isn't he? All those pavements and predictable tube lines. The sea is…insistent. It doesn’t care if you’ve had a long day and just want a lie-down. Insistent is a good word. It's demanding, isn't it? Reminds me of Professor Ainsworth, ironically. Always demanding meticulously referenced footnotes. Did you see Sarah’s post about her sailing trip? The one with the ridiculously expensive yacht? Yes. Looked idyllic. Though Sarah and "roughing it" don’t really go together, do they? Give me a windswept beach and a flask of tea over a cabin boy bringing me canapés any day. Definitely. Although, a cabin boy bringing canapés  does  sound rather appealing right about now. My feet are starting to ache. We’ve done a good stretch of the park, haven't we? We have. Though it’s hardly the same as feeling sand between your toes. I miss that. I haven’t been back to Norfolk properly in… goodness, nearly a year now. It's too long. You need a proper seaside fix. We should definitely plan something. Maybe a weekend in Whitby? It’s a bit gothic, but the coastline is dramatic. Whitby sounds lovely. Though I always feel a bit… exposed there. The North Sea just feels much bigger, much wilder, than the calmer waters around Norfolk.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  it. Sequins for daytime? In November? It’s a bit much, innit? Like, Vivienne Westwood was a genius and all, but sometimes she just…lost the plot a bit. I think it’s about making a statement, honestly. It’s not necessarily about practical wear. It’s art, really. Plus, she always had a point to make, didn’t she? Political, cultural… the sequins were probably a rebellion against something. I’m with Chloe. It's a bit ‘look at me’, isn’t it? But then again, fashion  is  about attention. I’m just trying to figure out what I’m wearing to Sarah’s birthday on Saturday. I was thinking that new burgundy dress, but… I don’t know. It feels a bit…safe? Burgundy’s lovely, love. Really flattering on you. But if you want to spice it up, maybe a belt? Or a statement necklace? I saw one in Doncaster market last week, all chunky gold and…well, it was a bit much even  for  me, but it made me think of you. You could pull that off. Ooh, a belt's a good shout, actually. And are we still talking about Sarah's party? I completely forgot to even  think  about what I’m wearing. I was planning on that black jumpsuit, but I wore it to a work do last week. Need something new. Or, you know,  new to this crowd . Don't worry, we’ve got time. It’s just… everyone always looks so effortlessly chic at Sarah’s. She always sets the bar so high. Remember that time she rocked up in a vintage Dior dress? Aye, I remember! I nearly choked on my crisps. Honestly, she looked like she’d stepped straight out of a magazine. I was wearing a Primark cardi and jeans. Mortifying. That's why I stick to sensible flats now. No more trying to be fancy. See, that’s the difference between us. You’re comfortably you, which is amazing. I feel like I always have to  try  to be stylish. It’s exhausting. I was listening to a podcast the other day about ‘capsule wardrobes’ and minimalist fashion. Maybe I need to just drastically simplify everything. Capsule wardrobe? Sounds a bit…clinical, doesn’t it? I like having options. Though, my options usually involve different shades of beige and a lot of cardigans.

…and then Mr. Harrison actually  laughed . Like, a proper belly laugh. I thought for sure he’d give me detention for trying to photograph the school goldfish during maths! Oh, Leo Harrison. He’s got a soft spot for a bit of mischief, deep down. Good for you, though, for even trying. You’re getting bolder with your photography, aren’t you? Are you still experimenting with that black and white film? Yeah! It’s… frustrating, actually. Getting the exposure right is so hard. Everything comes out either washed out or completely dark. I took like, twenty photos of the pier yesterday, trying to get the right light on the waves, and only two are even remotely decent. That’s the beauty of it, though, isn’t it? The challenge. You learn so much from the mistakes. It’s not about getting it perfect instantly. Remember that photo I took of the beach huts in Rye? Took me ages to get the colour balance right. You’re always so patient. I just get… annoyed. It’s like, I have this picture in my head, and it never  quite  translates. It’s stupid, I know. It’s not stupid at all. It’s wanting to create something beautiful. And it's a good skill to learn – dealing with frustration. It’ll serve you well, especially when you get to college and… well, everything gets a bit more real. Don’t remind me about college. I still haven’t really decided what I want to do. Everyone else seems to have a plan. Chloe wants to be a vet, Ben’s doing engineering… I just like taking photos and reading. Is “professional daydreamer” a career option? Not yet, but you've got time to figure it out. You’re brilliant at art, you know that. Maybe something creative? Have you thought about media studies? You could combine your photography with film-making. I did browse the prospectus. It looked… okay. But a bit scary. All that group work. I'm not great with new people. I get really anxious. Oh, sweetheart. Everyone gets anxious. Even me. Do you remember when I started at the hospital as a receptionist? I was terrified I'd mess up patient records, or say the wrong thing to a doctor. It took me ages to feel comfortable. You seem so confident now. It’s an act, mostly. A very practised act.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the state of young Timmy’s application form. Absolutely riddled with mistakes! Spelling, grammar, the lot. I offered to help, naturally, being a bit of a wordsmith in my day – well, passable, anyhow – but he just waved me away, said his mum’d done ‘em all for him before. What’s he gonna do when his mum ain't around to fill it in for ‘im, eh? Oh, Timmy. Bless him. He’s a good lad, really, just… a bit slow on the uptake. Reminds me of little Darren I used to mind. Couldn’t tell his left from his right when he started school. Though Darren was a sweetie. Timmy… well, Timmy’s got a bit of a temper. You wouldn't think so, lookin' at 'im, but his mum says he can be a right handful. Handfuls are my speciality these days. Had a lad, Kevin, just this week decided to “redecorate” the art room with glitter.  Everywhere . It's still coming out of the carpet. You get used to it, though. Bit like dealing with a particularly stubborn… cockerel, actually. Speaking of which, did that noisy bird next door ever quieten down? Not a bit of it, Arthur! Cock-a-doodle-doo at five in the mornin’. Drives me spare. I’ve been proper restless, tossin’ and turnin’ all week. Used to be I could sleep through anything, but now… everything seems to amplify. It's probably the age, you know. Everything's creakin’, including me. Oh, I know that feeling, Bernard. Honestly, I’m up and down all night. Either too hot or too cold. And then I start worryin' about things. Mostly the house, though. I was lookin' at that new extension Mr. Henderson built for the Millers, and honestly, the workmanship! It’s appalling. Wonky windows, brickwork that looks like a toddler built it. You wouldn't catch me lettin' anyone touch my place. You're right to be wary. Builders… generally a law unto themselves. I was thinking of getting something 3D printed, actually. A little bracket for the bird feeder. There’s a robin building a lovely nest in the apple tree. Found three tiny blue eggs this morning. Blue eggs! Lovely! Now  that’s  something to cheer a fella up. Makes all the grumbling about noisy cockerels worthwhile. Though I wouldn’t mind a bit of peace and quiet, mind you.

…and honestly, the thought of her navigating the NHS on her own gives me palpitations. It's just  different  over there, you know? Everything is so…streamlined in France, efficient. Here, it’s a bit of a battle sometimes, even  with  someone to help. I can see that. It's not exactly known for being user-friendly, is it? But she’s a resourceful girl, Elsie. Always has been. Remember when she built that ridiculous treehouse in the garden, almost took the whole thing down? She figured it out. Oh, don’t remind me. Your brother nearly had a fit. But that’s different from settling into a new country, finding a flat, dealing with utilities… It’s overwhelming even for someone resourceful. And she's bringing little Leo with her, of course. A six-year-old to add to the mix! Leo’s a good lad. A bit quiet, from what I recall of the video calls, but bright. He’ll settle. Children are remarkably adaptable. And it'll be good for him to have his cousins around. Millie's already talking about teaching him to build Lego castles. That’s sweet. It’s just… it feels so final, doesn’t it? After all these years of her building a life over there, with Jean-Pierre… It's a big upheaval for everyone. I keep wondering if I’m doing the right thing, encouraging it so much. Elsie sounded pretty certain when I spoke to her last week. She said the distance was getting too much. Not just for her, but for Leo too. He misses his father, of course, but she said he was asking more and more about being here, about seeing you, about spending time with Millie and Thomas. Isn’t that what you want, though? To have them closer? Of course I do. It’s just… I've been so used to my quiet life. The routine. The library, my book club, pottering in the garden. Having a six-year-old bouncing off the walls is… a prospect. Although, I admit, a rather appealing one. It’s been awfully quiet since Thomas moved to London. You’ll manage. You were a teacher for goodness sake! You corralled thirty unruly children for years. Leo will be a breeze. And it’ll give you something to focus on. You’ve been a bit… lost, since retiring, haven't you?

…and honestly, the whole thing with the Scottish referendum has left me completely drained. Just the sheer  volume  of opinion, you know? Every pub conversation, every social media scroll - it’s just…Scotland, Scotland, Scotland. I mean, I understand the importance, genuinely, but it's relentless. Tell me about it. It's been dominating everything, hasn’t it? Even down here in Brighton, you can’t escape it. Old Mrs. Higgins next door cornered me for a good twenty minutes about it this morning, convinced I was secretly a Scottish nationalist. Me! Born and bred in Brighton, supporting Albion since I was a lad! That’s brilliant. People just latch onto things. Speaking of latching onto things… how did the interview go? For the Head of Department role? You seemed pretty apprehensive about it last week. Oh, the interview. Right. Well… it was…an experience. They really grilled me on my experience with the new curriculum changes. Apparently, young Tim, the current Deputy Head, has been whispering about my “traditional methods”. Honestly, traditional  works . Tim? That little whippersnapper? He’s barely been teaching five years! He probably thinks PowerPoint is a revolutionary teaching tool. Exactly! It’s all about bells and whistles with him, no real substance. They asked me three times about ‘digital integration’ and I just kept steering it back to effective classroom management. I think they wanted someone who’d enthusiastically embrace all the new fads. I doubt I’m getting it. Don't be so sure. You’ve got years of experience, a proven track record. They’d be foolish to dismiss that. Although, let’s be realistic, some institutions prioritize buzzwords over genuine expertise. How’s Sarah doing, by the way? Still at university? She’s thriving, actually. Second year now, studying history. She called me last night, absolutely buzzing about a lecture she’d had on the Jacobites. Said it was ‘totally radical’. Kids these days… Anyway, she's considering a year abroad. Rome, she’s thinking. Rome! That’s fantastic. A bit of sunshine and pasta could do her good. My own situation is…well, it's ongoing. Still trying to get tenure at the university. The paperwork is endless. It feels like I spend more time writing reports  about  teaching than actually  doing  it. Oh, I remember that fuss. It's the academic world for you, isn’t it? Always hoops to jump through.

…and then, honestly, the sheer  volume  of sugar in everything! It was like they were actively trying to give everyone diabetes. Even the bread tasted sweet! You’re exaggerating, darling. It wasn't  that  bad. Though I do remember being slightly horrified by the size of the portions. Everything was supersized. I’ve seen it in films, yeah. Massive burgers, huge drinks… it’s a bit of a stereotype, isn't it? Can we  get  back to the mousetrap game? I've got a brilliant idea for a chain reaction involving this teacup and a length of string. Patience, Leo, patience. Your Auntie Margaret is reminiscing. It  was  quite a culture shock, though. We spent a summer in Boston when I was researching for my thesis, and it was…different. Much louder, much brighter, much more…optimistic, almost. Optimistic to the point of delusion, sometimes. They just assumed everything was the best, even when it demonstrably wasn’t. Remember that diner, David? The coffee tasted like dishwater, but the waitress swore it was “the best in New England!” Oh, God, yes. And endlessly refilling it! You couldn't get a word in edgeways. They were so relentlessly cheerful. It's exhausting, frankly. Still, the kids there… they were something else. What do you mean? They just seemed… remarkably self-assured. Even the little ones. Little four-year-olds boldly stating their opinions, running around with a confidence you rarely see here. It was slightly unnerving. I think it’s their schooling, or perhaps the emphasis on extracurricular activities. Every child seems to be involved in everything – sports, drama, music… They're encouraged to develop their individuality very early on. That sounds lovely, actually. Though I always worried about pushing young Thomas  too  hard. He was perfectly happy pottering about with his trains. Trains are cool! I wanted to build a really complicated train set, but Mum said it would take over my bedroom. You should’ve gone for the mousetrap game instead! This is potentially epic. Imagine the domino effect. Speaking of epic, remember when we considered working in California, Margaret? Before you decided to go fully self-employed? That would have been quite a change. Don’t remind me. It sounded wonderful at the time – sunshine, beaches, a completely different lifestyle. But the thought of leaving family…and the NHS… It was madness, really. Plus, the cost of childcare over there was astronomical!

…and honestly, the silk market was  mad . Utterly mad. But I think I navigated it pretty well, all things considered. Navigated it? That sounds… diplomatic. Usually ‘mad’ means you came home empty-handed, or with something completely impractical. Let me guess, another scarf? You have a  collection , darling. Oh, don’t even. It’s not just  another  scarf. And it wasn't empty-handed! Though, truthfully, the sheer volume of options nearly overwhelmed me. It’s just… different here, isn't it? Back home, you go to John Lewis, you see a scarf, you maybe think about it for five minutes, you buy it. Here, it’s a negotiation, a cultural experience, a potential assault on the senses! Sounds about right. So, what treasures did you wrestle from the clutches of the silk merchants today? Let’s see the damage. Okay, okay. First… this. It’s silk, obviously. And look at the embroidery! I’ve been wanting something like this for ages. It’s… surprisingly wearable. Not one of those ‘occasion’ dresses that sits in the wardrobe. It  is  beautiful. The colour suits you perfectly. You’ll look amazing in this, especially with those sandals you bought last month. And… surprisingly wearable, you say? Considering your usual preference for tweeds and sensible shoes? Hey! I can appreciate comfort  and  style. Just because I’m a lecturer doesn't mean I have to dress like a headmistress. Anyway, this is different. It feels… light. And it’s actually really well-made. Not like some of the fast fashion stuff back home. I agree. The quality is evident. It doesn’t look flimsy at all. What else have you got in the bag of wonders? These! I found this little stall tucked away, run by this incredibly skilled woman. She does all her own dyeing and weaving. I couldn’t resist. Honestly, I have no idea what I'm going to  do  with all of this. Maybe cushion covers? Or I could try to get something made. Stunning. The patterns are incredible. You could definitely get something made. A jacket, perhaps? Or even a skirt. You always said you wanted to learn more about traditional Chinese crafts. This is a perfect excuse. You think so? I’m just worried about committing to something before I’ve really figured out what I want. It feels a bit… wasteful if it just ends up unused.

…and honestly, the ref was blind! Absolutely blind, I tell ya. That penalty in the 78th minute? A clear knock-on by the French winger, clear as day! Robbed us, absolutely robbed us. But Dad, France were playing really well. They deserved to win, weren't they? Deserved, maybe. But deserved  that  win? No. We were building momentum, Oisin. Building! And then…bam! Penalty, three points, and the whole thing just deflates. Now, now, Seamus. Don't get yourself all worked up over a rugby match. It's just a game. Besides, you were shouting at the television the whole second half, the poor child nearly jumped out of his skin. I know, I know. It's just… it’s a big match. And to lose like that…It's frustrating. Och, a good loss builds character, Seamus! Reminds ye ye can’t win ‘em all. I saw a wee lad in the village once, same age as your Oisin, absolutely heartbroken after his football team lost the final. Took him a week to cheer up! Actually, I was talking to Mr. Davies at school today about rugby. He said they’re trying to get more kids involved, but a lot of people prefer football. That’s a pity. Rugby teaches ye teamwork, respect…it's a good sport. Did you tell him you play, Oisin? Yeah, I mentioned I play for the school team. He said I’ve got potential, actually. He wants me to try out for the county under 14s next year. Oh, Oisin, that’s wonderful! That’s brilliant news, darling! We’ll have to get you some new kit then, won’t we? That  is  brilliant news, son. County level! That's a proper achievement. We'll need to celebrate that. Perhaps a proper meal out, when your mother has a bit of breathing space. Aye, a celebration’s in order. Though I’m more of a supporter from the sidelines these days, me knees aren’t what they used to be. Though I remember teaching a whole generation of wee scamps the rules of rugby! Honestly, you probably taught them more about getting muddy than the rules, Margaret. Speaking of which, Oisin, it's getting late. Nearly nine o’clock. Time to think about heading upstairs. Aw, Mum! Can I just finish my dessert? Just finish it quickly, love. And maybe a quick look at the stars before bed?

…and honestly, the estate agent was  so  pushy. Like, "Oh, but think of the potential!" Potential for what, exactly? More damp? More wonky floorboards? It’s just…a lot. Oh, no! Sounds stressful. Still looking around Aylesbury then? Or are you widening the net? You said something about wanting a garden, didn’t you? A real garden, not just a postage stamp of grass. Yeah, widening slightly. Bit of Buckingham, maybe even towards Milton Keynes. Anywhere with a garden big enough for, well… for potential little humans to run around in. Though, honestly, the thought of tiny humans is also terrifying. Tell me about it! My sister keeps sending me pictures of her little Leo, and he's adorable, obviously, but all I can think is  sleepless nights . She’s convinced I need one. Says it completes life. Oh, is Leo walking yet? Last I heard he was just mastering the commando crawl. He took his first steps last week! It's all she talks about. Apparently, he went straight for the dog's food bowl. Classic Leo. Seriously though, she keeps trying to set me up on dates with dads-to-be. Says it’s efficient. Efficient. Right. Sounds…strategic. Speaking of little humans, have you thought about the language thing? If you did…you know. Would you want to raise them bilingually? That's something I’ve actually been thinking about a lot, funnily enough, with you working in language research and all. It feels almost…negligent not to. I mean, I did French GCSE, but I couldn’t hold a conversation to save my life now. It’s all ‘Je m'appelle…uh…Sarah?’ We’ve all been there. And GCSE French is a  long  way from fluency, definitely. It's interesting though, isn’t it? The cognitive benefits, the cultural understanding… I'm running a small project at the moment looking at early language exposure, actually. It's fascinating stuff. We're seeing a clear correlation between early exposure and later linguistic aptitude. See, you’ve planted the seed! I feel slightly guilty now. Maybe I should dust off my French textbooks. Though honestly, between work and house-hunting, I barely have time to eat, let alone relearn a language. Don't feel guilty! It’s a massive undertaking. And you’ve got that brilliant organisational skill - you’re the one who kept my dissertation on track, remember?

…and honestly, the bloke at the market tried to charge me twenty quid for a bag of runner beans! Twenty quid! Said it was ‘local, organic’. Looked exactly the same as the ones next door for two-fifty. Proper taking the mickey, innit? Twenty quid! Good grief, Liam. Bedford market’s gone mental. You gotta haggle, mate, you  gotta . My nan would have had him down to a fiver in seconds. She’s a master negotiator. It's a skill, honestly. Like linguistics - understanding  how  people try to persuade you. Nan’s got game, then. My yiayia, she just yelled at people until they gave her what she wanted. Worked a treat. She’d’ve told him the beans looked half-dead anyway. I should've done that! I just sort of…froze. I was thinking about that guitar I’m trying to sell online, actually. This bloke keeps messaging, offering fifty, but it's a beautiful Yamaha, worth at least a hundred and fifty. Fifty?! Seriously? You're being lowballed. Put it on eBay, Liam. Wider audience. Describe it perfectly, good photos. And don’t accept anything less than you’re happy with. I’ve sold loads of textbooks that way when I was skint at uni. Sometimes you get bidding wars, it’s amazing. I tried selling some tools online once. Nightmare. Someone tried to claim they never received it, then emailed me pictures of  my  tools in their garage! I nearly went down there. Seriously considered it. Oi, don’t go getting all Rambo on people, Danny! That’s why I’ve been taking those MMA classes. Not to go around assaulting folk, but to know how to look after yourself. You never know, do ya? See, that’s interesting, Liam. From a linguistic perspective, the way people talk about self-defence often frames it as proactive aggression, even though the intent is defensive. It highlights how language shapes perception. I was reading about it for a paper… Speakin’ of lookin’ after yourself, seen old man Hemmings’ dog again? The staffy. Keeps runnin’ into the road. Nearly got flattened by a van yesterday. He just lets it wander. It’s cruel, that is. Disgraceful. Should be reported, that should. They treat ‘em like toys, some people. No responsibility. Did you catch that documentary on animal testing last night? Gutting. I did, actually. Awful. My mum’s been trying to get me to go vegan.

…and honestly, the traffic on the A1 was  insane  today. It took me nearly an hour just to get from Stamford to here. An hour, Leo! For twenty miles! Ugh, don’t even. I was thinking of offering to pick up the spinach from Sainsbury’s, but knowing that… I’m glad I didn’t. How was work otherwise? Still drowning in spreadsheets? Pretty much. Old Mr. Henderson decided  today  was the day to ask for a full report on Q3 expenses, despite the deadline being next week. It’s just…managing everyone else’s projects is fine, but when I’m falling behind on my own tasks because of this…it’s frustrating. Sounds about right. Bureaucracy at its finest. Speaking of falling behind, have you given any more thought to the car situation? We really need to figure something out before winter properly hits. I have, actually. I was browsing Auto Trader on my lunch break. Everything is just so…expensive. Even something half-decent is pushing five grand, and then there’s insurance, tax, MOT…it all adds up. Tell me about it. Remember my old Fiesta? Bless its little cotton socks, that car saw me through Sixth Form and my first proper job. It was only worth about a grand, but it got me from A to B. Exactly! But even a grand is a stretch right now, isn't it? Especially with that kitchen re-do still looming. We agreed we’d start saving properly after Christmas, but… But the car feels more urgent. I agree. Commuting on the bus is killing you, and honestly, it’s not exactly ideal for me either, especially with all the kit I need to carry for the site visits. It’s not just about convenience, it’s about time too. Think of all the hours we're losing each week just  waiting  for transport. You’re right. I hadn't fully quantified the time loss. It’s…significant. Okay. So, car. What's our budget realistically? And are we looking used, or… even considering anything newer? I think used is the only sensible option. I’ve been looking at a few things, mostly smaller engines – good for fuel economy, right? A reliable little hatchback. I saw a couple of Vauxhall Corsas going for around £3500 - £4000 with relatively low mileage. Corsas are…functional. Not exciting, but functional. And probably surprisingly reliable.

…and honestly, lad, I don’t know  why  you left all your washing on the bedroom floor. It’s not a laundry hamper, is it? It’s a tripping hazard! Honestly, you’d think after eighteen years… But Mum, I was going to get it! I just… forgot. Big history test today, brain was a bit fried. Eighteen years, eh? Feels like yesterday he was a little nipper, running around with jam all over his face. Remember that, Arthur? Do I ever! Covered head to toe in strawberry jam. Your mother nearly had a fit. Said he looked like a victim of a particularly gruesome crime. Grandad! Don’t remind me. That was mortifying. It was! You refused to wear anything but that jam-smeared jumper for the rest of the day. Right, enough reminiscing, we’ve got a roast to get on. Grandma, are you comfy? Can I get you another cuppa? Oh, I’m grand, love. Lovely and warm in here. And yes, a little top-up wouldn’t go amiss. Earl Grey, if you please. You make a proper brew, you do. Not like some folk who just dunk a bag and hope for the best. I try my best. It’s a skill, you know. A Yorkshire skill at that. Now, about that shopping list… I need to get more potatoes. And a new tin opener, this one’s packed in. Tin opener, eh? I used to be able to open a tin with me pocketknife, back in the day. Show off. Just stating facts, lad! Times were different. We didn’t  need  fancy gadgets. More resilience back then, I tell ya. Resilience and probably tetanus. Right, whilst I’m making tea, can one of you carve the roast? I’m slightly distracted thinking about these exam papers I need to mark tonight. Absolute state of some of these answers…they think Pythagoras was a type of cheese! Pythagoras a cheese? Seriously? That’s…amazing. I’ll carve. I’m quite good, actually. Practice makes perfect, you know. All those roast dinners. He is, Arthur. A dab hand with a knife. Though he did once try to carve the turkey with a plastic spoon. A plastic spoon! Oh, that boy… always getting into mischief. I was six! And it looked a bit like a knife! More like a vaguely spoon-shaped object. Anyway, don’t go hacking at the roast like a lumberjack, alright?

…and honestly, the amount of glitter that ended up  everywhere  after the pirate hat making was unbelievable. I’m still finding it! Honestly, it’s like a glitter bomb went off. Did you two enjoy making them though? Mine’s the best! It’s got a  really  sparkly skull and crossbones! And a feather! Mine too! But…it’s a bit wobbly. It keeps falling off my head. That’s alright, Captain Wobbly-Hat. We can reinforce it later. We're having a pirate themed tea party later, right? We need to plan our ‘buried treasure’ - I was thinking chocolate coins. Ooooh! Chocolate! Can we hide them  really  well? Like, under the sofa cushions? No! That's too easy! We need a  map ! A proper pirate map with an 'X' marks the spot! Excellent idea! We can definitely make a map. Right, speaking of creative projects… Shakespeare week starts on Monday. I'm a bit nervous about introducing it to you two. Shake…spear? Is he a pirate? Does he have a sparkly hat? No, darling, he wasn't a pirate, although his plays did sometimes  feature  pirates. He was a writer, a very famous writer, a long, long time ago. He wrote stories, like… well, you haven’t seen  A Midsummer Night’s Dream  have you? No. Is it about dragons? Sometimes there are fantastical creatures! It's about fairies and magic and… well, lots of things happening in a forest. Actually, we’re thinking of going to Stratford-upon-Avon - that's where Shakespeare was born – during half term. Would you like that? Stratford-upon-Avon? Is there a castle? There are historical buildings, and we could visit Shakespeare’s birthplace. It’ll be good to see where he lived and learned. It's a little bit of history coming to life. Can we wear our pirate hats? You can wear whatever you want! Now, guess what else I booked? A circus workshop! A CIRCUS?! Really?! Really! And it's not just  any  circus workshop. It's at a real circus, with professional circus performers. You’ll learn some basic circus skills – juggling, maybe a little bit of acrobatics. Acrobatics?! Like, flipping? Can I be a flying trapeze artist? We'll see if you can fly! Maybe not  right  away, but you’ll learn some balance and coordination. It’s next Saturday. We’ve also been looking at the Easter pictures you made at school, they were  lovely .

…and honestly, the look on the harbourmaster’s face! Utter disbelief. He kept repeating, “But…Cyprus? From  Jeddah ?” As if it were the most ludicrous idea he’d ever encountered. Jeddah to Cyprus… good lord, Margaret, you always did have a flair for the dramatic, didn't you? That's… ambitious, to say the least. What possessed you? Oh, it seemed perfectly sensible at the time! It was the early eighties, I was teaching English in Jeddah, and desperately needed a holiday. Flights were…well, complicated and expensive. This chap, a slightly dodgy American, offered me a ride on his sailboat. Said he was heading that way. Ignored to mention  how  he was heading that way – directly across the Red Sea and the Eastern Mediterranean! Dodgy American, you say? I can see where this is going. Though, I confess, the sheer audacity of the attempt is rather impressive. Did you have any nautical experience at all? Precious little. I’d done a bit of dinghy sailing as a girl, but nothing like that. He assured me he was a seasoned sailor. Turns out he was more of a “seasoned drinker” who  thought  he was a sailor. We got about fifty miles out and were heading into a rather nasty swell when the Saudi coastguard intercepted us. Coastguard, eh? I imagine they weren’t thrilled with an American and a British woman attempting an unsanctioned trans-Mediterranean voyage from a major Islamic port. I bet they weren’t. So, arrested then? What were the charges? ‘Attempted madness’? Something along those lines! Illegal navigation, I think. And probably a hefty dose of ‘behaviour unbecoming’. They were considerably less impressed with the whole thing than I initially thought they’d be. We spent two days in a rather…basic holding cell. It wasn’t a pleasant experience, particularly considering the lack of, well, anything resembling comfort. And the complete absence of alcohol! That  is  a hardship. Reminds me of my time lecturing in Kuwait. Dry as a bone. You develop a profound appreciation for a decent glass of wine. Although, even in Saudi, you could  find  it, if you knew the right people and had enough money. Very discreetly, of course. Oh, absolutely. During my volunteer work with a dental charity in Bahrain, we had… reliable sources. A chap who imported ‘medical spirits’ - ostensibly for sterilisation, but conveniently available for after-hours relaxation. The things one does to maintain sanity… Medical spirits!

… honestly, I just don’t  get  it. He’s leaving wet towels on the bathroom floor  again . Honestly, it's like living with a teenager is a full-time job just policing basic hygiene. Oh, tell me about it. Liam was the same. Remember the great sock mountain of ‘08? It practically had its own ecosystem. You’d think they were actively  trying  to wind us up. It’s not that bad. Oh, it's not, is it, Ethan? You contribute to the chaos, young man. And don’t ‘it’s not that bad’ me when I’m the one finding a half-eaten biscuit  in  the bath. It probably fell off the side. Oh, he's got a way with words, doesn't he? You've raised him well, Sarah. Deflecting like a pro. Deflecting and leaving biscuit debris. It's a skill. Anyway, it got me thinking… we haven’t had a proper family holiday in ages. Just the two of us, and him. Somewhere… different. Not just Blackpool. Blackpool’s good fun! Though, yes, a bit different wouldn’t hurt. What did you have in mind? I was reading about those adventure holidays – kayaking, climbing… maybe a bit too much for Ethan? I wouldn't mind climbing. We do it at school. See? Opportunities are out there! I was thinking maybe something… historical? Like, visiting Hadrian's Wall. You’re from up North, aren’t you, Ethan? Doesn’t that appeal? All those Roman forts and stories of brave explorers... Oh, Hadrian’s Wall is lovely. Bitterly cold, mind, even in summer. Still, it’d be a good change. Better than another wet weekend in Skegness. Though, speaking of opportunities, I was talking to Mrs. Henderson at school today. Apparently, they’re looking for someone to help out with the after-school club, just a couple of evenings a week. Good experience for you, Ethan. Babysitting? No way. It's not just babysitting, darling. It’s responsible work. You could put it on your CV. Think about it. Building character. And it pays! Enough to maybe buy those trainers you've been eyeing up. Okay, maybe. What age kids? Mostly primary school. But the thing is, I don’t want you getting swamped. Your GCSEs are coming up. We need to focus on those. Then there’s the work experience. Have you thought any further about that? I was talking to Josh, and he's thinking of applying to that engineering firm in Burton.

…and honestly, the  burek  we had this morning was unreal. Like, genuinely the best pastry I’ve ever tasted. Better than anything back ‘ome, even Mrs. Higgins’ legendary Eccles cakes. Now that's saying something, love. Mrs. Higgins  does  make a good Eccles cake. Though, Croatian pastries are a different league, aren’t they? It’s all that flaky filo pastry, and the filling… divine. Can we talk about truffles again? I saw a guy shaving them over pasta at that restaurant last night. It smelled amazing. Like…earthy poshness. Earthy poshness. That’s a good description, actually. They’re a fascinating fungus, truffles. Ridiculously expensive, of course. The whole truffle oil industry is mostly a scam, did you know? Most of it is synthetic. Typical. Everything good has a catch. Right, so Dad, you were telling us about that chef you met, the one who used to work at The Fat Duck? Oh, yes! David, lovely bloke. He left Heston Blumenthal’s place to open a tiny restaurant over in Slovenia. Absolutely groundbreaking stuff. Molecular gastronomy, but with a real heart to it. He’s obsessed with local ingredients, just like these Croatians. It’s funny, isn't it? How everyone's always chasing the next big thing in food. But the best meals are often the simplest ones, made with good quality, fresh produce. Remember when we went to Italy with Sarah and Mark? Sarah nearly had a meltdown when the pasta wasn’t  al dente  enough. Oh god,  that  trip. Mark just kept stuffing his face and ignoring her. They are a pair. Have you spoken to them recently? Not for ages. Mark’s been on about moving to America again. Something about opportunities. He always says that. Never happens though, does it? America? Why would you want to live in America? It just looks…loud. And everything’s huge. Portion sizes, cars, flags… It’s a different culture, that's all. Overhyped, in my opinion. Though, their advancements in medical research are quite something. Especially stem cell technology. I was reading an article about… Dad, please, not the stem cell lecture on holiday. I’m still recovering from your explanation of the NHS funding model last week. Just saying, it’s incredible what they’re doing. Potential to cure everything from Parkinson’s to spinal injuries… We  know , dear. You’ve told us. Have you had a cigarette yet today?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is just  wild . We’re talking about tracking regional pronoun usage across five counties – not just ‘they/them’ but all the variations, the shifts in ‘me and him’ versus ‘him and me’… it's a rabbit hole, I tell you. A linguistic rabbit hole. Five counties? Right, the East Anglian Dialect Project, isn’t it? You’re the one leading that? I vaguely remember seeing something about it on the Press’ intranet. Sounds… intense. Intense is one word for it. Rewarding, definitely. But mostly intense. I’m Rosie, by the way. Rosie Bell. Language Research Co-ordinator. And you are…? Ben. Ben Carter. Digital Marketing, mostly for academic titles. Trying to make Heidegger accessible to TikTok, basically. It’s… a challenge. Sounds a lot more fun than my job, to be honest. I’m Liam. Projects Assistant. Mostly just chasing people for permissions and making sure everything is filed correctly. The glamour of academic publishing. Oh, we all have our roles to play, Liam! Don’t underestimate the importance of correct filing. My research would collapse into chaos without meticulously organised questionnaires. Though Heidegger on TikTok… that  is  ambitious, Ben. Tell me about it. We tried a short explainer on Being and Time with a trending sound and… let’s just say it didn’t exactly go viral. The comments section was… philosophical, in the worst possible way. Mostly people asking why anyone would bother. Fair enough. I think most students just skim the required reading and hope for the best. What kind of things are you actually  finding  with the dialect research, Rosie? Anything surprising? Loads. Actually, it’s confirming some suspicions, but with a lot more nuance. We knew there was a gradient between the more rural dialects and the Cambridge ‘standard’ English, but the speed with which certain features are being adopted – or rejected – is fascinating. For instance, the use of ‘were’ instead of ‘was’ with singular subjects… it's clinging on in the Fens but disappearing rapidly closer to the city. Really? That’s… specific. I thought a lot of that was dying out anyway. My nan used to say ‘were’ all the time, but she’s from Norfolk. Exactly! And Norfolk is a stronghold. But even within Norfolk, we're seeing generational shifts. Younger speakers are much more likely to self-correct, consciously aligning with the ‘correct’ grammar. It’s about social identity, really.

… honestly, I still can’t believe we made it across Germany without incident. That autobahn was  terrifying . All those cars just… flying past. You say that like you weren’t gripping the dashboard the entire time! It was fine, honestly. People generally know what they’re doing. And you were navigating, which is stressful enough, isn’t it? All those little Polish village names… they just roll off the tongue, don’t they? Roll off the tongue and look identical to twenty other villages! Seriously, I think I aged about ten years deciphering those road signs. And are you absolutely sure Kasia’s directions were right? We seem to have been driving  around  Tarnow for the last half hour. Pretty sure. Kasia’s lived there for nearly five years now, she knows the area. It's just… Tarnow isn’t laid out on a neat grid like Bury, is it? It's all winding roads and little lanes. Plus, this campervan isn’t exactly built for navigating tight corners. Tight corners is an understatement! I think I scraped against something back there, didn’t I? I heard a noise. Probably just a branch. Don’t worry about it. We’re almost there. She said to look for a church with a green dome, remember? Have you spotted anything remotely resembling a green dome? No. Just… trees. And more trees. And what I suspect is a very judgmental goat. Honestly, Poland is beautiful, but slightly bewildering. It’s a far cry from Cambridge, that’s for sure. Everything's so… expansive. It is different. But in a good way, I think. It’s nice to get away from the predictable, isn’t it? You need a bit of adventure. And Kasia’s promised proper Polish pierogi, so that’s motivation enough for me. Pierogi are good. Very good. Though I'm slightly concerned about the language barrier with her neighbours. My Polish is… non-existent. You'll be doing all the talking, I suspect. That's fine. My year abroad helped. Although, honestly, I’m a little rusty. Mostly I can order food and ask where the toilet is. Essential skills, really. Have you thought about how we're getting back? Are you happy to drive again, or shall we look at trains? Oh, God, no. Absolutely not. Trains sound  heavenly . Anything to avoid another six hours on the autobahn. Or, you know, getting lost in a labyrinth of Polish villages.

… honestly, that was a shocking tackle. Even with the sound off, you can  see  it was dodgy. Did VAR even look at that? Probably not, love. They’re notoriously inconsistent. Honestly, I’m getting so fed up with the Premier League. It’s less about football and more about… well, everything  around  football. The money, the sponsorships… it’s ridiculous. Tell me about it. Did you see Man U’s new strip? It’s… geometric nightmares. Honestly. Looks like someone’s had a bad trip and tried to design a football kit. All red and black triangles. It’s dreadful. You’ve seen it then! Yeah, it's a bit… much. It's like they're actively trying to alienate their fanbase. You know, remember when kits were just… kits? Now they’re designed to maximize exposure for whatever sponsor they’ve got plastered all over them. Exactly! And it's always the worst designs that get the biggest deals. It’s greed, pure and simple. I saw one article saying the design was 'inspired by the industrial heartland of Manchester'. Inspired by what part of the industrial heartland? The bit that looks like a glitch in the Matrix? Ha! That’s brilliant. It’s almost… ironic, isn’t it? They’re trying to be ‘authentic’ with a design that’s completely manufactured and over-the-top. And speaking of sponsors…have you noticed how many fast food brands are sponsoring football now? Oh, don't even get me started. McDonalds are  everywhere . Sponsoring kids’ football teams, having their logos all over the stadiums... It’s just… awful, really. Promoting unhealthy eating to young children. It’s vile. It’s the reach, isn’t it? Football is huge, especially with kids. They can get their brand in front of a massive audience. It’s cynical, but effective. I remember being a kid and wanting a Happy Meal just because of the football cards they used to give away. See! Brainwashing from a young age! It’s the same with sponsorship on the shirts. I mean, I love football, but I don’t need to be constantly reminded that a betting company or a fast-food chain is paying to have their logo on my team’s jersey. Honestly, I'd prefer a plain kit. Or maybe a sponsor that… I don't know… sells books? Or supports a local charity? Something that isn’t actively bad for people.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit weird, didn’t it? Like, he was  really  fixated on getting me to record a little ‘soundbite’ for his mate, about how lovely Mum and Dad are. Sounded like some kind of…proof of concept for a YouTube channel or something. Right. ‘Proof of concept.’ That sounds about right for Darren. Always needs something to…validate him, doesn’t he? Remember when he tried to build that ‘self-sustaining ecosystem’ in the shed? Ended up smelling like old socks and despair. Oh god, don’t remind me! The stink was unbelievable. No, this was different. He kept going on about ‘content’ and ‘engagement’. It’s just…intrusive. Anyway, what about you? How was the job centre? Did they at least pretend to care today? Pretend is the operative word. Another form. Another interview scheduled for next Tuesday. Another lecture about applying for everything, even if it’s stacking shelves. Honestly, Sarah, stacking shelves at my age…it’s humiliating. And the advisor actually said, and I quote, “Have you considered delivery driving?” Like I haven't thought of that! Well, you’ve got a valid point. Delivery driving is… demanding. And the petrol costs these days? It's insane. Speaking of costs, Mum was moaning about the gas and electricity bill again. Said it’s gone up another hundred quid. A hundred?! Seriously? How are people supposed to cope? It’s like they  want  us to be cold and hungry. And don't even get me started on the Job Seekers Allowance. They keep finding reasons to delay it, claiming I missed a phone call or didn't update something online. It’s a full-time job just proving I’m unemployed! It's a nightmare, isn’t it? I’m just grateful I’ve finished my degree and can focus on finding something  relevant  and hopefully, well-paid. Though even that's looking daunting. Did you see that dress I ordered on eBay finally arrived? Good for you. What colour is it? Teal! It's perfect for Lily’s school play. She's playing a mermaid, can you believe it? Growing up so fast, that one. Keeps asking when she can have a phone. Tell me about it. Leo’s already obsessed with Fortnite. And he's only eight. It’s a constant battle to get him to do anything other than stare at a screen.

…and honestly, the sat nav just decided it preferred the scenic route through three tiny villages. Added a good forty minutes to the journey! I was already late for the client meeting, you can imagine. They weren't thrilled. Forty minutes? Blimey, that’s a proper nightmare, that is. Sat navs, eh? More trouble than they're worth sometimes. I stick to knowing the roads myself, mostly. Less stressful. Stressful! You think  that’s  stressful, love? Try driving in London in the sixties. Now  that  was stressful. No sat navs then, mind you. Just a map and a prayer. And hoping you didn’t get stuck behind a lorry full of…well, never you mind what. I can only imagine, Mum. It sounds terrifying. Though, a map and a prayer sounds rather appealing right now, actually. Less arguing with a robotic voice. Speaking of stressful, I was reading about that plane crash yesterday. Awful, wasn’t it? Makes you think, doesn't it? All that way up in the air… So tragic. Poor people. It does make you appreciate just being here, having a cup of coffee. Though, this coffee  is  a bit weak, isn’t it? I made it myself, dear. It’s perfectly good coffee. Maybe you’re just used to that fancy stuff you get at those coffee shops. All froth and no substance, if you ask me. No, no, it’s lovely, Mum, honestly. Just…could do with a bit more kick. How are you feeling, by the way? Did you manage to get to the doctor’s about that wart? Oh, that darn wart. It’s still there, stubbornly clinging on. The doctor said it’s harmless, just an age thing. But it’s irritating, that’s what it is. Right on my thumb, where I used to do all my gardening. I’ve got a cousin who swears by apple cider vinegar for warts. Says you dab it on every night. Sounds a bit…old wives’ tale-ish, but apparently it works. Cider vinegar? Really? That’s a new one. You’ll be recommending leeches next! Don’t be daft, dear! But honestly, anything's worth a try at this point. I don't want it spreading. It's a right nuisance when I'm trying to knit. What are you knitting at the moment? Another one of those beautiful scarves? A jumper for young Thomas.

…and honestly, Miss Davies just  stares . Like, she expects us to magically  know  what a dangling participle is! It’s ridiculous. Honestly, it feels like she's actively trying to make English less enjoyable. Oh,  don’t  even get me started on English. Mr. Harrison’s alright, but he's so… distracted. You can tell he’s still figuring things out. He’s a trainee, isn’t he? Yeah, fresh out of uni. He keeps saying things like “right, so, the subtext…” and then trails off. It’s endearing, but also… frustrating when you've got a mock exam next week. I swear he spends half the lesson googling Shakespearean insults. No way! Seriously? Oh, that's amazing! Though, yeah, not ideal exam prep. At least Science is consistent. Mrs. Patel is a machine. A wonderfully terrifying machine. But at least you know where you stand with her. Did you finish that practical report on osmosis? I’m still battling with the data analysis. It just… doesn’t  make  sense. Nearly. Liam helped me with the calculations this morning. He’s a lifesaver. Honestly, he understands Science so effortlessly. I’m convinced he's part robot. Liam’s brilliant. He's also the only person who can explain why Mr. Finch keeps talking about the mitochondria being the powerhouse of the cell  every single lesson . It’s becoming a running joke. It is! I heard Chloe trying to mimic him last week, doing the little ‘powerhouse!’ hand gesture. It was brilliant. Speaking of Chloe, did you see her art project? The one she’s doing for the sculpture competition? No! Is it the one with the recycled materials? She mentioned something about that. It’s incredible! It’s this huge phoenix, made entirely out of plastic bottles and bits of wire. It’s seriously impressive. She's spent weeks on it. She says she's really nervous about the judging. She should be proud. It sounds amazing. Art’s the one subject I truly can't grasp. I tried pottery last term and… let’s just say it looked less like a vase and more like a collapsed mud pie. Oh, no! Honestly, I'm terrible at anything requiring actual skill. Give me an essay any day. Although, those English essays are currently the bane of my existence thanks to Miss Davies. Tell me about it. So, about that History test… are you revising with Ben tonight?

…and then Mr. Davies just  launched  into this thing about how Scientology is the only true path. Honestly, it was mental. Like, spaceships and auditing and all that. It’s just… weird, innit? Oh, Mr. Davies. Bless him, he's a bit lost, isn't he? Always chasing something. It’s just… desperate, really. Trying to find meaning where there probably isn’t a neat little package to be found. Ba-ba! Ship! He reckons it's got all the answers, though. Like, life, the universe, everything. He said it's like… like The Matrix, but real. You gotta ‘clear’ your thetan or something. The Matrix? Oh, don’t even get me started. That film got everyone thinking they were living in a simulation. It’s a bit much, isn’t it? Though, sometimes, with everything going on… you  do  wonder. Still, definitely better to focus on the real world, like getting young Finn here to eat his peas. He's right about the questioning thing, though. It made me think about… well, everything. Remember Mrs. O’Malley, from primary school? The really strict nun? Oh,  Mrs. O’Malley . God love us all. She ruled that classroom with an iron fist and a rosary. I’m pretty sure she believed having fun was a sin. Exactly! She'd tell us stories about… well, about heaven and hell, and how to be ‘good’ to avoid the bad place. It always felt a bit… scary. And, like, unquestionable. You just  had  to believe. That’s the thing with a lot of religion, isn’t it? That absolute certainty. It's comforting for some, I suppose. But I always needed a bit more wiggle room. My Nan was the same. Proper Catholic, she was. Always worried I wasn’t praying enough. Nana! Yes, darling, Nana. She'd want you to eat your vegetables, too. Now, where were we? Oh yes, religion. I never really felt a strong pull to anything in particular. I mean, I went to church with Nan, and it was… nice. The hymns were pretty. But it didn’t  feel  true for me. It’s just… how can anyone be  sure ? Like, Scientology, Catholicism, even just believing in… nothing. It’s a massive leap of faith, whatever you choose. Precisely. And the thing is, people use religion for good, and for bad. It can bring communities together, but it can also be used to justify terrible things.

…and honestly, the cha-cha is  way  harder than it looks. I thought I was coordinated, but apparently not. Mr. Henderson keeps saying my frame is all wrong. “Shoulders down, lass, shoulders down!” Like I haven't heard that a million times. Sounds…intensive. You’re sticking with it though, right? You were so excited about it. Though, thinking about it, competitive dancing feels a bit…intense for a Tuesday night. Aye, I am. It's good to learn something new. Keeps the brain ticking over. And it’s a laugh, mostly. Though, I’m starting to think a week in Spain instead of waltzing would have been a better use of my money, mind. Should we actually finalise those dates for that, by the way? October still good? October’s perfect. I’ve already started looking at potential hikes. There’s a really good one near Ronda, apparently. Spectacular views. You’d love it, even if it's not ballroom-dancing spectacular. Ooh, Ronda sounds brilliant. Better than getting yelled at about my posture. Reminds me though, Gran used to talk about the area. She was fascinated by Old English, did ye know? Said Ronda came from a very ancient word meaning 'round’ - simple as that, but linked to all sorts of older settlements. She was proper clever, our Gran. Seriously? That’s amazing. I always thought she just liked a good cup of tea and complaining about the telly. Though, she did have that encyclopedic knowledge of celebrity gossip, to be fair. Remember when she insisted David Beckham secretly trained as a surgeon? Oh God, yes! “He’s got the hands for it!” she said. She was convinced. Speaking of the telly, are you still hooked on that medical drama? The one with the ridiculously good-looking doctors?  Grey’s Anatomy ? Guilty pleasure, definitely. It's utterly ridiculous, but…compelling. And actually, some of the medical stuff is surprisingly accurate, or so my mate Liam, the actual surgeon, tells me. He says it's the dramatic license that gets him. Predictable. Speaking of Liam, how’s work going for him? Still complaining about hospital bureaucracy? Oh, constantly. He’s arguing with management about funding for new equipment, apparently. Honestly, it's infuriating. They always prioritise profit over patient care. Actually, it's why he volunteers with that medical charity in Sierra Leone, I think. Something to balance it all out.

…and honestly, the truffle pasta at that little place in Rovinj was  divine . Absolutely divine. Way better than anything you get back home, Mum. I'll believe it when I taste it, love. Bolton's got some decent Italians, you know. Though I doubt they’re using proper Istrian truffles. Right, nearly there, lads. Just past this olive grove. Smell that? That’s proper Croatian sunshine bottled up in those trees. Smells…green. Like Gran’s garden, but hotter. Are we nearly at the Roman ruins, then? Dad said they were proper massive. We are, Finn. Another fifteen minutes or so. Pula has some incredible Roman architecture. Reminds me a bit of the Forum in Rome, actually, though admittedly on a smaller scale. It'll be good to get out of the car for a bit, though. This drive is… scenic, let's say, but a bit winding. Winding is an understatement, Dad! You're gripping the steering wheel like you’re auditioning for  Sons of Anarchy ! Honestly, you’d think you were escaping a rival motorcycle gang, not looking at an olive grove. Very funny. Just being careful. These roads weren’t built for modern cars, you know. And besides, I booked that lovely agriturismo just outside Pula. Apparently, they make their own olive oil and wine. Ooh, now  that  sounds good. Proper homemade olive oil. Not that watery stuff in supermarkets. I’ll have to get a couple of bottles to bring back. It’s just so much nicer, that flavour. I’ll try and find some fig jam at one of the markets, too. Markets? Are there any with PlayStation games? Seriously, Finn? We're in Croatia, not GameStop. They’ll have local crafts, fresh produce, maybe some leather goods… definitely not PlayStations. There's a big one in Porec, apparently. Very touristy, but good for souvenirs. Although, I'm more interested in the wine tasting. I read a review of a place that does a Malvazija tasting menu. Malvazija? Sounds fancy. Can we maybe go to a beach after the ruins? I saw pictures of these little hidden coves, with crystal clear water. Perfect Instagram material. We can certainly look. Though honestly, after all this driving, I'd be happy with a sit down and a glass of something cool. I packed some elderflower cordial, if we can't find anything immediately. Ooh, yeah, the elderflower! That's good.

…and honestly, I still don’t get why you’re all so obsessed with that new game. It just looks…pointless. All that building and resource gathering? Give me a good RPG any day. Pointless? It's  strategic , Elara! You’re thinking of Minecraft, maybe. This is, like, a whole economy simulator, and the social aspect is brilliant. We could all play together! You’d love it. Aye, she’s right, Elara. It's properly addictive. I’ve lost a week already, probably. Nearly failed me driving test 'cos I was thinkin’ about optimising me wheat farm. A week? Ruby, you didn’t even  have  a driving test this week! You changed it! And honestly, wheat farms? Seriously? It's not just wheat farms, it's about the networks you build, the trades you make… it's fascinating. Although, I did spend three hours yesterday trying to get a rare mineral. My lecturer thought I was taking notes! See! It's madness! You're all turning into digital hoarders. Speaking of digital… did anyone see that video Liam sent round? The one he said was ‘hilarious’? Oh god,  that  one. I barely watched it. It was…intense. Why is he always doing stuff like that? Recording himself doing…that? He’s just a lad bein’ a lad. Gets a bit much sometimes, mind. Proper attention seeker. I quickly skipped through it, to be honest. Didn't fancy seein'… well, you know. It was incredibly awkward. He needs to understand boundaries, especially when sharing things with a group chat. It’s one thing to do whatever you want in private, but to  broadcast  it? Exactly! And then he put a little caption like ‘For the lads!’ as if that makes it okay. It's… well, it involved…  that  and I'm still slightly mortified. I blocked him on Snapchat for a bit. I think he's just trying to appear… cool? Like, pushing boundaries. It’s a really immature way to do it, though. I mean, honestly, the whole thing felt… exploitative, even. Aye. A bit much, even for Liam. Makes you wonder what other stuff he’s got hidden away on his phone. Remember that time he tried to convince us he’d wrestled a badger? Oh, don't remind me! That was a disaster. He had scratches all over his arms and tried to blame it on a rogue bramble bush.

… honestly, I’m still regretting that pasty. It looked lovely, all golden and whatnot, but the filling was just… sad. Like someone’d forgotten the seasoning entirely. Oh, aye? Where’d you get it from? The uni cafe? They're usually alright, a bit bland, but alright. No, no, not there. I tried that little place on the way in, ‘Pasties & Perks’. Should’ve stuck with a Greggs, to be honest. You can’t go wrong with a well-made sausage roll from Greggs. It’s a scientific fact. Scientific fact, is it, Alan? You and your Greggs. You're a creature of habit, aren’t you? I appreciate consistency, Mark. Keeps a man grounded. Unlike some people who are always chasing the latest avocado and quinoa thing. Hey! I just like trying new things. I had a really good Korean fried chicken wrap the other day. From that street food van near the MediaCity tram stop. It was  amazing . Korean fried chicken? Sounds… complicated. I'm a simple man, Sarah. Give me a bit of beef and onion, maybe a bit of pickle, and I’m sorted. You’re a dinosaur, Alan, a delightful dinosaur. Though I will admit, finding decent food around here can be a struggle. I was craving a proper chippy tea last week – you know, with mushy peas and gravy – and everything was just… underwhelmed. I know what you mean! I tried that new ‘gastro-pub’ that opened up, The Alchemist’s Elbow or something. They served chips with rosemary salt and aioli.  Aioli  with chips. It’s just wrong. Rosemary salt?! What’s wrong with a good dollop of vinegar? It’s a travesty, I tell you. A culinary travesty. My mam used to make the best chips. Proper chips, fried in dripping. You don't get that anymore. My grandma was the same. Dripping was the key. It’s the flavour, innit? Everything's too clean these days. Too… healthy. Though, on the health front, I did make a really good lentil soup last weekend. Very nutritious. Lots of veggies. Lentil soup? Now you  are  trying to tempt fate. I've got nothing against lentils, per se, but they’re not exactly a hearty meal, are they? She’s trying to balance out all those Greggs, Alan. It’s a noble effort. Exactly! Gotta have some balance. Anyway, I’m thinking of trying that new Vietnamese place near the station tonight.

… honestly, I still don’t get TikTok. My daughter’s glued to it, but it's just… people dancing, isn't it? And lip-syncing? What’s the appeal? It's a bit more than that, isn’t it, Barry? There’s a whole cottage industry of information sharing, even educational stuff, surprisingly. Though I grant you, a lot of it  is  just people having five seconds of fame. Saw one yesterday of a bloke balancing a biscuit on his nose. Oh, you're missing out, lads! It’s absurd, utterly absurd, and that’s the point. I started using it to try and understand what the students are actually  doing  with their time, and… well, it's a rabbit hole. I’ve learned more about obscure 80s synth-pop in the last month than I have in the last decade. 80s synth-pop? Right. See, that's just not my thing. Give me a good historical biography any day. This whole social media business feels… ephemeral. Like it'll all vanish tomorrow. That's a fair point, Barry. It  does  feel a bit transient. But think about it, we’re librarians. Information’s our stock-in-trade, and people are getting their information – however curated or… questionable – from these platforms. We need to understand the landscape. Exactly! It’s outreach, you know? Used to be we had posters and flyers. Now it’s Instagram reels and Twitter threads. Trust me, I tried a “BookTok” review last week. It didn’t exactly go viral, but it got a few more students interested in the Victorian novel collection. BookTok? Is that… TikTok for books? Sounds… terrifying. Did you have to  dance  with a copy of  Middlemarch ? Thankfully, no! Although, a student suggested it. I just did a quick, enthusiastic review. Apparently, the key is to be “authentic.” Which, considering my age, felt… ironic. I've been slowly getting into Twitter. Mainly just following accounts related to library science and archival work. It’s good for keeping up with new trends. Though the sheer amount of… opinion can be exhausting. Twitter. That’s the one where everyone just yells at each other, isn't it? I tried it once. Lasted about five minutes. Someone told me my punctuation was atrocious. Sounds about right. It's not known for its civility. I mostly stick to reading, not replying. Less chance of a digital shouting match that way.

…and honestly, Geoffrey, the sheer scale of it is quite daunting. A brand new hospice, not just a refurbishment, but a completely new build. It feels… enormous. We've got to get the consultation  right . Absolutely, Eleanor. Daunting, yes, but also a phenomenal opportunity. Think of the impact. And the consultation is key. We’ve got the initial outreach planned with the local councils, but it feels… superficial. They’ll pay lip service, then complain about parking if we dare put up a decent-sized building. Exactly! And it's not  just  the councils. We need to get the GPs onside, the community nurses, the existing hospices – St. Julian’s, for example. We don’t want to be seen as stepping on toes. They provide a fantastic service, but they’re stretched. This isn't about competition; it's about capacity. Have you seen the business case modelling on projected patient numbers? It's alarming. I have. Dry reading, but alarming is the word. The demographic shifts in Kent are significant. Aging population, influx of retirees… the pressure on existing services will only intensify. That's why I pushed for this location in Tunbridge Wells. It’s central, good transport links, reasonably affluent catchment area… though finding a suitable plot has been a nightmare. The rationale for Tunbridge Wells is solid, undeniably. But ‘reasonably affluent’ doesn’t automatically equal supportive, Geoffrey. There's a Nimbyism streak a mile wide in parts of this county. They like the  idea  of a hospice, until it’s proposed for a field near their perfectly manicured gardens. We need to clearly articulate the benefits to  everyone . The easing of pressure on the NHS, the specialist palliative care… We do. And we’re including that in the full business case, of course. But it's more than just demographics and pressures. It's about how we integrate with the existing local health service structure. Have we had proper conversations with the integrated care board about referral pathways? Preliminary talks, yes. They’re… cautious. Understandably. They're juggling budgets tighter than ever. Someone mentioned something about diverting funds from preventative care. Which, frankly, is madness. Investing in end-of-life care isn’t just about comfort; it’s about dignity, and ultimately, potentially reducing the need for expensive hospital stays. Precisely. We need to frame it as cost-effective. And not just in monetary terms. Think about the impact on family carers.

…and honestly, that hat was  atrocious . Millicent always did have questionable taste, didn’t she? Look at her, bless her, trying to pull off that fuchsia number at Ascot. Remember Ascot, David? 2008, I think? 2008, you're right. The year it rained relentlessly. I remember being soaked to the bone, trying to look dignified while sheltering under a frankly inadequate umbrella. And Millicent  did  look like a particularly flamboyant flamingo. Though she was convinced she was channeling the Queen Mother. Oh, this is a good one! You two look so young! Mum, you had  so  much hair back then. And Dad, that tie... is that paisley? Paisley was  in , darling. Don't you dare mock the paisley! And yes, a lot of hair. Before the stress of nursing and raising a copywriter took its toll. Speaking of which, how did that interview go today, Chloe? It was… okay. A lot of talking about brand voice and target demographics. The office is really cool, very modern. But the guy interviewing me kept fiddling with this massive phone ring. It was, like, light-up and sparkly. Completely distracting. A sparkly ring? Good grief. Some people. What kind of company was it, anyway? A tech start-up. They’re developing some app for… I honestly couldn’t follow half of what the guy was saying. Something about NFTs and the metaverse. It feels a bit… much, you know? Sounds exhausting. Are you still thinking of applying for that role at the museum? The one you mentioned last week? It seemed more ‘you’. Yeah, I think so. Less metaverse, more history. Which, let’s be honest, is a win. It’s just… a bit lower paid. You can’t put a price on happiness, Chloe. Besides, you’re good at what you do. You’ll find something. Remember old Mr. Henderson, your great-grandfather? He was a master craftsman, wasn’t he? That’s where you get your creativity from. I remember mum telling stories about the things he used to make. Oh, yes. Wonderful things. Tables, chairs, even a rocking horse for your Auntie Brenda. He was a proper artisan. Apparently, he almost went to London to work on some commissioned piece for a rather posh family, but his father got ill and he stayed to run the farm. That's a bit sad, isn't it? Giving up a dream like that?

…and then the  thing  just… slides out from under the bed! Honestly, Chloe, I nearly jumped outta me skin. I thought me heart was gonna give out. Oh, come  on , Maisie. You said you weren’t scared! You were practically hiding behind the popcorn bowl five minutes ago. It was just a shadow, a dodgy angle, and some dramatic music. Dodgy angle?! It were a hand! A proper, claw-like hand! And it weren't a shadow, it were  pale . Pale as a ghost, it were. Don't tell me you weren’t even a bit spooked by ‘The Hollow Ones’? Spooked? No. Mildly…discomforted? Perhaps. The CGI wasn't  that  convincing, to be honest. It felt more…silly than terrifying. Like a low-budget Halloween costume come to life. You know I prefer psychological thrillers anyway, things that get under your skin. Not jump scares. Oh, now you’re being proper snobby. Just 'cause it’s not some fancy, artsy film about repressed childhood trauma doesn’t mean it’s bad! Sometimes you just want somethin’ to make ya scream a bit. It’s a release, innit? Gets the adrenaline going. I suppose. But screaming isn’t really ‘watching’ a film, is it? It’s more… reacting  to  a film. I like to analyse, to think about the motives, the symbolism. This just felt…cheap. Remember ‘Relic’? That was genuinely unsettling. The way it portrayed dementia… that stayed with me for days. ‘Relic’ were depressing, though! That were proper bleak. I watched that and then couldn’t get outta bed for a full day. This one… this one's just a bit of fun. A bit of a thrill. Besides, I’m from Yorkshire, we’re built tough. Scares don’t really bother us. Built tough? You literally yelped when the cat jumped out at you last week. From  behind  the sofa. That were different! Winston’s a ninja in fluff. He's got stealth, that cat. And besides, I didn't  yelp , I issued a startled exclamation. There’s a difference. So, are you saying you don’t like  any  scary films? Not even ‘The Babadook’? ‘The Babadook’ was good. Very good, actually. Again, it wasn't about monsters under the bed. It was about grief, and motherhood, and trying to cope with…everything. It  felt  real, you know? I also thought ‘Hereditary’ was masterfully done. Truly disturbing, but in a… sophisticated way.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just a faff. Three emails back and forth trying to clarify if the double glazing was included in the price!
