Honestly, you’d think Airbnb hosts would just be clearer from the start. Airbnb, eh? Sounds terribly complicated. Back in my day, you stayed in a proper hotel, paid a proper price, and everything was… proper. No emails, just a bellboy. A very polite bellboy, I might add. Things have changed a bit, Grandad. It  can  be lovely, and often cheaper, but yeah, the online booking stuff…it's a minefield. I’m trying to find somewhere for Mum and Dad for their anniversary next month. Somewhere near the coast. Devon coast is lovely. Used to take your grandmother to Seaton. She loved a good cream tea. Still do, actually, when Elsie brings one round. Though they're not quite the same without your grandmother. They sound lovely. I’ll have to suggest Seaton to Mum. Speaking of Elsie, did she manage to order that new iPad she was talking about? She was struggling with the website. Oh, she did! Took me an hour, mind you. She kept clicking things randomly. Kept trying to pay with her library card! Had to explain, very slowly, the concept of a debit card. They don’t make ‘em like they used to, these gadgets. All buttons and screens and… well, it’s just not cricket. Elsie and technology! That sounds about right. She’s wonderful, though. I’m glad you have her. She’s a good woman. Keeps me on my toes, that one. Now, what about you? Long day at school? It was. Year 5 are doing a project on volcanoes. It involved a  lot  of papier-mâché and glitter. I’ll be finding glitter in my hair for weeks. It’s nearly bedtime for me, actually. Just finishing a cup of tea and checking emails. Though, I'm considering turning the email notifications  off  permanently. It's relentless. Relentless is a good word for it. Never used to get this much correspondence. Mostly bills and the occasional letter from your Aunt Mildred complaining about the price of cheese. Though, remember when young Thomas was trying to sell those… what were they? Those energy-saving lightbulbs? Sent me a pamphlet every week for six months. Oh, Thomas! Yes, he was very keen on those lightbulbs. He’s doing well now, isn’t he?

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it, Hamish. It wasn’t just the temples, it was  everything . The way the jungle just… swallowed the stone. You felt like you were the first person to stumble upon it in centuries. Aye, I can imagine. Angkor Wat, right? You finally made it then? Been talkin' about it for, what, five years now? Five years and three cancelled flights! But worth every bit of the hassle. Honestly, it put everything into perspective. All this work, these deadlines… feels a bit flimsy when you're standin’ in front of somethin' built to last a thousand years. It’s also made me revisit my reading list. I’ve been meaning to properly tackle Norman Lewis’  A Dragon Apparent  for ages. Oh, brilliant choice. Lewis is a master. Did you know he spent a fair bit of time in Scotland, actually? Up in the Hebrides, writing, I think. Makes sense, that wild landscape would suit his temperament. Have you read  Jackdaw Cade ? It’s lighter fare, but a brilliant character piece. Not  Jackdaw Cade , no. Added to the list, of course. The pile is gettin’ alarmingly high! But  A Dragon Apparent  already feels different than most travel writing. It's not just about the places, it's about the people, the feeling of being utterly  lost  and simultaneously completely immersed. Reminds me a bit of… well, remember that disastrous hiking trip we did in the Cairngorms when we were students? Disastrous is an understatement! Lost for nearly twelve hours, completely soaked, and fueled only by oatcakes and sheer stubbornness. Don't remind me. Your mum nearly killed us both when we finally staggered back into Livingston. She was right to be furious! But even  that  had a strange beauty to it, didn't it? That feeling of being completely at the mercy of the landscape. It’s a similar thread, I think, to what Lewis gets at. It’s not about conquering places, but about letting them… affect you. I get that. And I think that’s why we both gravitated towards travel in the first place, isn’t it? Not for the Instagram shots, although that's a side effect for some, but for that fundamental shift in perspective. Have you started plannin’ the next adventure, then? Don't tell me you're thinkin' South America again. Tempted, aye. But I’m thinking a bit closer to home, actually.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt…off. Like they were more interested in how many hours I could  commit  than what I actually  could do . It was a five-minute chat about overtime before they even asked about my portfolio. Sounds dreadful, love. Still, good you walked away. You don't want to start a job feeling already undervalued. Was it that Foster & Bell place? The one near Canary Wharf? Yeah, Foster & Bell. Apparently, they’re expanding, big time. But at what cost? I’m still relatively new to being fully qualified, Mum. I need somewhere I can  learn  properly, not just be a drafting machine until midnight. Exactly. You’ve got a brilliant mind, Chloe. That Masters wasn’t easy, and you came out top of your year. Don't let some flash firm make you feel anything else. It's a competitive world, I know, but your talent will shine. Thanks, Mum. It’s just… disheartening, you know? I sent off an application to Harrison & Croft last week, and I haven’t heard anything. They’re doing really interesting work with sustainable housing. That's  really  what I want to focus on. Harrison & Croft, now  they  have a reputation. A good one. And that sustainable stuff is important. Remember old Mr. Abernathy at school? Always going on about building for the future. Vaguely! He smelled of wood shavings and optimism. But yeah, it's crucial. Anyway, I was looking at the job description again, and they specifically mention proficiency in Revit. I'm… competent, but not an expert. Oh, Revit. That sounds complicated. Is that one of those computer things? It is. It’s basically 3D modelling software for architects. Everyone uses it now. I took a short course, but I feel a little shaky compared to some of my classmates. I’m worried that’s what's holding me back. Well, perhaps you could do another one? A more… intensive course? I know it's money, but wouldn’t it be worth it in the long run? I’ve been looking. There’s one at the Bartlett School of Architecture, a four-week intensive. It’s expensive, around £800, and it's during the week, so I'd have to ask about taking some time off from the firm… not that I’m particularly keen on asking after the Foster & Bell fiasco. Hmm. That is tricky.

…and honestly, the price of petrol these days! Remember when you could fill up for a tenner? Now it’s almost sixty quid for a full tank. Sixty! It's daylight robbery, I tell you. Daylight robbery. Sixty quid, you say? Sounds about right, Arthur. Though I mostly just potter about these days. Don’t need to go far, thankfully. Though getting to the shops is a bit of a palaver with the buses being what they are. They used to run every fifteen minutes, now it's more like every half hour if you're lucky. Oh, don't even  start  on the buses, George. I tried to get into Norwich last week to see Bethany, and the first one just…didn’t turn up. Just a blank space on the app. Had to wait forty-five minutes for the next one! And it was packed, standing room only. Forty-five minutes? That’s scandalous. They say they’re trying to encourage people to use public transport, but how can they expect that when it’s so unreliable? It’s all this government, isn’t it? Cutting back on everything. Used to be, Norfolk had a decent bus network. Always blaming the government, Arthur. Though I suppose there’s a bit of truth in it. It’s not like they’re putting money  into  things, are they? All this talk about levelling up…seems to me they’re just shifting things  around . It's the housing too, isn't it? Bethany’s trying to find a place of her own, a little flat, and the prices…absolutely ridiculous. She’s working two jobs and still can’t afford anything decent. Remember when a young couple could actually  buy  a house? Buy a house? Don’t talk to me about buying a house. I used to be a civil engineer, y’know. Involved in developing a whole estate out near Drayton. Nice houses, perfectly reasonable prices…back in the eighties. Now? Those same houses would cost half a million, easy. Half a million! It’s bonkers. Remember old Mr. Peterson who lived next door to us in Costessey? He bought his house for, I don’t know, a couple of thousand pounds, I reckon. Said he could remember when fields were all around, not houses crammed in everywhere. It’s just…where are the young people supposed to live? And then they wonder why people aren't having children.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of bags people are leaving in the old art room is ridiculous. It's not a storage facility, David! We’re trying to convert it into a proper workshop space for the pottery classes, remember? Right, the pottery. Yeah, Mrs. Henderson was moaning about it yesterday, wasn't she? Said she nearly tripped over a suitcase the size of a small car. I'll put a notice up, something about a two-week limit on stored items. Though knowing some of ‘em, they’ll ignore it. A notice is a start. It really feels like we're constantly battling against things just…accumulating. It’s not helped by the fact we’re offering space seemingly for free to every community group under the sun. We need to be stricter about what we offer, and what we  charge  for it. Easier said than done, Eleanor. It  is  a charity, after all. Though I agree, that yoga class that uses the main hall on Tuesdays? They're bringing in a good donation each session, but it doesn’t feel like enough for the wear and tear. Especially with all the mat rolling. Precisely! And we need to think about more revenue streams. I was looking at the bookings for next month. A lull after the vegan baking workshop. We need something…different. Perhaps a weekend craft fair? We could charge stall fees. A craft fair… not a bad shout. Might be a logistical nightmare though, getting everything set up and cleared away. We’d need extra hands. And we’d really need to sort the fire escapes first, wouldn't we? Remember what happened last year with the health and safety inspector? A repeat of  that  and we're sunk. Don't remind me! That was mortifying. And yes, the fire escapes are a priority. I’ve emailed Maintenance, but they’re always so slow to respond. I might have to chase them again. Speaking of maintenance, did you see the state of the roof garden? Someone's been feeding the pigeons again. It’s covered! Ah, Old Man Hemmings, probably. He thinks they're his little buddies. Harmless enough, but a right mess. I’ll get young Liam to give it a sweep. He owes me a favour – apparently his auntie booked a space for her macrame class and he wants to make sure it’s perfect.

…and honestly, the pub lunch yesterday was  almost  worth the drive. Almost. That gravy was phenomenal. Though, Rhys, you barely touched your pie. Everything alright? Aye, it was a good pie. Just…a bit rich, that’s all. Too much pastry, if you ask me. Though, I wouldn’t say no to a slice of that apple crumble Elin’s made, would I? Smells divine. Rich? You’re a Welshman, Rhys! You practically  live  on lamb and gravy! Something’s going on. Spill. Besides, that crumble  is  pretty special. Elin’s got a gift, she does. Don't pressure him, Dave. He's been a bit off all day. Just let him enjoy the crumble. It  does  smell good, though. Proper comfort food. Oh, go on, Rhys. A little crumble won't hurt. You always did have a sweet tooth, even as a boy running around Cardiff. Remember trying to sneak biscuits from my pantry? Alright, alright. It’s just…seeing all this countryside, it’s making me think. Remember Old Man Pritchard’s farm back home? Proper Welsh farm, that was. His wife made the best bara brith. This is lovely, Elin, honestly, but it's…different. Different how? It's apple crumble, Rhys! A classic. Though, I suppose coming from Wales, everything does feel a bit…English. I spent my childhood bouncing between Cape Town and boarding school, so I get feeling a bit adrift sometimes. Now, now, Elin. England’s not so bad. Though, it’s true, nothing beats a good Welsh bake. Pritchard’s farm…ah, memories. He always had a flask of something strong hidden in the barn. Offering it to us ‘volunteers’ helping with the hay! He was a rogue, that man. A rogue is an understatement! I remember him trying to convince us that sheep were just fluffy, four-legged lawnmowers. He claimed no actual farming was involved. He had a way with words, that one. Always stirring up trouble. A good man, though. Always willing to help a neighbour. He'd give you the shirt off his back, even if it smelled of sheep. So, Rhys, is that what's bothering you? Homesickness for Pritchard’s ? It’s not just that, I suppose. It’s…feeling a bit useless, really. I’m used to  doing  something. Teaching, marking papers…and now I’m on leave, supposedly relaxing. But I feel like I should be helping, contributing  something .

…and honestly, the traffic was  brutal . Like, genuinely thought I was going to be stuck there 'til next Tuesday. Did you see that advert on the radio this morning though? The one for the garage? Absolutely mental. They were doing sound effects of screeching tires and then a bloke shouting about 'amazing deals'! It was proper unsettling first thing. No, thankfully missed that one. My commute was pretty smooth, actually. Though I did get stuck behind a learner driver for a bit. Very patient testing of my inner calm, that was. Amazing deals shouted at you at 8 am… sounds delightful. Where were you coming from anyway? You looked a bit frazzled when you got in. Just dropping little Elsie off at Nana’s. She’s got a drama workshop thing today, full of glitter and probably chaos. Honestly, that bairn is a whirlwind. It's good for her though, lets her burn off some energy. Though, Nana will be knackered after. Speaking of frazzled, how was that conference in Birmingham? Still hearing about it. Birmingham was… intense. A lot of networking, a lot of presentations about modular construction and sustainable materials. Honestly, half the time I was just nodding and trying to look engaged. It’s all very important, obviously, but after a while, it’s just a blur of PowerPoint. Did manage a decent curry though, so not a total loss. Have you ever been to Birmingham? Never. Always seemed a bit… grey. I’m more of a coastal lass, you know? Give me Sunderland, or even Whitby, any day. Somewhere you can smell the sea air. I've been trying to convince you we need to go proper on holiday this year. Not just a weekend in the Lake District, something  proper . Maybe Spain? Or Italy? Italy sounds good! We talked about Florence a while back, didn't we? All the art and the pasta… could be very persuasive. Spain’s good too, though. Maybe somewhere a bit quieter, not one of the big resorts? I’m still recovering from Benidorm with the lads after uni. Too much sangria, not enough sleep. Oh, I can  imagine . Your stories from that trip are legendary. No no, definitely not Benidorm vibes. More… rustic? You know, little villages, local markets. And speaking of needing a holiday, how are your parents? Still planning on visiting them in Harpenden next month? Yeah, end of next month.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the appointment was just… chaotic. They’d moved Mum’s colonoscopy forward a week, hadn't told us, and then acted surprised when we weren’t there! Honestly, the NHS is stretched to breaking point, isn’t it? You’d think something as crucial as that would be handled with a bit more… care. Oh, bless you, Sarah. That  is  stressful. My Arthur had a similar thing with his knee replacement referral. Kept being told ‘we’ll call you’, then nothing. Had to chase it myself three times. Seems like you have to fight for everything these days. How  is  your Mum doing, though? Is she… well, is she coping with everything? She’s… managing. It's more the waiting than anything, I think. The uncertainty. And then, on top of that, Uncle George passed last week. Completely out of the blue. Heart just gave out, apparently. Oh, Sarah, no! Poor George! I haven’t seen him in years, but I remember him being such a character. Always telling those terrible jokes. I'm so sorry. Is it a recent loss, then? Just last Tuesday. We're trying to sort out the funeral now. My sister, Emily, is… well, Emily is being Emily. Completely falling apart, demanding everything be ‘perfect’. She wants a horse-drawn carriage, can you believe it? For Uncle George, who loathed horses! Oh dear. Sounds like Emily. She’s always been a bit…particular. It’s hard, isn’t it, when grief comes out sideways? My nan, when my grandad died, started rearranging all the furniture. Every single day. Said it helped her feel in control, but it drove my mum mad. Exactly! My brother, David, is just… silent. Completely shut down. He used to be so close to George. It’s like he’s trying to pretend it hasn’t happened. And Mum… Mum just keeps saying she feels fat. Fat? Now that  is  odd. At a time like this? I know! She said she’s comfort eating, and feeling terrible about it. She's been on and off these diets for years, you know. Always trying to slim down. She's a perfectly healthy weight, but she’s so self-conscious. She was saying, “I don't want to look a mess at the funeral!” Honestly, it’s like she’s more worried about her appearance than about losing her brother!

…and honestly, the revisions were  brutal . Apparently, “impactful synergy” is now passé. Who knew? They wanted “dynamic collaboration” instead. Honestly, marketing jargon gives me a headache these days. Dynamic collaboration? Sounds…made up. Like something a robot would say. It is a bit, isn't it, Leo? It’s all about appearing innovative. I’ve got meetings all week just discussing ‘leveraging core competencies’. It's exhausting. Though, at least it pays the bills. How’s the proofreading side going, Sarah? Still finding typos in important documents? Oh, constantly. You wouldn't  believe  the grammatical errors I found in a legal contract last week. Seriously threatening the whole deal. It's stressful, but satisfying when you save the day. It's decent money, fills the gaps, lets me work around school runs and… well, life. School runs are the  worst . Especially when it's raining. Did you see Mr. Henderson’s car today, Dad? It was covered in mud. He said he got stuck in a field. No way! Classic Henderson. He’s always getting into scrapes. Probably trying to take a shortcut. Speaking of cars, I was looking at a new SUV. Something practical for getting up to the slopes this winter. Oh, skiing! That sounds amazing. I haven’t been in ages. Remember that trip to Austria, David? We nearly got stranded in that chalet because of a blizzard! How could I forget? You were convinced we'd have to eat all the cheese and crackers we had left. And Leo was determined to build a snow fort that reached the roof. It was a good fort! Until your dad accidentally walked into it. He was NOT happy. He swore he saw a yeti. He did! He blamed it on the altitude. Honestly, we had some good times. We need to go again. What about this winter, David? I’d love to. I'm already thinking about it. We just need to book early. It gets expensive, though. Ben, are you doing anything for work experience this year? Have you thought about what you'd like to do? I was thinking maybe something with computers. Like, building them or something. Mr. Davies said I’m pretty good at it. He runs the computer club at school. That’s brilliant, Ben! That’s a really valuable skill. You could even look at cybersecurity. It’s a growing field. Cybersecurity? Sounds complicated.

…and honestly, the light in that one is dreadful. Really flat. You can barely make out the Torii gate at all. It doesn't do Fushimi Inari justice  at all . Remember how vibrant it was? Oh, don’t be so harsh, darling. It’s a photo album, not a gallery showing! It’s the memory that counts. Besides, I remember  you  fumbling with the settings the whole time, convinced you were going to get the perfect shot. You were muttering about aperture and ISO like you were conducting an orchestra. Well, a photographer has standards! And it  was  a bit fiddly. That bright sunlight, then darting in and out of the shadows… It’s tricky. Though, looking at it now, it does capture the sheer number of gates. It was overwhelming, wasn’t it? Like walking through a red tunnel. Absolutely. And the little fox statues everywhere! I spent ages trying to photograph them all with different expressions. Did you ever manage to get a good one? I think so. There's one further on, I'll dig it out. Not a masterpiece, but the little guy looks particularly mischievous. Speaking of animals… this reminds me. Remember that night in the garden, back in Chelmsford? With… him ? Oh, don’t tell me you're going to bring up Bartholomew again. Bartholomew was a legend! A badger, bold as brass, raiding your mum’s rose bushes. He was a menace! Mum was  furious . She’d spent weeks pruning those roses. And you just stood there, filming him on your phone, cackling like a maniac. It was comedic gold! He was waddling away with a rose stem dangling from his mouth. Looked like he was enjoying a particularly fragrant cigar. He even glanced at the camera! You’re exaggerating. He probably just saw the light. Though, he was remarkably brazen. We never had anything like that here in Norfolk. Mostly just hedgehogs and the occasional fox. Which are lovely, but they lack the…gravitas of a badger. They’re not quite as discerning about their floral choices, you see. You're such a romantic about badgers. It's ridiculous. Look, here's one of us at the Golden Pavilion. Honestly, this one’s not bad. You actually managed to capture the reflection in the pond. See? I  can  take a decent photo occasionally. It just requires the right subject matter. And optimal lighting conditions, obviously.

…and honestly, the Guinness  did  taste better in Dublin. I don’t know if it's the water or what, but it’s a whole different experience. Though, nearly getting arrested for attempting to climb the Molly Malone statue wasn't ideal. Oh, you and your antics, Leo! Climbing statues? Seriously? I thought you were supposed to be the sensible one. Though, I’ll admit, Ireland was amazing. Bit soggy, but amazing. Much more…atmospheric than East London, innit? Atmospheric? It's grey and damp! Birmingham’s grim, but at least it's  honestly  grim. Ireland’s trying too hard to be picturesque while simultaneously raining on your head. Anyway, you were talking about Guinness… Did anyone actually go skinny dipping in the sea like we planned? Nah, too cold even for an Aussie. I mean, I’ve swam with sharks, ridden a camel in the outback, but the Irish Sea? No thanks. Though, there  was  this one bloke on the beach in Dingle… clearly thought he was Poseidon. Hilarious. Right, the Poseidon bloke! I saw him. He didn’t last long. And yeah, it was freezing. We  briefly  considered it, me and Amelia. Brief emphasis on briefly. Mostly we just huddled in the pub. Speaking of freezing, I reckon if a zombie apocalypse hit, Ireland would be ironically ideal. No one would want to go there. Oh, amazing. A zombie apocalypse strategy based on dampness. You are a genius, Leo. Though, realistically, I'd head straight to Australia, Mat. Seems fairly isolated. And you lot have… spiders. Zombies wouldn’t bother with spiders. Spiders are our first line of defence, actually. They pre-clear the area. But yeah, isolated is a good point. Though, we’d probably just build a fence and charge entry. "Zombie-Free Zone: $50 a head." You two are ridiculous. Honestly. Though, I'm more worried about the neighbour's snoring. It's like a freight train going through my café at 3 am last night. I swear it's getting worse. It’s driving away my customers! Old Man Hemmings? He's a legend. Though, yeah, the snoring is… industrial. Maybe we should get him a CPAP machine as a collective gift? Good idea. Speaking of gifts, I baked challah! It’s still warm. My nan’s recipe. She got it from this book by Claudia Roden, you know, the Jewish cookbook writer? It’s divine.

… honestly, I still can’t believe you’ve never had a proper bag of proper peanuts. Like, the ones with the shells still on? Not those pre-shelled, sad little things. Alright, alright, lay off the peanut slander, eh? I’ve  had  peanuts with shells, just… not regularly. My nan always kept those salted ones, massively overdone with salt, and they stuck to your fingers something awful. Put me off a bit, I think. It’s a texture thing, maybe? Texture? What’s wrong with the satisfying  crack  of breaking the shell? It’s practically meditative! You’re a PhD student, you should appreciate little moments of mindful shell-cracking. I appreciate mindful data analysis, thank you very much. And avoiding sticky fingers. Speaking of things you wouldn't understand… I spent the last three hours battling a raid boss in ‘Eldoria Online’. Proper, frustrating, glorious victory. You wouldn’t last five minutes. Oh, here we go. Still on that game then? I thought you said you were supposed to be writing your thesis? Research requires… downtime. Strategic recreation. It’s about optimal brain function! Besides, Mark’s on there too, and we need to coordinate. He’s utterly useless without my tactical guidance, honestly. Right. Tactical guidance. So, ordering him to run directly into danger while you snipe from afar? It’s more nuanced than that! It’s about calculated risk assessment. Anyway, we were talking about entertainment. Have you thought any more about Alton Towers for our birthdays? I found a deal that includes fast passes. Alton Towers… Hmm. Still a bit apprehensive. Nemesis Inferno looks terrifying. I’m more of a gently-rolling-coaster type, you know? Something you can enjoy with a pint afterwards without needing to lie down. Gently rolling? You went on The Smiler with me last year! You screamed the whole way. That was… a moment of weakness. And I’d had two Pimms. It doesn't count. We could go see a film instead? That new sci-fi one, ‘Echo Protocol’? The reviews are decent. Films are nice, I suppose. But a rollercoaster provides a much more… visceral experience. A release of endorphins! It’s practically psychological therapy. Plus, have you  seen  the queues for decent films these days? It's like trying to get through border security at Heathrow. Don’t even mention border security. I flew back from a conference in Amsterdam last week, and the whole thing was a shambles.

…and honestly, the blisters are  brutal . I didn’t realise how much pressure you put on your hands when you’re learning to row. It’s not graceful at all, you know? It’s just… gripping, and pulling, and trying not to fall in. Oh dear, that sounds awful! I always imagined rowing as being quite elegant, all sweeping movements. You’re proving me wrong. Is it at least enjoyable, despite the hand trauma? It  is  actually, when it clicks. There’s a moment, when you get the timing right with everyone else in the boat, and it just… glides. But that moment is fleeting! Mostly it’s just feeling like a slightly uncoordinated octopus. Have you ever tried kayaking? It’s a bit more my speed, less reliant on perfect synchronicity. I have! Years ago, in the Lake District. Absolutely loved it. Such a peaceful way to see the scenery. Though I did manage to capsize. Twice. The water was freezing! Reminded me I really need to invest in some proper waterproofs. You know, the kind that actually  work ? Everything claims to be waterproof these days, but it rarely is. Tell me about it! I’m trying to find a decent jacket for rowing. Something that won’t weigh me down when it’s wet, but also won’t let me resemble a drowned rat. It's proving difficult. Everything seems to be designed for…mountain climbing, not gently propelling oneself down the Cam. It’s the same with trousers, isn’t it? Trying to find something that dries quickly and doesn’t chafe. Speaking of which, did I tell you I finally met my cousin Brenda’s daughter? No! Brenda, from…Australia? I thought you’d given up hope of ever meeting her. I had! Brenda and I haven’t seen each other since we were children, our mothers were sisters, but they fell out over…well, something terribly trivial, and it just escalated. Years of silence. Then her daughter, Chloe, started researching our family history. Found me online and just…messaged. She’s lovely. We spent a whole afternoon in York last month. That's wonderful! It must have been really special, bridging that gap. It's funny how family connections can get lost. Thinking about family… I had some difficult news last week. Oh? What is it, darling? You sound worried. It's Uncle George. They found something on a scan.

…and then I genuinely thought I’d messed up the history essay completely. Like, totally blanked on the dates for the Treaty of Versailles! Honestly, Dad, I was panicking. Aye, well, panicking doesn't help, does it, lass? Though I remember feeling the same before me O-Levels. Used to get right knotted. Still, you're a bright lass, you always have been. Didn't expect you to be worried about history though, thought it were the physics that had you in a state. Physics was… alright. It’s just, history feels really  important  for what I want to do at uni. They said the personal statement is key, but the grades obviously matter too. When are the results actually released? Is it still Thursday? Thursday morning, as far as I know. Though knowing Vodafone, I bet I'll get a text about it before  you  do. They seem to know everything about me, those lot. Sent me an offer for a new phone yesterday, just because I looked at a glass water bottle on Amazon. Honestly. They're creepy, aren't they? Oh! Remind me to check eBay later, I saw some really nice chunky boots on there. My current ones are falling apart. Need something decent for campus. Boots, eh? You’ll be trampling through mud on that campus, you know. Speaking of, have you sorted the student finance yet? Your mum was on about it this morning. Mostly. It’s just a massive headache, all the forms and things. I think I’ve done everything, but it's just…  money , isn't it? It's so stressful. And I still need decent pens. Like, proper ones. Not those cheap biros the school gives out. Ah, a good pen is crucial. I always say that. Remember your grandad? He had a whole collection. Ballpoint, fountain pen, even one of those old dip pens. Used to use them for Morse code, believe it or not. Morse code?! Grandad? Seriously? Aye, during the war, he worked as a signals operator. Taught me a bit when I was a lad. Dot-dash, dot-dash… actually, let me see if I remember... …here, try texting me something. Just a simple word. Right… okay. “Hello.” Dot-dot-dot, dash-dash-dash, dot-dot… That's an 'H'. See? It  is  coming back to me. Waste of time now, though, isn't it? Everyone just uses emojis.

… honestly, the deadline for the dissertation proposal is stressing me  out . I’ve barely touched it. Been too busy trying to debug this ridiculous code for Professor Davies. Feels like I'm building his entire research project, innit? Tell me about it, man. Davies is a proper taskmaster. Remember last year with the data analysis? He wanted everything perfectly formatted, down to the millisecond difference in timestamps. Nightmare. But dissertation proposals… that’s a whole other level of panic. What’s yours on again? It’s looking at the impact of social media algorithms on political polarisation. Super broad, I know. I’m trying to narrow it down to focus on a specific platform, maybe Twitter… or X, whatever Elon’s calling it this week. It feels… weighty, you know? Like, significant. Yeah, that  is  heavy stuff. But good heavy, if you catch my drift. Potential to actually say something meaningful. I'm doing mine on the representation of Jamaican patois in contemporary British literature. Thankfully, plenty of source material, just gotta wrangle it all. Sounds fascinating! You always pick the interesting stuff. Speaking of interesting… you still planning that trip to Japan after exams? You were talking about Tokyo for ages. Definitely. Booked the flights last week, actually. Going for three weeks, should be amazing. Thinking of hitting up Akihabara, the electric town, for all the latest computer gear - see if I can snag a new graphics card or something. The prices are supposed to be ridiculously good. Ooh, serious! Don't forget to send me a link if you find anything good. My PC is practically begging for an upgrade. Honestly, I’m jealous. I’m firmly stuck in exam hell for the foreseeable. I haven't even  thought  about holidays. You should! You  need  a break. Seriously, studying non-stop isn’t good for you. You look knackered. Remember that little ramen place near Camden? 'Menya Musashi'? We should go there next week, just to de-stress. Proper good food. Actually, that sounds brilliant. I’m craving ramen  so  badly. And yeah, you're right. I’m running on fumes. It’s just… feeling the pressure, you know? Uni feels so… consequential. Like everything hinges on this. I get it, believe me. But it doesn't. It feels like that now, but it really doesn't. There are so many paths. My cousin, remember Keisha? She completely changed careers after graduating.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of photos Mum posts on Facebook is astonishing. It's Buckfast Abbey, Buckfast Abbey, Buckfast Abbey! Beautiful place, I'm sure, but I've seen every stained-glass window approximately seven times now. Oh, now, be kind, love. She’s enjoying sharing it. And it  is  a lovely place. Remember when we took your Grandad there, Arthur? He was fascinated by the monks. Fascinated is putting it mildly. I interrogated them about their accounts, you know? Spent a good half hour trying to understand how they managed their endowments. Accountants never truly retire, you see. Always assessing the fiscal responsibility of…well, everyone. Grandad! You tried to audit the monks? That sounds about right. Did they even answer you? Oh, they were polite enough. Young lad, very earnest, kept saying “Bless you, sir” whenever I asked a particularly pointed question about their investment strategy. Though I suspect he just wanted me to go away. He probably did! He was a bit…intense about things like that. Speaking of trips, what did you think of the idea of a cruise, darling? I was looking at one around the Mediterranean. A cruise…hmm. It’s not really my thing, is it? Feels a bit…confining. I’d rather actually  be  somewhere, you know? Wandering around, getting lost. Plus, I've heard some horror stories about norovirus. Oh, don't be silly. They’re very good at hygiene now. And think of all the food! And not having to unpack and repack. It’d be a lovely, relaxing break. Relaxing? Surrounded by hundreds of other people all vying for the same buffet? Sounds like a tax return deadline to me! No thank you. Though, I did see something on the news about David Cameron and some offshore accounts… now  that’s  something worth investigating. Dodgy business, that. Please, Grandad, not politics first thing on a Saturday. I’ve just spent the week arguing with teenagers about Brexit. I need a break  from  current affairs, not a deep dive into tax avoidance schemes. He gets fired up, you know. It’s a habit. Though, he has a point about Cameron. Always seemed a bit… slippery. Anyway, we were talking about holidays. How’s the car doing, love? Still making that funny noise? It is. I took it to the garage, and they said it's the something-or-other, and it’ll be about £300 to fix.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the SAT NAV was just  stressful . Dad, you were convinced it was actively trying to lead us into canals! Well, it felt like it, didn't it? Honestly, that thing had a mind of its own. Kept telling us to turn down streets that weren't even there. And the roundabout in Bruges… a disaster. A complete and utter disaster. Oh, don’t even  start  on the roundabouts. They’re designed to confuse the British, I swear. All those lanes! And everyone just… merges. It’s terrifying. But Bruges was lovely, wasn't it? The chocolate shops… Absolutely gorgeous. Although, Mum, you did buy  so  much chocolate. How are you fitting it all into your suitcase? A girl needs her comforts! And it was a good price. Much cheaper than anything you get here. Speaking of prices, the coffee in Belgium was… interesting. Not as good as this, is it? This is lovely stuff. No, no. Coffee’s better here. And the service. They were a bit… abrupt in some of those cafes. Not rude, just…efficient. No chit-chat. Efficient is one word for it. I think ‘impatient’ is another. Remember that little market we went to in Ghent? That was much more my speed. All those little stalls with cheese and flowers and… everything. Oh, Ghent was wonderful! I got a beautiful little linen tablecloth there. And the waffles! Oh, the waffles. Were they not heavenly, John? Heavenly is a strong word, Margaret. They were…sweet. Very sweet. I had one with strawberries. Good, but gave me a sugar rush that lasted for hours. I nearly cycled into a canal, actually. You and your cycling! You were determined to cycle everywhere, weren’t you? Even with your dodgy knee. It's not  dodgy , it's… experienced. And it was the best way to see the countryside. Much better than being stuck in that car, following that demonic SAT NAV. I’m seriously considering getting rid of it when we get home. Don’t do that, Dad! What if we need it for something? Although, maybe we can download a better app. I got a new phone just before we went, you know? A Pixel 8. It's amazing. The maps are so much clearer. Oh, you did? Let me have a look. My phone is ancient. Still on one of those flip ones, practically.

…and honestly, the rosemary is  completely  overpowering. I thought a little sprig would be nice with the lamb, but it’s like Christmas in every mouthful. A little enthusiastic with the herbs, were we? I told you, you’re a bit heavy-handed in the kitchen, love. It's endearing, though. Endearing? It’ll taste like potpourri! Honestly, I’m starting to think I should just stick to boiling pasta. Speaking of which, how’s the sauce coming along? Is it needing salt? It’s good. Needs a touch more balsamic, I think. And a tiny bit of chilli flakes. It's the sauce Nonna used to make, remember? Though hers always smelled faintly of…well, her perfume. That incredibly floral stuff. Oh, God, yes! Like walking into a greenhouse after a particularly aggressive floral arrangement. What  was  that, anyway? Lilacs and… something horrifying? I think it was tuberose. She loved tuberose. Said it reminded her of her garden in Florence. You know, it’s funny, doesn’t it sound terribly posh when I say Florence? Especially coming from someone who grew up in Leith. My accent practically vanishes. It does! You sound like a character in a Merchant Ivory film. And your accent is lovely, by the way. Even when it  doesn’t  disappear. It's that Edinburgh lilt. It's very… distinguished. Flattery will get you everywhere. Although, I do get a lot of “Oh, you’re Scottish?” even down here in London. People can’t place it. They think I’m Irish, or Welsh sometimes. It’s not as distinctive as a West Country accent, I suppose. Although, even  those  get muddled these days. I was reading on Facebook – oh, don't roll your eyes, it wasn't deliberate eavesdropping – but Brenda was commenting on how she could barely understand young people speaking these days. Said it sounded like a foreign language. Brenda always thinks everything is going to the dogs. Remember when she was convinced TikTok was the downfall of civilisation? How could I forget? Still, she has a point. Language is changing so fast. Anyway, Facebook. Sarah posted pictures of her new garden. Absolutely stunning. All hydrangeas and peonies. Sarah's got green fingers, that's for sure. Maybe we should get some more flowers for the living room. Something…less aggressively scented than your rosemary, perhaps? Absolutely. Some lilies? Or maybe freesias? Something delicate. Although, they do shed petals  everywhere .

…and honestly, the heat! I’d prepared for warm, of course, but Queensland in December is another level. It just  hits  you. Not a dry heat either, terribly humid. Did either of you venture up that far? Queensland… aye, a bit. More around Brisbane, though. Business trip, years ago. Had to wear a suit, can you imagine? Linen, thankfully, but still. Felt like I was melting into the pavement. All those young lads in shorts and t-shirts looking at me like I’d landed from Mars. You're telling me! I spent a year in Perth, teaching English on a working holiday visa when I was younger. Suits are an alien concept over there, generally. Although, you do see a lot of the ‘suits’ – as in, blokes in sharply tailored things – heading into the mining offices. Very different vibe to Brisbane, Perth felt much more… western, if that makes sense. More laid back. Perth sounds lovely. I was over on the East Coast, mainly Brisbane and a bit of the Gold Coast. I was visiting my niece, she’d emigrated with her husband. She's a solicitor, very successful. They’d taken out a huge loan to buy a place, though. Said the interest rates were manageable, but still… gave me the shivers thinking about it. Back home, you wouldn’t dream of borrowing that kind of money. Bank loans, eh? Always a worry. I used to deal with those all the time, running the company. Always a balancing act. You wouldn’t believe the lengths some chaps would go to, trying to dress the part for a meeting. I remember one fellow, desperate to impress, turned up in a suit that was clearly a size too small. Looked like he’d been poured into it. All shiny polyester, too. Didn't do his cause any good, I can tell you. Oh, dear! The power of presentation, eh? It’s funny though, isn’t it, how we judge people on things like that. Speaking of presentation and judgement… you two both have fairly distinct accents. I can place you, right as rain. You’re from Manchester, aren't you? Spot on, lass. Born and bred. Still got the tang, apparently. You're from Yorkshire, I’d wager? Sheffield, actually. Though people often think Yorkshire means just…one accent. We’ve got a lot of variation, even within the county. Try to get a proper Sheffield lad going on about ‘owt, and you'll be there all day.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of it all is exhausting. I deactivated my Facebook account again last week. Just…too much. Everyone presenting this perfectly curated life. It's draining. Oh, I know what you mean, Aunt Carol. It's a performance, isn't it? Everyone's a little actor. Though, to be fair, I still use Instagram. It's visually less…demanding, I think. Plus, it’s good for keeping up with what my students are doing when they go home. Visuals are the problem, though! All those posed photos, filters…it just breeds comparison. I felt like I was constantly measuring my life against other people’s highlight reels. And the arguments! Don't even get me started on the political arguments. It’s just… unpleasant. It is. I mostly follow travel accounts and, weirdly, accounts dedicated to vintage sewing patterns. Keeps things light. Though even  those  get comments sometimes. People debating thread weights! Honestly. What have you been doing instead, then, if you’re off Facebook? Anything good? Well, I've been trying to rediscover…proper television. Remember when television  was  a thing? Before everything was streaming and algorithms? Vaguely! My parents definitely talk about “appointment television.” Waiting all week for the next episode of something. Sounds…stressful. I’m very much a binge-watcher myself. Have you seen anything good? I finished ‘Severance’ recently, that was brilliant. Really messed with my head. Oh, I’ve heard of that! Is it on Apple TV? I rather resisted getting an Apple TV for ages but eventually caved. I’ve been watching a lot of historical documentaries, actually. BBC ones, mostly. Keeps the brain ticking over. And I’ve finally got into ‘Call the Midwife’. It’s terribly moving. 'Call the Midwife' is a classic! My grandma absolutely  loves  that. I’ve tried watching it with her, but it’s a bit…slow-paced for me, I think. I need more twists and turns. Have you discovered podcasts yet? That's where I’m spending most of my audio time these days. Podcasts? I’ve dipped my toe in. My nephew, Thomas, recommended one about…ancient Roman history. It was quite good, actually. Very well presented. But there’s so much choice! It’s overwhelming, like social media all over again. What do you listen to? Everything and anything! I’m obsessed with true crime podcasts at the moment - don’t judge me!

…and honestly, the way she just  launched  herself off the side! I thought for a moment she was going to bellyflop right onto poor Mr. Henderson, the lifeguard. He’s funny! He blows his whistle  really  loud. He told me to stop splashing! He did, didn’t he? Well, splashing is fun, but maybe not  in  Mr. Henderson’s face. Are you two excited about having Pippy over tomorrow? Yes! Can we build a fort in the living room? A really, really big one? With all the cushions! And blankets! We’ll see. We might need the living room for…operation Blue Peter badge photo. Oh! The circus one! Exactly. Pippy showed me the letter. They need a photograph of you two  with  her, doing something circus themed. And she wants it quickly! Can I wear my lion mask? Perfect! That’s brilliant. We’ll need to find some sparkly things too. And maybe practice balancing on one leg, just in case. Now, Pippy also mentioned something about pocket money… She said she’s saving up to buy a unicorn! She is, isn’t she? She's a very determined little lady. So, I was thinking, a little extra pocket money this week to help her out, what do you think? It wouldn't be a huge amount, just a couple of pounds each. Can I get a pound? I want to buy dinosaur stickers. Absolutely. As long as you promise not to stick them on the cat. Max wouldn’t  like  that! Definitely not. Speaking of Pippy, did you know she’s…well, she’s a bit vague about her age. She just says she’s ‘old enough to run a circus!’ That could be one! It could be! She's certainly energetic enough. It's just… it’s hard to pin down. It makes planning things like potential trips a little tricky. Like, remember we talked about taking her to that travelling circus in Cambridge? The one with the elephants? That’s the one. We'd need to check if she needs a child ticket, or an adult ticket, depending on her actual age. And it got me thinking… have you both got your passports okay? We might want to think about a little day trip to France next summer. I have a blue one! Mine has stickers in it! Good! That’s good. It’s just always best to be prepared.

…and honestly, I just felt awful. Like, a proper idiot. I kept trying to play it cool, but inside I was panicking. He probably thought I was just…not interested, didn’t he? Oh, love, you're being hard on yourself. It happens. Honestly. It doesn't mean he thought you weren't interested, it could be anything. Stress, tiredness… you said he’d had a really long week at work, right? Aye, he had. But it was just… the timing, innit? We were getting into things and then… nothing. It just  stopped . Yorkshire bluntness ain’t exactly helpful in these situations, ya know? I just mumbled something about needing a cuppa and practically legged it to the kitchen. Right. A tactical retreat to the tea-making station. Classic. Look, it’s probably just a one-off. Men get self-conscious, too. It's not always about  you , even though our brains immediately go there. I know, I  know . But it got me thinking. Like, what if it’s…something else? You know…  down there ? I read something online, scrolling through TikTok of all places – don’t judge – about erectile dysfunction. And it suddenly just… clicked. Woah, okay. Slow down. TikTok is the  worst  place to self-diagnose. Seriously. But, alright, you're asking about ED? It’s a really common thing, actually. Particularly with stress, like you said. It doesn't mean there’s something physically wrong with him. But what if there is? It feels awful even  talking  about it. Like I’m being disrespectful, or…rude. And what if he finds out I’ve been googling it? He'll be mortified! He wouldn't be mortified that you care enough to be a bit worried. He might be a bit embarrassed if he found out you were on TikTok researching it, though! Seriously though, it's good you're thinking about it. But jumping to conclusions isn’t helpful. Have you… talked to him at all since then? Not really. Just a few awkward texts. I sent him a meme about needing more sleep, trying to be subtle. He just replied with a thumbs up. Honestly, it’s like walking on eggshells now. I don’t want to bring it up directly, I'm scared of upsetting him. I get that. Look, maybe don't mention the ‘erectile dysfunction’ thing directly, not yet. But you could just ask him if he’s been feeling okay, generally.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  how anyone manages to eat a full Healthy Extra B choice and still feel satisfied. It’s always either a ridiculously dry wholemeal roll or, like, a tiny bit of pasta. Right? It’s supposed to be the substantial bit, isn’t it? The thing that fills you up! I had a Alpen Light bar earlier. Technically HEB, but… it was basically sweetened cardboard. I'm craving actual food. Are those onions softening? Slowly. I put them on a really low heat. Don’t want them burnt. And yeah, the Alpen Lights… are a commitment, let’s put it that way. I’m thinking of just using some Quorn mince in a jacket potato tomorrow. Is that a sensible HEB? Definitely. Quorn's surprisingly good for Slimming World. Sainsbury's have the best range, I think. Tesco's is a bit… sad. Though, talking of free food, did you see they have that new free recipe on the app? The one with the syn-free chilli? Oh, I saw! I haven’t looked at the syns breakdown properly though. Is it genuinely free, or is there some sneaky hidden oil in something? Because I’m suspicious of everything now. Even mint. I read someone saying mint tea counts as a syn because of the flavourings. No way! That's ridiculous. It's a leaf! Although, you're right to be cautious. Everything seems to have a sneaky syn these days. I’m using that 0 calorie syrup in my tea, though. I have to have  something  sweet, and it's the only way I’m surviving. I'm the same. Though I do wonder what's  in  that stuff. It can’t be completely natural, can it? Everything’s artificial flavour these days. Still, beats sugar. Right, onions are nearly there. We’re making a proper effort with dinner tonight, aren’t we? Cauliflower cheese with the roast chicken. We are! It's practically a celebration. Speaking of celebration… Treat Day on Saturday. What are we thinking? I was contemplating a small portion of chips. Chips are good. I was eyeing up a little bit of Ben & Jerry’s. Just a small pot. Though Siri keeps reminding me about my calendar, and it guilt-trips me. She’s so judgmental. “You have a weigh-in on Monday, are you  sure  you want to plan a treat?”

… honestly, I just think Italy feels  safe . You know? We’ve been to France a few times, Spain’s lovely, but Italy… it just feels…right. Plus, I’ve been reading about Tuscany, and I really want to do a cooking class. Proper pasta making, not just watching someone else do it. Tuscany  is  beautiful, I’ll give you that. But safe? Darling, anywhere’s safe if you’re not actively looking for trouble. And honestly, after the absolute chaos of Brexit and everything that’s followed… politics feels like actively  seeking  trouble these days. Makes you want to just… disappear to a remote Scottish island, doesn’t it? Don't start on politics, please. I’ve had a day of dealing with Mr. Henderson’s increasingly bizarre demands and the office's ongoing printer crisis. The last thing I need is a dissection of current affairs. A remote Scottish island sounds lovely, though. Maybe  after  Italy. Or instead of. Depends how much the flights are. Always practical, aren't you? That's one of the things I love about you. Although, you  could  write about the printer crisis. Seriously. "The Siege of the HP LaserJet 4350." It’s got drama, tension, a villainous malfunctioning toner cartridge… You think so? I've been toying with getting back into writing, but I keep getting stuck. All these little story ideas, but nothing seems… substantial enough. It all feels a bit… frivolous. Frivolous is good! Don't aim for Tolstoy on your first attempt. Write about what you know. The absurdity of modern office life. The passive-aggressive notes left in the kitchen. You're brilliant at observing people, use it. Mmm, maybe. It’s just…a bit daunting, isn't it? Putting yourself out there. And then there’s the whole “what if it’s rubbish?” thing. Speaking of putting yourself out there, have you… thought any more about the tattoo? Oh, that again. I've been… contemplating. It feels a bit impulsive, doesn’t it? Middle-aged IT consultant getting a dragon on his arm. It screams mid-life crisis. It doesn't scream mid-life crisis, it screams ‘you’ve always wanted one’! You’ve been talking about it since university. And a dragon suits you. You're fiercely protective, a bit fiery when provoked… You think so? Most people just think I’m grumpy. Although, I did see a really good design online.

…and honestly, the bougainvillea was absolutely thriving. Didn’t realise they could get  that  colourful in the Algarve. Sent you a postcard, did I? I seem to remember popping it in the postbox at Lagos. Yes, lovely postcard, Arthur. Right there on the fridge, amidst the children’s dubious artwork. Very vibrant. Much needed, given this perpetual grey we’ve been enduring. Though, if I’m honest, I’m more interested in logistics right now. Doreen’s 70th is looming, and we  need  a plan. Good heavens, is it already? Time flies, doesn't it? Seventy. She’ll hate all the fuss, of course. She always has. Remember her 50th? She threatened to run off to the Lake District. I remember! And nearly succeeded. No disappearing acts this time, though. Margaret’s taken the lead on the party at the village hall, which is sensible. But we need to sort out transport. Nigel’s offered, but his car… well, it’s seen better days, hasn't it? And he drives like a Formula One driver with a limited pension. He does have a certain…enthusiasm. Perhaps I could offer? I’m perfectly happy to drive a few folk. It's not as if I have any pressing engagements. Though, the garden does need weeding…a less glamorous offer, admittedly. That would be brilliant, Arthur, absolutely brilliant. Perhaps you could do a round-trip for the Harworth contingent? Saves me having to navigate Auntie Brenda and her endless stories about garden gnomes. Harworth contingent it is, then. Sounds…colourful. Speaking of colourful, have you been following this latest polling on Scottish independence? Quite a surge for the ‘Yes’ campaign, if the reports are to be believed. Don’t get me started. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Another referendum? After all the upheaval with Brexit? It feels like we’re constantly picking at scabs. And the economic implications…I've been running some analyses at work, and frankly, it's a mess either way. I agree, a deeply divisive issue. I find myself increasingly sympathetic to the idea of stability, of leaving things as they are. Though, one can understand the desire for self-determination, of course. It’s a deeply rooted feeling in Scotland. Still, I’d hate to see the Union fractured. It impacts everything, doesn't it? And it's not just Scotland. The ripples are felt everywhere. It changes business planning, investment… everything.

…and honestly, the headmistress’ email was just… well, a bit much. "A collaborative art project to welcome our new Syrian families." Collaborative! As if a drawing is going to magically solve everything. Is it gonna help them, Mummy? Are our drawings gonna help them? It’s a nice thought, darling. It’s about showing them we're friendly and that we’re thinking of them. It won’t  solve  everything, no. It’s a small thing, but small things add up. I’m drawing a really good chair! It’s got, like, arms! And a headrest! Oh, fabulous! That sounds amazing, Leo. What kind of chair is it? A comfy one! For a king! Or… or someone who’s been travelling a long way. I’m drawing a chair too! But mine’s just… a chair. It hasn’t got arms yet. That's perfectly lovely, Lily. Remember what we talked about? These families have had to leave their homes, everything they know. They've travelled a long, long way. A comfy chair is a really nice thing to imagine them sitting in. Will they like our chairs? They probably have better chairs at their  real  house, don’t they? That's a really thoughtful question, sweetie. They probably did have wonderful homes, and lovely furniture. But right now, they’re starting over. It’s like when you move your toys around in your bedroom and make a new arrangement. It's not necessarily  better  just… different. My chair has stripes! Red and blue! Is red and blue a good colour for a chair? Red and blue are  excellent  colours for a chair, Leo. Very patriotic! Though I suspect they might appreciate any colour, just knowing you thought of them. You know, my grandma, she used to collect antique chairs. She had everything – Windsor chairs, Chippendale chairs, even one that was all woven willow. What’s a Windsor chair? Oh, it’s an old-fashioned chair, wooden with a high back. Very sturdy. She always said a good chair should feel like a hug. My chair’s not sturdy. It’s wobbly when I colour it. Well, maybe we can reinforce it with more colour! Speaking of reinforcing things, I did promise Mrs. Davies I’d help sort out the welcome packs for the families. She wants something a bit more than just leaflets about clubs and schools. Like the drawings?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of tiny clothes is terrifying. I mean, they grow out of things  so  fast, don’t they? It feels incredibly wasteful. It does. Though, you know Sarah was saying she’s joined one of those baby clothing swap groups? Apparently, it’s brilliant. People just exchange stuff as the kids grow. Saves a fortune, and less landfill. Oh, that’s a really good idea! I must ask her about it. She seems to have everything figured out, doesn’t she? Being a second-time mum probably helps. Seems so calm about everything, unlike… well, unlike me currently. I'm a nervous wreck planning the nursery. She's a pro, definitely. But you’re allowed to be nervous! It’s a massive change. And you're brilliant at planning things – remember the entire reorganisation of the kitchen? That was  military  precision. This is just…slightly more emotionally charged. Fair point. The kitchen was a logistical challenge; this is a tiny human. Speaking of Sarah, did you hear back from her about the weekend? She said she might be free to come down, but I wanted to check before I started making plans. I did, actually. She’s in! She’s really excited to see the “construction site,” as she called it. She said Mark's got a big football match on, so she’s happy for a weekend away. Excellent! That’s lovely. It'll be good to catch up properly. It feels like ages since we’ve just  talked  – not lectured, or graded, or discussed birth plans. It's all been a bit… saturated. I know. Teaching has been  mental  lately. The deadline for submissions is looming, and everyone's suddenly realised they left everything to the last minute. I spent all of yesterday afternoon basically repeating "Have you read the guidelines?" a hundred times. Oh, the joys. I had a student email me at 11 pm last night asking what plagiarism was.  Plagiarism . After a lecture dedicated to it. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if they even read the emails I send. It’s exhausting, isn’t it? You put so much effort into trying to explain things, and then… nothing. Still, there are some good ones. Remember Liam from last year? The one who wrote that incredible dissertation on post-colonial literature? Oh, Liam! Yes. He was fantastic. Such a genuinely engaged student. It's students like him that make it worthwhile.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just  mortifying . Old Mrs. Higgins genuinely believed I’d cursed her prize-winning marrow with a pointed look. A  pointed look , Ben! No way. Seriously? You've cursed a marrow? That’s… wonderfully absurd. Though, to be fair, Norfolk villagers and their marrows are serious business. I’ve heard tales. It IS serious business! Apparently, my ‘negative energy’ was radiating outwards. She actually brought me a sprig of rowan to ward off evil spirits. I had to pretend to be really grateful. It’s just… I was trying to explain the concept of fungal disease to her during the village fete. Not cast a horticultural hex! You lecturing about fungal disease at a village fete? That's peak you, actually. It's the image of a slightly exasperated academic trying to explain mycorrhizal networks to someone obsessed with oversized vegetables. Exactly! And then PC Davies just  happened  to be there, observing the whole exchange. He gave me  that  look. The one that says, “We’re watching you, professor.” Oh, Davies. He’s a character. Thinks he’s Sherlock Holmes in uniform. Probably convinced you’re running a secret marrow-sabotage ring. I wouldn’t put it past him! Honestly, sometimes I think he’s deliberately engineered situations just to have something to investigate. Remember last year with the missing garden gnomes? Oh, God, yes! He treated it like an international incident. Full forensic sweep of Mrs. Peterson’s garden. Turns out her grandson had hidden them in the greenhouse as a prank. Absolute chaos. And the local paper loved it. "University Lecturer Suspected in Gnome Heist!" The publicity was dreadful. My Head of Department wasn't amused. Well, you  do  attract attention. It’s your charm. And your… unusually detailed explanations of plant pathology. Look, speaking of university, have you finalised the module outline for the spring semester? I'm stressing about the workload already. Almost. I’m trying to incorporate more practical fieldwork. I think the students get too bogged down in the theory. Perhaps a weekend trip… somewhere like the Broads? It would be good to get them out of the lab. That’s a brilliant idea. They’d love that. Though lugging equipment around on a boat isn't my idea of a relaxing weekend. Still, better than marking endless essays on the socio-political implications of potato blight. You and your potato blight.

…and honestly, Dad, trying to explain to Grandma how to video call is  exhausting . She keeps holding the phone further and further away, convinced that makes her face bigger! It's like talking to a brick wall sometimes. Oh, she’s a character, your Grandma. Always has been. Used to tell me off for looking at the television too much. Irony, considering she’s got ‘Coronation Street’ on repeat all day now. Still, bless her. It's just… things move so fast, innit? When I were a lad, a telephone was something bolted to the wall, with a rotary dial. Now everyone’s got these little computers in their pockets. Exactly! And she thinks someone is  in  the phone listening. It's a conspiracy, apparently. Speaking of pockets, have you sorted out getting a van for moving some of your stuff into the new place yet? No, not yet. Been meaning to. Thought I’d give that Steve down at the hire place a ring tomorrow. He’s a good lad, Steve. Knows his stuff. Though, they're pricey, vans. Absolutely eye watering these days. Reminds me of the price of fishing permits! Used to be a quid, now… forget about it. Tell me about it. Everything’s going up. Maybe if you won the lottery...though your luck with those numbers is notoriously bad. Don't I know it! More chance of catching a marlin in the Thames. Still, a man can dream. Anyway, the new place… it's a bit smaller, but it'll do. Less garden, mind you. Won’t have room for all my… treasures. Treasures? You mean the piles of antiques you’ve been accumulating for decades? Honestly, Dad, you need to have a clear out. You’re becoming a hoarder! Now, hold on a minute! They're not just ‘piles’, they're historical artifacts! A potential fortune, waiting to be discovered! That old radio, for instance, a Bush V820… they're going for a pretty penny online. Right. And the chipped tea set? Or the collection of rusty tools? They’ve got character! Look, the point is, getting everything moved is a pain. And I was hoping young Liam – you know, Sarah's son? – might be able to help. He’s always on those computer games, needs to get some fresh air. A bit of lifting might do him good. Liam? He’d probably complain the whole time and then ask for a reward in V-Bucks.

… honestly, the audacity of it! They’re talking about demolishing the library. The  library , David! It’s been there since, well, since forever. I saw the notice. Dreadful, isn't it? All that talk of ‘regeneration’ and ‘modernisation’. It always means knocking something lovely down and putting up another glass box. Exactly! And they’re saying it’s underused. Underused because they’ve let it slowly fall into disrepair! Less funding, shorter opening hours…it’s a self-fulfilling prophecy. Honestly, the council. It’s the same story everywhere, isn’t it? They want everything to look…new. Sterile. They don't appreciate the character of these old buildings. Remember Old Man Hemmings used to say the library was built on the site of the old apothecary? All that local history…gone. He did! And he knew everything about everyone. Good old Mr. Hemmings. We really need to do something. Sign a petition, write to the local paper…something. Already on it. There’s a Facebook group forming. Quite a lively discussion, surprisingly. Though half of it’s people arguing about parking. Naturally. Of course. Parking always trumps everything. Speaking of things needing attention, have you had a chance to look at those fabric samples I ordered for the new chairs? They arrived this morning. Just a quick glance, actually. They’re… colourful. Very colourful. Colourful is good! I was thinking something to brighten the living room up. It's all a bit beige at the moment, isn’t it? I was leaning towards the teal one, the one with the subtle floral pattern. Teal's nice. A bit bold, though, isn't it? Maybe a little too much for the room? What about that muted grey one? It would tie in with the sofa. Muted grey? David, that’s just…sad. It’s practically admitting defeat. I want something with a bit of life. We spend so much time in here, it needs to be a cheerful space. Alright, alright, cheerful. Just trying to offer a practical opinion. You know how I am. Although, before we finalise anything, have you priced up re-upholstering versus just buying new? I did. Re-upholstering is actually surprisingly affordable. And it feels…better, somehow. More sustainable. Plus, the frames are solid. It’d be a shame to waste good furniture. Like the library, actually. There you go again! Everything comes back to the library.

… honestly, I still can’t believe she got me that miniature railway set. A miniature railway! At my age! It’s… ambitious, isn’t it? Ambitious is one word for it, Dad. You’ve been hinting about wanting a shed for, like, five years. A shed! She went straight for the full-blown hobby. Bless her. It’s sweet, though. Shows she listens when you ramble on about steam engines and landscape architecture. Though, where  are  you planning to put it? That's the question, isn’t it? The garden’s not exactly expansive. And your mother is already giving me ‘the look’ about taking up yet more space. She says I’m turning the back garden into a ‘man cave’. She’s not wrong, is she? You’ve got your workshop, the barbeque area… it’s a dedicated zone back there. But a railway? That’s a new level. Though, I must admit, sounds fun. Always fancied a good model railway. See, Dad? Even Uncle David thinks so! It’s a valid hobby. You can get really into the detail. There are entire communities online about this stuff. I've had a peek, actually. It's…surprisingly intense. There’s ballasting, weathering, point motors… it’s a whole language! I need a course! Perhaps even a dedicated room… Woah, hold on. Dedicated  room ? Your wife will stage an intervention. Let’s start with the garden, shall we? What about that little patch near the flowerbeds? No, no, that’s prime rose real estate. Your mother would never allow it. Besides, it needs to be level. And close to a power source. It’s surprisingly complicated. Speaking of complicated, anyone see that new detective show on BBC One?  Silent Witness  is getting a bit predictable, but this one… really drew me in. Proper twists and turns. Oh, yeah! The one with the locked room mystery? I liked that. Bit dark, though. I prefer something fluffier, like  Bake Off . Although, Prue Leith is getting a bit… harsh, don't you think? Harsh is her brand. She’s the antithesis of Mary Berry’s gentle encouragement. I'm currently obsessed with that Korean drama everyone's talking about. It’s subtitled, so I have to  really  pay attention, but it’s brilliant. Korean dramas? Really? That's a bit of a leap from  Last of the Summer Wine , isn't it? It’s good to broaden your horizons, Dad.

…and honestly, lad, the price they’re asking for it is daylight robbery. Three thousand for a ten-year-old Fiesta? They’re having a laugh, aren't they? It’s got a bit of rust around the wheel arches, you know. Perfectly serviceable, mind, but not  three thousand  serviceable. Yeah, but Dad, everyone wants a Fiesta. They’re proper reliable. And if I pass my test, I  need  a car. Ms. Harrison said getting to sixth form college will be a nightmare on the bus, especially in winter. Aye, well, reliable doesn’t mean immune to rust, does it? And a bus is a perfectly good mode of transport. Builds character! Though I do understand the appeal of having your own wheels. It's just…the insurance. That’s what’s giving me palpitations. That’s what I was going to ask about. How much do you reckon it'll be? I got a quote online, but it was… scary. Like, four thousand scary. Four thousand?! Lad, they're taking the mick with young drivers. They assume you’ll all wrap ‘em around lamp posts the minute you get a license. It’s based on statistics, apparently. But it doesn’t mean it’s  fair . We need to shop around, properly. And there are things we can do to bring it down. Like what? I thought it was just age and where you live that mattered. Well, those are big factors, aye. Being a young male driver in North Yorkshire isn't exactly a recipe for cheap insurance. But there's more. We can add me as a named driver, that will help. A lot, actually. And we could consider a higher excess. What’s an excess? Right, good question. The excess is the amount  you  pay towards any claim. So, if you had a bump and the repairs were, say, eight hundred quid, with a two hundred pound excess, the insurance would pay six hundred. But you'd have to stump up the two hundred yourself. Higher excess usually means a lower premium…but it’s a risk. You need to be sure you can afford it if something  does  happen. Oh, I see. So, cheaper insurance, but more money out if I crash. Makes sense. Still…two hundred’s a lot. It is. We can play around with it. Another thing is the car itself. A Fiesta’s in insurance group B, which isn't bad, but some cars are lower.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the servers being down again? Jaysus, it's relentless. Another all-nighter patching things up. I swear, if I have to look at another line of code for network security, I’ll… well, I won’t say what I’ll do. Sounds rough, Dad. Is it, like,  really  stressful? You always say it’s busy, but this sounds… different. It is, Leo. It's different. It's wearing me down. I’ve been trying to figure out how to even  measure  how stressed I am, you know? There are those apps, aren’t there? Heart rate variability and all that? Feel like a right eejit strapping myself up with sensors just to figure out I’m knackered. Oh, Kevin. You and your tech solutions for… tech-induced problems. Honestly, just talking about it, venting, is often the best thing. Though, maybe  not  to Leo while he's trying to eat his dinner. Ah, now, he's old enough to hear a bit of the real world, isn't he? Besides, it’s good to model healthy coping mechanisms. Like complaining strategically. So, what about that vote back in… when was it, 2015? About the marriage stuff? Was  that  stressful for you, Mum? Seeing everyone get so worked up over… people loving each other? It was… intense. Not stressful in the same way work is for your dad, Kevin, but emotionally draining. There was so much vitriol. I remember being genuinely worried about what it would mean for friends. And the relief when it passed… it was palpable. It felt like a truly good thing for Ireland. A proper step forward. Absolutely. A long time coming. Though, I’ll tell you what  was  awkward. My auntie Bridie. She kept sending me emails with Bible verses. Awkward doesn't even begin to cover it. Bible verses? Seriously? Seriously. And I’d reply with links to the economic benefits of tourism due to increased inclusivity. She didn’t appreciate that.    So, Kevin… are you worried about being… recorded? You’ve been glancing at the phone a couple of times. What are you on about? You’ve got that look. The one you get when you suspect someone's eavesdropping. You were talking about work, and then looked at the phone like  it  was listening. Just thinking about podcasts, actually. There's a good one about cybersecurity I’ve been meaning to listen to.

…and honestly, Dad, I still think you’re mental for wanting to drive all the way to Whitby. It’s practically Scotland! Couldn't we have flown? It'd be quicker, less stressful. Now, El, where's your sense of adventure? Flying is… soulless. You don't  see  anything. This way, we get to potter, stop at those little hilltop villages, maybe find a decent pub lunch. Besides, your Mum gets car sick on planes. It’s not  just  car sick, love. It’s the feeling of being utterly helpless, stuck in a metal tube. Give me four wheels and a nice view any day. Though, honestly, this M6 is testing my resolve. Look at that weather brewing over there. Is it gonna rain, Gran? I brought my football, but I don’t wanna get soaked. Could do, Liam. Looks a bit grey. Best be prepared. Your Dad always says, “There’s no such thing as bad weather, only unsuitable clothing.” Although, even  he  admits some weather’s just plain miserable. Wise words, even if I do say so myself. Speaking of preparation, El, are you still stressing about starting that Law Conversion Course? Seems a world away from Shakespeare. Trying not to. It’s just… a massive change, isn’t it? All those rules and regulations. All those… people. It’s not exactly like dissecting poetry. What’s a Law Conversion Course? Is it like learning to be a police officer? Not quite, love. It’s for people who have a degree in something else - like El has with English - who want to become lawyers. It teaches them all the legal stuff they didn’t cover in their first degree. Exactly. And it's all about weighing things up, isn't it? Like, kilograms versus miles. It’s all relative. I still think in stones and miles, honestly. Feels more… natural. A stubborn remnant of the pre-metric system, my dear. Though I confess, even I occasionally fumble with the conversions. It's a habit, ingrained over decades. Reminds me of the Brexit debate, actually. People clinging to what they knew, regardless of whether it was objectively better. Oh, don’t start on that again, Arthur. We've had enough Brexit talk to last a lifetime. Remember Old Man Hemmings down the street? Reckoned the EU was the work of the devil. The devil? Gran, is the devil real?

…and honestly, the texture was  almost  right. It just needed a bit more… something. Maybe paprika? You know, a smoky thing. You're still on about the ‘shmeat’ Bolognese? Honestly, Liv, you've been tinkering with that recipe for weeks. Just admit defeat and have a lentil bake. It's less… existential angst inducing. It  was  pretty good, Liv. A little bland, yeah, but definitely better than anything else I’ve tried mimicking meat with. And less depressing than thinking about where actual meat comes from. Depressing is the point, Euan! It’s about acknowledging the… the moral complexity of the whole thing! I mean, I’m trying to eat ethically, right? And ethically sourced meat is expensive and, let's face it, still involves… well, you know. This is  grown  in a lab! No suffering! But is it ethically sound to create life purely to… dismantle it for consumption? It feels… Frankenstein-y. I get the animal cruelty aspect, genuinely, but this feels like a different type of weird. It's not  life , though, is it? It’s cells. Like growing skin grafts. It’s already done in medicine. And honestly, the environmental impact of animal agriculture is insane. We're talking deforestation, methane emissions... Honestly, I'd happily eat lab-grown beef if it meant saving the Amazon. Exactly! And it’s not just the environment. Think about the conditions in those abattoirs. It's barbaric! My aunt Carol used to work near one, told me stories… absolutely horrifying. It's so much cleaner, and less… violent, to cultivate it. Okay, okay, you’ve made your point. But it still feels… manufactured. Like everything’s being sanitised. Remember that hunting trip your uncle took you on when you were little, Liv? Oh god, don’t remind me. That was awful! I was ten. He made me help pluck the pheasant. I vowed vegetarianism then and there, briefly. Plucking a pheasant  is  arguably more 'ethical' than a factory farm. At least the animal had a life roaming around. It's brutal, obviously, but it's... honest. It's the circle of life and all that nonsense. See, Euan, you're getting it! It's all horrific, regardless. But there’s something fundamentally unsettling about creating meat in a petri dish. It feels like a step too far. It's like something Larry David would complain endlessly about on  Curb Your Enthusiasm .

…and honestly, the delivery driver just  launched  it over the garden fence. A garden fence, Liam! It landed right next to Mrs. Henderson’s prize-winning roses. Sounds about right. Amazon’s getting worse, isn’t it? They’ll fling a fridge over if they think it’ll save them thirty seconds. Did you at least get your new headset? That’s all that matters, right? Yeah, thankfully. It's brilliant, proper surround sound. Ready for the new Call of Duty. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think a physical copy might be safer than risking another 'fence launch' from Royal Mail or whoever they’re using these days. You two are obsessed with that game. Honestly. It's just shooting people, isn't it? Though, I have to admit, the graphics  are  amazing. What are you watching anyway? Just some rubbish sci-fi flick, Amy picked it out. Something about space pirates. It’s… okay. Distracting from the impending doom of Christmas shopping, mostly. Christmas! Don’t even  mention  it. Mum's already started asking what I want. Like I’ve got money growing on trees. It's always “what can  you  do for  us ” isn’t it? Lay off, mate. She just wants to make it nice. And besides, you could always get a job. Just sayin’. Easy for you to say, Mr. ‘Going to Uni’. It’s not like there’s anything around here. Unless you fancy working at the Sellafield canteen, which, trust me, is as grim as it sounds.
