Honestly, Liam, you’ve been saying that for years. You used to be brilliant at building computers, remember? You could do that from home, freelance or something. Yeah, well, that was  years  ago. I’m rusty. And needing a new graphics card costs more than my rent. Plus, explaining to Mum I'm “working” when I'm sat in my pyjamas all day… that's a conversation I’d rather avoid. You could tell her you're a digital nomad. It sounds impressive. Like you’re travelling the world whilst making millions. You think she'd fall for that? She barely understands how to use her mobile phone. Speaking of which, she tried to video call me the other day… from the camera app. It was a blurry picture of her nose for five minutes. Oh, bless her! She's a technophobe. Remember when she thought the internet was a series of tubes?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of olives was  alarming . Like, mountains of them. Different kinds too - green, black, stuffed with peppers… It was a beautiful little taverna, right on the harbour in Rhodes, but I genuinely thought I’d be living on olives for a week. Oh, God, that sounds…intense. Rhodes, huh? You actually went! I was half expecting you to chicken out after all that dithering about potential sunburn. Don’t remind me! I went through approximately five different factor 50s before settling on one. But it was worth it. Honestly, the sun, the sea… even the olives. It was a proper escape. What about you? Still planning that trip to Italy? You mentioned Venice, didn’t you? Venice is on hold, sadly. Work has just been… a bit mad. Alumni Day Four is proving to be a beast. Trying to wrangle all these graduates and remember who donated what to the Faculty library is exhausting. Plus, Professor Davies decided  this  year we need individual thank you notes for everyone over £500. Oh,  no . Davies and his… details. That man is a machine. Is that why you look so frazzled? You usually thrive on this sort of organised chaos. I usually do, yes, but this is beyond. And Mum keeps phoning about Dad's knee, which, apparently, is now “acting up” again. Honestly, I think he just enjoys the sympathy. Oh, bless him. He's a drama king, your dad. Remember when he convinced everyone he'd pulled a muscle reaching for the biscuit tin? Don’t even! Gran genuinely had the ambulance on speed dial. It’s exhausting, but you know, that's just Dad. How were your parents about you jetting off to Greece? Mine were all sensible warnings about pickpockets and dodgy gyros. Pretty chilled, actually. Mum was thrilled I was going somewhere sunny. She kept sending me sunscreen recommendations, which was sweet. Dad just wanted to know if they had good beer. Apparently, that’s the metric for a successful holiday in his book. Sounds about right. My brother, Ben, has just landed a job in Berlin, which is exciting. He's always wanted to live abroad. He was working at that awful call centre after graduating, so this is a massive step up. No way! Berlin? That’s brilliant! Doing what? I thought he was on the fence about IT versus something… creative?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of Dr. Ainsworth to assign another reading list that's thicker than War and Peace! I swear, he just enjoys watching us suffer. It’s not even essential reading, it’s ‘further exploration’! Further exploration of my rapidly diminishing sanity, more like. Calm down, love. You'll give yourself wrinkles. It's just uni. And Ainsworth  is  a bit of a…taskmaster. Remember that time he spent twenty minutes debating the semiotics of a biscuit tin in a lecture? Don’t even  start  me on the biscuit tin! That was a low point. But seriously, I'm drowning. I had a library session booked solid today, then a seminar, then tried to fit in some revision... and barely managed to eat a pot noodle for tea. Right. Sounds rough. You need to factor in self-care, El. You’re burning the candle at both ends. Did you manage to book that massage I mentioned? Oh, actually… yeah! I did. Saturday afternoon. I was thinking full body, because frankly, everything aches. My neck is permanently stuck at a forty-five-degree angle from hunching over textbooks. Good lass. You deserve it. You put so much pressure on yourself. Postgrad life isn’t  that  different to sixth form, is it? Just…more reading. And slightly more sophisticated complaining. Easier said than done! Sixth form was practically a holiday camp compared to this. At least Mrs. Davies didn't quiz us on post-structuralist theory while wielding a digestive biscuit. And it’s not just the work, it’s the lectures. Some of them are just…monotonous. This one bloke, Professor Eldridge, he genuinely sounds like he’s reading a shopping list. Eldridge? He’s actually alright. A bit dry, yeah, but he knows his stuff. I had him for the history of economic thought. Turns out the history of economic thought is…remarkably dull when spoken in a monotone. See! You agree! It’s a talent, honestly. He can suck the joy out of literally anything. I keep finding myself drifting off, then panicking I’ve missed something vital about the Austro-Hungarian empire. You probably haven’t. He repeats himself. A lot. Look, what is it you're really struggling with? Is it the academic stuff or just…feeling overwhelmed? I think…a bit of both. It’s just, everyone else seems to be coping so well.

… honestly, I still think a roast is the only proper Sunday lunch. Though, I suppose I  did  enjoy that paella you made last month, Sarah. Still, a good Yorkshire pudding… nothing beats it. Dad, you say that  every  Sunday. And you ate three helpings of the paella, don't pretend otherwise! Besides, Yorkshire puddings are a nightmare to get right. They either go rock solid or collapse like soufflés. It’s just not worth the stress. He's a traditionalist, love. You know that. Though, I agree, a flat Yorkshire is a tragedy. How are your students doing, Sarah? Any particularly… colourful characters this week? Oh, you know. The usual. Little Leo tried to convince everyone dinosaurs still exist and that he'd seen one in his garden. Bless him. Progress is slow with the Year 6 SATs looming. It's just constant pressure. Pressure, eh? Different pressure to what I faced, of course. Back in my day… Still, working’s working. At least you have something  to  do. Now, don’t start that again, Arthur. You’ve plenty to keep you occupied. The garden looks lovely, and you’ve been reading a surprising amount lately. Reading about the world falling apart, more like. Did you see the news this morning? That situation in Calais is just… appalling. More boats, more people desperate. It’s a mess. It is awful. It makes you feel so helpless, doesn't it? I was reading an article about the conditions in those camps. Truly heartbreaking. And the political rhetoric just fuels everything. It’s a complex issue, isn’t it? No easy answers. People are risking their lives, and for what? A chance at something better. We should be offering help, not building walls. Well, someone has to put a stop to it. It can’t just go on and on. Open borders, it'll be the end of everything. It’s not sustainable. Dad, that’s a bit extreme, isn't it? No one's talking about open borders. It’s about compassion, and finding humane solutions. Besides, look at our own history. This country was built on immigration. Let’s not get into a political debate over lunch, shall we? It'll spoil the lemon drizzle. Speaking of which, Sarah, did you manage to get a delivery slot for those meringues you wanted to make for Mum’s birthday next week? I tried!

…and honestly, the tiling is just  awful . Absolutely awful. I mean, I knew Derek wasn’t a master craftsman, but I didn’t realise ‘enthusiastic amateur’ was his peak. Derek, eh? Still at it then, is he? Always offering his services, that one. You know, bless him, he tries. But I always say, leave it to the professionals. Especially with tiling. It’s a dark art, that is. A dark art is putting it mildly! It’s wonky, the grout’s inconsistent, and I’m fairly certain he used the wrong adhesive in places. It’s the downstairs loo, thankfully, not the main bathroom. Though, frankly, after this, I’m considering just boarding up the main bathroom and pretending it doesn't exist. Oh, don’t say that! Bathrooms are a necessary evil, aren’t they? Though I’ll grant you, renovating them is… an experience. Remember old Mrs. Davies? She completely gutted hers, went for a Jacuzzi and everything. Then the floorboards gave way. Apparently, the plumber hadn’t accounted for the weight. Oh, I remember! The entire village knew about Mrs. Davies’ damp patch. She was furious. I’m starting to feel a bit like that now, waiting for the next disaster with Derek's handiwork. I’m thinking of getting a proper tiler in to fix it, but they're all booked solid for months. And ridiculously expensive. They are. It’s the same with kitchen fitters. Apparently, everyone decided 2024 was the year for a new kitchen. I was talking to Gareth the other day, he’s been waiting six months for someone to start his. Six months! He’s living on takeaways and a camping stove. Six months! Good grief. I’m only doing the downstairs loo, and it’s already a pain. I was hoping to get it done before my daughter comes home from Australia. She's been promising a visit for ages. Doesn’t she realise her mother and I are perpetually locked in a home improvement nightmare? Daughters rarely do, do they? Mine lives in Bristol, and she’s constantly telling me I need to “modernise.” She saw a picture of my wallpaper last week – floral, mind you, a lovely Morris design – and nearly choked. Said it looked like “something out of Downton Abbey.” Oh, they’re brutal. Mine's obsessed with Scandinavian minimalism. All greys and clean lines. It's lovely, I suppose, but it feels… cold.

…and I’m tellin’ ya, the man looked  mortified . Absolutely mortified. Like I’d offered him a pint of Guinness mixed with battery acid. "No, thank you, Mr. O’Connell," he says, all stiff, "I wouldn’t dream of it." What were you offering him? I offered him a wee sip of my homemade elderflower cordial! He thought it was… potent. I may have used a generous hand with the vodka this year. Generous is an understatement, Liam. You could strip paint with that stuff. Honestly, you and your foraging. More curry! Hold on, Finn. Let your food go down, love. You’ll choke. Liam, seriously, you need to label it next time. "Warning: May induce temporary superpowers and questionable decisions." Ah, it’s good craic, isn’t it? Though, thinking about superpowers… young Master Finn here tried to eat a bottle cap earlier. Thought he could bend it with his mind. No way! Really? Shiny! Shiny and thankfully unsuccessful. A bit of a fright, to be honest. I had to fish it out before he swallowed. He didn't even seem to  feel  it, the little rascal. Just kept grinning. That’s… weird. I stubbed my toe earlier and nearly cried. Boys will be boys. Finn’s probably developing his iron stomach. Remember when your cousin Eamon ate that toy car when he was little? Don’t remind me. The doctor nearly had a fit. Right, anyone fancy another bit of this curry? It’s a vindaloo, so be warned. Yeah, I’m good. This is spicy! So, Mum, about Tom’s birthday… are we still going with the park thing? The one with the history re-enactors? That’s the plan, darling. Unless you've changed your mind? Apparently they're doing a Viking village this year. Nah, no. Vikings are cool. But… Mr. Henderson says they're really gruesome. He's reading this  Horrible Histories  science book and he said the Vikings did, like, really bad stuff to people. Mr. Henderson sounds like a cheerful chap. They were a bit rough around the edges, alright. But it’s history, lad. You can’t sanitise it. He’s trying to be sensitive. He’s a good kid. Liam, you haven’t forgotten to sort the cake, have you? Sorted! Chocolate fudge, his favourite. Picked it up from Mrs. Doyle this morning. She does a mean sponge. Speaking of organising things, I need to drop off the night deposit at the bank tomorrow.

…and honestly, the amount of plastic tat they give away these days! Used to be an apple, maybe a toffee. Now it’s light-up skeletons and things that’ll end up in landfill before Bonfire Night. Still, little Maisie seemed to enjoy herself, didn't she, Doreen? Oh, tremendously! She was a very convincing little witch, all bundled up. Though I did have to wrestle a plastic spider off the cat. Honestly, Winston nearly had a heart attack. He's getting on, you know. Sensitive. Sounds like a typical Halloween! Though, to be fair, the kids are expecting a bit more spectacle these days. My class went all out with decorations. One little boy even built a miniature haunted house out of cardboard boxes. Impressive, actually. It  was  good, Mr. Davies. Liam’s one was really scary, with fake blood everywhere. Mum nearly fainted! Fake blood, eh? Back in my day, it was beetroot juice. Much healthier, wouldn’t you say? Though it did stain somethin’ awful. Remember that time I decorated the shed with it, Ethel? You weren’t pleased. Oh, don't  start  on that shed, Arthur! It took me a week to get the beetroot out of the paintwork. A week! And the smell… honestly. Sounds… colourful. Maisie, how was school today, apart from the Halloween fun? Any particularly interesting lessons? It was okay. We started a new topic in History, about the Romans. It’s quite cool, but there's loads of dates to remember. And Miss Peterson said we have a test next week. Romans, eh? They built some good roads, the Romans. That’s what I remember learnin’ about ‘em. Though they probably didn't have much use for a road to Costessey, did they? Not much to see there, even then. Arthur! Be nice. Maisie loves Costessey. Besides, the countryside is lovely. Did you manage to get out riding this week, dear? You were saying your back was playing up. Oh, it's a bit better, thank you, Doreen. Had a gentle potter around the fields with Old Bess. Lovely day for it, crisp sunshine. Just lovely. Though my joints still complain afterwards. She’s a good old girl, Bess, but she’s not gettin’ any younger either. I helped Amy with her pony on Saturday. She was being really stubborn and kept stopping. It’s hard work making them do what you want sometimes!

… honestly, it’s barely moved in the last twenty minutes. I thought leaving at eight would’ve avoided the worst of it, but look at this! A complete standstill. Is this always this bad getting to the Steam Fair, Grandad? Worse, usually. People come from all over, love. All over. Used to be, you could get here relatively easy. Not anymore. Used to be fields all the way, now it's houses, houses, houses. That's the problem, innit? Too many people. He's right, it's the building. Every bit of green space gets slapped with a housing estate. Remember old Mrs. Henderson’s field, just past Blandford? Beautiful it was. Now it’s “Meadow View Estates,” all identikit houses. It’s just… where are all these people  coming  from? I mean, Gillingham's bad enough, but even out here? It’s ridiculous. And then they wonder why the roads are jammed. They build ‘em, they come. Simple as that. Council needs somewhere to put ‘em, don’t they? Though half of ‘em shouldn’t  be  built, if you ask me. Shoeboxes, most of them. And all crammed together. No room to breathe. And think about the older people, George. Where are  they  meant to go? My Nan’s talking about needing to downsize, but there’s nothing suitable. Everything’s either ridiculously expensive or a tiny flat with no garden. She needs somewhere she can potter, you know? Exactly! And the waiting list for council housing must be years long. Mum, you deal with this stuff at work, isn’t it? What’s the situation like? Awful, Lila. Truly awful. People waiting years, proper years. And the stuff that  is  available…well, let's just say it's not exactly luxurious. We had Mr. Davies last week, eighty-seven years old, needing supported housing. He ended up in a place that was damp and the heating barely worked. I reported it, of course, but… it takes time. Time he doesn’t have, really. When I were a lad, the Council built proper houses. Big gardens, solid build. Now? It's all about getting as many units as possible onto a plot of land. Profit margins, that's all it is. Don't care about the people living in ‘em. It’s the same with parking too, isn’t it? Even just getting a space  here  at the Steam Fair will be a nightmare.

…and honestly, the slugs were  brutal  last year. Absolutely decimated the hostas. I’m thinking this year, a proper barrier. Copper tape, maybe? Though that gets expensive quickly, doesn't it? It does. Copper tape is good for a small patch, but for a whole allotment plot? You'd need a second mortgage! Have you considered beer traps? It’s a bit gruesome, admittedly, but surprisingly effective. Beer traps! Oh, that's a good shout. A bit messy, though, isn’t it? Imagine having to empty those every day… plus, the smell… are we attracting more than just slugs with beer? Probably! But hey, a slightly tipsy garden gnome isn’t the worst thing. Seriously, though, you don’t have to empty them  every  day. Every other day is usually sufficient, and you can bury them so the smell is less noticeable. We used them at my Nan’s allotment for years. She swore by them. Your Nan was a gardening legend, wasn’t she? Remember those tomatoes? Huge, perfect, unbelievably red tomatoes. I’ve never managed anything like that. This allotment is a whole different ball game to my little balcony garden. A lot more responsibility. It is, isn’t it? But incredibly rewarding. And you have a good head start, knowing what  not  to do, after last year's hosta massacre. So, allotment plot number 12, right? Have you had a chance to properly survey it? See what the soil’s like? I’ve walked over it a couple of times. It’s fairly level, which is good. But it’s  weedy . Seriously, knee-high weeds in places. And the soil… feels heavy. Clay-ish, I think. I did a little squeeze test – it clumped together like playdough. Oh, clay. That’s a challenge, but not insurmountable. Lots of compost is your friend. And green manure over winter. Have you thought about what you want to grow? Beyond the anti-slug warfare, that is. I’ve got a massive list. It’s probably wildly ambitious. Everything from potatoes and runner beans to trying to grow some unusual salad leaves. I want to grow cut flowers too, a little patch for the house. Thinking sunflowers, definitely. And maybe some lavender. That sounds lovely! Sunflowers are always a winner. Lavender will attract the bees, which is brilliant. Have you considered companion planting? It can really help deter pests and improve yields.

…and honestly, I still can’t believe she said that to Liam. Right in front of everyone at the pub! Like, what was she  thinking ? It just weren't called for, not at all. Oof, sounds brutal. Liam takes things to heart, doesn't he? Poor lad. What exactly did she say? You've been leaving me hanging all afternoon! We only just got to the coffee shop. Oh, it was awful. He was talking about his photography exhibition, right? All excited, been working on it for months. And she just… said it looked ‘a bit amateurish’ and asked if he’d considered taking a class. Just  blunt . No way! That’s… remarkably insensitive. Honestly, Zara can be so tactless sometimes. I mean, she's lovely, really, but she just… says what she thinks, consequences be damned. It's a Cambridge thing, I reckon. We're all a bit too direct. A Cambridge thing? What’s that supposed to mean? We’re perfectly polite up north, thank you very much! We just don’t need to dress it up in fancy words. It’s straight to the point, like. No, no, I didn’t mean polite! I just mean… less worried about appearances, maybe? More likely to just  tell  you what they think. It’s a generalisation, obviously. But still. Anyway, poor Liam. Did he say anything back? He just went quiet. Proper stony-faced. It was even more embarrassing watching him  not  react, if you get me? Then he made an excuse and went to the loo and didn’t come back for ages. I ended up having to drag him out. Blimey. Okay, that's rough. Maybe you should talk to Zara? Gently, of course. You’re better at that sort of thing than I am. I tend to just… escalate. I thought about it, but then I thought, nah. She needs to learn herself. She does this sort of thing all the time. It's like she thinks being honest means being deliberately hurtful. Anyway, enough about Zara's questionable social skills. What about  you ? How's everything with Ben going? You seemed a bit down last week. It’s… complicated. Actually, that’s why I was a bit late. I had a bit of a… confrontation with him this morning. Oh, no. What happened? Spill the beans. Don't tell me he’s been talking to Chloe again?

Right, right, gotta flank…Nah, got totally tunnel vision there. Absolute state of me. You were too busy moaning about your internet lag to notice the sniper, Liam. Honestly. You sound like my granddad complaining about the wireless. It  is  laggy! Seriously, it’s been buffering all night. It's ruining my K/D ratio. It's a travesty, I tell ya! A Yorkshire travesty. Can we maybe keep the volume down a bit? Trying to get some reading done here. And honestly, K/D ratio? You all take this way too seriously. It’s just a game. He’s just upset ‘cause he keeps getting owned, mate. Don’t worry, Liam, we’ve all been there. Remember last week when you tried to rush a whole squad with just a pistol? Legendary. Don't remind me! That was a moment of pure madness. I thought I was Rambo. Turns out, I was more…a very easily dispatched lamb. Anyway, anyone seen the new trailer for ‘Nexus Dawn’ yet? Looks absolutely mental. Oh yeah! The one with the cyborg squirrels? It looks properly over the top. I’m cautiously optimistic. The last one was a massive letdown. All hype and no substance. Cyborg squirrels? Seriously? Is that even a thing? I thought I'd escaped this level of…intensity when I left high school. It was all Fortnite and TikTok dances back then. It's a  metaphor , Mateo! For advanced robotics and… never mind. It's got spaceships and lasers and exploding stuff. What more do you want? I’m more excited about the new season of ‘The Crown’. Apparently, Princess Di is getting a proper spotlight. Proper juicy stuff, I’ve heard. Ooh, yeah, I read something about that. I’m a sucker for historical dramas. Although, sometimes I wonder how accurate they actually are. They probably exaggerate everything for effect. They  always  do. Remember 'The Tudors'? Henry VIII was practically a Greek god. He was probably just a bloke with bad teeth and a dodgy temper. Speaking of dodgy, have either of you managed to sort out your accommodation for next year? I'm still stuck in this tiny room, and the guy next door practices the tuba at 6 am. Oh, the tuba player. Poor you! I applied for a flat with Sarah and Emily. Fingers crossed we get it. It’s near the library, which would be ideal.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  what Patricia was wearing to Brenda’s birthday. Honestly! A jumpsuit. A bright orange jumpsuit! At our age! It just…doesn’t suit, does it? She said it was ‘fashion forward’. Fashion forward to a garden party! Gran, you’re terrible. But I can picture it. Patricia does have a… unique sense of style. Was Brenda alright with it? Brenda just smiled politely, bless her. She’s too nice to say anything. But I saw Margaret rolling her eyes! Honestly, the things people wear these days. It's not like when we were growing up, is it? Everything was much more…considered. Definitely different. Everything's faster now, Gran. Trends change every five minutes thanks to TikTok. You see something on there and it’s instantly ‘in’. It's a lot. TikTok? Goodness me. Sounds exhausting. I stick to my telly, thank you very much. Speaking of which, have you seen that new film,  Everything Everywhere All at Once ? Your cousin, Liam, was raving about it. Something to do with universes and bagels… sound a bit bonkers if you ask me. Oh, yeah! I watched it last week. It  is  bonkers, Gran, totally bonkers. But really good bonkers. It's hard to explain, it’s… about a Chinese-American woman who has to connect with versions of herself from other universes to save the world. And the bagel is…well, it's a metaphor. A metaphor? For what, pray tell? Honestly, I’m not entirely sure! Something about existential dread and finding meaning in the chaos. It's one of those films you just  feel  rather than understand, you know? Sounds a bit heavy for a Tuesday evening. I prefer something a bit lighter. Something like… oh, what was that one with George Clooney?  Ticket to Paradise ? That was nice. Escape to the sunshine. That’s a bit cliché, isn't it, Gran? Clooney and Roberts bickering in Bali? Predictable. Although, to be fair, it  is  pretty relaxing. You need something easy sometimes. Work's been chaotic. Chaotic how? Still with that production company? Are they treating you alright? You’re a clever girl, you shouldn't let them walk all over you. They're alright. It’s just… a big project launched and everything went a bit sideways. Supply chain issues, delays with the set design… you name it. I’m basically fire-fighting all day.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of him to suggest Scrabble was a ‘team building exercise’ when he clearly just wanted to win! It was brutal. He challenged every single word, even ‘cat’. A  cat , Jess! Oh, Rhys is hopeless. Competitive to a fault. You know he secretly practices, don't you? He probably has a Scrabble dictionary hidden somewhere. I wouldn’t put it past him. It completely derailed our evening. We were supposed to be relaxing, you know? Prepping for my interview tomorrow. Honestly, the stress of that is enough without added Scrabble-related trauma. Right, the interview! How are you feeling about it? Still a bit wobbly? You’re brilliant at what you do, El. Don't let Rhys' word games get to you. What's the research co-ordinator thing  actually  involve, anyway? You always just say “language research” which sounds very… clandestine. It’s a bit of both, actually. It’s for a project looking at dialectal variations in social media, which is fascinating. Lots of corpus linguistics, phonetics, data analysis… basically, tracing how different regions are using language online. It’s at UCL, which is why it’s so competitive. They said in the briefing it’s quite a fast-paced environment. Sounds intense! UCL is posh though, isn’t it? Loads of fancy people. Still, you'll be amazing. You’re practically fluent in linguistics-speak. Remember that time you corrected Mrs. Davies’ grammar at the village fete? Don’t remind me! I was eight and thought I was a linguistic genius. She was not impressed. Anyway, enough about my anxiety. How was your week? Still battling through edits on that magazine? Anything juicy? It's…a slog, honestly. We're doing a feature on "self-care" which is ironic since the workload is actively destroying my self-care. Lots of articles about overpriced bath bombs and weekend retreats. Though, I did pitch an idea for a piece about finding joy in small things – like a really good cup of tea, or a perfectly organised bookshelf. Got shot down. Apparently, it’s not “aspirational” enough. Ugh. Magazines. Always wanting you to buy something to be happy. Speaking of which, have you seen this series,  The Undateables ? It’s strangely heartwarming, and also horrific. Some of those dates… I  love  that show! It's a glorious train wreck. But also genuinely lovely. It puts everything into perspective, doesn't it?

…and honestly, the error code just blinked at me. Like it was  mocking  me. E22. Apparently, it’s the drain pump, which honestly sounds expensive. I spent a good half hour googling it, convinced I could fix it myself, you know, save us a fortune. E22, huh? Sounds… ominous. You and DIY, love. It’s a dangerous combination. Remember the time you tried to fix the bathroom tap and flooded the kitchen? Hey! That was a learning experience! And it wasn't  flooded , it was… damp. Significantly damp. This is different though, this is a machine that cost us a grand! I feel responsible. Responsible for a washing machine malfunctioning? Don't be daft. They break, that's what they do. Look, I’ll take a peek at it later. My flatmate back in Brum was a bit of a wizard with appliances. Picked up a few things just by osmosis, I reckon. You think? That would be brilliant. I’ve got that report deadline looming and honestly, wrestling with plumbing is  not  how I want to spend my evening. Speaking of looming, are you hungry? I was thinking of making a shepherd’s pie. It's proper comfort food, especially with this grey weather. Shepherd’s pie sounds… divinely northern. Yes, please. Though, a bit of a contrast to the Thai green curry you promised last week. Well, my mum sent me a load of lamb mincemeat. You know how she is, always shoving food at me, even though I live three hundred miles away. It’s a maternal instinct, I suppose. She called yesterday asking if I was "getting enough iron". Classic. My mum’s the same, but with vitamin D. Apparently, Cambridge is a vitamin D desert. She keeps sending me those effervescent tablets. Honestly, mothers. They just worry. Though, it  is  getting dark so early. Anyway, shepherd’s pie it is. It’ll remind me of home. Actually, did you manage to speak to your sister about Christmas? I did. It’s… complicated. She’s still touchy about the whole… incident with Uncle Barry at last year's Boxing Day drinks. Oh dear. The infamous trifle incident? The  only  trifle incident. Apparently, Barry's comment about her new boyfriend being "a bit too keen on beard oil” was deeply offensive. Honestly, it was a harmless observation. Barry is… Barry. He means well, but his filter is permanently broken.

…and honestly, the estate agent was practically giddy. "A viewing booked for tomorrow, Mrs. O'Malley! Interest is  high !" High for a damp cottage in Hunsonby, I ask you. It’s charming, I’ll grant you that, but high is a strong word. Well, it’s the Lake District, isn’t it? People pay a premium for…well, for the view, mostly. And the ‘quaintness’. It’s a different market entirely to Birkenhead, believe me. You could get a  mansion  for what they're asking for that little place down south. Mansion might be a bit strong, love. But you're right, the disparity is…remarkable. Remember when we were looking near Guildford? The shoeboxes they called 'apartments' were going for half a million! Half a million for somewhere you can hear your neighbour breathing! Exactly! And don’t even get me started on the commute. Dublin traffic was bad, but that M25… it's a soul-destroying experience. This, though, this is peace. Quiet. Though I suspect the peace will be shattered the moment a dozen tourists descend, all wanting to see ‘the charming Cumbrian cottage’. You’re a cynic, Mary. But a justified one, I think. Still, selling your place in Surrey was a good move. Even with the current…everything, house prices down there are insane. Did you see that article about the VW emissions scandal again? It popped up on my newsfeed this morning. Oh, don’t remind me. That was a right mess. All that fiddling with the software, pretending they were meeting emission standards. Utterly disgraceful. And the impact on resale values! People were practically giving those cars away for a while. It’s a brilliant example of corporate greed, though, isn't it? Just… breathtaking. They knowingly cheated consumers and the environment, all for a bit of extra profit. Makes you wonder what else they’re getting away with. It's like the housing market, really. Artificial inflation, pushing prices higher and higher, making it impossible for young people to get on the ladder. That’s a bit of a leap, Mary, isn’t it? Comparing a car manufacturer's criminal activity to…well, the complexities of the housing market? Is it? Both are driven by profit, aren’t they? Both involve a degree of…deception, let's say. Estate agents aren’t exactly known for their honesty, are they? “Characterful features,” they call damp patches.

…and honestly, Doreen, you’d have thought after all this time, young Tim would’ve realised tact isn’t a foreign language. Just barging in, asking about the pension like it’s a public handout! Honestly. He’s always been a bit… direct, hasn't he? Your Tim. Never could suffer fools gladly, even if  he  is often the fool. Still, shouldn't upset yourself about it, Arthur. It’s your money, earned fair and square. Though goodness knows  how  you saved anything on a civil engineer’s wage. Always fiddling with bridges and whatnot. Fiddling is a strong word, Bernard. I designed them! And a decent wage it was, back in the day. It's just… it feels like everyone’s got their hand out. Especially with the price of everything these days. And then he starts on about needing help with his computer again. Honestly, I don't understand those blinking boxes. Well, you never were one for gadgets, Arthur. Remember when you refused to get a microwave? Said it ‘ruined the flavour of a proper roast’. I stand by that! A microwave is an abomination! But that’s different. This is… intrusion. And he isn’t the only one. Margaret keeps hinting about us downsizing. “Oh, all that space, you two rattling around…” Like we're a burden. Margaret’s just worried, that's all. She sees all the new housing developments going up around Costessey. Says it's tempting to move into something smaller, easier to manage. No garden to worry about. Though I tell her, what’s life without a bit of gardening? Easier to manage for  who , Bernard? It’s not about us managing, it’s about them wanting to sell this place and pocket the difference. They’ve always had an eye for a bargain, that family. Now, now, Arthur. That's a bit harsh. They just want what's best for you both. Maybe a bungalow would be nice. One level, no stairs… think of your knees, Arthur. My knees are fine! They ache a little in the damp, that’s all. It’s the  principle  of it. This house has been in my family for generations. My grandfather built the extension himself. It holds memories. Aye, it does. Remember old Mrs. Higgins next door? Used to bring us fresh rhubarb from her garden. And the summer fetes… Oh, the summer fetes! You two always won the egg and spoon race, didn't you?

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  loves  to hear himself talk about mitochondria. Like, we get it, they’re the powerhouse of the cell, but does he need to dedicate an entire lesson to it? It’s just… exhausting. Tell me about it. Biology is brutal this year. I’m struggling with the evolution stuff. Natural selection just feels… random. Like, how can something so complex come from just  chance ? It’s not entirely chance, is it? It's about advantageous traits being passed on. It's pretty logical when you think about it. Though, explaining it to my nan is another matter. She still thinks we came from monkeys. My grandad thinks the Earth is flat. Trying to explain scientific consensus to  him  is like talking to a brick wall. Anyway, back to Davies… did anyone see that TikTok of him trying to do a dance trend? It went viral for all the wrong reasons. Oh my GOD, yes! It was mortifying! He thought he was being cool, but he looked like a confused flamingo. I think half the school has seen it now. Seriously. The comments were brutal. Someone said he looked like he was having a seizure. A bit harsh, maybe, but… accurate. It’s amazing what gets traction online. Remember Liam’s accidental livestream of him eating a banana? That was gold. That  was  gold. But it makes you think, doesn’t it? About what people put online. Like, everything’s permanent. And everyone’s judging. There's this girl, Chloe, getting flak for her opinions on feminism… Oh, yeah, I saw. Some bloke was going on about how feminists just want special treatment. Honestly, the ignorance is astounding. It's not about wanting special treatment, it’s about equality! It’s basic stuff. It always seems to be guys who don’t understand the concept who are shouting the loudest. It's just… frustrating. My sister keeps trying to explain intersectionality to my uncle, and he just shuts down. Says it’s “too complicated”. It's the same with racism, isn't it? People are quick to dismiss it or say it’s not a problem anymore. Like, hello? Have you looked around? It’s still  very  much a problem. It’s weird, though. You try to have these conversations and some people get so defensive. Like acknowledging there's a problem means they’re personally to blame.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just a blur. They said the infection markers were still a bit high, even after the second course of antibiotics. Dr. Sharma is being very cautious, which I appreciate, but it’s frustrating waiting around for things to  actually  get better. Oh, you poor love. Still battling then? That sounds awful, Sarah. Are you still taking all those tablets? Seems like you're rattling with them! Aye, it does sound a strain. Remember my hip operation? Weeks on end of pills, and still ached something chronic. Though it weren’t an infection, thank goodness. Just old age catching up with me, I suppose. Old age catches up with all of us, Elsie. Though you still move faster than me sometimes! Sarah, what kind of infection was it again? Not pneumonia, was it? That’s a nasty one. No, thankfully not pneumonia, Dad. It was, they think, related to the initial surgery on my knee. Something just didn't quite take, and then got infected. They’re running more tests to be sure, ruling out everything nasty. It’s just… exhausting. So many hospital appointments. I can imagine. All that travelling to Addenbrooke’s, it’s a right trek. Is Mark driving you each time? He is, bless him. He’s been amazing, really. Taking time off work, making sure I’m comfortable…He even suggested acupuncture! I laughed, honestly. Me, with needles? Acupuncture? Oh, don’t scoff, dear. Old Mrs. Higgins swore by it for her arthritis. Said it did wonders. Though she also swore the neighbour’s cat was a spy for the government, so take that with a pinch of salt! Elsie’s always had a vivid imagination. Acupuncture… sounds a bit newfangled to me. Give me a good old-fashioned liniment any day. Reminds me of the time I pulled a muscle playing rugby… Oh here we go… another rugby story! Well, someone’s gotta keep the tradition alive! It was 1968, the Peterborough Barbarians against St. Ives… a proper mud bath it was. I tackled this lad, a big fella, and… well, let's just say I didn’t get up for a while. Had to be carried off, and old Doc Miller just slapped some liniment on it and told me to ‘man up’. Things were different then, weren’t they, George? They wouldn’t let you  near  a rugby pitch with a dodgy knee these days.

…and so, the ships weren’t just carrying goods, Leo. They were carrying people. People who were  forced  to be there. Taken from their homes, families broken apart. Does that sound fair, sweetheart? No! That’s… awful. Like when Mrs. Higgins took my sparkly pen without asking. It’s a bit like that, but… much, much worse. Mrs. Higgins just wanted a pen. These people were treated like… like objects. Not people at all. Objects? Like my LEGOs? Can you break people like LEGOs? No, darling. You can't  break  people like LEGOs, thank goodness. But sometimes people do terrible things to other people, and treat them as if they don’t matter. That's what slavery was. Taking away someone’s freedom. Making them work without pay, and hurting them if they didn’t. Why would they  do  that? That’s a really good question, Lily. It's complicated. A long time ago, some people thought they were better than others because of the colour of their skin. They wanted to make money, and they thought they could do that by forcing people to work for them. It was horribly wrong, and it’s something we have to remember so it doesn’t happen again. But why didn’t they just… stop them? The people doing that, I mean. Well, some people  did  try to stop it, Leo. There were people who fought against slavery, who tried to rescue people and help them escape. But it took a very, very long time. And it wasn’t just one person doing it; it was a whole system. It’s a bit like if everyone in your class started laughing at someone – it’s harder to stop if everyone is doing it, isn’t it? Yeah. It’s mean. But Miss Davies always stops it. Exactly. Miss Davies is doing the right thing. And eventually, people realised slavery was wrong, and it was made illegal. But even then, the effects lasted for a long time. It's still something we’re dealing with today, trying to make sure everyone is treated fairly. So… it's like the war, then? Grandad told me about the war, and bad people were doing bad things then, too. In a way, yes. War is another example of people doing terrible things to each other. Sometimes countries fight because they disagree, or because they want something another country has.

…and honestly, the storylines are just getting  ridiculous . Honestly, who writes this stuff? It’s like they’re actively trying to lose viewers. You still watching ‘The Coastal Clinic’, then, Brenda? Thought you’d given up on it after that business with the vicar and the runaway llama? Don't remind me, David! I keep hoping it'll go back to being a decent medical drama, but it’s just… soap opera at this point. Still, it's something to put on while I’m folding laundry. Honestly, the state of television these days. It’s all streaming now, isn't it? No one  watches  television anymore, they binge-watch things on Netflix or Disney+. I’ve just finished ‘Severance’ – properly messed with my head, that one. ‘Severance’? Sounds a bit grim. I’m more of a ‘Countryfile’ man myself. Give me rolling hills and a good sheepdog any day. Sheepdogs are clever, they are. Old Man Hemmings down the road used to have a border collie that could practically  read  your mind. Knew exactly when you were thinking about sneaking a biscuit. Oh, Bertie! That dog was a menace. Though he was awfully good with Mrs. Higgins’ cat, Mittens. Remember when Mittens got stuck up that oak tree, Geoff? How could I forget? The fire brigade had to come! All for a fluffy feline having a bit of an adventure. Cost the council a fortune, I reckon. Speaking of adventures, anyone hear from Sarah and Mark? They were supposed to be back from their Italian holiday yesterday, weren’t they? Mum sent a text this morning. They're still in Rome. Apparently, Mark’s developed a bit of an obsession with ancient mosaics. He’s convinced he’s going to recreate one in the garden. Oh, Mark. Bless him. He and his projects. The last one was the birdhouse that looked suspiciously like the Eiffel Tower. He’s a good lad, your Mark. Always busy. Reminds me of myself when I was working in the kitchens. Always inventing some new way to present the vegetables. It's nice they're having a good time, though. We all need a break. This weather's been dreadful for gardening, hasn't it? My tomatoes are looking a bit peaky. Mine too. Needs proper sun. Though Brenda’s got a knack for growing things, doesn’t she? Her roses are always spectacular. It’s just a bit of love and a decent feed, that’s all.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Tupperware is astonishing. Whose is this, do you even  know  what was in this one? Mine! It had… blueberries. Blueberries. Right. Well, blueberries have a habit of staining plastic, so thank you for that, darling. Leo, are you even helping, or are you just contemplating the structural integrity of the cereal bowls? I’m making sure they’re facing the right way, Mummy! So they don’t fall. Facing the right way? Oh, good grief. Bless you, sweetheart. Okay, right, dishwasher unloaded. Now. Operation ‘George Stephenson’ commences. Is George Stephenson a wizard? Like Harry Potter? No, sweetheart, George Stephenson wasn't a wizard. Though he did work wonders, in a way. He was an engineer. A really,  really  important engineer. What’s an engineer? Is it like building with LEGO? It's a bit like building with LEGO, actually! Engineers design and build things. George Stephenson built… well, he built railways! He invented the first public railway line that used steam locomotives. Steam? Like… steam from a kettle? Yes, a bit like steam from a kettle, but much,  much  bigger. He figured out how to use the power of steam to pull carriages full of people and goods along metal tracks. Before that, people travelled mostly by horse and cart. Can you imagine how long everything took? A really long time! Like when we go to Grandma’s and it feels like forever! Exactly! A  very  long time. And George Stephenson’s railway, the Stockton and Darlington Railway, changed everything. It meant things could be transported much faster and cheaper. It kick-started the whole railway boom. Was he rich then? He became quite successful, yes. But it wasn’t just about money, you see. He was a clever man, and he was determined. Apparently, when he was a little boy, his family didn’t have much money, and he had to walk miles to school every day. Miles?! That IS a long time! Did he have a magic carpet? No magic carpet, sadly. Just very determined little legs. And he wasn’t very good at school at first, apparently. He was supposed to be looking after the sheep on the farm, but he was always fiddling with things, trying to make them work better. He built a little model engine when he was a teenager! He sounds a bit like Ron Weasley, always taking things apart to see how they work.

… honestly, I’m telling you, Beatrice keeps challenging me on words I  know  are valid. Like “za,” just “za!” She claims it’s not a word. It’s a perfectly good Scrabble tile combination! Oh, relax, Leo. It's just Words With Friends. And honestly, she’s probably just trying to distract you from her blatant tile-hogging strategy. She always saves the high-scoring letters. She’s ruthless. I’ve played against Bea a few times. It’s less a game and more a strategic power play. Though, I find myself spending more time planning this supper club menu than battling her for triple word scores, to be honest. Supper club, eh? That sounds…ambitious, Chloe. You haven't even finished redecorating the café yet. Remember that whole 'slightly-illegal-electrical-work' situation we talked about last week? It’s  fine , Dan! I got a proper electrician in, alright? And the supper club is a low-risk thing. Just once a month, different theme each time. I was thinking Moroccan next. Leo, you’re good with spices, right? Maybe you can give me some pointers? Spices I can do. Though, I’m currently more proficient in spotting dodgy Words With Friends plays. Seriously, “za” is a word! I even looked it up on the dictionary website! You looked up “za” on the dictionary? That’s dedication, Leo. I’m more worried about whether this lentil stew is going to be edible. I’ve never made anything this big before. Usually, I’m just whipping up sourdough and pastries. It smells pretty good, Liv. You’re a baker, you’ve got the precision thing down. Stew’s just…scaling up, right? Like, put in more stuff. Easier said than done. My problem is I keep wanting to add cardamom and rosewater to  everything . It's a baker's curse. Don't! Leave the rosewater for the Moroccan night. We're aiming for authentic! I’ve been scouring food blogs all week. Found this amazing site, ‘Zaytoun Kitchen’ – seriously good recipes. See? Zaytoun! It's got a "z" in it! Proves my point about "za” being a legitimate letter combination! Oh my god, Leo, let it go! So, how many people are you thinking for the supper club? Ten, max. Keep it intimate. Plus, it gives me a chance to test out new dishes. I'm thinking of doing a whole vegan night eventually, but that's a legal minefield with labelling and allergies and… everything.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of detentions Mr. Harrison handed out today was ridiculous. Ten! For talking. Talking, Anya! It's a school, isn't it supposed to involve  some  talking? Ten? Wow. He really clamped down, didn't he? Maybe he had a bad morning. Though, I still think he’s a bit… intense. He stares. A lot. Intense is one word for it. I think “power-mad” is closer. Anyway, enough shop stewing about work. How was your weekend? Did you get to that pottery class you were telling me about? It was good, actually. Really relaxing. The pottery was… messy. Very, very messy. I think I spent more time cleaning clay off myself than actually  making  anything. But it was fun. I did manage a rather wonky plant pot, though. It’s drying at the moment. Wonky is good! Character. I always say, imperfections are what make things interesting. My little Leo is obsessed with building things, but they rarely stand up straight. He’s nine, full of energy. Drives me up the wall sometimes, but he’s a good kid. Nine is a fun age. Full of questions, I imagine? My little sister is seven. She video calls me constantly, asking about everything. Mostly ‘Why is the sky blue?’ and ‘Do penguins have knees?’ Oh, constantly! And the ‘why’s never end. It's a philosophical onslaught, honestly. Speaking of which, did you manage to get to the village fete on Saturday? I took Leo, he won a goldfish. It's living in a rather elaborate castle made of Lego. No, I didn’t, unfortunately. I was trying to finally sort out the filing system in the reprographics room. It’s… a disaster. Old invoices, copies of copies of copies… it’s a paper archaeologist’s dream, but a practical person’s nightmare. I did make a really nice raspberry and apple crumble though. Ooh, lovely! You’re a whiz in the kitchen, aren't you? I’m hopeless. I can make a passable shepherd’s pie, but that’s about it. Leo requests pancakes every other day. It's exhausting. Where do you learn all your recipes? Mostly from my grandmother. She’s an amazing cook. Very traditional Russian recipes. Lots of dumplings, pickled things… Actually, she sent me a huge jar of pickled mushrooms. They are… an acquired taste. Pickled mushrooms? Sounds… adventurous. I think I'll stick to my shepherd’s pie.

…and honestly, the assistant at Sports Direct just looked  bored . Like, I was asking about running shoes and she was scrolling on her phone! Honestly, Preston town centre is going downhill, isn’t it? It's not helping that they're trying to pedestrianise all those streets. It makes getting  anywhere  a nightmare. Remember when we could just park outside Boots? Now it’s a fifteen-minute walk from the car park, even with shortcuts. Are we nearly at Mothercare? My feet are killing me. Aye, it's a right mess. All these changes. They don’t think it through, do they? Fifteen minutes? You’re being generous, love. And no, not yet. Just past the roundabout at Fulwood. Should be five minutes. You need a drink, Anya? I've got that bottled water in the door pocket. Oh, yes please, Dad. Thank you. Much better. I’m just…thinking about the house survey. They found damp in the downstairs loo. Damp! After all the money we’ve spent. Damp’s a nightmare, isn’t it? Gran always said damp was the sign of a house with a bad soul. Bit dramatic, but she wasn’t wrong about things like that. Remember how mouldy Uncle Barry’s kitchen was before he finally got it sorted? Your Gran had a point, actually. It’s not just about the structural damage, it’s… unsettling. We'll get it sorted though, Anya. The surveyor said it’s minor, just a bit of pointing needs doing. It’s an old house, these things happen. We knew it’d need a bit of work. Easy for you to say, you're not the one facing a potential renovation project on top of everything else. I was hoping we could just move in and…relax. I keep picturing decorating the nursery, getting everything ready… Speaking of nurseries, did you see those amazing little blankets in there? The ones with the sheep on? I was thinking about little Leo. They were so soft. Proper baby soft. I did! They were lovely. A bit expensive though, weren’t they? We’ve got plenty of blankets already, haven't we? My mum sent loads. She’s already knitting a whole wardrobe of tiny clothes. It’s lovely, but… overwhelming! Your mum's a whiz with the needles. Always has been. Remember that awful green cardigan she made me when I was a lad?

…and then, honestly, the lag was  terrible . Like, I shot him, I  know  I shot him, and it didn’t register for a full three seconds! He just stood there, healing, laughing, and then  boom  – I'm dead. It’s so frustrating with ‘Apex’, you know? Sounds stressful, love. All that shooting and… Apex? Is that one of those computer games where you’re running about pretending to be soldiers? It’s a battle royale, Mum. And it’s really not  pretending . It’s strategic, it’s about teamwork, and the skill ceiling is really high. It's not just running around! She’s right, it's fairly intense. I tried watching Liv stream it the other day – I had no idea what was going on half the time. So many different abilities and weapons… See! Even  you  admit it’s complex. Anyway, I lost all my rank points. Ugh. It's just… I was having a bad day already, you know? Mr. Henderson gave me that essay back, and it was covered in red pen. Oh, the history one? About the suffragettes? I thought you were quite keen on that topic. I  am ! But he said my arguments weren’t ‘nuanced’ enough. What even  is  that supposed to mean? It felt like he just wanted to be critical. Honestly, it ruined my whole afternoon. I just felt… bleh. Henderson’s notorious for that. He likes to sound clever. Don’t let it get to you, El. You were explaining the complexities of the movement to  me  just last week, you're definitely capable. Maybe you just need to re-read it with a fresh pair of eyes? Maybe. I just… I overthink things, I think. I read somewhere about how perfectionism is a form of anxiety, and that really resonated. Oh, darling, you've always been a worrier. Your granddad was the same. Always planning for every eventuality. It’s a family trait, I suppose. It’s not always a bad thing, being thoughtful, but you do have to learn to let things go sometimes. Have you started thinking about university applications yet? That’s enough stress for anyone. Ugh, don’t remind me. I’m trying not to. I've got a vague idea – astrophysics, probably. But the thought of writing the personal statement… it’s terrifying. Astrophysics, wow! Serious stuff. You always were good at science. Remember building that ridiculously complicated volcano for the science fair in Year 7?

…and honestly, the sheer amount of iron you need for even  basic  tools in Minecraft is ridiculous. It’s like, where are all these villagers getting their furnaces? It's not like they’re mining it themselves! But diamonds are  best . You can make a diamond pickaxe and it breaks obsidian! Yeah! And you can enchant diamond stuff! I got a diamond sword with ‘Sharpness V’ yesterday. It did  so  much damage to the zombie. Sharpness V, well done! See, that's where the real value lies. But even to  get  to diamonds, you need iron. It’s foundational. You know, it’s the same in the real world. Iron Age, all that. It's a really important metal. What's a metal? Is it shiny? Well, some metals are shiny! Gold is very shiny. Silver, too. Iron isn’t  quite  as shiny unless it’s been polished. They’re all… elements, things from the earth. We build things with them. Your bike frame, parts of cars, even things in your phones. Is LEGO made of metal? No, LEGO is plastic. That’s a different kind of thing. Plastic comes from oil. We were talking about metals...though some plastics are surprisingly strong. Speaking of materials, I was reading about different fabrics. Did you know there's a fabric made from orange peels? Ewwww! That sounds sticky! It doesn’t  smell  of oranges, thankfully! It's a new process. They’re trying to find sustainable materials, things that don’t harm the planet. Like, cotton is good, but it needs a lot of water to grow. Silk is lovely, but… well, you know about silk worms, don’t you? They make the stringy stuff! But it’s a bit… sad. It can be, yes. That's why people are looking for alternatives. Anyway, enough about fabrics and metals. I’ve been working on a new legend. Ooh! A legend! Like about King Arthur? Sort of. This one is about the ‘Glimmering Guardians’ of Comberton. They protect the village from… dust bunnies. Dust bunnies? They’re not scary! These are  super  dust bunnies. Sentient dust bunnies. They’re powered by forgotten socks. And they only appear when people forget to take their vitamins. Vitamins? Like the orange fizzy ones? Exactly! Those are the Glimmering Guardians’ fuel. Each vitamin gives them power to fight off one dust bunny. So, if I don’t take my vitamin D, a dust bunny will take over Comberton?

…and honestly, I still can’t believe Old Man Hemmings from down the road got away with it. Fifteen years ago! Fifteen! It makes my blood boil just thinkin’ about it. Folk ‘round here still whisper about it, ya know? Aye, I do. It’s grim. Proper grim. I remember me mam warnin’ me and little Liam to stay away from his garden, even when we were just kickin’ a ball. It makes you sick, doesn’t it? The thought of…well, you know. It does. It really does. And the way they just…downplayed it. Said there wasn’t enough proof. Proof! What more proof do you need than the stories from those girls, eh? It just feels like some people are more protected than others. Anyway… sorry, didn't mean to go all dark on ya. Been readin’ too much true crime, I reckon. No, no, it’s right to be angry. It IS dark. And horrifying. It’s a good thing people  do  talk about it, keeps it in the light, even if justice didn’t happen then. What were we even on about before all that? Oh, right… the gig? Aye, the gig! The Static Waves. Thinkin’ about goin’. They’re playin’ the Red Lion next week. Red Lion? Decent sound system there, isn't it? Static Waves are alright. A bit… shouty, maybe? But good energy. You still playin’ that acoustic, lass? Sometimes. Still can't get me head 'round barre chords properly though, honestly feels like I’ve got hands made of sausages. I was thinkin’ about gettin’ an electric, somethin’ a bit easier on the fingers. You still got yours? The red one? Aye, still got ‘er. Dusted 'er off last week, actually. Been messin’ about with some new pedals. Trying to get a sound a bit like Bloc Party. Failing miserably, mind. It’s harder than it looks, makin’ it sound… clean. Bloc Party! Ambitious. You always were ambitious. Remember when you tried to build your own amp out of a cereal box and a Radio 1 competition win? Don't remind me! That thing sparked somethin’ fierce! Nearly burned me mam’s kitchen down. She was livid. Said I was gonna end up electrocutin' meself. She wasn't wrong to worry, lookin' back. She was always a worrier. But she loved you, ya know. And she had a point. You were a menace with wires.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of reading for the EPQ is criminal. Like, seriously, Mrs. Davies clearly thinks we have nothing else going on in our lives. It's all about the socio-economic impact of fast fashion, which, okay, important, but… mountains of articles. Tell me about it. Mine's on the evolution of grime music, and I’m drowning in interviews and production techniques. It’s not even  writing , it’s just…absorbing. Though, finding primary sources is surprisingly hard. Everyone wants to charge you for access. You guys are ambitious! Mine’s comparatively light – a photography exhibition based on urban decay in London. Less reading, more wandering around dodgy areas with a camera. Though Dad’s worried about me going alone. Dodgy areas? Be careful, yeah. Speaking of wandering, remember when we all went to that Polish deli near your house, Anya? The one that smelled permanently of pickles? Oh my god, yes! And Mr. Kowalski always tried to get us to try some weird sausage. I think it was once rabbit. I definitely pretended to eat it. He tried to convince  me  it was pheasant! He was a legend. Food reminds me, are we still on for that Korean BBQ next week? I’m starving just thinking about it. Definitely. Though maybe we should factor in some prep time for this EPQ nightmare. I’m already falling behind. Honestly, thinking about university applications  and  this… it’s stressful. Have you guys decided what you want to do? Still leaning towards engineering, probably. Got an open day at Imperial next month. It's terrifying, thinking about the fees. My mum's already having kittens. I’m thinking about photography, obviously, maybe something combined with journalism. I want to do something…meaningful, you know? Not just chase money. Meaningful is good. My dad keeps pushing me towards law, because “good prospects.” But honestly, it sounds soul-crushing. I was thinking about maybe something in international development? Maybe after uni, volunteer somewhere. Like where? I was looking at a charity that does work in Montenegro. Remember old Mr. Petrovic who used to live down the road? He always talked about how beautiful it was, and how much poverty there still is. It got me thinking. Montenegro? That sounds amazing. Although, poverty's everywhere, isn't it? Even here, honestly. You see it if you actually  look . It’s easy to get caught up in our little bubble.

…and honestly, the state of this kitchen is a  disgrace . I swear, someone used my washing up liquid to clean the floor last week. The  floor ! Tell me about it. Found a half-eaten Pot Noodle stuck to the side of the sink this morning. Seriously, people have no respect. And it’s not like accommodation is cheap, is it? Considering what we’re paying, you’d think they’d actually  clean  it regularly. You lot are lucky you even  have  a kitchen in your accommodation. My halls had… well, let’s just say ‘communal cooking facilities’ were optimistic. It was basically a microwave and a kettle in a cupboard shared by forty people. Forty? Blimey. We only share with six, and half of them are never actually  in  the kitchen. Except, like, now. Lucky you, Leo. Six is manageable. Though, half of  our  six seem to think leaving their mess is a perfectly acceptable lifestyle choice. Honestly, my mum would have my hide if she saw this. She’d be scrubbing for hours. Your mum’s a clean freak, isn’t she? Always has been. Remember that time she made you take apart your Lego castle brick-by-brick because there was a tiny bit of dust on one of the pieces? It wasn’t a tiny bit! And it was a limited edition castle! She just likes things… tidy. It's a Cornish thing, I reckon. We're all a bit pedantic down there. She keeps texting, by the way. Asking if I’m eating enough vegetables. Mine just wants to know if I’m getting enough sleep. Classic Indian parent move. It’s not about how well you’re doing academically, it’s about whether you’re getting eight hours a night and drinking enough water. Apparently, that’s the key to everything. My dad just sends memes. Awful ones. Like, really terrible. One yesterday was a picture of a sloth… with the caption ‘Me trying to motivate myself to do my physics homework.’ It wasn’t even funny. Oh, bless him. My dad just tries to subtly suggest I move back to Falmouth and take over the family boat repair business. "Steady work, lovely sea air," he says. As if I'd trade all this for… well, for fixing boats. Speaking of steady work, how’s the job hunt going, Amelia? Still no luck with finding something to cover rent?

…and honestly, the kids were  exhausted  by the time we got back. Little Leo insisted on wearing his reindeer antlers the entire journey, even for his nap! It was quite a sight. Oh, bless him. He sounds exactly like Rhys when he was small. Remember that pirate costume he refused to take off for a week? Went to the supermarket in it, everything. Mortifying, but hilarious now. Oh, I’ve heard stories! You and Dad always had quite the handful. This Christmas feels different though, doesn’t it? More…reflective. It does. Perhaps it’s because the children are getting older. It slips away so quickly, doesn’t it? One minute they’re believing in Father Christmas, the next they're teenagers rolling their eyes. Are Maisie and Finn excited at all? Maisie’s at that stage where she  says  she's too cool for it all, but I caught her making a list for Santa last night. Finn is still proper enthralled, thankfully. He's been planning his letter for weeks. He wants a telescope. Apparently, he wants to find aliens. A telescope! Lovely. Rhys went through a space phase. Spent hours looking at the stars, convinced he’d discover a new planet. He was going to name it “Rhysworld”. Honestly! They're so precious, aren’t they? It makes all the chaos worthwhile. Speaking of chaos, how's the consultancy going? Still travelling all over the place? It's…steady. I was in Birmingham last week, doing some training for a local council. It’s tiring, constantly being ‘on’, but it’s fulfilling. I enjoy helping people, genuinely. Though I do miss having a set routine sometimes. I’m thinking of scaling back a bit next year, maybe focusing on online workshops. Less travel, more time for…well, for things like this. That sounds sensible. You deserve a bit of downtime. And it would be lovely to see you more often. We haven’t had a proper catch-up like this in ages. Although, I'm always worried about you driving all that distance. Nonsense. I enjoy the drive, honestly. Gives me time to think. Plus, the M5 isn't  that  bad. Though I do avoid it during school holidays! Speaking of drives, you never did tell me about your trip to Spain this summer. How was that? Still teaching English to sun-kissed teenagers? Something like that! It was hot.

…and honestly, the signal was  awful  in that village. I tried to video call Gran, and it just kept freezing. She looked like a glitching robot. It was hilarious, but she wasn't impressed. Your Gran isn’t one for technology, is she? Still prefers a good old-fashioned phone call, bless her. Speaking of phones, mine’s been acting up again. Keeps dropping calls. I swear, these companies just want you to upgrade. It used to be reliable, this one. They always do, Dad. It's designed obsolescence. But hey, look at this place. It’s changed so much since I was last here. All those new houses… Crayford’s really expanded. It has. Too much, if you ask me. Used to be fields around here. Now it’s all concrete. And the speed cameras! They’ve sprouted up like mushrooms after rain. Nearly lost my license last month, speeding just doing 32 in a 30 zone. They’re just revenue generators, that’s all they are. Seriously? 32? You’re a careful driver, Dad! They really are just out to get people. How’s work been, by the way? Still dealing with angry customers all day? You have no idea. Last week, someone screamed at me for fifteen minutes because their internet wasn't working. Fifteen minutes! I’m surprised my ears still work. I’m thinking of trying to transfer to a different department, maybe something less… public-facing. I had a bit of a bug last month too, a nasty chest infection. Knocked me for six. Had to take a week off. Oh no, that sounds awful! You need to look after yourself, you do. So, Brighton… are you still thinking about moving closer to me? I am, yeah. It's a big decision, though. Leaving this house… your mum loved this house. But… being nearer you, and the grandkids… it makes sense. I was looking at places last weekend. Small flat, overlooking the sea. Sounds idyllic, doesn't it? It does! It really does. We've got plenty of space, you know. You're always welcome to stay with us while you look. Appreciate that, son. Appreciate it. Remember that trip we took to Tanzania? Years ago. You were only ten. You insisted on trying to wrestle a monkey. I do! It was a tiny monkey! And it stole my biscuit. Good times. I keep meaning to show you the photos I took.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of people in Sainsbury’s was  stressful . I just needed oat milk and a lemon, a lemon! It felt like navigating a rugby scrum. Did you have any better luck at the market? Oh, don’t even  start  me on supermarket shopping on a Saturday. It’s designed to erode your will to live, I’m convinced. The market was… less chaotic, definitely. Though Old Man Hemmings was trying to convince me his parsnips were “practically medicinal.” Hemmings always does! He’s a character. Did you get enough for the roast? I'm thinking we can actually  have  people over next weekend, if the weather holds. I think so. Got a beautiful bit of lamb, some proper roasting potatoes, all the trimmings. It's just… work has been draining, you know? Even a simple grocery trip feels monumental when you've spent all day untangling university PR disasters. PR disasters? Oh dear. What now? Another student union kerfuffle? Worse, actually. Apparently, Professor Davies gave an interview to that student newspaper,  The Vanguard , and… well, he decided to share his very strong opinions on modern music. Specifically, he described Billie Eilish as “sonic wallpaper for the emotionally stunted.” Oh,  no . Davies? Seriously? That’s… spectacularly tone-deaf. Spectacularly is putting it mildly. The internet has exploded. The student body is furious. The Vice-Chancellor is having kittens. And I’m stuck drafting apology statements and trying to convince everyone that academic freedom doesn’t extend to publicly disparaging Gen Z’s musical tastes. That’s… a lot. You’re a saint, honestly. I’m just dealing with essays on Milton, which is bad enough, but comparatively, that’s a whole different level of headache. It’s amazing how quickly things blow up these days. It is. One poorly chosen phrase, and suddenly you’re trending on Twitter for all the wrong reasons. I suggested he maybe issue a clarification, saying he appreciates  all  forms of artistic expression, but he’s dug his heels in. He says he’s entitled to his opinion. Entitled, yes. Tactful, not so much. Poor you. Look, you need to de-stress. Forget the parsnips, forget the roast for a bit, and let's just… listen to some ‘sonic wallpaper for the emotionally stunted’. You’re offering a musical antidote? I like it. Though I suspect a full immersion in Billie Eilish might be a bit… intense after a day of damage control.

…and honestly, the yarn is just  flying  through my fingers. I think I’m actually making progress on this beanbag. It's going to take forever, though, isn’t it? I underestimated the sheer volume of stuffing required. Forever is a strong word, love. But yes, it's ambitious. You've been at it for… what, three weeks now? At least you’re not starting another scarf. Remember the one that was supposed to be for your mum, and ended up being long enough to tie around the house? Don’t remind me. She politely suggested it might be better as a draught excluder. This is different! This is  functional . The kids need somewhere comfy to collapse after school, and honestly, it's quite therapeutic. More therapeutic than… dealing with the bathroom, anyway. Oh, the bathroom. We were circling back to that, were we? What horrors have you discovered now? Is the grout still crumbling? Worse. The shower curtain. It’s… faded. Terribly faded. It looks like a washed-out watercolour painting of what  used  to be cheerful sunflowers. And frankly, it’s a bit mildewy around the bottom. Mildewy? Right. That’s a definite upgrade needed then. I thought we agreed to tackle the décor in there after Christmas. I was picturing a bit of a revamp, some nice tiles… Revamp? That sounds expensive. I was thinking just a new shower curtain. And maybe a fresh coat of paint. The blue is… rather sad, isn’t it? It’s the shade of a rainy Tuesday. Sad blue is an accurate description. But if we're doing paint, are we talking the whole room? Because a patchy repaint won't look any better. And new tiles aren't  that  expensive, especially if we do it ourselves. I’m quite handy, you know. Handy with a paintbrush, maybe. I still haven't forgiven you for the wonky shelves in the spare room. Anyway, dinner first, bathroom later. What are you making, by the way? It smells lovely. Just a simple chicken and vegetable stir-fry. Nothing fancy. I thought we could do with something quick and easy tonight. You've been so busy with the beanbag and everything, you deserve a break. How’s the pattern going? Is it complicated? It's mostly garter stitch, thankfully. Very soothing. The colour changes are the tricky bit. I keep dropping stitches when I’m trying to remember whether it's supposed to be navy or teal.

…and honestly, Doreen, I still reckon they overcharge for the sprouts at Morrisons. It's daylight robbery, I tell you. Daylight robbery. Used to get ‘em for pennies down at the farm shop, didn’t we? Before Old Man Hemmings sold up. Oh, Arthur, you and your sprouts. You complain about the sprouts every year. They’re just sprouts. And Morrisons is closer than traipsing out to wherever a farm shop  is  these days. Remember your knees? My knees are perfectly alright, thank you very much. A bit creaky, admittedly, but alright. It's the principle of the thing, Doreen. Pure principle. Everything costs more now. Not like in our day, is it? You two are at it again, I see. Sprouts at this hour, honestly. Should be enjoying the quiet before the news comes on. Brian! Just telling Doreen here about the scandalous price of brassicas. It’s a tragedy, I tell you. A tragedy for the working man. Even if I haven’t  worked  for… well, a good while now. Don’t start that again, Arthur. You were a perfectly capable gardener. You  chose  to retire early. Several decades early. He prefers ‘leisurely pursuit of horticultural interests’, if I recall. Though I suspect mostly it involved sitting on a deckchair watching the runner beans grow. Well, someone had to  supervise  the runner beans, didn’t they? It’s a skilled job, knowing when to support ‘em. And I did a lovely pot of geraniums that year. Red ones. Doreen, remember the red geraniums? I remember you nearly collapsing trying to move them into the greenhouse. Nearly gave me a heart attack, you did. Honestly, Arthur, sometimes I think you actively seek out a bit of a drama. He does enjoy being fussed over. It’s a tactic. Works every time. Doreen, more tea? I’ve put a biscuit or two out. Digestives, your favourite. Oh, go on then, Brian. You spoil me. Thank you. It’s nice to just sit for five minutes, isn’t it? Before the chaos of the evening news descends. All doom and gloom. Doom and gloom is right. They’re always going on about something or other. Strikes, weather, politics… Makes a man regret ever being born, it does. Now, now, Arthur. Don't be morbid. You’ve had a good run. Plenty of years, good food, a loving wife… and an endless supply of sprouts, apparently.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Brussels sprouts Mrs. Henderson requested this year is frankly alarming. It's like she’s planning to single-handedly resolve the national vegetable shortage! Old habits die hard, love. She’s always been a sprouts fanatic. Remember that Christmas, back in '98, when she brought enough to feed the entire hospital ward? Oh god, yes! Uncle Dave was trying to subtly hide them under the table for the dog. Which, knowing Buster, he probably would have eaten them. He’d eat anything. Buster was a legend. Though, honestly, sprouts are underrated. If you roast them properly, with a bit of balsamic glaze… delightful. Balsamic glaze doesn't change the fact they smell like… well, you know. Anyway, it's not just the sprouts. She’s already started hinting about wanting a specific brand of brandy, the really expensive one. And your mother’s at it with the posh chocolates again. Honestly, Christmas is becoming a financial endurance test. Now, now, don't get yourself into a state. We budgeted for it, didn't we? A little bit of overspend at Christmas is practically tradition. Besides, they only do it because they like spoiling everyone. He's right, Mum. And think of their faces when they open everything. It's worth a bit of a strain, isn’t it? Plus, I'm coming home early this year, which is a proper Christmas miracle considering the deadlines at work. That  is  lovely, darling. It won't be the same having Christmas without you rushing off back to London the day after Boxing Day. What about flights back from Barbados next year, though? Have you looked at prices yet? Briefly. They’re… astronomical. Seriously, you'd think they were made of gold. I was checking for next September, hoping to get ahead, and even then, it’s looking pricey. Trying to find deals, but it’s tough. Barbados sounds amazing, though. A proper escape. I’ve never been anywhere so far afield. Rochester to Margate was the height of my exotic travels as a teenager! You and me both, love. Southport wasn’t exactly a hub of international glamour. Although, we did once go to Skegness… that was an adventure. Skegness! Oh, Lord. You haven't told her about Skegness, have you? She knows about Skegness! It's a treasured family anecdote. It involved a lost donkey, a stolen bucket and spade, and a truly dreadful fish and chip shop.

…and honestly, the driving here is something else, isn’t it? Back in Dorset, a roundabout is a roundabout. Here, it's more of a  suggestion  of a roundabout. Nearly lost my nerve merging onto the main road yesterday. Oh, you get used to it, dear. You absolutely get used to it. It’s…spirited, let’s call it. Strategic chaos, perhaps. Been coming here for fifteen years now, you know. My daughter, Penelope, she bought a little place in Paphos, and I come over a few times a year to visit her, and generally escape the grey. Fifteen years! That’s a long time. You must know the place inside out. I’m only just getting my bearings. This is my first time, actually. A colleague suggested it - said it was a hidden gem. So far, it’s…different. In a good way, mostly. Different is a polite word. It’s…relaxed. That’s the best way to put it. British rules don’t  quite  apply. Though I suspect that’s part of the appeal for many. So, you’re a teacher, you said? What do you teach? Secondary English. Year 10 and 11, mostly. It's...challenging, as you can imagine. Lots of teenagers with opinions. Honestly, sometimes I think  they  should be teaching  me  about resilience. Ah, teenagers! Universal experience, that. My Penelope was a handful. Artistic, bless her, but a handful. Always covered in paint or arguing about… well, everything. What brought you all the way to Northern Cyprus for a holiday? Escaping the teenagers, perhaps? A little bit of that, to be honest. It's the half-term break. My husband, David, he’s a keen birdwatcher, and apparently this is a brilliant spot for migratory birds. I’m more of a…beach and book kind of person myself. Birds, you say? Ah, yes, there are plenty. The flamingos are quite a sight in the spring. Have you been up to the Karpaz Peninsula yet? It's a bit of a drive, but absolutely stunning. Wild donkeys roaming everywhere, ancient ruins...it feels a million miles away from everything. No, not yet. That’s on the list. David’s already got his binoculars out and is plotting routes. He’s very… focused. I’m trying to convince him we need a day or two just lounging by the pool. Good luck with that! Men and their hobbies. My late wife, bless her soul, used to say the same thing about me and my stamp collecting.

…and honestly, the student just kept arguing! He claimed my interpretation of Woolf was “entirely subjective” as if  all  literary criticism isn’t subjective, to some degree! Honestly, the audacity. Sounds like a typical Tuesday, then. You’d think after three years, they’d grasp that engaging with a text isn’t about finding ‘the’ right answer. You’d think!
