My Arthur was a terrible smuggler. Always got caught! Just a little something to brighten the days, you know. It wasn’t about extravagance, just… a tiny bit of normal. My mother-in-law had a rather more dramatic wartime experience. She was born in Siberia, and somehow ended up travelling  all  the way to Africa during the war. Can you imagine? A little girl, uprooted and moved across continents. She never really spoke about it much, but you could tell it left a mark. Extraordinary. It makes all our current little worries seem rather… small, doesn’t it? Though navigating the gluten-free options at the Village Shop  does  feel like a major operation sometimes. Honestly, they’ve improved, but it’s still limited. The Farm Shop is better, definitely. More choice. Though pricier, naturally. Arthur refuses to go now, says it's all "poncey produce." He's a simple man, my Arthur, happy with a good Cumberland sausage and a strong cup of coffee. Speaking of which, could I trouble you for a refill, Beatrice? This is lovely. Of course, Margaret. And Arthur does have a point about the price! It's getting ridiculous. Though, you’ve got to admit, freshly baked bread from the Farm Shop… unbeatable. Absolutely.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of bunting requests this year is mental. Mental, I tell ya! People want bunting for  everything  now. It’s not just village fetes anymore, it's corporate team-building days, influencer parties, even… a dog’s birthday. A DOG’S BIRTHDAY. No way! A dog’s birthday? That’s… dedication. Or maybe just owners with too much disposable income. Seriously though, you sound stressed, Elle. Is it just the bunting? It’s the bunting, and it’s Brenda from accounts breathing down my neck about budgets, and it’s Mr. Henderson deciding he  needs  a live falconry display for the regional sales conference. A FALCONRY DISPLAY, in a Marquee! I’m telling you, Becca, some people. You don’t have this at your place, do you? Controlling the flow of… widgets or whatever it is you control? Widgets is a bit harsh. We manufacture precision components for aerospace. It’s slightly more sophisticated than widgets. And no, thankfully, no requests for avian entertainment. Though, we did have a slight panic last week when a shipment of titanium alloy was delayed. That caused a right kerfuffle with Boeing. But it’s problem-solving, you know? Analysing, adapting… far less… feathered. Boeing, wow! That sounds intense. I just spend my days battling the office printer and trying to decipher Sharon’s handwriting. Honestly, I think she writes in code sometimes. It’s amazing I get anything filed correctly. Sharon sounds like a character. At least your problems aren't airborne threats. Honestly, I'm starting to think I need a holiday. A  long  holiday. Somewhere with no bunting, no falcons, and definitely no demanding middle-aged men. You do. You absolutely do. Remember that pottery course you were talking about? Maybe book a weekend away, somewhere in the Peak District? Get your hands dirty, forget about Henderson and his birds… That  does  sound good. Though, leaving Brenda to handle the budget… that's a risk. She'll probably try to replace all the coffee with instant. It's her passive-aggressive way of asserting dominance. Oh my god, Brenda sounds terrifying. You deserve a break. Remember last year when you organised that charity gala? You pulled it off brilliantly, Elle. You’re capable of so much more than dealing with bunting emergencies. Thanks, Chloe. That was good, that was. Although, even  that  had a slight debacle with the chocolate fountain.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it! They just announced it at the last Borough Council meeting – no consultation, no consideration for what the library  means  to people. Just ‘land deemed more valuable for residential development’. As if a few more overpriced flats are more important than literacy! It’s appalling, isn’t it? I saw the notice tucked away in the Plumstead Progress. Honestly, you’d think they’d make a bigger deal of shutting down a library. Especially ours. Old Man Hemmings practically  lives  there. He’ll be devastated. Exactly! And the kids! Where are they going to go after school? It's a safe space, it offers computers for homework… it's not just books, David. It’s a community hub. We  have  to do something. I was thinking… a petition. A proper, online one, and paper copies we can leave in local shops. A petition’s a good shout. Gets people involved. I can help with that. I’m reasonably tech-savvy, can set up a Change.org one, no problem. Though I'm dreading the shift rotas this week, so time might be tight. They’ve stuck me on late nights again. Oh, you poor thing. Still? Is it because of Brenda leaving? They always pile it on when someone leaves, don't they? That's what I suspect. They’re ‘restructuring’, apparently. Which means fewer people doing more work for the same money. It’s the same old story. Honestly, sometimes I think I need brain training just to remember what department I even  work  in anymore. You and me both. My transcription work is getting… repetitive. Long stretches of legal jargon. I’m starting to forget how to form a proper sentence myself. Speaking of brain training, I was reading about mnemonics the other day – apparently, they’re surprisingly effective. Mnemonics? Like… ROY G. BIV for the colours of the rainbow? Exactly! Or ‘Never Eat Shredded Wheat’ for the Great Lakes. Apparently, building those little mental frameworks helps with recall. Maybe we should employ some for remembering all the arguments  against  demolishing the library. "L-I-B-R-A-R-Y... Locals Invest Brilliantly, Resisting Arbitrary Removal of Yesteryear!" That’s… impressively terrible. But I like it! Actually, focusing on the benefit to locals is a good angle. We need to get the stories of people who genuinely use the library. Old Man Hemmings, definitely.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the cheek of ‘em. Knocking on the door, two of ‘em, bright as buttons, all smiles. Jehovah’s Witnesses, naturally. Said they wanted to ‘share a comforting thought’. Comforting thought! At half past eleven on a Tuesday morning, trying to sell me religion. Always a polite bunch, though, aren't they? Can’t fault ‘em for effort. Old Mrs. Henderson down the road, she got proper hooked, you know. Went to all their meetings. Oh, poor Margaret! She was a lovely woman. A bit lonely after George went, I suppose. Easy to get drawn in when you’re feeling vulnerable. Though I’ve always thought it a bit odd, going door-to-door like that. Makes you wonder what they're  really  up to. Exactly! And the literature, piles of it! I tried to be polite, said I was quite content with my own beliefs, but they just kept going on. Reminded me a bit of trying to explain Brexit to Brenda, frankly. Endless loop. Now  that's  a comparison! Brenda hasn’t forgiven me for voting Leave, she hasn’t. Still brings it up at every family gathering. "Arthur," she says, "you've ruined the country!" Oh, Brenda and her politics. She’s a force of nature, that one. Still, it's good she cares. Though honestly, does anyone really understand what's going on with taxes these days? It's all so complicated. It is a mess. And speaking of messes… Have you seen old Mr. Peterson’s garden? It’s gone completely to seed. He used to take such pride in his roses. Now it’s just nettles and… well, just a general state of chaotic abandonment. Poor chap. He hasn’t been the same since Elsie went. Lost all his spark, he did. Remember when he used to win all the prizes at the village fete? Best Victoria sponge, best marrow… Oh yes! And Elsie’s knitting! She could knit anything. I remember she made little hats for all the babies in the village. You hardly see that kind of thing anymore. It's all disposable now, isn't it? That’s true. Everything’s so fleeting. Which reminds me, have you two managed to book a table at The Crown for next week? I fancy a proper roast. I tried, but they're completely booked solid until the following Tuesday.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of logs we’ve gone through this winter is startling. I thought we’d have some left over from last year, but no. It’s like they vanish into thin air. Well, with the weather being as consistently cold as it has, I suppose it’s not entirely surprising. Still, we should definitely get a bigger stack ordered before next winter. Perhaps from that place near Melton Mowbray? They deliver, don’t they? Melton Mowbray? Goodness, are we resorting to industrial logging now? We used to get ours from Old Man Hemmings, just down the lane. Proper seasoned oak, that was. Much better than anything you'll find in a yard. Hemmings retired twenty years ago, Margaret. You remember perfectly well we had to find a new supplier then. Though, I will admit, his logs  were  excellent. This stuff is perfectly good, Eleanor. Burns well enough. It does burn well, Dad. It’s just… the cost. It’s creeping into the budget, and with the rising price of everything else… Speaking of rising prices, have you two tried that new Italian place on the High Street? “Bella Notte”? It’s ridiculously good, but… not cheap. Italian? Oh, no thank you. Far too much garlic. And frankly, I prefer a good, honest roast. Though, I did see a lovely antique shop when we were parking. Had a rather charming little whatnot shelf. You and your whatnot shelves, Margaret. Always have been a magpie for a bargain. I told you we shouldn’t have taken the scenic route through the village. Delayed us getting here by a good fifteen minutes. No worries at all, Mum. We’re just glad you both made it. How was your journey from Edinburgh? Was the train alright, Dad? Perfectly adequate. Though the young man next to me was determined to tell me  all  about his trip to Tokyo. Apparently, the vending machines are extraordinary. Said he bought a suit from one. Ludicrous. A suit from a vending machine? That  is  quite something. Things have certainly changed since your last trip abroad, haven’t they? Oh, travelling! I do miss travelling. We used to go to France every summer. Proper French cuisine, not this…fusion nonsense. Honestly, have you seen Mrs. Higginbottom next door? She's clearly had work done. Absolutely dreadful. I’m thinking of getting the armchair re-upholstered. It's starting to look a bit threadbare.

…and honestly, the whole thing’s a fiddle. A complete and utter fiddle. They tell you one thing, then it’s another entirely. I swear, these council tax bands haven’t been looked at properly since… well, since I were a lad! You and me both, Arthur. My band seems alright, but Old Man Hemmings down the road, his is ridiculous. He's built an extension, see, a proper nice one, but they haven’t reassessed him. Says he’s written letters and letters. Useless. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? My sister in Harrow, she’s having the same trouble. They’re threatening to put her up a band because a few new houses have been built nearby. As if  she’s  responsible for new builds! It’s infuriating. Exactly! And it’s all down to the fact nobody understands how these things  work . I was looking at houses, you know. Just browsing, mind you. Not seriously thinking about moving, not at my age, but just…seeing what’s out there. Oh? Whereabouts? Still Norfolk, I presume? Don’t fancy you trekkin’ off to Scotland! No, no, still Norfolk. Found a little place near Brancaster Staithe. Quite remote, looked lovely in the pictures. But then you start looking at the details… stamp duty, solicitor’s fees, the surveys… it’s a mortgage in itself just to  buy  the place! Then there’s the talk of capital gains tax if you ever sold it. Don’t even mention taxes! It’s enough to give anyone a headache. Honestly, they seem to invent new ways to take our money every year. And all this talk about increasing the state pension age… it's scandalous. We paid into it all our lives! They say we're living longer. That's their excuse, innit? Longer to spend the pension they're delaying giving us! I remember when 65 was the magic number. Now it's creeping towards 70. It's the young 'uns who'll suffer, though. They won't have anything left. I was trying to explain to my grandson the other day about ISAs and pensions, and he just looked at me blankly. All he cares about is his phone and that…that TikTok thing. They live in a different world, don't they? Though, I have to admit, I enjoy watching a bit of YouTube myself. My granddaughter showed me this channel about decluttering.

…and honestly, the fella in the shop just shrugged. “Out of warranty,” he said. Like it’s  my  fault the graphics card decided to give up the ghost after eighteen months! Eighteen months, I tell ya! Eighteen months is rubbish, Dad. My computer’s three years old and still going strong. Mostly because you built it, though. Aye, well,  this  one was a pre-built. Me trying to save a bit of time, you see. Big mistake. I shoulda just put the hours in. Now I'm looking at a hefty bill, or spending the weekend wrestling with soldering irons. Honestly, Liam, you and your computers. You'd think you were building rockets, the amount of stress you put yourself under. Don't you think you should just bite the bullet and pay for the repair? It'll be less hassle. Less hassle, and a hundred and fifty quid lighter! I’m thinking I could pick up a used card, maybe, and try to fit that. It’s just…I  hate  being ripped off, you know? Sticky out! Sticky out! Oh, love, let Daddy finish talking. Yes, you have lovely sticky-out ears, just like your father. Remember when we tried to get those ear flaps for you to hold them down? That lasted about five minutes. Five minutes, that's generous. It was more like five  seconds . He just pulled them straight off and tried to eat them. Anyway, back to the computer… speaking of things needing repair, has anyone thought about rugby training tomorrow? Young Finn’s match is on Saturday, and I need to confirm if I’m driving. I think Ben’s mum said she'd do the driving, Dad. I was talking to him at school. I need to practice my passing though, I missed loads today. Right. And while you’re both talking rugby, I’m trying to figure out what we're doing for dinner. This chicken is almost ready, but what goes  with  it? I was thinking fajitas, but I'm out of decent fajita sauce. Fajitas sound grand. I can run to the shop after I've wrestled with this laptop for a bit. They'll have fajita sauce, surely. Although, knowing my luck, they’ll only have the sweet chilli one. Drives me mad, that. Give me a proper smoky salsa any day. Can we have proper peppers with it, Dad?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of glitter that ended up in the living room after the fairy garden building was…concerning. I'm still finding it. But it  sparkled ! The fairies needed sparkle, Miss Emily! They did, yes, they absolutely did. Though, perhaps not quite enough to resemble a disco ball. Leo, are you still attempting a handstand against the fridge? It doesn’t look terribly stable. Almost…almost got it! This pizza is making me strong! It's got pepperoni! It  is  a particularly robust pepperoni. Right, so, pizza-fuelled strength aside, we need to talk about Saturday. Aunt Carol is very excited about your party outfits. I want the sparkly dress! The one with the twirly bits! No fair! I want to wear  my  dinosaur costume! Everyone likes dinosaurs! Now, now. We talked about this. The dinosaur costume is brilliant, Leo, truly. But Aunt Carol’s party is a bit…dressy. How about your blue shirt and smart trousers? But dinosaurs are smarter than shirts! They lived a long time ago! A very good point. But sometimes, we dress up for fun, even if it doesn't involve being the king of the dinosaurs. Speaking of fun… did you two manage to explain to Grandad what you wanted for pudding? He looked utterly bewildered when you started listing every flavour of ice cream imaginable. I told him I wanted strawberry  and  chocolate  and  mint choc chip  and … …and bubblegum and pistachio and rum raisin, apparently. It’s a wonder he didn’t need a calculator. Leo, did you contribute to the Grandad-confusion? I told him about the Loch Ness Monster! The Loch Ness Monster? And how did that fit into the pudding conversation? Because Nessie likes ice cream too! She needs something cold to swim in! She lives in cold water already! Silly! But  really  cold water! Like, ice cream cold! That is… a surprisingly logical argument, actually. Although I suspect Nessie gets by just fine with the natural temperature of Loch Ness. We’re getting sidetracked. This is what happens when we talk. I always say we're terrible at staying on topic. What's 'sidetracked'? It means we start talking about one thing, and then end up talking about something else completely. Like ice cream, dinosaurs, and the Loch Ness Monster instead of party outfits. Can we talk about adding up now? I learned about adding today!

…and honestly, the mussels were  massive . I’ve never seen anything like it. Proper king scallops too, not those tiny ones you get at home. Did you try the Malvazija, Mum? It was really crisp, perfect with the seafood. Aye, I did, love. Lovely bit of wine, it was. A little dry for my usual, mind, but I’d happily have another. This whole place is just… peaceful, isn’t it? Beats Bolton, hands down. Even if it  is  a bit roasting. Honestly, I’m melting. It’s not  that  hot. I swam in the pool for ages this morning. It was dead good. Proper big, that pool. Bigger than Mr. Henderson’s, definitely. You’re always comparing everything to Mr. Henderson’s pool, aren’t you, Leo? Though, you're right, this  is  a rather impressive spread. And this restaurant, Istria… a lovely hidden gem. My driver, Ante, recommended it. He’s a local, knows all the best places. Ante’s brilliant! He took us to Rovinj yesterday, didn’t he? Absolutely stunning. So much prettier than Porec, I thought. All those little cobbled streets… I got some amazing photos. Porec was alright. A bit too… touristy, for my liking. Packed full of Germans, all lathered in suncream. Still, the basilica was beautiful. I’m glad we went. Though goodness knows how anyone manages to navigate those immigration officers at the airports these days. They were giving me the stink eye at Manchester, just because I had a slightly wonky passport photo. They’re under immense pressure, you know. Post-Brexit, increased security… it's a difficult job. Though, a little courtesy wouldn’t go amiss. Speaking of pressure, did you see that thing about the new Ebola outbreak in Uganda? Rather frightening. Oh, God, don’t even. I saw something on the news. It's awful. Makes you appreciate being on holiday, I suppose. Trying  not  to think about it. Actually, thinking about travelling… where are you wanting to go next, Dad? You mentioned Japan, ages ago. Japan is definitely on the list. Though, increasingly, I’m fascinated by South America. Peru, Bolivia… the ancient cultures, the landscapes. It's a completely different world. Before that though, perhaps a bit closer to home. Spain perhaps? Can we go on a safari? I wanna see lions! And giraffes! A safari? Oh, love, that’s a bit expensive, isn’t it?

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the cheek of ‘em. Another letter. Saying I owe ‘em for PPI. PPI! I never  had  PPI! It’s just… relentless, innit? They reckon it's from… oh, what was it? Some bank I’ve never even heard of. Oh, Stanley, bless you. It’s the same with me, you know. Getting letters about things from years ago. Seems they just dredge it all up and hope you’ll pay something rather than argue. Honestly, it's daylight robbery. Did you bin it straight away? Binned it! I practically set fire to it! Though, I suppose I should keep the envelopes, just in case. Old habits, you see. Used to keep everything, just in case. My mother was like that. A right hoarder, she was. Actually, Stanley, concerning these letters... I had a look at your post yesterday, while I was here. And the phrasing is… aggressive. You really shouldn’t ignore these completely. They  can  take you to court, even for a small amount. Court?! Good heavens, Reginald! At my age? What would they do, cart me off in an ambulance? Reginald’s right, Dad. Best to write a strongly worded letter, stating you never took out PPI. There are templates online, I can find one for you this afternoon. It's a nuisance, but avoiding it will likely make things worse. Speaking of nuisances, has anyone seen that gardening magazine? The one with the article on growing sweet peas? I was going to copy out the bit about staking them. They said to use hazel sticks, which sounds rather lovely, doesn’t it? Sweet peas? You and your gardening, Doreen. Don’t know how you have the energy. I was thinking of just relaxing in front of the telly later. There’s that documentary on about Norwich Cathedral, you know. Been meaning to watch it. Always loved the singing there and at the Abbey. Used to go with my mother. Oh, Norwich Cathedral! Lovely. Did you ever sing in the choir, Grandad? No, no singing  in  the choir, lad. My voice is more suited to… well, not singing. But I used to enjoy listening. Such beautiful acoustics. It reminds me of when we’d go to see Auntie Elsie. She lived near Bury St Edmunds, did Elsie. Always had a party going on. Elsie  loved  a party! Always did. And the food!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is just  insane . Seventeen essays to mark tonight, minimum. All on the passive voice. You’d think it was a life or death skill, wouldn’t you? Seventeen, you say? Och, that  is  a bit much. Still, at least it’s…contained, isn’t it? You’re marking in your own home, at your own pace. This courtroom… it’s a constant stream. One minute it’s a shoplifting case, the next a domestic dispute. Never a dull moment, but draining. Draining is the word. I sometimes wonder if they truly  understand  the implications of what’s happening in there. The young ones especially. They just seem… lost. It's a bit like teaching grammar sometimes, you're explaining something fundamental and they just… blank. Aye, well, a lot of them haven't had the chances you and I did, love. My grandson, wee Jamie, he's doing alright at school, thankfully. But even  his  teachers are saying the funding's getting tighter. Cuts everywhere. It’s a shame, really. Access to a good education shouldn’t depend on where you live, or how much your parents earn. Absolutely. It’s heartbreaking. I try to make my lessons engaging, relate them to real life. Talk about how language shapes perception, even in the justice system. The way things are  worded  can make all the difference. But you're right, the system feels…under pressure. Have you noticed more cases lately? Oh, significantly. I think it's a lot to do with everything being so expensive these days. People are desperate. And the weather! Honestly, this constant rain… it feels like autumn in July. It’s unsettling. You think it’s down to this climate change business, don’t you? I’m starting to. It’s hard to ignore the evidence, isn’t it? And it's not just the weather. The rising cost of everything… even getting here today was a nightmare. The train was delayed again, and then packed like sardines. They keep talking about investment in the railways, but I’m not seeing it. Tell me about it! I drive, you know. And the petrol prices are scandalous. I used to enjoy a wee drive to visit my sister in Dundee, but now it costs a fortune in fuel. Keeps me closer to home, which isn’t always a bad thing, mind you.

…and honestly, the best part of the day wasn’t  getting  the good grade back on the essays, it was seeing your faces when I told you. That was brilliant. Truly brilliant. Mummy, you got a  really  good grade! Like, a superstar grade? A pretty superstar grade, yes. A very, very good one. Enough to make me do a little happy dance, which you both witnessed, didn’t you? You wobbled! You wobbled like jelly! I did  not  wobble like jelly! Perhaps a… energetic shimmy. But that’s because I was happy. And talking of happiness… what makes  you  two happy? Ice cream! And puppies! And… and sparkly things! Dinosaurs! And building really, really tall towers! And… if I had a million pounds! A million pounds, eh? What would you  do  with a million pounds, my clever boy? I’d buy ALL the dinosaurs! The big ones, the small ones, even the ones with feathers! And a HUGE garden for them to live in! And a robot to feed them. Ooh! And I’d buy a castle! A pink castle with a slide that goes straight into a swimming pool full of… of gummy bears! Gummy bears? Now that’s ambitious. A swimming pool of gummy bears sounds…sticky. But yummy! Very yummy, I’m sure. Hmm. It’s interesting, isn’t it? You both immediately think of things to  buy . Do you think having lots of money makes people happy? Yeah! Then you don’t have to worry about anything! You can just… have it. That’s a good point. It would certainly take away some worries. But do you think it makes people  always  happy? Think about people we know… or even characters in stories. Miss Higgins at school has lots of jewellery and she’s always… frowning. That’s a very astute observation, darling. Miss Higgins does seem to have a permanent frown. And you’re right, she has lots of nice things. So maybe having things isn't the same as being happy. Maybe you’re happy if you have friends? And cake? You're onto something crucial there. Friends  definitely  make me happy. And cake is a very good bonus. But it's more than just having them, isn't it? It's  doing  things with them. It’s sharing silly jokes, and helping each other, and feeling like you belong. Like when we built that fort in the garden?

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels a bit pointless. Like, why are we even learning about the intricacies of Victorian poetry when, realistically, it’s not going to help me design the next big thing in AI? Harsh, man. Mrs. Davies is a legend. And poetry  does  help you think, apparently. Mr. Harrison went on about symbolism and all that yesterday. It’s supposed to make you a better… communicator? A better communicator for writing code? I doubt it. I was reading about this guy, a teenager actually, who’s already patented a new type of solar panel. Way more efficient than anything currently on the market. He’s getting offers from investors left, right and centre.  That’s  what I want to be doing. Not analysing metaphors. Wow, seriously? A teenager? That’s mental. What’s he, like, a genius or something? Well, he's clearly switched on. He said he got the idea thinking about how butterfly wings absorb light. Completely random, apparently. He’s from California, though. Always seems to be the Americans who are doing this stuff. Probably because they’ve got all the money. Speaking of money… Dad was going on about investments again at dinner. He’s convinced everything’s going to be made in China soon and he’s looking at putting some money into tech companies over there. China, huh? That’s… interesting. I mean, they  are  massive, aren’t they? Like, the population alone… it's insane. It makes you think about how quickly the whole world is changing. Remember when everyone was obsessed with India being "the next big thing"? Now it’s all about China. Exactly! Dad keeps saying they're cornering the market on rare earth minerals, which apparently are crucial for all sorts of tech. He reckons if you want to invest in the future, you need to invest in whoever controls those resources. He was rambling on about supply chains and geopolitical strategy. It went way over my head. Sounds like Dad. Mine just keeps going on about property being the only safe bet. Boring. But honestly, investing feels… scary. Like, you could lose everything. That’s what I said! He kept saying “calculated risks” and “diversification,” but it just sounds like gambling with extra steps. This guy with the solar panel, though, he’s not relying on luck. He made something useful. That feels… reliable.

… honestly, I think that run was a bit ambitious for a first one back. My legs are  burning . And I’m pretty sure I saw a small child overtake me. A  small child , Bev! Oh, don’t be so dramatic, Sarah! It was a blue, relax. You haven’t skied in… what, three years? It’s going to take a bit to get your ski legs back. Besides, Bulgarian ski instructors are excellent. They probably nurture tiny skiing prodigies. Prodigies or not, it was humiliating. And I’m still convinced my ankle’s a bit dodgy. Remember what happened in Andorra? I don't want a repeat of that. Three days in a cast, missing all the après-ski… no thank you. Oh, stop dwelling on Andorra! That was a freak accident, a rogue patch of ice. This is Bansko, beautiful sunshine, perfectly groomed slopes… relatively speaking, of course. And your ankle looks fine. You’re just being a worrywart. How’s the goulash? It’s actually pretty good for a hotel restaurant. The goulash is… surprisingly edible. Though I’d kill for a proper Sunday roast right now. Mum’s, preferably. She does the Yorkshire puddings  just  right. Speaking of Mum, have you spoken to Dad recently? He was insistent on daily updates. I did, this morning. He and Mum are fine. Dad was mostly concerned about the snow conditions, naturally. He’s already planning next year’s trip, apparently. Wants to come to Bansko with us, and Uncle Geoff. Oh, heavens. Dad, Geoff, and two sets of questionable skiing abilities… that sounds like a disaster waiting to happen. Though it  would  be nice to have them here. It’s just… a lot. I know, I know. But think of the stories! And Mum would love to see us both actually enjoying ourselves on the slopes. Remember how she worried when we first started? "Too dangerous!" she said. Now look at us, seasoned skiers in Bulgaria! Seasoned is generous. More like… occasionally upright. Listen, about tonight… Are you still up for trying that ‘Happy End’ bar you read about? Apparently, they do live music. Absolutely! I need to forget my own less-than-graceful attempts at skiing, and a bit of live music sounds perfect. What about Emily and Mark? Are they joining us? They were looking a bit tired after their lesson this morning. I messaged them. Emily said Mark’s back is playing up, so they’re going to have a quiet night.

… honestly, Derek, you’re tilting your head all wrong. It’ll be wonky. Just  still  now. Right, almost there… just a tiny snip… oh! Oh dear. Ouch! What was that? Felt a bit… close. Oh, blast it all! I am  so  sorry! I thought it was just a stray bit of grey…it’s… it’s a stripe, isn’t it? A rather fetching stripe, actually, but undeniably snipped. A fetching stripe I’ve cultivated for twenty years, Margaret! And now… diminished. Slightly. It’s alright, it’ll grow back. More importantly, are we back to the rackets? Because this haircut distraction is not helping my concentration on potential profits. Profitable rackets! That’s what we need to focus on. Forget the follicular tragedy. Right. Strings. The breaking, specifically. You were saying about reinforcing the areas around the grommets? Cable ties, you suggested? Precisely. Small, black cable ties. Discreet. We’re not looking to  replace  strings, Margaret, we’re looking to  extend  their life. A preventative measure. Think of it – a ‘String Saver’ kit. We could sell it online, at local badminton clubs… And the costings? Cable ties are cheap enough, but the packaging, the instructions… and the marketing. We’d need a proper leaflet. A website, even. Website later. Let’s start small. Leaflets are fine. Cost of the ties themselves, say, ten pence each. We pack five in a kit, plus a little tool for tightening them – maybe a repurposed teaspoon handle? So 50p for materials. Selling price… a pound fifty? Two pounds? Two pounds sounds more… respectable. But what about different racket types? The dimensions of the grommets vary, don’t they? And the string tension. A heavy-hitting player needs stronger reinforcement. Good point. Perhaps different sized cable ties. A ‘Standard’ kit, a ‘Pro’ kit… we could even offer a ‘Fleet’ kit for clubs! Buy ten, get one free! A ‘Fleet’ kit? Derek, you’re sounding awfully corporate. It’s cable ties, not aircraft carriers. It’s a turn of phrase, Margaret! A marketing term! Think of the collective noun! A fleet of rackets! Actually, it’s quite clever. I suppose… But thinking practically, would this even work for school use? Primary school rackets are different to adult ones. The strings are usually much… softer. True. Primary schools might not be our initial target. Secondary school badminton clubs, though… huge potential market. They go through strings like nobody’s business, those teenagers!

…and honestly, I still don’t get it. All that splashing about with paint, lookin’ like a right mess, and people callin’ it ‘art’? Back in my day, art was a nice landscape, maybe a portrait. Somethin’  recognisable , see? Oh, Harold, you’re such a traditionalist. It's not always about representation, is it? It's about how it  makes  you feel. That Jackson Pollock stuff, all the drips and splatters… it's chaotic, yes, but it can be quite powerful. Gran, it’s about deconstructing the idea of art itself, really. Pollock wasn’t trying to paint a picture  of  something, he was trying to paint a picture  about  painting. About the process, the energy… Paintin’ about paintin’? Sounds a bit…roundabout, don’t it? Waste of good paint, if you ask me. My mother, bless her, she did a lovely oil of the Broads. That was art. You could  see  it was the Broads. Smelled of linseed oil, it did. It’s a shift in perspective, Harold. Think about it like music. You don't need lyrics to have a powerful piece of music, do you? It's about the harmony, the rhythm, the texture of the sound. Abstract art is similar. It’s about the composition, the colour, the texture of the paint. Exactly! And it’s a reflection of the time it was created in, isn't it? Pollock was painting after the war, a time of great upheaval and anxiety. That chaos is in his work. Anxiety? Good grief. We had rationing!  That  was anxiety! Though I suppose there was a bit of a dust up with the Germans…but still, a nice picture of a windmill is far more cheerful than a bit of splattered paint, I reckon. It's not about cheerful, Gran. It's about… honest expression. And it’s not just Pollock. Think about Rothko, the colour field paintings. Massive blocks of colour. They're meant to envelop you, evoke a feeling. Have you seen any of his work? Rothko? Sounds German. Not keen on Germans, still. Reminds me of…well, never you mind. Is it colourful, then? Like a sunset? Some of it is. Lots of maroons and oranges and yellows. But it's less about depicting a sunset and more about creating an  experience  of warmth or melancholy. We took Sophie to the Tate Modern a few years back, remember?

…and honestly, Chloe just  had  to tell everyone about her promotion on Instagram before her boss even officially announced it. Like, who does that? It’s just… desperate. Oh, Chloe. Classic Chloe. Always needing validation. It's exhausting just  knowing  her, let alone being friends with her. Did she at least get the promotion? Apparently. But Dave was saying it was only because someone else left, it wasn't a genuine upward move. So it feels even more…performative, you know? Ugh. Right, I need wine. Speaking of performative, my inbox is a disaster. Three project updates due Monday and I haven’t even  started  one. Don’t tell me. Is it the Henderson account again? They’re the bane of your existence. Honestly, they change their minds more often than I change my socks. Worse. It's the "Innovative Sustainable Packaging" thing. Which is ironic, because the whole project feels incredibly unsustainable – mainly on my sanity. And the brief is just…circular. “We want innovative, but also familiar. Sustainable, but cost-effective. Cutting edge, but classic.” What does that EVEN mean? The English language is a cruel mistress. Seriously. It’s designed to frustrate project co-ordinators and mental health nurses alike. I had a patient today tell me they were experiencing ‘existential dread with a side of mild inconvenience.’ A  side of mild inconvenience ?! Oh my god. They’re just making things up now, aren't they? We need a new word for people who over-intellectualise their feelings. I’d settle for people who just… say how they feel, plainly. It’d save me about three hours of assessment time per patient. Anyway, enough work talk. It's Friday. Should we be tackling this mountain of washing up, or shall we actively embrace procrastination? Procrastination, 100%. It's a vital part of the weekend ritual. Though, looking at it, maybe a tactical clean is necessary. It's starting to grow its own ecosystem. You’re not wrong. Remember when we tried that KonMari method? Lasted about five minutes. We ended up just shoving everything into the spare room. It's a strategic storage solution! Besides, I’m fairly sure half my clothes are in there, strategically hidden from any potential motivation to go to the gym. Fair enough. I'm much the same. Speaking of hidden things, did you ever find that blue sweater I lent you? The cashmere one?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails Mr. Harrison expects me to deal with is ridiculous. It's like he thinks I have a clone. Did you have a better day battling the silicon demons, darling? Silicon demons is a good one. Pretty much sums it up. Old Man Hemmings decided  today  was the day to “explore the cloud.” At seventy-two. It involved a lot of gentle redirection and explaining that the cloud isn't a fluffy white thing in the sky. Oh, Hemmings. He’s a character. Still, sounds exhausting. You deserve a large gin and tonic. Though, honestly, we’re both leaning a bit heavily on those lately, aren't we? Is that a judgement, or an observation? Because if it's a judgement, I'll point out you polished off half a bottle of Pinot Grigio last night while watching  Great British Bake Off . Fair point. It was a stressful day! And Mary Berry just brings out the best – and the wine – in me. Still, I’m trying to cut back on the cigarettes. I’ve got down to… well, less than a packet a day. Which is progress, I suppose. Progress is progress. I tried to give them up years ago. Lasted about four hours. Then Mrs. Peterson at number 38 tripped on the paving stones and needed comforting. A cigarette felt… appropriate at the time. Exactly! It’s the rituals, isn’t it? The little crutches. It makes me think about that article I was reading, about how intelligence doesn’t necessarily equate to common sense. Seems like a lot of very clever people make spectacularly silly decisions. You mean like trying to explain the internet to a retired accountant? Amongst other things. It was about cultural differences too. Apparently, in some cultures, directness is considered incredibly rude, whereas here, we pride ourselves on it. It made me think about how frustrating it can be when you’re trying to communicate with people from different backgrounds. It’s true. I did a project with a team in India a few years ago. Took me a while to understand why they weren't volunteering opinions in meetings. Turns out, challenging a senior colleague directly is… frowned upon. Precisely! And then there's the whole feminism conversation. I’ve been reading a lot lately about intersectionality, and how different women experience oppression in vastly different ways. It's… complex.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of mud was astonishing. I thought we’d be digging it out of our ears for a week! Did you two have a good time despite being practically coated in the stuff? It was  amazing ! The piglets were SO fluffy! And I got to hold a chick! A real, tiny chick! I wanted to hold a chick too, but it pecked my finger. Oh, darling, that’s just a little nip. They don’t mean any harm. You were probably being a bit too…enthusiastic with your grabbing. I wasn’t! I was being gentle! Alright, alright. Gentle as a…tractor, perhaps? Look, the important thing is you both enjoyed it. Did you manage to feed the sheep? Yes! They were really greedy, Mummy. They tried to eat my gloves! Well, they  would  try, wouldn’t they? Everything looks like food to a sheep. Right, who wants some toast? You two need to refuel after all that farmyard adventure. Chocolate spread! Chocolate spread it is. Though perhaps not  too  much. Speaking of refuelling, how was school today? Any particularly exciting news? Miss Davies said I did really well in writing! I wrote a story about a unicorn who lived on a farm! Oh, that’s wonderful, sweetheart! I’m so proud of you. A unicorn on a farm…that sounds rather delightful. And you, my little rascal? Anything interesting happen at school? Nothing. Nothing at all? Come on, Leo. Mrs. Peterson emailed me this morning. Something about an incident in art class? It wasn’t my fault! Well, that’s a start. What wasn’t your fault? Thomas kept poking me with his paintbrush, and then I… I accidentally knocked over the paint. Accidentally? The email said a  significant  amount of purple paint ended up on Thomas. He started it! I told him to stop, but he didn’t! It’s not nice to poke people with paintbrushes, Leo! You didn't see anything! Right, okay. Let’s all calm down. Leo, it's not acceptable to retaliate, even if Thomas  was  poking you. We’ve talked about using our words, remember? And paint doesn't just magically jump onto someone. It sounds like you need to apologize to Thomas and maybe help Mrs. Peterson clean up. Fine. But he’s still mean. I’ll talk to Mrs. Peterson, okay? We'll get this sorted. Now, eat your toast.

…and honestly, the tension was  palpable . Like, you could cut it with a knitting needle. Old Mrs. Higgins practically vibrated with outrage when Brenda admitted she’d unravelled half a jumper to make a scarf for her grandson. Unravelled! The audacity! Oh, the knitting circle dramas. They sound… intense. It’s a world away from particle physics, thankfully. Although, some academic debates  are  pretty cutthroat. Just less wool involved. Less wool, more ego. Aye, I can imagine. Did you see that article about Benedict Cumberbatch learning to knit? Apparently, it’s “therapeutic” for him during breaks from filming. Honestly, the man’s a national treasure, but knitting? Feels a bit… performative, doesn't it? Perhaps. Though, I wouldn’t knock it. Anything that helps manage stress. And he probably has someone to teach him, so he doesn't end up with a misshapen mess like I did when I tried to learn from YouTube. Remember that scarf? It looked like a particularly disastrous geological formation. Oh,  please . I'm still trying to forget the "scarf". It was… structurally unsound. No, seriously though, it’s the celebrities doing it for the ‘aesthetic’ that gets me. Like, suddenly everyone needs a rustic hobby. Speaking of aesthetics, have you been following the Team GB selection for the Olympics? A little. It’s a bit overwhelming, isn't it? All the disciplines. I’ve been trying to keep up with the swimming, obviously. I always get invested in the 100m freestyle. Pure adrenaline. Me too! But I’m more excited about the artistic gymnastics, surprisingly. The sheer athleticism  and  the artistic expression… it's brilliant. It reminds me a bit of sculpture, actually. You were saying you wanted to go to the Fitzwilliam Museum next week? I did! I was reading about that new temporary exhibition – the pre-Raphaelite drawings. Apparently, it's a real find. They've uncovered a lot of sketches that weren't previously attributed. I think you’d really enjoy it, especially considering your obsession with Rossetti. Obsession is a strong word! Appreciative. Very, very appreciative. And yes, I’d love to. It’s ages since we had a proper cultural outing. Everything feels… work, work, work recently. These research grants don’t write themselves, eh? Tell me about it. My supervisor is breathing down my neck about the data analysis. It's like he thinks a groundbreaking discovery will magically  appear  if I just stare at the spreadsheets long enough.

…and honestly, Arthur, queuing for an hour just to  get  into the British Museum? It's a disgrace. A right disgrace! I thought you said you’d booked tickets online? I  did  book tickets, Brenda! For the Egyptian collection. But there was a separate queue for timed entry, and then another queue for security… it was chaos, pure chaos. I thought we'd be alright, getting here for half past ten, but it was already rammed. Rammed is putting it mildly. It was like Piccadilly Circus on New Year's Eve. And elbows, Arthur! People shoving, pushing… Honestly, I nearly lost my handbag twice. I don’t mind a bit of a crowd, I used to deal with thirty screaming teenagers a day, mind you, but this was just stressful. Well, what did you expect? It’s a Sunday, Brenda. And London. Everyone and their dog wants to go to a museum on a Sunday. I thought you’d enjoy seeing the Rosetta Stone, though? You’re always going on about Ancient History with your students. Oh, the Rosetta Stone was lovely, alright. And the mummies were… well, mummies. But honestly, the crowds ruined it. You couldn’t get close enough to  really  see anything. It’s not like when we went to the Walker Art Gallery back home, is it? Peace and quiet. You could actually  look  at the paintings. Different beast, love. London’s on a different scale. Speaking of scale, I was thinking after this, we could try and get into the Science Museum? I read they've got a new IMAX film on about space exploration. It's in 3D. Oh no, Arthur, not another queue! And 3D gives me a headache. Remember that disaster with ‘Avatar’ all those years ago? I felt seasick for a day afterwards. Besides, getting  to  the Science Museum is another hurdle. Getting around on this London transport is a nightmare. Now, Brenda, don’t start on the buses. They're perfectly serviceable. Serviceable? They're packed like sardines! And slow. And confusing. I keep getting lost trying to figure out the zones and the changes. Back in Liverpool, you know where you are with the buses. One route, straight there. Simple. This is all contactless payment and Oyster cards and… Honestly, it’s enough to give someone a migraine. Alright, alright, calm down. We can get the tube. It’s quicker.

… honestly, the traffic getting back from the university yesterday was mental. Absolutely mental. Took me nearly two hours to get home. You wouldn’t believe the scooters, just weaving in and out of everything. Two hours?! Blimey, that  is  bad. I was lucky, finished up a bit earlier and caught the metro. Though even that was packed tighter than a Christmas stocking. Speaking of which… Christmas. Have you started thinking about it at all? Just the beginnings. Mostly stressing about what on earth to get Mum. She says she doesn’t  need  anything. You know how mothers are? It’s a classic. What about you? Any grand plans? Are you sticking with the usual Mancunian Christmas feast? You know me too well. Yorkshire puddings are non-negotiable, even three thousand miles from Yorkshire. I was thinking… we should do something together this year. A proper Christmas dinner, just us and maybe Sarah and David. It feels a bit odd being here, so far from everyone, without at least  attempting  some sort of festive cheer. That’s a brilliant idea, actually. I was feeling a bit lonely about it too. Sarah and David would be great. They haven’t quite got the hang of Chinese Christmas, have they? Last year David tried to explain Boxing Day to a shop assistant… it didn’t end well. Oh, I remember! The look on her face! “A day for giving boxes… to people?” Hilarious. Right, so Christmas dinner at one of our places? Yours is a bit bigger, isn’t it? More space for Yorkshire puddings? It is, yes. And the kitchen’s slightly more… equipped for a full-on roast. Though honestly, sourcing a decent turkey here is a challenge. We might have to compromise. Duck? Goose? Goose sounds a bit… posh, doesn’t it? Let's aim for a turkey, even if it’s a frozen one. We can try and find one that isn’t completely sawdust-filled. What about film-wise? We  have  to have a Christmas movie marathon. Absolutely. It’s the law! I'm lobbying for ‘Love Actually’. It’s terribly cheesy, but it's essential viewing. You'll probably hate it. I will  not  hate it. It’s… acceptable. I’m putting forward ‘Die Hard’. It’s a Christmas movie. Don't argue with me. ‘Die Hard’? Really? Okay, we can compromise on that too. Maybe one cheesy rom-com, one action blockbuster, and one classic.

… honestly, the replies to that tweet were  brutal . Like, I was just sharing a picture of my nan’s cat, and suddenly I’m getting ratioed about the socio-political implications of feline ownership. It’s Twitter, innit? Just a bit of fun. Sounds exhausting, Leo. Seriously. You get so invested in what randoms on the internet think. I deleted the app off my phone weeks ago. Best decision ever. More time for sourdough, less time for… whatever that was. Sourdough sounds  much  better. I’m still dealing with the fallout from Brenda’s review. Brenda? Oh god, not Brenda from last Tuesday? The one who demanded a gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free Victoria sponge? The very same. She left a one-star review saying the atmosphere was “oppressive” and the music was “an assault on the ears”. We were playing acoustic Joni Mitchell! Oppressive! People are genuinely mental. I had a bloke complain his croissant wasn’t  French  enough. Like… mate, I’m in Birmingham, not Paris. I use British butter, it’s fantastic! What does he want? It's always the petty stuff, isn’t it? I saw a restaurant in Margate got absolutely rinsed online because their tables were “too close together”. It was a Tuesday afternoon, and the place was empty! People are just looking for something to complain about. Margate… That's a good shout actually. Remember we were talking about somewhere to go next weekend? We could do a day trip. Apparently, there’s a really cool vintage shop area down by the harbour. Ooh, I’m in. I need a distraction from flour and furious customers. And honestly, a change of scenery. Everything feels a bit… grey here. Yeah, Margate sounds perfect. I’ve been meaning to go check out the Turner Contemporary gallery too. Apparently, it’s pretty wicked, the design and everything. I've heard good things about it. I’m thinking of redesigning the café anyway… it’s just… daunting. I’ve got loads of Pinterest boards, but turning that into a reality is another thing. I want something a bit more… me, you know? Less beige. Beige is the enemy! Definitely ditch the beige. You’ve got a good eye, Chloe. Remember that amazing window display you did for the Christmas market? Everyone was talking about it. Seriously! It was incredible. You could even offer interior design as a side hustle, Chloe.

…and honestly, the slugs have been  terrible  this year. I thought I’d protected the raspberries well enough, but they’ve decimated them. Absolutely decimated. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe it. 'Sberries are yummy! You should get some of those copper rings, Miss Davies. My Grandad uses them for his lettuces. Keeps the slugs off, apparently. They don’t like crawling over copper. Oh, that’s a good tip, Leo. I’ll have to look into that. It's just… disheartening, you know? I was really hoping for a good raspberry crumble this summer. Don't worry, Sarah, we can get some from the shop. Or, even better, we can focus on the blackberries. Remember that massive bush we found on our walk last week? It’s overflowing! True, the blackberries are looking good. Though Oisin here seems to prefer anything that isn’t fruit. Honestly, he’d live on chicken nuggets if I let him. No peas! Peas are icky! Exactly! "Icky" is the official verdict on all things green. It’s like negotiating with a tiny, adorable dictator. I'm the same with sprouts. Absolutely not. Even when Mum tries to hide them in the roast potatoes. I can always  tell . You’re both just like your fathers. Stubborn as mules when it comes to vegetables. Speaking of which, Oisin, just  one  more bite of broccoli? For Nana? Fine. But just one! See? Negotiation. It's a constant process. How are the revision notes coming along, Leo? Big exams next week, aren't they? It’s… going. Science is alright, but history is killing me. All those dates! And battles! It’s just… a lot. It is a lot. Remember when I told you about how I used to revise? Making little song lyrics out of facts? Maybe that could help? You  told  me that! I thought I’d blocked it out. A song about the Battle of Hastings… I don’t think my friends would appreciate that. Oh, come on, Leo, it's a brilliant idea! Anything to make it stick. And honestly, if it gets you through the exams, who cares what your friends think? Exactly! Plus, you could write a ridiculously catchy chorus. It’s all about making it memorable. Have you thought about rewarding yourself afterwards? Maybe an ice cream? Chocolate ice cream! With sprinkles! That’s a good idea, Oisin. Leo, chocolate ice cream with sprinkles is  definitely  on the table if you do well.

…and honestly, the eyebrows were just getting  away  from me. I tried to shape them myself, you know, with those little tweezers? Disaster. Looked like a couple of angry caterpillars had taken up residence. Oh, I know that feeling. I used to try and trim my own fringe. Ended up looking like I’d had a run-in with a hedge trimmer. That’s why I stick to Maureen at the salon now. She knows what she’s doing. Maureen’s a good girl. Been doing my hair for… oh, goodness, near thirty years now. Though it’s not what it was, is it? Getting thinner every year. Not much to  do  with it these days, just a tidy up. You look lovely, Mum. Honestly. It’s just… maintaining things gets harder, doesn’t it? I was thinking about a proper haircut too, actually. Something a bit shorter for the summer. But finding the time… it just vanishes. Tell me about it. Between here and Mrs. Higgins' I'm run ragged. Though she did offer me a lovely victoria sponge yesterday. Said her grandson made it. Sweet kid. You’re too kind, helping everyone out like that. It's lovely of you, truly. I feel bad I haven't been around much lately. Work’s been mental, closing that big deal. Don’t you worry about that, dear. Work’s important. Though it’s not everything. Remember when your father used to talk about nothing  but  accounts? Drove me mad! We need to make time for a proper meal out, all three of us. Not just grabbing something quick. That’s a brilliant idea, Mum! We haven’t done that in ages. Where shall we go? That new Italian place on Bridge Street? Everyone says it’s lovely. Ooh, that sounds nice. Though a bit pricey, isn't it? I remember seeing the menu online and nearly choked. Maybe just a pub lunch then? The Fox and Hounds does a good Sunday roast. The Fox and Hounds is nice, but Mum deserves something a little more special. It's her birthday next month, after all. We can do the pub later. Italian it is! I can book a table for, say, the 15th? The 15th sounds lovely. As long as there's a nice pudding. I’m partial to a good tiramisu. Consider it done. Right, now… how's Uncle George doing?

…and honestly, the amount of puree that ends up  on  him, rather than  in  him, is frankly astonishing. It’s like painting a tiny, orange abstract masterpiece all over his little face. Sounds about right. Leo was the same with sweet potato. I think he enjoyed the sensory experience more than the actual eating. Are you finding he’s taking more now, though? Is he actually swallowing some? A little bit more, yes. He had a decent go at the carrot this morning. Still prefers milk, obviously, but he didn’t actively  spit  it out immediately, which is progress. Dr. Sharma said we should be trying a new texture each week, but honestly, I’m sticking with smooth for as long as humanly possible. The thought of lumps… I get it! It feels weird, doesn’t it? Like you’re trusting him with something really important and slightly terrifying. Speaking of terrifying, Mum keeps asking when we’re all coming down for Sunday lunch. Are you up for it? Oh, goodness. Mum. Always keen for a roast. I am… cautiously optimistic. How's little Alfie doing with the crowds? Last time he was a bit overwhelmed. He’s getting better. I think he's just starting to recognise everyone. But short visits are best. I was thinking we could aim for around one, leave before the inevitable post-lunch slump hits. Is that okay with you? It'll be good for you to get out too, honestly. You’ve been glued to this little one, and rightfully so, but a bit of adult conversation would do you good. You're absolutely right. I’m starting to forget what my own name is. One o'clock sounds perfect. I’ll text Mum and give her a heads-up. What about Tuesday? Any plans? Sarah mentioned she might be free for coffee. Ooh, yes! That would be lovely. I've been meaning to catch up with her properly. I’ve been promising to go to that new art exhibition in town with her for weeks. It’s supposed to be really good. It’s just… finding the time is difficult now. Tell me about it. Life has officially become scheduled in fifteen-minute increments. She understands, though. She's practically an expert on chaos now, with two toddlers under five. True. Right, I'm just thinking ahead to next week. I'm starting those baby sign language classes on Wednesday evening.

… honestly, it’s just so  flat  here, isn’t it? I mean, beautiful, obviously, but after London… it’s a shock to the system. I forgot what it was like to not see a building on the horizon, or… a hill! You say that like it's a bad thing. Flat is good, El. It’s peaceful. London just…  presses  on you. This is breathing space. And it’s not entirely flat, you know. Look over there, towards Brancaster. See that slight rise? That's a hill in Norfolk terms. A slight… ripple, maybe. Honestly, it’s a generous definition. I think the biggest elevation change we’ve encountered today was stepping  over  that gate. Remember when your grandmother used to go on about the Brecks? "Rolling hills," she'd say. Rolling… pebbles, more like. Gran had a romantic view of everything. And the Brecks  are  different. It's not the same gentle farmland we're walking through now. It's more… ancient. Flinty. It feels older, wilder. Plus, you’ve got those pine forests – which admittedly don’t scream “hill,” but break up the flatness. True. I suppose. It's just… I feel like I need to climb something. Anything. I need a proper vantage point, a view. I used to love Primrose Hill, just because you could see absolutely ages. We can get a view. We could drive over to Holkham dunes later. They’re not hills, exactly, but they’re substantial. And you get a proper panoramic of the coast. It’s different to a London view, though. Less… built-up. More sky, more sea. Mmm, that sounds good. Actually, really good. It  is  incredibly beautiful here, I just need to recalibrate my definition of beauty, I think. It’s all so… subtle. Everything blends together. In London, beauty is in the grand gestures, the iconic buildings. Here, it's in the nuances – the different shades of green in the fields, the way the light changes… Exactly! And the villages. Have you noticed how each one is subtly different? Burnham Market is all posh shops and holidaymakers now, of course, but walk a little further and you find places like Cley-next-the-Sea. Still proper, still working. You can almost taste the history. I liked Wells-next-the-Sea. The harbour was lovely, and that little narrow-gauge railway. Very charming. But they all feel… contained, don't they?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of him, thinking he could just cycle down the middle of the road like he owns the place! Nearly gave me a heart attack, I tell you. Nearly took my wing mirror off. Right? Cyclists. It's a constant battle, isn’t it? Especially around here. They just don't seem to grasp the concept of road positioning. I mean, I get it, they’re vulnerable, but… Vulnerable and  annoying . Sorry, it’s just got my goat, that lad. He had headphones in, too! How can you even  hear  anything? It’s bonkers. Reminds me of that documentary we watched about people who think they're cats. Just… disconnected from reality. Okay, that's a bit harsh. But I see your point. It’s the lack of awareness. Anyway, changing the subject before we both end up ranting about Lycra-clad road users… how was your day at work? Still wrestling with linguistic data? Oh, you know. The usual. Trying to make sense of what people  actually  mean versus what they  say . It’s fascinating, honestly, but also incredibly frustrating. Old Mrs. Henderson gave me a recording of her complaining about the price of milk, and it went on for fifteen minutes, practically a monologue. Deciphering the subtext about the perceived decline of British society from a rant about semi-skimmed… that’s my Tuesday sorted. Sounds… enriching. My day involved a lot of spreadsheets and a client who thinks 'ASAP' means 'sometime next week'. Exciting stuff. Speaking of work, did you hear what happened to Liam? Liam? From uni? No! What happened? He was doing so well at that design firm, wasn't he? He was. He got made redundant. Apparently, they're restructuring after losing a big contract. He’s absolutely gutted. He messaged me earlier, said he's scrolling through LinkedIn like it's his full-time job now. Oh, no, that’s terrible! Poor Liam. He was always so dedicated. Remember how he stayed up all night finishing that project in second year? That awful graphic design brief about… what was it? Promotional material for sentient garden gnomes? How could I forget? It was a masterpiece of unintentional comedy. But seriously, this is rough on him. He was really enjoying the work. What do you reckon he'll do? I don’t know. He’s brilliant, he’ll land on his feet.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of buttercups is just ridiculous this year. It’s like a yellow sea. Reminds me of being a kid, making buttercup chains, staining your fingers. Do you remember doing that? Vaguely. Mum always warned me they were poisonous if you swallowed them, so I mostly just admired them from a safe distance. More interested in kicking a football, probably. Still, it's beautiful out here, isn't it? Proper Norfolk. Completely different pace to London. It is. That’s why I love it. You wouldn’t get this… vibrancy of colour near Euston station, would you? Though, thinking about vibrant colours and farms… have you been following the debate about diversifying cash crops? A little. It's mostly blipping past on Twitter, to be honest. Something about moving away from just oilseed rape, right? Trying to encourage more… floral displays for tourism? It's more complex than that. My colleague, Dr. Davies, is doing some fascinating research into the economics of it. Apparently, the initial outlay for things like lavender or sunflowers is substantial, and the return isn’t guaranteed. It’s all about risk mitigation for the farmers, really. They’re used to a very specific market, and these 'beauty crops' are… volatile. Sounds about right. Farmers aren't exactly known for gambling. Speaking of risk, I’m currently wrestling with my research grant proposal. Trying to convince them that a comparative analysis of dialect acquisition in bilingual children  is  vital for societal cohesion. It feels like pulling teeth. Oh, don't even get me started on grant applications. It feels like writing fiction more than academic research sometimes. You have to  sell  the importance, not just demonstrate it. What languages are you focusing on? Welsh and English, primarily. Seeing how children code-switch and how their first language influences their acquisition of the second. It’s surprisingly complex. There's a real interplay between societal prestige and linguistic patterns. It’s not just about grammar. That sounds fascinating. It’s amazing how deeply ingrained language is in identity. It’s funny, isn't it? We both lecture about complex systems – you linguistics, me behavioural economics – and yet sometimes the simplest things, like a field of buttercups, are the most profound. Absolutely. It's a good counterpoint to all the abstract theories, isn’t it? Although, you could probably  apply  behavioural economics to why people are drawn to fields of flowers.

…and honestly, the parking situation ‘round there is a nightmare. Absolute nightmare. I swear, people park on double yellows like it’s a personal challenge. Did I tell you about Old Man Hemmings on Acacia Avenue? He literally argued with a traffic warden for  forty-five minutes  about whether his shopping trolley counted as a vehicle. Seriously? Forty-five minutes? That’s dedication. Or…stubbornness. Probably both. So, this flat… is it near a Metro station at least? Because driving into Newcastle every day… you’d lose the will to live. Aye, thankfully. It’s about a fifteen-minute walk to Haymarket. Not bad at all. It’s a bit…smaller than what we’re used to, mind. But it’s got a little balcony and it's properly soundproofed – which is crucial, considering the neighbours. Apparently, the woman upstairs is a champion clog dancer. A  champion  clog dancer? You’re making this up. I wish I was! My friend Sarah, she lives in the building, told me. Apparently, practices are…enthusiastic. Anyway, what about you? How was the site visit down in London? Any progress on that bridge thing? It’s…going. It's incredibly frustrating though, honestly. Trying to convince people that the supporting structure  needs  to be reinforced. They keep focusing on cost and… well, you know engineers. Always about the budget, never about, like, not having the thing collapse. Sounds about right. My dad was a builder, same story every time. Cheap now, expensive to fix later. Speaking of things collapsing... have you seen what they’re doing with the Angel of the North? They were repainting it when I drove past last week. Looked a bit…dramatic, all scaffolded up. Like it was having a bit of an existential crisis. Really? I hadn't heard. It does need a refresh every now and then, doesn’t it? That steel gets battered by the weather. Though, you're right, it’s a bit jarring to see it not looking…imposing. It’s the iconic Geordie landmark, isn’t it? It's practically a religious experience for visiting football fans. Oh, tell me about it. Remember that time we went to a match and half the stadium was decked out in West Ham colours? Awful. Just awful. And the parking… don't even get me started. It took us an hour to get out of a car park that was basically a muddy field.

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels  wrong . I mean, a full-on public spectacle. Regardless of what he’s accused of, doesn’t everyone deserve some semblance of privacy? It’s just… ghastly. Ghastly is a good word for it, that. All over the telly, every night. Poor woman, she must be absolutely devastated. Though, if he’s done what they say… well. You reap what you sow, don't you? Still, it’s nasty to watch. Exactly! It’s the watching part that gets me. The rubbernecking. And the commentary! Everyone’s an expert overnight. It’s just… draining. Speaking of draining, I really needed this coffee. It’s been a hectic week at work. Tell me about it. This week’s been busy for me too, lots of spring cleans going on. Everyone wants their houses sparkling after the winter. Though, honestly, I prefer it when it’s quieter. More time to… just  be . Be? What’s all this talk about being? You two sound like you’ve got the weight of the world on your shoulders. Oh, hello, Gran! Just a bit of a chat, that’s all. We were talking about the… well, the celebrity trial, mostly. And work. Hmph. Celebrities. Bunch of overpaid youngsters, the lot of them. Never had to work a day in their lives. Give me a good nature programme any day. Did you see that David Attenborough one last night? About the geese? Magnificent. I did catch a bit of it, actually. The way they fly in formation, thousands of them… incredible. Thousands! And to think, they fly all that way, from here to… well, wherever they go. Spain, is it? Or France? Somewhere warm, anyway. Remarkable creatures. Used to see them gathering in the fields near here when I was a girl. Massive flocks, honking away. They still come through, don't they? I saw a small skein heading north last week. Over the fields behind the house. Oh, aye. Plenty of geese around. Though mostly the resident ones. They’re getting bolder, they are. Had one hissing at me in the park the other day. Near the bandstand. Nearly gave me a heart attack! Bold they are! Used to be they'd take one look at a person and be off. Not anymore. They know we won’t hurt ‘em. They rely on a bit of bread, too, don’t they?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I had last week was  criminal . They really need to reassess the workload for Key Stage 3. It’s just unsustainable. Anyway, enough moaning from me. This quiche is absolutely gorgeous, Anon. Did you make the pastry yourself? Thanks, Lucy! Glad you like it. And yes, I did, though I nearly had a disaster. I forgot to add the butter at one point and nearly started again, but thankfully caught myself. It’s a good job I wasn’t rushing, unlike when I’m trying to get little Leo fed and dressed before nursery. Speaking of which… are you still thinking of trying for another one? That’s… complicated. Mark and I are on the fence. Thomas is a handful enough as it is! He’s at that stage where everything is “NO!” and he’s discovered the joy of throwing things. Mostly food, which is just brilliant when you've just spent an hour cooking. But, yeah, we talk about it. I just feel so tired sometimes, the thought of going through another pregnancy and the sleepless nights… it's daunting. I get it. Leo was a surprisingly terrible sleeper to begin with. Everyone told me babies "sleep, feed, poo," but he seemed to mostly just  scream . It took months to get him into any kind of routine. Though he’s a little angel now, mostly. Except when he's decided he wants to rearrange the furniture. What about work? Any news on that Head of Department role you applied for? That’s what I wanted to tell you. I had the interview on Tuesday. It… didn't go well. Oh no! What happened? You’re brilliant at what you do. I think I just completely froze. They asked me about my vision for the department, and I just… rambled. Honestly, it felt like I'd rehearsed three different answers and then delivered none of them. And then Mrs. Davies, you know, the Deputy Head? She kept asking really pointed questions about budget and resources, and I just kept repeating something about "collaborative learning environments." It sounded so empty even  to me . Oh, Lucy, that sounds awful! They  always  ask about budget. It’s a classic interview trap. Did you at least manage to ask some questions back? I tried! But they seemed really keen to steer the conversation back to  my  performance.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt…pointless. Three hours on a Zoom call about streamlining the widget-ordering process when we’re already three weeks behind on everything? It's just moving deckchairs on the Titanic, isn't it? Sounds about right for a Monday, doesn't it? Still, gotta pay the bills. You’re lucky you even  have  a job that requires Zoom calls about widgets. I’m mostly just…filing. Endless, soul-crushing filing. Though Mrs. Hawthorne did ask me for my opinion on the new office plant today, so that was a highlight. A highlight? Seriously? A ficus is the pinnacle of your week? Don’t judge my small joys, Chloe! It's Cambridge, not exactly brimming with excitement at the best of times, especially not in admin. Besides, it got me thinking. I mean, we’re both postgrads, remember? We both spent years busting a gut…for  this ? Don't start. I’m trying not to have an existential crisis before lunchtime. My mum keeps dropping hints about me applying for the Civil Service fast stream. "Stable income, good pension, Chloe!" That's all she cares about. Oh god, the fast stream. Sounds…intense. My mum’s more subtle. Just a lot of wistful sighs when I mention my work, and then casually bringing up Sarah next door, who’s ‘doing so well’ as a solicitor. It’s the comparing, isn’t it? Everyone seems to have a five-year plan, and I'm over here just trying to figure out what I'm having for dinner. Remember when we swore we’d be travel bloggers by now? Backpacking through Southeast Asia, living our best lives? Oh, Chloe, those were the days. Pre-responsibility, pre-mortgage anxiety…pre-realising Southeast Asia is actually really expensive. But honestly? I don't regret the degree, even if I’m not exactly leveraging my Masters in Ancient History. It made me  think , you know? It did. It just feels…underutilised. I keep seeing these recruitment ads for data analysts, saying “fast-track your career!” and thinking I should just bite the bullet and learn Python. But then the thought of spending my evenings staring at code makes me want to curl up and die. You and me both. I've been looking into evening classes – pottery, surprisingly. Apparently, it’s very therapeutic. Plus, you get to make mugs.

…and then ‘e just  looked  at ‘er, proper stunned like. Like a rabbit in headlights, ‘e did. Honestly, I thought ‘e was gonna ask ‘er to dance right then and there. But no, ‘e just… stood there. Oh, you’re killin’ me, Liv! You always see all the drama, don’t ya? Was it Liam, that lad from the pub quiz? Aye, Liam. Though I reckon any lad would’ve been struck dumb lookin’ at Chloe tonight. She looked… well, she looked really nice. Bit more effort than usual, mind. Chloe  always  looks nice. She has that effortless Cambridge thing going on, you know? Everything just…  works  on her. Effortless?! She spent a good hour in the bathroom, Maisie! I heard ‘er! And let’s not start on the fact she’s been ‘borrowing’ my eyeliner for a week now. Oh,  someone's  a bit jealous. Didn’t realise you were harbouring secret feelings for Liam. Don’t be daft, Jess. It’s not about Liam! It’s about Chloe always gettin’ all the attention. And…and Ben practically ignoring me all night. Ben wasn't ignoring you, Olivia. He was talking to Pierre about… was it astrophysics? He gets completely absorbed when he starts talking about that stuff. Absorbed? He didn't even  look  at me when I tried to tell ‘im about me essay. I had a right good point to make, about Brontë sisters and… and just, he wasn't listenin'. And then I saw him laughin' with Chloe about somethin'. Oh, come on now. He probably just thought she was bein’ funny. Chloe’s a bit of a comedian, innit? Remember that time she tried to order snails and accidentally asked for slugs? That was  hilarious , I’ll give ‘er that. But it feels like… she always manages to steal the spotlight. And Ben falls for it every time. He's like a moth to a flame. You're reading too much into this, Liv. Ben genuinely likes Chloe, she's intellectually stimulating. That doesn’t diminish how he feels about you. You’re his girlfriend. But it's always academic stuff with ‘er. I'm not a Cambridge graduate like she is, am I? I’m just… me. From Doncaster. Do I need a PhD just to hold his attention? Oh, don’t talk like that! You’re brilliant! And you’ve got a wicked sense of humour and you’re proper down-to-earth, which is way more important than fancy book learnin’.

…and honestly, the carbonara was  almost  worth the drive back from Birmingham. Almost. It needed a bit more pepper, though, don’t you think, David? Mmmph. Yeah, a good grind of black pepper would’ve perfected it. Though, after dealing with that delivery issue all day, anything vaguely resembling a decent meal felt perfect. Honestly, the warehouse nearly imploded. Imploded? Like,  boom ? Not literally, Leo! Just… chaos. They sent the wrong order to Henderson & Sons. Five hundred garden gnomes instead of industrial sealant. Five. Hundred. Garden gnomes?! That’s brilliant! What did Henderson & Sons say? They weren't amused, Ethan. Not at all. Lots of shouting. Lots of emails. It took four hours to sort out. Which is why I was late getting home. Serves them right ordering so late on a Friday. They always leave everything to the last minute. Anyway, Leo, you were telling us about the hockey match earlier. How did it go? Did you manage to get a goal? Nah, not this time. We lost 3-2. It was a really close game, though. Ben in Year 10 scored a screamer, though! Right in the top corner. Unreal. Ben's good. He’s been practicing loads. Did Mr. Harrison shout much? Just a bit. He shouts at everyone, it's part of his coaching style. Mostly it was about passing, apparently we weren't moving the puck fast enough. It's good to see you’re still enjoying it. It’s such a good outlet. David and I were talking about taking the boys to watch a professional game soon. Maybe the Nottingham Panthers? That sounds good. I’ve always meant to take them. It’s a long drive, though, isn’t it? From here? Not too bad. About an hour and a half. We could make a day of it. Maybe combine it with a bit of shopping or a nice lunch. Can we go to that arcade place in Nottingham? The one with the VR games? We’ll see, Ethan. Let’s sort out the hockey first. David, are you free next weekend? They’re playing the Sheffield Steelers. I think so. Let me check the work schedule. Honestly, things have been mad lately. Speaking of mad, I got an email from Auntie Ji-Hye this morning. Oh? Is everything alright? She was sounding a bit homesick last time we spoke. She's decided she wants to come and visit!

…and honestly, the sheer scale of these trees is just… humbling, isn’t it? I mean, photos don’t do it justice at all. Did you see that one we just passed, the one you could almost drive  through ? Almost! I was bracing myself for Barry to try. He’d absolutely love that. You know, a proper ‘look at me’ moment. Though I suspect the rental agreement might have something to say about altering the vehicle. Knowing Barry, he probably thinks the rental agreement is merely a suggestion. Speaking of which, how  is  he? Last I heard he was still wrestling with that dodgy boiler. Oh, the boiler saga continues. Apparently, it’s escalated. Now it’s not just not working, it’s making… noises. He described it as a ‘metallic groaning’. Mum is losing the plot. She keeps threatening to move in with him just to supervise the repairs. Oh, bless her. She always did mother hen everyone, didn’t she? Even us, well into our thirties. Remember when she packed us both spare jumpers for that camping trip in the Lake District? We were twenty-eight! How could I forget? I was mortified. She insisted we’d get hypothermia. And honestly, it rained the  entire  weekend. She was secretly smug. She just worries, that's all. It’s exhausting being worried about everyone. Still, metallic groaning… sounds ominous. Has he called someone proper out? Or is he still trying to fix it with YouTube tutorials and a wrench? The latter, naturally. He’s convinced he can ‘figure it out’. Says it’s a ‘character-building experience’. He did call a plumber eventually, but the plumber couldn’t come until next week. So he’s battling the groaning beast until then. Honestly, I think he enjoys the drama. He does love a bit of a project, doesn’t he? It’s admirable, in a slightly infuriating way. What about Sarah? How's her new job going? Still loving the marketing world? It's… complicated. She started really enthusiastically, all about ‘synergy’ and ‘brand narratives’ and things I barely understood. But she's finding the office politics quite draining. Apparently, there’s a real power struggle between her boss and the head of sales. Oh, fantastic. Always the office politics.
