Same as the country, really. They keep talkin’ about ‘levelling up’ but all I see is London gettin’ even shinier. Exactly! “Levelling up”. Such a simplistic phrase for such a complex problem. And wasn't Tony Blair the master of that kind of simplification? All soundbites and no real long-term vision. He had a knack for making everything sound… hopeful, even when you knew it wasn't based on anything solid. He was a brilliant communicator, I'll grant him that. But brilliant at  what  is the question, eh? Aye, he could talk the hind legs off a donkey, that one. I remember watchin' him on the telly durin’ the Iraq War. Smooth as you like, makin’ it all sound right and proper. My old man, God rest him, he wasn't havin’ it. Said it was all a load of… well, I won't repeat it here, bein’ in a university office and all. But it weren't pleasant. He felt betrayed, y’know? 'Cause New Labour were supposed to be different. That’s precisely the feeling. There was such a sense of potential wasted. I was teaching at the time, actually. The students were so energized by the prospect of change, and then… disillusionment settled in. It's a pattern, isn't it? Promise, hype, then a slow realization that things aren’t quite what they seem. It is. You see it in football, too.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data in those BNC recordings is just…daunting. Thousands of hours of naturally occurring conversation. It's brilliant for my research, obviously, but sifting through it all to find examples of specific dialect features? It's a slog. I spent three hours yesterday just trying to isolate instances of non-high rising terminal contours in East Anglian speech. Three hours! Oof, sounds rough. You're a braver woman than I am. I deal with enough linguistic chaos just  editing  articles. Someone sent me a piece yesterday riddled with passive voice and split infinitives. It was a crime against grammar, I tell you! I almost messaged them a link to Strunk & White. Oh, you would! You’re such a pedant, Carys. A lovely pedant, but a pedant nonetheless. Speaking of online…have you updated your LinkedIn again? I swear it changes every other week. I did, actually. Added a couple of freelance gigs I picked up. It’s just… feels a bit performative, doesn't it? Like everyone's building this ridiculously polished online persona. It is. It really is. All filters and carefully curated moments. Exactly! It’s exhausting. I’ve started just… ignoring most of it. Except for cute dog pictures, naturally. Honestly, give me pugs over influencers any day. Pugs are the superior life form, agreed. Have you seen Fiona’s new one? Tiny little thing, utterly squashed face. Adorable. Although, thinking about travelling to see Fiona… she's talking about moving to Australia. Australia! No way! Really? That’s… far. Though, thinking about escaping the grey…I get it. Still, Australia. I'm terrified of flying, you know? Absolutely petrified. I know, you are! You practically need sedating just to get on a short-haul. What about somewhere a bit… easier? Like Spain? I was thinking about maybe a weekend in Barcelona before it gets  properly  busy. Spain sounds lovely. Much more manageable. Although… I was idly browsing holidays online last night – no real intention of booking anything, you understand – and I saw the Maldives. Turquoise water, overwater bungalows... it looked unbelievably relaxing. Ooh, Maldives. Now you’re talking! Expensive, though, isn't it? Though to be fair, after the last few academic terms, you  deserve  some serious relaxing. That’s what I told myself! Trying to justify it to my bank account is the tricky bit. I was thinking, maybe next year?

… honestly, Mum, I still don’t get why you’re so fixated on the placement. It’s  my  arm! A little bit of ink on the bicep isn’t exactly going to scandalise the WI. Don’t be ridiculous, Leo. It’s not about scandalising anyone, it’s about… longevity. You’ll still be applying for proper jobs after your degree, won’t you? A visible tattoo might… raise eyebrows. And honestly, the bicep? A bit cliché, don’t you think? Cliché? It’s a classic! Besides, I’m doing a Masters in Creative Writing. No one expects me to look like a city banker. It’s a tiny swallow, Mum, a nod to… well, you know. Gran. I know, darling. It's a lovely tribute to your grandmother. Just… think about it. Maybe a slightly more discreet spot? Whilst I'm thinking about discreet, have you finalised the kitchen tile samples? That’s far more pressing than avian body art. No, not yet. I was going to look at them again this weekend. Honestly, this whole renovation is a nightmare. It’s taking forever, and I’m starting to feel like a project manager, not a homeowner. Hellooo! Am I interrupting a domestic dispute about swallows and tiling? Smells amazing in here! Maya! No, thankfully, it was just Mum gently questioning my life choices. Just offering some maternal guidance. Come in, darling, you must be starving. We’re making a proper Sunday roast. Don’t mind if I do! Honestly, this place is looking good, even mid-renovation chaos. Still living with builders, then? Constantly. They’re currently arguing about the plumbing. It’s riveting. They are… enthusiastic. Maya, how are things with the interns? Are they finally getting the hang of submissions? Oh, Lord. They're… learning. One of them thought Virginia Woolf wrote  Fifty Shades of Grey . I nearly choked on my tea. Honestly, the expectations of young graduates these days. They expect everything to be instant, instant, instant. No appreciation for the craft. Sounds like university. Everyone expecting a first-class degree for minimal effort. Precisely! Speaking of things needing effort… have you two started thinking about Christmas yet? I'm dreading it. My aunt Mildred is already asking what I’m getting her. Don’t even mention it. I’m already mentally preparing myself for the annual argument with Uncle George about Brexit. I'm boycotting political debate this year.

…and honestly, the downward dog was just  not  happening. I felt like a beached whale. Honestly, Fiona, you make it look so effortless. Effortless? Darling, that's the Instagram filter talking. My face was puce, and I’m pretty sure I was making noises like a distressed walrus. Though, admittedly, I  am  getting a bit better. It's the core strength, isn’t it? That's what Mrs. Patel keeps banging on about. Core strength. The eternal enemy of the comfortable. Speaking of comfortable, this smells  amazing . What are you making? It’s not one of your complicated Thai curries, is it? My chilli tolerance is currently at ‘mild salsa’. No, thankfully. It's just a slow-roasted lamb shoulder. My mum’s recipe, actually. She swears by rosemary and garlic – and a generous glug of red wine. Simplicity itself, really. Though, finding a decent lamb shoulder in Birmingham has been…an experience. London butchers just  understand  lamb. Oh, I know what you mean. Everything feels slightly…different here. Even the supermarkets. I miss Waitrose. Don’t get me wrong, this place is lovely, and the house is gorgeous, but little things just take getting used to. Remember when I tried to buy crumpets and they looked at me like I'd asked for a unicorn? Oh, that was brilliant! "Crumpets? What are crumpets?" Honestly. You’d think they’d never seen a proper breakfast item. Though, I did find a bakery that does a fairly decent sourdough. That’s a win, isn’t it? A massive win. Sourdough is life. Right, let’s talk clothes. I’m having a crisis. I need something…new. Something that screams ‘competent language teacher who also has a life’ and not ‘slightly frazzled woman who lives in tracksuits’. Oh, I’m on it. We  need  to hit the Bullring on Saturday. I’ve been eyeing up a gorgeous coat in Reiss. It’s ridiculously expensive, but…investment piece, right? And there's a John Lewis, so we can tick off sensible shoes if necessary. Sensible shoes are always necessary. Especially when you’re chasing after teenagers who are deliberately misunderstanding subjunctive moods. But Reiss…that sounds tempting. I’ve been really trying to avoid buying anything new, ethically and financially, but… I feel like I need a little pick-me-up. Exactly! Treat yourself. And we can always hit one of the charity shops afterwards.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of essays I have to mark this weekend is criminal. Thirty first years all arguing about post-structuralism and the semiotics of noodles. Noodles, Ben! Noodles? Seriously? That's… specific. Sounds exhausting though. My lot are slightly less culinary-focused, thankfully. More focused on the political implications of garden gnomes, apparently. Garden gnomes! Oh, don't even get me started. It’s the  effort  of reading it all, you know? Trying to find the original thought amongst the paraphrased articles. Do you ever just want to… give them all a ‘C’ and be done with it? Tempting. Extremely tempting. But then the appeals… the emails from mums… It's not worth the hassle. I had one student last year who genuinely tried to argue that his essay was plagiarised  from himself , because he'd written something similar in high school. No way! That’s brilliant. And utterly ridiculous. You just can’t make this stuff up. It's definitely lacking the intellectual rigour we had when  we  were students. Remember Dr. Armitage? He’d tear your arguments to shreds in a heartbeat. Oh god, Armitage. A legend, and a terror. Still, it made you think, didn't it? Made you really  defend  your position. Speaking of thinking, have you heard from Sarah lately? I tried to message her on WeChat, but no response. No, not for a couple of weeks. I assumed she was just busy. She did mention she was attempting to grow her own mushrooms, which sounds… ambitious, even for Sarah. Mushrooms! Of course she is. That woman is a whirlwind of eccentric hobbies. I’m slightly worried about her, though. She’s been quieter than usual. Remember how stressed she was about her visa renewal? Yes. I messaged her a quick 'thinking of you' a while ago, but nothing back. Perhaps we should actually try calling her? A proper phone call? Good idea. I'll do it tonight. It's just… she's always been so fiercely independent. I don't want to overstep. Although, knowing Sarah, she’d probably appreciate someone checking in. She's all bravado, but secretly a softie. Definitely. That’s Sarah all over. Right, changing the subject completely… I have a minor foot-related crisis. Oh? Do tell. One of my toenails is… rebelling. I think it's ingrown. It's subtly, but persistently, painful. I tried to deal with it myself, which was a terrible idea.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt  pointless . Three hours of CGI dragons and brooding heroes. It’s all been done before, hasn’t it? I mean, did it even  try  to be original? You’re talking about ‘Emberfall’, right? I saw the trailer. Looked a bit…much. I’m more of a gritty realism kinda guy these days. Give me a good Ken Loach film any day. Though, to be fair, even I’m starting to get sucked into the superhero vortex. My son’s obsessed. Oh, Ken Loach, now  there’s  a filmmaker. Proper stories. It’s just… everything feels like event cinema now. No one’s making small, character-driven films anymore. It's all about box office numbers and celebrity endorsements. Speaking of which, did you see what happened with that reality TV star, Bronwyn Blake? Bronwyn Blake? The one who married that… footballer? What now? Another scandal? They’ve been through more dramas than a daytime soap. Worse. Apparently, she's convinced the government is replacing world leaders with clones. Posting all about it on X, the lot. Full-blown conspiracy theorist. It’s a bit sad, actually. Imagine having that much money and… well, that much time, I suppose. Right. The deep state and all that. It’s a rabbit hole, isn’t it? My uncle Geoff went down that road a few years back. Started talking about 5G and microchips. Ruined Christmas, it did. Tried to convince my Auntie Maureen she was being monitored. Oh, that’s awful. My students are surprisingly well-versed in some of that stuff, actually. It seeps into their worldview so easily. Makes teaching media literacy a nightmare. They’ll argue with you using ‘facts’ from YouTube videos. They always have, haven’t they? Remember when everyone was convinced Elvis was still alive? At least that one was harmless. This stuff…it’s divisive. Anyway, enough about the end of the world as we know it. How’s work going? Still wrangling teenagers with present participles? You know me. The battle continues. Actually, I'm applying for that head of department role. Bit daunting, but I think I'm ready for a new challenge. More meetings, more paperwork… but also more influence, hopefully. That’s fantastic, Sarah! You’d be brilliant. You’ve got the patience of a saint, and you actually  care  about the kids. That's rare these days.

…and then Mrs. Higgins said it was absolutely  ghastly  staying there, all creepy and windswept. Honestly, Jamaica Inn! Sounds like something out of a bad horror film. Did you read it, Dad? Daphne du Maurier? Aye, I did, a long time ago. When your mum and I first started going out, actually. Right spooky, it was. Not surprised old Mrs. Higgins found it unsettling. It  is  a bleak spot, that. Look at the colour of the moorland now, though. All purples and browns. Not like London, is it? Everything's grey back there. Definitely not. It’s… dramatic. Like the Wicked Witch’s land in the Wizard of Oz before Dorothy lands. All harsh and threatening. Speaking of dramatic, do you think Sherlock Holmes ever took a holiday? Like, did he ever just…chill on a beach? Sherlock Holmes? Chill? Now that's a thought. Probably not. Too much thinking going on in that head. He’d probably be deducing the life story of every sandcastle builder. Though, I reckon even  he’d  appreciate Cornwall. Good mystery potential in all these little villages, eh? Maybe. It’s just… everything feels a bit…older here. Even the houses. Not in a bad way. They’ve got character. They don’t all look like perfectly-squared boxes. That’s the difference between building with stone and building with…well, whatever they build with these days. And these aren't boxes, lass. They're built to withstand a proper gale. Look at those wind turbines on the hill. Used to be just fields there, when I were a lad. Progress, I suppose. They’re a bit…hypnotic, aren’t they? Just going round and round. Like something from a Lewis Carroll story. All nonsense and illogical spinning. You always were a bookworm, weren’t you? Got yer head stuck in a tale. Speaking of tales, remember I told you about Grandad sending telegrams to Gran when he was away at work? Vaguely. Was that before…texts? Like,  really  before? Before texts, before phones even! Telegrams were short, sharp messages. Then there was the telegraph, using Morse code. Remember learning a bit about that at school? Dots and dashes. Imagine relying on  that  to tell someone you’d be late for tea! Wow. That sounds…stressful. And what about Braille? How did people without sight read books before all that tech? Clever stuff, Braille. Raised bumps you read with your fingers.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data is mental. Like, terabytes of transcribed speech. It’s fascinating, don’t get me wrong, building the corpus and all, but sometimes I feel like I'm drowning in ‘umms’ and ‘ahhs’. Proper Geordie ‘aye’s’ though, that’s the good stuff. Makes a change from southern accents, I’ll tell ya. Southern accents? Bah. All a bit…wishy-washy, aren't they? Can’t understand a word half the time. Now, a good Mancunian drawl…that has  character . Reminds me of my days at BT, dealing with customers all over the country. You heard everything, you did. Especially complaints about slow connection speeds. You worked at BT your whole career, didn’t you, Grandad? That’s… a long time. Things must have changed massively. Changed? Son, you have  no  idea. When I started, everything was manual exchanges, switchboards… you actually  connected  people’s calls. Now it's all digital, robots doing the work. And petrol stations used to be full service! Someone would come running out, fill your tank, check your oil. Now you’re lucky if they even have someone  in  the kiosk. They’re expensive now too. Honestly, filling up the car feels like a second mortgage. I’m considering cycling more, but Wincanton’s… hilly, to say the least. It wouldn't be a Channel swim, that’s for sure. A Channel swim? Seriously, Liv? You and a Channel swim? I thought you were more of a sofa and Netflix kind of person. Don't underestimate me! I did the Great North Run once. Nearly died, admittedly, but I  did  it. Though even that was easier than my primary school cross-country. Absolute torture. Mrs. Henderson, the teacher, was a nightmare. Used to shout at us for not running fast enough. Proper old-school. Cross-country? We had that at Timperley Primary. Cold, muddy, miserable. Though nothing compared to what  my  father went through. He was in action during the war, you know. Dunkirk, North Africa… never spoke much about it, but you could tell it haunted him. Different world, then. It’s hard to imagine now, isn’t it? Everything feels… comfortable. Though rent's still ridiculous. I'm looking at flats in Bristol, and they’re tiny for what they cost. Makes you wonder if saving for a deposit is even worth it. Tell me about it! I’m still living back at Mam’s.

…and honestly, Mum, the jet lag is  brutal . I thought I’d be alright after just the one flight, but no. Felt like a zombie all yesterday. Did you manage to get the curtains closed in the spare room properly? The morning light was… assertive. Oh, darling, you poor thing! Yes, I wrestled with those curtains. They’re always a bit temperamental. Had a right struggle, I did. Though, assertive light is better than no light, isn’t it? Keeps you on a schedule. You need to eat something properly, love. Just had a bit of toast, haven’t you? I’ve made a shepherd’s pie, your favourite. It’s warming up now. Toast was a start. Honestly, all I wanted to do was collapse. Shepherd’s pie sounds… magnificent. Thank you. You always know how to look after me. We should really tackle that moving checklist again. I’m starting to panic about how much stuff I actually have. Don’t you worry your head about that. We’ll sort it. I’ve started a list, actually. Mostly things you’ve forgotten, like all your childhood trophies. Remember that dreadful pottery penguin you made? Oh god, don’t remind me! Bertram. He was… uniquely shaped. Yes, I’d completely forgotten about Bertram. He’s probably best left in the past. How’s Dad doing, by the way? Haven’t had a chance to properly speak to him yet. He’s alright, pottering about in the garden. Got a new batch of tomatoes coming along nicely. He keeps asking when you’re bringing that nice Amelia down to meet us properly. He’s taken a shine to her, you know. Keeps saying she has a ‘sensible head on her shoulders’. He always says that. It means she doesn’t talk back! But yeah, she’s brilliant. We’re… well, we’re talking seriously about getting engaged. Oh, Oliver! That’s wonderful! That’s absolutely lovely news! I knew it! She’s a sweet girl. Has she any family nearby? We must get to know them. She does. Her mum’s in Manchester, her dad’s… a bit of a character, actually. Travels a lot. He used to be a marine biologist. Apparently, he’s obsessed with weaver fish. Says they’re incredibly intelligent. Weaver fish? That’s… niche. Your father will love that. He’s got a thing for peculiar facts himself.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the appeal of those really long, layered haircuts everyone's getting now. It looks like they’ve been attacked by a particularly enthusiastic pair of scissors. Remember when everyone just had bobs? Simple, effective. Bobs are… functional. But a bit severe, aren't they? It's all about texture now, isn't it? And layers give you texture. Though I agree, some of them  are  a bit much. My supervisor’s got one that’s basically a waterfall of hair. A waterfall! That’s… descriptive. She's a scientist, isn't she? Should be more concerned with empirical evidence than hair volume. Speaking of things needing tending, have you repotted the snake plant yet? It’s looking a bit… stressed. No, not yet. Been swamped with this data analysis. Honestly, the NHS waiting lists are making me anxious, and that just feeds into my procrastination. I need to book an appointment for… well, never you mind. But it’s just another thing on the list. It’s ridiculous how long it takes now, isn’t it? Even for basic stuff. It's appalling. My mum was telling me about waiting  six weeks  for a physiotherapy appointment. Six weeks! For a bad back! It's a disgrace when you consider how much tax we pay. And then they moan about people going private. It's a self-fulfilling prophecy. Precisely. And it all comes back to funding, doesn’t it? Which comes back to… well, everything being a mess. Did you read about the latest A-Level reforms? Oh, don't even get me started. Another overhaul. Honestly, they change the goalposts so often, it’s a wonder anyone gets a decent education anymore. Making things more modular, less linear… it just feels like they’re constantly tinkering instead of addressing the core issues. My little cousin is starting Year 10 next year, and honestly, I’m worried for her. It's the endless assessment, isn’t it? Everything is about ticking boxes. It sucks the joy out of learning. They need to focus on fostering a genuine curiosity, not just regurgitating information. Remember how much fun Physics was at A-Level when Mr. Davies used to do those demonstrations? Oh god, yes! The exploding custard demonstration. Health and safety would have a field day with that now. Still, it made you  remember  it. Speaking of things that are making a mess, have you been to the petrol station lately?

…and honestly, the lecturer just kept going on about the socio-economic impact of the Black Death like it was  fascinating  dinner conversation. Like, yeah, okay, millions died, but did he need to describe the buboes in  that  much detail? I practically lost my lunch. Oh, God, lecturers. Mine did that with the French Revolution. All the guillotining. It’s supposed to be academic, isn’t it? Detached? Doesn’t always feel that way. Though, buboes do sound… grim. Grim is an understatement. It’s horrifying! Think about living through that. No antibiotics, no understanding of germ theory… Just… plague. Makes uni stress seem a bit, well, manageable, doesn’t it? Speaking of stress, how’s the dissertation going, El? You were looking proper frazzled last week. It’s a mess, honestly. I’m trying to tie in Yorkshire mining history with feminist theory, and it’s just… not clicking. All I’m getting is a load of angry men in historical records. Not exactly empowering. Oh, that sounds… challenging. Mining's a really male-dominated field historically. You might have to lean heavily into the women who  were  involved, even if their stories are harder to find. My grandad was a miner, and even he admitted it was a brutal life. Not exactly a hotbed of equality. It's a good topic though, even if it's difficult. It shows you’re thinking critically. I’m stuck on whether to even  do  a dissertation. The thought of another 10,000 words… I’m starting to question all my life choices. Plus, I need to actually  earn  some money over the summer, or I’ll be living off pot noodles until graduation. Tell me about it. I’ve been applying for everything – bar work, retail, even weeding a garden! Anything to avoid going cap in hand to Mum and Dad again. They’re wonderful, but I feel awful constantly asking. I got a job at that new Italian place down Kirkstall Road. It's… hectic. Long hours, loads of dishes, but the tips are decent. It's not glamorous, but it's keeping me afloat. I’m sticking with my shifts at the library. It's quiet, pays enough, and I can actually read books when it’s slow. Which, for an English Lit student, is basically paradise. Though, someone tried to smuggle a cigarette  inside  the library last week. Honestly, the audacity!

…and honestly, the whole weekend just felt  exhausting . Like I was performing friendship, you know? Constantly topping up the energy, agreeing, nodding… it was draining. Ugh, I  know  that feeling. It's the worst. It's like you're mentally cataloguing all the things you disagree with, or all the things they’re saying that are… well, just  them , and it’s suddenly amplified. So, with Sarah, is it… is it just that you’ve grown apart? Or is there something  specific  that's bothering you? It’s…complicated. It’s not like a massive falling out. Just…layers of little things. She's still stuck in that phase of constantly needing validation, and every conversation somehow circles back to her work drama, which, let's be honest, is usually self-inflicted. And I’ve moved on from needing to be a sounding board for that. I’ve got my own stuff going on, and I need friends who feel…reciprocal. Reciprocal is the key word! It's so easy to fall into those patterns, isn't it? Especially with people you've known for ages. You feel guilty about wanting less. It’s like you owe them something. Exactly! That’s what I’m struggling with. I feel awful even  thinking  about… phasing her out. It sounds so cold, doesn't it? Like I'm just discarding a friendship. No, it doesn't make you cold! It makes you…self-aware. And sensible. Friendships change, people change. You're allowed to outgrow people. I had this with Chloe after uni. We were inseparable, but then she became obsessed with this Instagram lifestyle and all she wanted to talk about was influencers and filters. It just… wasn't me anymore. Oh god, that sounds painful. How did you handle it? Did you have “the talk”? Because I am  terrified  of that. Nope. Absolutely not. I learned the hard way that “the talk” rarely goes well. It just leads to defensiveness and guilt-tripping. I just… gradually created distance. I started being less available. Said I was busy more often. Responded to texts less promptly. It took months, honestly, but eventually, the contact just fizzled out. That sounds…efficient. A little ruthless, maybe? But efficient. I think I’m leaning towards that. I've been trying the "busy" route, but she's  so  persistent. She'll text three times if I don't respond to the first one.

…and honestly, the reading list is  brutal . Professor Davies clearly thinks we have nothing else to do with our lives. Three books a week, plus journal articles? It’s a bit much, innit? Oh, university. Brings it all back. Though when  I  was studying, it wasn't quite so… relentless. More discussion, less sheer volume. What are you reading, anyway? Something interesting? It’s for my Masters in History. Right now, it's mostly about post-war British social changes. Lots of austerity, the birth of the welfare state… and a frankly depressing amount about rationing. It makes you appreciate a decent Sunday roast, that's for sure. Rationing… yes, I remember that vividly. Vienna wasn't much better, even after the war officially ended. It took a long time for things to settle. Though, comparatively, it wasn't the same as what Britain went through, I suppose. You know, your grandmother – my Elsie – she was a marvel during those years. Made something from absolutely nothing. I’ve heard stories. She was a proper East End girl, wasn’t she? Tough as nails. I wish I’d asked her more about it when I had the chance. You should have, dear. They all have stories, don’t they? Ones that need telling. Speaking of stories, have you spoken to your sister recently? She hasn’t rung in a while. Is that backpacking trip going alright? Yeah, I messaged her yesterday. She's in Thailand at the moment, apparently volunteering at an elephant sanctuary. Said it's amazing, but the humidity is killing her. Typical Sarah, throwing herself into the deep end! Keeps sending me pictures of these gorgeous elephants. Makes all this reading feel very… insignificant. Good for her. Always loved animals, that one. And Thailand! I’ve always wanted to go. Maybe when I’m finished with this exhibition prep. It's… consuming, you know? All the varnishing and framing. It's good work, truly, but it takes it out of you. The exhibition… it’s the landscapes, right? The ones inspired by Cornwall? I saw a few photos online, they look incredible. Really vibrant. Landscapes, yes. And some of the smaller studies I did last autumn. Trying to capture the light, you see. It’s always the light. I was thinking of calling it “Ephemeral Shores”. Bit cliché, perhaps? No, not at all! It’s perfect. It suits your style.

… honestly, I just don’t  do  well with intense exercise on an empty stomach. It makes me feel lightheaded and grumpy. Which, let’s be honest, isn’t a great look on anyone. Especially not after I’ve been complaining about the Polish roads for the last hour. Grumpy is a bit of an understatement, actually. You were practically conducting an orchestra of disapproval with the steering wheel. And it's not the roads’ fault you decided a gym session was a brilliant idea after pierogi. They were  delicious  pierogi! And it's not just  any  gym session, it’s attempting to recreate that yoga flow class we did in Bristol. Remember? The one where I nearly pulled a hamstring? Good times. Good times for you to provide entertainment, maybe. I was genuinely concerned you’d need rescuing. Look, we’re almost at Tarnow. Let’s grab something small – a yoghurt, a piece of fruit – before we even  think  about contorting ourselves into pretzels. A yoghurt sounds… acceptable. Though honestly, I'm starting to suspect this whole 'active holiday' was your elaborate plan to make me feel inadequate. Inadequate? Oh, come on! It’s about pushing ourselves a bit. You said you wanted to feel… invigorated. Less ‘comfortable semi-retirement’, more ‘adventurous spirit’. I said I wanted to  consider  an adventurous spirit, not actively embody one. It’s a subtle difference! And it’s easier to be adventurous when you’re not worried about your aging ligaments. Speaking of which, do you think they look at us strangely in these gyms? Two slightly scruffy English women turning up in athletic wear after driving all day in a campervan? Probably. But honestly, who cares? We’re paying customers. And let’s be real, most gyms are full of people pretending to be a lot fitter than they actually are. It’s a universal truth. What  does  bug me, and I was thinking about this earlier, is the sheer… testosterone. It’s always so overwhelmingly male-dominated. Oh, absolutely. The grunting, the mirror-gazing… It’s a bit much. And the way they subtly try to ‘help’ you with your form. Always men. Exactly! Like we’re incapable of understanding our own bodies. It’s frustrating. Remember that article we read about how gym equipment is often designed based on male physiology? Vaguely. Something about seat widths and resistance levels? It’s ridiculous.

…and honestly, the handle on that one’s just  perfect . Not too chunky, not too delicate. Proper hand-thrown, you know? Not like those mass-produced things you get in supermarkets. It just  feels  right in your hand. Aye, it does. Lovely colour too. A bit like that heather on Ilkley Moor, isn't it? Though I’ve never been much of a coffee drinker myself. Always preferred a nice cup of tea. Strong builder’s, mind you. None of that fancy Earl Grey business. Still the builder’s brew? After all these years? I thought you might’ve branched out! Anyway, this coffee is decent. And the milk’s good, from Old Man Hemmings down the lane. He says the cows are benefitting from all this rain. Though I'm starting to think  we  aren't. Rain, rain, rain! It’s been relentless, hasn’t it? My poor roses are getting waterlogged. I spent all morning tying them up after that gust yesterday. Nearly lost ‘Peace’ completely. Oh dear. You’re a marvel with your roses, you are. Mine are looking a bit… bedraggled, to be honest. I keep meaning to get out there and deadhead them, but… well, you know how it is. Aye, I do. Always something else, isn't there? Speaking of something else, did you see a spider the size of my hand in the bathroom this morning? Nearly gave me heart failure! Don't! I hate spiders. Absolutely detest them. I left you to deal with the last one in the attic, remember? Nearly had a coronary myself just thinking about it. That  was  a big one. Nearly as big as Doris Prickett’s chihuahua! Remember Doris? Always carried that thing around in a handbag. Such a sight. Oh, Doris. What a character. And her husband, Arthur… bless him, always trying to keep her in line. I wonder what’s become of them. Haven’t seen them at the Gala for ages. No, haven't. They moved to Devon, I heard. Said the winters were getting too much for their joints. Though I suspect Doris just wanted to be closer to a proper cream tea. It’s the Gala next month, isn’t it? Are you going to enter your Victoria sponge again? I was thinking about it. Though I’m not sure I can beat Brenda Sykes. Her baking is legendary. Remember last year?

…and honestly, the thought of another week of rain just  depresses  me. Seriously, Dad, are you sure about Scotland? Beaches are way more my vibe. Now, now, Elsie. Scotland is beautiful! Think lochs, mountains… dramatic scenery. It’s not all grey skies and bagpipes, you know. Aye, she’s got a point, lass. Dramatic scenery  and  bagpipes. Can’t beat it. Though, I admit, a bit of sun would be nice. I’m getting too old for damp tweed. But Dad, you  love  damp tweed! And Mum, lochs are just… cold lakes. And mountains? Just big hills! I want to build sandcastles and eat ice cream on the seafront. Like we did last year in Cornwall. Remember Cornwall? Of course, I remember Cornwall. It was lovely. But we go to Cornwall almost every year, darling. We need a bit of variety. Your father’s always wanted to see the Highlands. Been meaning to for years, I have. Always gigging, never had the time. And old Hamish McGregor – you remember Hamish, Elsie? From the pub in town? – he raves about the fishing up there. Says the salmon are fantastic. Hamish McGregor? The one who always smells of stale beer and tells really long, boring stories? Elsie! Be polite. Hamish is a lovely man. And even if you don’t fancy the fishing, there are castles! Proper, ancient castles. You’re learning about British history at school, aren’t you? This is a chance to see it in person. Yeah, yeah, castles. Everyone goes to castles. It’s…predictable. What about Liam? Is he even coming? He said he might have a football camp. I spoke to his mum this morning. He’s definitely free. He’s really looking forward to it, actually. Said he wants to try and spot the Loch Ness Monster. That lad. Always up for a bit of mischief. Good lad, Liam. Reminds me of myself at his age. Always getting into scrapes. Ugh, seriously? Liam? He'll probably try to convince us all to go monster hunting in the dark. That sounds terrifying. And what about wifi? Will there even  be  wifi? Elsie, honestly! You and your wifi. I'm sure many places will have it. We can look it up. And honestly, a few days offline might do you some good. Your mum’s right, pet. Disconnect. Breathe the fresh air. I might even bring my guitar and we can have a proper singalong.

…and then Kat Stratford  literally  just walks away! Like, after Heath Ledger’s character pays her dad?! Honestly, the audacity! It’s so good though, isn't it? 10 Things I Hate About You is just… a classic. Oh my  god , I know! It’s iconic. And the soundtrack! Don't even get me started. But yeah, Kat was being so stubborn. Though, I kinda get it. Having to pretend to date someone for money... gross. Still, Heath Ledger was… well. Heath Ledger. Exactly! He’s just…  swoon . But seriously, the whole 'I hate everything' act? I think I do that sometimes. Not the paid-to-date thing obviously, but the just wanting to be left alone vibe. Especially when it comes to school. You and me both. Ugh, Maths today was brutal. Mrs. Davies is determined to make us all quadratic equation experts whether we  want  to be or not. I swear, I just stared at the board for the whole hour, pretending to take notes. Oh, same! I was doodling little Heath Ledgers in my book. Don't tell anyone. And then she called on  me  to answer a question! I just mumbled something about the discriminant and hoped for the best. You brave soul. I’d have just feigned illness. Honestly, I'm starting to think I’m failing Maths. It’s just… not clicking. What about you? Are you worried about the mocks next month? Terrified. Honestly. I’m mostly okay with English Lit – I actually  enjoy  analysing Shakespeare, surprisingly – but everything else is a disaster. My history teacher thinks I’m going to ace it, which is just putting more pressure on me. It’s like, thanks for the vote of confidence, but also, no pressure! Right? Teachers always do that. And then they’re all, “Oh, but you’re so capable!” Like, yeah, capable of stressing out beyond belief. Have you thought any more about what you want to do after school? Properly thought, I mean? Sort of. I’ve been looking at universities, but it all feels so… final. And expensive. My mum keeps dropping hints about apprenticeships, which honestly sounds a lot more sensible. But I kinda have this dream of studying English at a proper university. Honestly? I have no idea. Everyone's talking about university applications, and I'm just thinking about surviving the next Science practical. Although… remember we were talking about going to London for a weekend after our GCSEs?

…and honestly, Doreen, I still don’t understand this Facebook business. Young Emily – bless her heart – she’s trying to show me how to ‘friend’ people, but it just seems like… showing off, doesn’t it? All these pictures of what you ‘ad for yer tea! Good grief. Back in my day, if you ‘ad a nice bit of cod and chips, you  ate  it, you didn’t photograph it! Oh, Harold, you’re such a Luddite! It’s just a way of keeping in touch, dear. Seeing what the grandchildren are up to. Though, I agree, some of it is a bit… much. Brenda keeps posting motivational quotes. Brenda! She's never motivated a day in her life. It's definitely a curated reality, Gran. It's easy to fall into comparing yourself, which isn’t helpful. Actually, it's something I was discussing with some students today – the impact of social media on mental health. Yeah, there’s a lot of research showing a correlation, particularly with anxiety and… well, obsessive tendencies. It can become a bit of a compulsion, checking for notifications, needing validation. Obsessive? Now that’s a word. Reminds me of poor old Mr. Higgins down the road. He used to wash his hands, oh, dozens of times a day. Couldn't leave the ‘ouse without checking the gas was off six times over. Said ‘e ‘ad these… thoughts. That sounds like it could have been Obsessive Compulsive Disorder, Gran. It's a really common condition. It’s not just about cleanliness, it’s about intrusive thoughts and then performing rituals to alleviate the anxiety those thoughts cause. Poor man. He was a lovely bloke, Higgins. Always offered you a sprout from his garden, even if you didn’t want one! Remember when little Timmy caught chicken pox? He was convinced he’d given it to Higgins, and spent a week leaving notes under his door apologising. Chicken pox was  rough . I remember being covered head to toe. Itchy beyond belief. Mum used to put calamine lotion everywhere. Calamine lotion! Smelt like a chemist’s shop, that did. My mother used to swear by a cold compress. She believed in simple remedies. Didn’t ‘ave all this fancy medicine you youngsters ‘ave today. And she was a devout woman, your grandmother. Went to church every Sunday, rain or shine. Was she very religious, Gran? Oh, very.

…and honestly, the all-inclusive was  worth  it. Not having to think about a bill at the end of every meal? Absolute bliss. Though, Mark nearly bankrupt us at the duty-free on the way back. He insists he got a bargain on aftershave. Oh, Dad! He  always  thinks he's getting a bargain. Remember that time he came back from Spain with fifteen bottles of sangria? Said it was “practically free!” Don’t remind me. We were drinking sangria for months. Still shudder at the thought. So, southern Spain, eh, Sarah? Was it hot? Scorching. But lovely. The kids loved the beach, naturally. Though, little Amy tried to build a sandcastle  in  the swimming pool. That was…fun to explain to the lifeguard. Bless her. She gets that from you, Mum. Always a little bit chaotic. Speaking of flights, anyone remember Uncle George trying to speak German on that trip to the Black Forest? Oh,  please  don't. I've blocked most of it out for my own sanity. It was less German, more… enthusiastic shouting in English with a random ‘Ja’ thrown in occasionally. He was convinced if he spoke loud enough, they’d understand him! He’d practiced a few phrases from a phrasebook, bless him. "Wo ist die toilette?" was his favourite, naturally. And delivered with the same volume as an order in a pub! He did have a point, though. German is a tricky language. All those long words! I tried learning a bit before we went to Berlin a few years back, but it just wouldn’t stick. Their accents are a bit…intense, too. I always thought their 'R' sound was hilarious. Like they're gargling pebbles! Now, now, let’s not be unkind. Everyone has an accent. You two with your Kentish drawl aren't exactly neutral, you know. Sounds like you’ve swallowed a bit of the countryside! Hey! I think it’s charming! It's a proper, authentic sound. It's not like posh accents, all clipped and… affected. Agreed. Proper Kentish. Reminds me of old Mr. Hemmings down at the blacksmith’s. Used to tell the best stories, voice like gravel and honey. Remember him, Dad? Do I ever! A real character. Used to tinker with cars, that man. Could fix anything with a bit of wire and a good swear word. Speaking of cars… anyone seen the state of my classic Mini? Needs some attention before the summer show.

… honestly, the sound in that pub was atrocious. You could barely hear Liam sing. And you  know  how much his voice carries usually. Yeah, The Red Lion is…rustic, shall we say? Good beer, terrible acoustics. Was it busy though? I heard they had a decent crowd in for Open Mic night. Packed. Absolutely rammed. Mostly students, I think. A few older lads, drinking cider and complaining about the volume. Liam did alright, considering. He was testing out a new song, bit raw still, but loads of potential. Speaking of music, have you been listening to anything good lately? I’m stuck in a bit of a rut. Actually, yeah! Been properly getting into this band, ‘Static Bloom’. They’re… kind of alt-rock, bit grungy, but their drummer is insane. Proper fills, really inventive. You’d appreciate it, knowing your obsession with drumming. Oh really? ‘Static Bloom’? Never heard of them. Send me a link, I'll check ‘em out. I’ve been revisiting a lot of older stuff, actually. Radiohead, Portishead…comfort listening, you know? Wanting something a bit… substantial. But a good drummer always gets my attention. I’ve been practicing myself, trying to get my double bass technique up to scratch. It’s brutal. Double bass? Proper commitment! I barely have time to pick up a pair of chopsticks these days, let alone drums. Kitchen life, innit? It’s all speed and precision, just… with knives and pans instead of sticks. It's a different kind of rhythm, I suppose. A rather more stressful rhythm, I imagine. How’s the new head chef treating you? Still breathing down your neck? He’s calmed down a bit, thankfully. Realised I actually know what I’m doing. Though, he did try to get me to make a soufflé the other day. A  soufflé , mate. Like I’ve got time for all that faff. It's all gastropub these days, moving away from the fancy stuff, thank goodness. Serves him right! Soufflés are notorious. Remember old Mrs. Henderson trying to teach us that in Food Tech at school? Disaster. Speaking of school… how’s Tom doing? Haven't seen him since Christmas. He’s good, last I heard. Still slaving away at his internship in London. Said it's pretty intense, loads of long hours, but he's learning a lot. He's properly obsessed with coding now. Barely recognises him when we Facetime.

…and honestly, the noise in here is  something  else, isn’t it? I can barely hear meself think, let alone you. Did you want to move to a quieter corner, lad? Though I doubt there  is  one, look at the queue for the drive-through! Nah, it’s alright, Mam. Just a bit… buzzy. I’m used to worse at school, honestly. Besides, I wanted to talk about the summer. Are we definitely going to Durham again this year? Durham? Aye, we are. Your Dad's already booked the caravan. Same pitch, number 23, overlooking the river. Though he did grumble about the price going up again. Loyalty schemes, he said, are just a way of fleecing honest folk. He’s started doing that thing where he compares prices on everything, even coffee! Typical Dad. So, the usual then? River walks, the cathedral, that awful souvenir shop… And your auntie Maureen and Uncle Stan. Don’t forget ‘em! They'll be wanting to take you to another domino drive. Honestly, I think they live for those things. It’s like a secret society. Ugh, dominoes. They don’t understand I’d rather be… well, doing anything else, really. Can I maybe bring Jamie this year? He’s been asking about the Cathedral. Jamie? That’s a thought. Your Dad’ll have a fit if you bring another mouth to feed, but we can ask. We might need the bigger tent, or at least an extra sleeping bag. I need to make a list. I’ve got that loyalty card for the outdoor shop, might get a discount on one. Speaking of lists, remind me to get more biscuits. I’m almost out. Biscuits are crucial. Always. Listen, Mam, have you seen that new football documentary on iPlayer? It’s about Alan Shearer, it’s brilliant. Alan Shearer? Footie… isn’t that what's keeping all the lads glued to their phones these days? Honestly, they don’t look up! It’s the obesity epidemic, I tell you. No fresh air, no exercise. Back in my day… Here we go! “Back in your day…” Well, it’s true! We were outside all the time. Building dens, playing football in the street… not sat indoors staring at screens. Anyway, what was that about Shearer? Did he talk about Newcastle much? Loads. It’s about his whole career, but the stuff about playing for Newcastle is the best.

…and honestly, the sound quality on that recording is atrocious. I spent ages trying to get a decent sample of West Midlands dialect for my students, but all I got was a muffled ‘Alright, mate’ from my neighbour. It’s just… not linguistically useful, is it? Sounds about right. Bronsgrove boys aren't known for their clarity when greeting people, especially not for academic purposes! You’re still doing the accent stuff then? Thought you’d have moved onto something less… niche. Niche? It’s fascinating! People don't realise how much information is packed into an accent. Plus, it pays the bills. How’s the assurance analyst life treating you? Still battling spreadsheets? Battling and… mostly winning. It's alright. Solid, you know? Good salary, which is crucial these days, especially with the way everything’s going up. Speaking of which, this flat is lovely, really modern. Did you have to remortgage to afford Sussex? Ha! Thankfully not. My Grandad left me a bit, and I’ve been… frugal. Trying to, anyway. It’s a lot cheaper than London, that’s for sure. So, huge news – remember Sarah from Uni? Sarah? Vaguely. Red hair, always sketching? That’s the one. She’s… pregnant. No way! That’s brilliant! Is she alright? Happy? Over the moon. Absolutely terrified, naturally, but happy. She and Mark are trying to navigate the whole ‘adulting’ thing. Thinking about joint bank accounts, the cost of everything… It's bringing back memories of trying to budget at Uni. Remember eating just pasta for a week? Vividly. Though I think I augmented the pasta with questionable sausages from the market. Speaking of memories, we need to get the whole crew back together. A proper reunion. It’s been way too long. Totally agree. Although coordinating everyone these days feels like a logistical nightmare. Everyone's scattered - Korea, Spain… Remember Liam trying to learn Spanish just so he could impress a girl? Oh,  that . He ended up just asking her where the nearest pub was, in heavily accented Spanish. It was a disaster. Though, he did pick up some useful phrases. Like, “Donde esta el baño?” – vital. Classic Liam. So, are you thinking of settling down anytime soon? Any potential mini-analysts in the pipeline? Woah, hold your horses! Marriage and kids feel…a long way off. Plus, Amy and I are still debating living abroad. She's got her eye on South Korea, teaching English, actually.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Even knowing it was what she  wanted . Saying ‘yes’ to assisted dying felt…like giving up on her, even though she was the one desperately clinging on, but to a life that was just…gone. It absolutely is. It’s a strange, twisting guilt. You’re not letting go  of  her, you’re letting go  with  her, acknowledging something truly awful. My Nan, when her cancer came back, she was so fiercely independent. Refused help with  anything . It was exhausting for all of us, watching her struggle, but offering felt like… insulting her strength. Exactly! Mum was the same. Right until the end, trying to make her own tea, fussing with her hair. It was like she was trying to prove she was still…her. And then finally, admitting she needed help, admitting she was scared…it just broke my heart. Did your Nan ever talk about…what it felt like? Being scared, I mean. Not really. She was very stoic. Staffordshire girls are made of stern stuff, you know? Mostly she talked about being a burden. Said she didn’t want to be ‘a nuisance’. It’s a horrible thing to hear, isn’t it? Especially when you’re the one desperately trying to give back even a fraction of the care she’s given you over the years. God, yes. Mum kept saying she didn’t want to be ‘a weight’. It was awful. And the practicalities…the endless appointments, the forms, the trying to navigate the system… it feels like you're fighting a war on two fronts. The emotional one, and the bureaucratic one. A war is exactly the right word. It drains you, doesn’t it? And then you’re supposed to just… carry on afterwards? Like nothing’s changed? I’m trying to be there for David, you know, his mum's been struggling with depression since her diagnosis. It's brought everything up for her. He’s torn between being supportive of her and trying to just…breathe. Oh, bless him. That's a lot for anyone to handle. How is she coping? Has she sought any help? She’s started counselling, which is good. But she keeps shutting down. Says it’s just a ‘phase’. David worries she’s minimising it. He’s been on at me to suggest she talk to someone at work, their employee assistance program is pretty good.

…and honestly, the amount of homework they’re sending home now is ridiculous. It's not quality time, it’s just…filling time. Harry, you look like you're about to fall asleep in your peas. Everything alright? Just thinking about Mr. Davies’ history lesson. It was on the referendum. Really boring. All dates and stuff. The referendum, eh? That  was  a bit of a turning point, wasn’t it? Even now, years later, we’re still feeling the ripples. It's important to understand it though, Harry. Even if it felt…dry. I actually found it quite interesting. We talked about how people thought it would be better for the economy. But then we also talked about how it  wasn't  better for the economy. Good for you, Leo. You’re always the one to look at both sides. Though, honestly, I still think we made the wrong decision. But here we are. Anyway, enough politics at the dinner table. How was tennis today, boys? Did either of you manage to actually hit the ball over the net consistently? I did okay! Mr. Peterson gave me some really good tips on my serve. He said I’m getting stronger, but need to work on my follow-through. Mr. Peterson is a good coach. He really knows his stuff. I was thinking, with the boys’ improving, maybe we should look into investing a bit more in proper coaching? Not just the group sessions, but a couple of one-on-ones each month. It would be good for their technique, and for Leo, it could really help with his County tryouts. That’s a thought. It’s just…money, isn’t it? Everything always comes down to money. My contract with Henderson & Bell is a bit slow at the moment, and with the cost of everything going up… Don’t worry about it, Mum. I’m happy with the group sessions for now. I’d rather you didn’t spend extra. I'm also thinking about maybe doing an apprenticeship when I leave school. Something practical. An apprenticeship? That’s…interesting, Leo. What were you thinking of? I was talking to Mr. Evans, the mechanic who fixes our car. He said he’s always looking for apprentices. It would be good to learn a trade, you know? Not everyone needs to go to university. But what about football? You were saying you wanted to try for the academy again!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had to wade through before leaving was  criminal . It's like everyone decided this week was the week to ask me everything all at once. Did you manage to clear your desk before we left, Jess? Mostly. Just left a note for Barry about the transcription request for the Norfolk dialect samples. He's pretty good at picking those up. It felt good to actually  switch off , you know? Even just stepping onto this train felt like a weight lifted. Lancaster, though…bit random, isn’t it? Your Aunt Carol’s always had peculiar taste in places to visit. Random, but lovely. She's got a little cottage just outside the city centre. Proper fairytale vibes. And she's insisted we absolutely  have  to go to Morecambe Bay. Said the sunsets are magnificent. Morecambe…isn't that where that awful cockle-picking disaster happened? I remember something about that on the news years ago. Really tragic. God, you’re right! That  was  awful. Chinese cockle pickers, wasn’t it? So sad. It puts things into perspective, doesn't it, when you’re moaning about emails? Hopefully we'll just be enjoying the fresh air and…fish and chips. Aunt Carol's already said she's taking us for the best fish and chips in Lancashire. Oh, good. Fish and chips are a necessity when you're by the sea. Speaking of necessity, you're still dead set on Lancaster University for your Masters, yeah? How are the dissertation ideas coming along? Last time we spoke you were still wrestling with the whole sociolinguistics of online gaming communities thing. Still wrestling. Honestly, it feels like quicksand. I’ve narrowed it down a bit. Thinking maybe focusing on the linguistic features of raid leading in a specific MMO. It’s niche enough to be manageable, hopefully. The Lancaster department is genuinely brilliant though. The lecturers seem really supportive, and their corpus linguistics facilities are amazing. Sounds intense! I'm glad you're feeling good about it. I’m still a bit…wobbly about my career path. Being an administrator is…fine. But it's not  inspiring , you know? I’m starting to wonder if I should’ve gone straight for a Masters too. You could still do it! It's never too late. Plus, you’re brilliant at what you do, Jess. You’re so organised, and you're amazing with people.

…and honestly, I still can’t believe Old Man Hemmings actually  liked  that band. Stone Cold Killers? Seriously? Sounds like something my grandad would listen to after a darts match. Aye, well, Hemmings has always had… eclectic tastes. Remember when he was obsessed with that Icelandic techno stuff? Drove us all mad in the common room. But Stone Cold Killers aren't  that  bad. Bit shouty, maybe. Shouty is an understatement! It was like being trapped inside a washing machine full of angry wasps. No, give me The Reytons any day. Proper lyrics, proper tunes, proper Doncaster lads makin' music. You going to their gig next month? I’m tryin’ to, I am. Tickets are like gold dust, though. Keeps sellin’ out. Liam’s got one, apparently, offered to try and get me one through a mate who works at the venue. Fingers crossed. Ooh, Liam? Good man, Liam. He’s sorted me out before. Is he still painting miniatures? Last I heard he was building some massive Warhammer army. Still at it. Says it’s therapeutic. He’s got a whole room dedicated to it now, apparently. Mum’s not overly thrilled about the smell of the paints though. Says it gives her a headache. Sounds like Liam. Always going full-throttle into something. Remember when it was birdwatching? He had that ridiculously expensive pair of binoculars. Oh, God, aye. And the camouflage gear. He looked like he was going on a military operation, not lookin’ at robins! What have  you  been up to, other than sufferin’ through Hemmings’ music choices? Still doing the photography? Yeah, still at it. Mostly landscapes at the moment. Been up to Langsett Reservoir a couple of times. The light’s been amazing this past week, real moody stuff. I’m tryin’ to build up a proper portfolio, get some stuff online. It's slow going though, with uni work and all. That sounds good. You're proper talented, you are. Should definitely put some up. Everyone needs to see 'em. Are you still workin’ on that project about the old mills? Yeah, still chipping away at it. It’s proving harder than I thought, gettin’ access to some of ‘em is a nightmare. Most are boarded up, or someone's turned 'em into flats. Lost a lot of the character, you know? Aye, shame that. They're a part of our history, aren’t they?

Right. Another outbreak in North America. Honestly, this is just cruel. Rhys, you  knew  I was saving my researcher for Europe! Now, now, Seren. Don't look at me like  I  caused the global pandemic. It’s a game, remember? And a fiendishly difficult one at that. Besides, you were dithering about spending action points on building research stations instead of curing diseases! Honestly, you two are taking this way too seriously. It’s a board game! I haven't even contributed to the potential downfall of humanity yet, just been quietly stockpiling event cards. The power corrupts, you know. I think Seren has a point, though. Rhys  does  enjoy the chaos. He’s secretly hoping we all lose. Me?! Never! I’m just… strategically challenging. This is about teamwork, Dai! Teamwork! Though, I admit, watching Seren’s face when Southeast Asia went down  was  satisfying. Very funny. Okay, okay. Let’s focus. Dad, any bright ideas? You're the seasoned veteran of these things. Well, dear, I think you need to consider the long game. Don't just patch up outbreaks, think about containment. Have you considered utilizing the Operational Expert's ability to build a research station quickly? It's invaluable. And, frankly, someone needs to get a move on with finding a cure for the black disease. It’s spreading like wildfire. Reminds me of the fundraising efforts for the tsunami relief… completely overwhelming. He's right, you know. Containment is key. Remember that time we played this in Aberystwyth, and Gareth just kept trying to cure everything at once? Complete disaster! We lost before we even reached the eradication phase. Oh,  that  game! Gareth insisted on naming each disease after a particularly irritating politician. It was…distracting. I remember! The “Boris Bug” was particularly virulent, apparently. Honestly, you lot. Okay, so Dad's right. Containment. I’ll move my dispatcher to Atlanta, hopefully slow things down in North America. Rhys, you focus on Europe,  please ? Fine, fine. But if I get another outbreak card for Europe, I'm blaming you. And then  you’re  naming the diseases after politicians. Maybe we should all agree on a theme for the diseases. Historical figures? Famous villains? Ooh, I like that idea! We could have the "Nero Plague" and the “Dick Turpin Toxicity”. Now you’re just being silly, Gwyn. But it’s certainly more entertaining than losing! I think I'll play an event card.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just  bonkers . Did you see Mr. Tumble trying to fly? Honestly, a grown man with a spotty bag thinking he could take off! It was funny, Mummy! He flapped his arms really hard! Was he wearing his spotty bag? Because he  always  wears his spotty bag! He absolutely was, darling. Always prepared, that Mr. Tumble. Honestly, the CBeebies pantomime is a tradition now, isn’t it? Every Christmas Eve. Though, frankly, my brain cells are slowly being eroded by the repetition of ‘Something Special’. I like ‘Something Special’! Makaton is good! It  is  good, sweetheart. Very good. It’s just… pervasive. Anyway, speaking of things being good, have we completely finalised plans for Elsie’s birthday? It's creeping up, you know. July's not that far off. Can we have a bouncy castle? A REALLY big one? We'll see, Leo. We'll see. We discussed a garden party, remember? Perhaps with a theme? Any thoughts? Princesses! And unicorns! And glitter  everywhere ! Glitter everywhere is… a very Elsie request. Okay, princesses and unicorns it is. We can manage the glitter. Though I’m issuing a pre-emptive apology to anyone who visits afterwards. It gets  into  everything. Can we have a chocolate cake? With sprinkles? And those little sugar flowers? Absolutely a chocolate cake. Sprinkles are non-negotiable. And yes to the sugar flowers. You two have excellent taste. It's just… remembering to actually  order  the cake. Last year was a bit of a disaster, wasn't it? Remember ending up with the Victoria sponge from the supermarket at the last minute? It was still yummy! It was. But not quite the majestic unicorn cake Elsie had envisioned. Right, I'm writing it down  now . Cake – order. Before I forget again. Has anyone been watching  Bluey  lately? Honestly, that show is a revelation. Bluey is good! Bingo is the best! She's so silly! She is, isn’t she? It's teaching me so much about imaginative play. I was telling Mrs. Davies at school about it – she's got a little one the same age as Leo – and she said her mother used to always say ‘if you can't say something nice, don’t say anything at all’. Grandma says that! Your Grandma does, doesn't she? It's a classic. A bit outdated maybe, considering we want children to be able to express their feelings, but… a sweet sentiment.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork involved with even  thinking  about moving to Switzerland is ridiculous. It’s not just a visa, it’s registering your socks, practically! Sounds…thorough. Though, you’d think a country known for its efficiency would streamline the process a bit. Are you still set on Zurich, then? It feels a long way from…well, from having a proper Sunday roast. Zurich's lovely, I’ve been. But Anna's right, the food is...different. All cheese and precision. No comforting gravy. But honestly, Liam, if the job's genuinely a step up, it has to be worth the paperwork and the potential culinary disappointment. What does Sarah think about it all? That’s the tricky part. She’s…hesitant. She’s built a really good life here, her friends, her yoga studio. Leaving that behind feels huge for her. And she’s just landed that promotion at the university - leading the postgraduate media course. Oh wow, that's brilliant for Sarah! That  is  a significant thing to leave. Maybe you two need to sit down and really map out what you both want in the next five years. Independence is important, but so is compromise. We have been. Endless discussions. She worries about the language barrier, even though she’s amazing at picking up languages. Swiss German is apparently… a beast. And honestly, I think a part of her is scared of a complete life reset. After everything with… well, you know. With Mark. Right. That was rough. It's understandable she’d be cautious about disrupting things again. Maybe Switzerland feels too much like starting  completely  over. Has she considered maybe looking for teaching opportunities over there, even initially part-time? It might make it feel less like she's sacrificing her career. I suggested that! She’s explored a few options, but nothing that feels quite right. Apparently, the education system is…very rigid. Less room for her innovative teaching methods. It’s frustrating. The engineering role is perfect for me, genuinely. It’s leading a team working on sustainable energy solutions. Something I really believe in. That  does  sound perfect. It's always the sticking points with partners, isn't it? It’s rarely the big picture, it’s the details. Have you tried just acknowledging how hard it is for her to even consider this? Not trying to 'fix' it, just…validate her feelings?

...and honestly, the profiteroles were a disaster. They just  collapsed . Absolutely flattened. I think I overwhipped the choux pastry. It looked like a pile of sad, cream-filled pancakes.      Oh, dear! That's always a risk with choux. It's so temperamental, isn't it? You need a surgeon’s precision, I swear. Mine usually turn out okay, but I follow Delia Smith’s recipe religiously. Are you a Delia devotee, Helen?      I admire Delia, I truly do, but I tend to… improvise. Which, in the case of profiteroles, is clearly a mistake. Speaking of disasters, remember when we were kids, and Sarah insisted on ‘improving’ Mum’s trifle with pickled onions?      Oh my god! How could I  forget  that? The look on Grandad's face! He just silently pushed his plate away. He was a man of few words, your Grandad, wasn’t he?      He was. A very… stoic man. He wouldn’t dream of complaining. He'd just suffer in silence, bless him. And Sarah, well, she always was a little… experimental. Even now. Though thankfully, her experiments are usually confined to fashion, not food.      True. She’s still rocking those bright orange Doc Martens. Which, coming from someone who spent their teen years in floral dresses, I find quite… bold. It's funny how our tastes change, isn’t it? I mean, I was obsessed with My Little Pony. I had the whole collection!      Oh, My Little Pony! I was more of a Sindy girl myself. Though I did briefly dabble in the pony world. It’s weird, isn’t it? The toys we fixate on. Do you think it's a regional thing? I mean, being Essex girls, were we predisposed to Sindy over Barbie, or something?      That’s an interesting thought. I wonder. I was Sindy all the way. Although, Peterborough isn’t  quite  Essex, is it? It’s sort of… a halfway house. We definitely had a bit of a different vibe. Much less…glamorous. More practical. My mum always said we needed sensible shoes.      Sounds like my mum. Sensible shoes and a firm belief in sensible accountancy. Which, thankfully, I followed through on. Though sometimes I wonder if I should have opened a My Little Pony emporium.      You’d have made a killing! Seriously! Nostalgia is huge right now. Do you ever think about your dialect growing up? My nan always used to say things that I didn't understand until I moved away from Essex.

…and then the seagull  actually  tried to steal Dad’s sandwich right off his plate! It was audacious, honestly. You should have seen his face. No way! Dad and seagulls, a classic battle of wills. He probably just offered it a chip to distract it, didn't he? He always does. Oh, he did offer it a chip, alright. A very soggy chip. Said it deserved it for the cheek of it. Honestly, that harbour area at Whitby is  full  of 'em. Bold as brass, they are. Bold as brass and probably riddled with germs. I told him he should have stuck to the fish and chips  from  a shop, not attempting to have a picnic amongst avian thieves. You always worry, Dad. It was a nice picnic! Though I admit, the seagull did raise the stakes. Mum, weren't you sketching at that point? You missed the whole drama! I was. Trying to capture the abbey, you know? It's such a dramatic building, especially when the light’s right. Honestly, Whitby is stunning. We hadn’t been since… well, since you two were little terrors running around the beach. Terrors? We were exploring! And building magnificent sandcastles. Which the tide inevitably destroyed. It was a valuable life lesson about impermanence. More likely you were chucking buckets of water at unsuspecting tourists. Okay, maybe a  little  water chucking. But Mum's right, Whitby is gorgeous. Did you go up the 199 steps? I remember being utterly exhausted after that as a kid. We did! Twice, actually. Once during the day, and again at dusk. The views are breathtaking. Though my knees were complaining a bit on the way down the second time. Getting old, you know. You're not old, Mum! Just… vintage. Besides, Dad would have carried you if you’d asked. He’s secretly a strongman. Don't exaggerate. I managed to  support  myself with my walking stick, thank you very much. And the fish and chips were worth every step. They do a proper battered haddock there, you know. None of this frozen nonsense. Good to know. We should go sometime. Maybe a weekend trip? It's only a few hours drive. I’m in! I could do with a bit of sea air. And we could take Buster. He’d love the beach - though he'd probably try to chase the seagulls, wouldn’t he? Oh, don’t even think about it!

… honestly, I still think the sourdough was a bit dense. Did you use enough hydration, Sarah? It felt like trying to chew through a brick. Oh, come  on , Mark. It was perfectly acceptable sourdough! A little rustic, perhaps. And you ate two slices! Morning, you two. What’s this about brick-like bread? Sounds ominous for a Saturday. Just Sarah’s latest baking experiment. Let's just say my jaw got a workout. It's a learning curve, isn’t it? I’m trying to get the hang of it. This recipe said 75% hydration, which seemed like a lot… 75%? Crikey. That  is  a lot. I tried making macarons once. That was a disaster. Tiny colourful biscuits of despair. Speaking of disasters, did you see what happened with that influencer, Bethany Bloom, and her ‘organic’ skincare line? Apparently, it was anything but. Bethany Bloom? No, missed that one. Is she one of those ‘clean living’ types who charges a fortune for glorified scented water? Exactly! Turns out the ‘natural’ ingredients were mostly chemicals and she was massively misleading people. The journalist investigation was brutal. I’m actually working on a piece about the regulation – or lack thereof – of influencer marketing. Good! It’s ridiculous how much sway they have. My students are constantly talking about what they’ve bought because some TikTok person told them to. It’s exhausting trying to teach them critical thinking skills when their heroes are selling them nonsense. It's the same with tech, isn't it? Everyone believes the hype. I was explaining to my dad the other day about the limitations of AI. He thinks it's going to solve all our problems and build him a self-cleaning shed. Bless him. My mum thinks everything can be fixed with a bit of WD-40. Speaking of fixing things, how’s the project going, Mark? The one with the…what was it, the wastewater treatment plant? Slowly. It’s a nightmare, honestly. Bureaucracy, budget cuts, and a client who keeps changing his mind. It's all very 'scope creep' at the moment. I spent all of Friday arguing about sensor placement; he wants to save money, but it’ll compromise the whole system's accuracy. I swear, sometimes I wonder why I bothered with a postgrad degree. Sounds stressful. You need a proper weekend. Are you still on for that walk on Sunday? I need to get out of London for a bit, clear my head.

…and honestly, the satnav just decided I was going to drive  through  Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning rose bushes. It was terrifying. I swear, these things have a mind of their own. You and technology, eh, Chloe? You always blame the machine. Google Maps never lets me down, ever. Though, to be fair, I usually just follow what I already know. My internal Peterborough satnav is pretty solid. Google Maps is alright. Bit battery-hungry, though, innit? Especially when you’re already lost. Happened to me last week, ended up down a farm track looking for Dave’s. Farm tracks? Ha! Reminds me of a trip to Saudi, years ago. Trying to find a barracks outside Riyadh. The map they gave us… well, let's just say it hadn’t been updated since Lawrence of Arabia. Ended up asking a bloke herding camels for directions. He pointed vaguely, and said, “That way. Past the big rock.” Worked a treat, actually. Saudi Arabia? Wow, Reg, you've seen some things! It's a bit different from our farewell dinner at The Red Lion, isn’t it? How was it, generally? Apart from the navigational challenges. Hot. Very hot. And dusty. But good people. Very hospitable. They offered me mint tea everywhere. Couldn’t say no, even though I was practically dehydrated by lunchtime. Different world, though. Appreciate a proper pint even more after that, I can tell you. Speaking of appreciating things... Chloe, are you still stuck with that beige box of a flat? You said you were thinking about decorating? Oh god, don’t even  mention  the flat. It’s… beige. Profoundly beige. I’ve finally got a weekend off, so I’m planning on tackling the living room. But I have absolutely no idea where to start. I keep pinning things on Pinterest, then realise I have neither the skills nor the budget. Decorating’s a nightmare. I helped my Nan re-do her bedroom last year. She wanted magnolia…  everywhere . Three coats. I nearly lost my mind. Magnolia. The colour of no hope. You need a splash of something cheerful, love. A nice dark blue, maybe? Ground things nicely. Remember your Auntie Maureen’s parlour? She had a lovely burgundy wallpaper with gold trim. Very…regal. Burgundy and gold… that's… bold. Maybe a little  too  bold. I was thinking something more along the lines of a muted green? But then I worry it'll make the room look smaller.

… honestly, I think it’s the pollen. Stockholm’s beautiful, absolutely stunning gardens, but my sinuses are  killing  me. I feel like I’ve got a permanent head cold. Oh, poor love. You said you were feeling a bit rough yesterday, didn’t you? I told you, you need to remember your antihistamines. You always forget when we travel. It’s the classic Alistair move. It’s not  always ! Just… frequently. And they make me drowsy, you know? I’ve got that investor call tomorrow, can’t be nodding off mid-pitch. Besides, I thought Swedish air was supposed to be pristine. Pristine, yes. Pollen-free, not so much. Especially in a botanical garden, darling. They're deliberately cultivating all sorts of flowering things. Look at those rhododendrons – glorious, but notorious pollen producers. She’s right. And honestly, a little drowsiness might make the investor call  more  agreeable. No high-pressure tactics from Alistair, finally! Very funny, both of you. I’m serious though. I feel…off. Not just the sinuses. A bit fatigued. Maybe I’m coming down with something. Hmm. You’ve been pushing yourself incredibly hard with the new venture. Sleepless nights, endless meetings… you need to listen to your body, Alistair. You’re not a machine. And you’re terrible at delegating. Honestly, you try to do everything yourself. That's even  more  exhausting than the investor pitches. Remember last year, the whole debacle with the website copy? You stayed up for forty-eight hours straight! That was a  critical  issue! And I got it sorted, didn’t I? Look, I appreciate the concern, genuinely. It’s just… I’m wired a certain way. I need to feel in control. Control is an illusion, love. A very attractive, but ultimately illusory one. Look, there's a wonderful little health food shop near our hotel. They do these amazing herbal teas – apparently really good for boosting the immune system. We could pop in after we finish looking at the orchids. And they have elderflower cordial! Perfect for a sniffly nose. And maybe some of those Swedish pastilles – the ones with lingonberry and honey. That’ll soothe your throat. You two are ganging up on me. Fine. Herbal tea and pastilles it is. But no lectures about 'work-life balance', agreed? No promises. Although, speaking of balance, have you noticed how the Swedes manage their public spaces? The way they integrate greenery into the city is incredible.

…and honestly, the Siri on my phone  still  doesn’t understand me half the time. It’s like, I’m speaking perfectly clear English, but because I draw out my vowels a bit, apparently I'm speaking Martian. It's ridiculous! You wouldn't believe the things it thinks I'm saying. Martian, eh? Sounds about right. They design these things up in London, don’t they? All clipped vowels and fast talking. Doesn’t stand a chance against a proper Kentish accent. Mine’s faded a bit, mind you, living in London for so long, but…it’s still there. Oh, definitely. I find myself slipping more and more into a…well, a bit of everything now, working in Harlow. You pick up bits from patients, you know? Though I still get stick from my daughter for saying ‘loo’ instead of ‘toilet’. She thinks it’s ancient. Loo’s fine! Sounds perfectly normal. Though, to be fair, hearing anyone talk about ‘loo’ just reminds me of Nan. Always sending me out to check if anyone else needed the ‘loo’ at family gatherings. Nan was…a character. Remember that time she tried to teach Dad how to ride a bike in the garden? He was about forty and absolutely terrified. Terrified is putting it mildly! He ended up in the rose bushes. Said he nearly broke his hip. Your mother just stood there, calmly pruning, offering advice like, "Lean into the turn, dear!" She never did understand why he didn't enjoy cycling. Said it was good for his weight. Speaking of weight... have you seen Dave lately? He’s really filling out. I worry about his health. He says he’s fine, just putting on a bit of winter padding, but… He's been hitting the pubs more, hasn't he? Ever since… well, you know. Things with Sarah. Honestly, it's just sad. He doesn't cope well with anything. Turns to the booze. It’s awful. And it’s not fair on little Leo, is it? Seeing his dad like that. I try to take him to the park, get him out of the house, but…it's not the same. Custody battles. Always messy. Your mother and I had our moments, you know. Not Sarah and Dave level, thankfully. But still… difficult. The thing is, once you bring a child into the world, you've got a responsibility.

…and honestly, the meringue just wouldn’t peak. I whipped it for  ages . Absolutely ages. It just stayed… floppy. Like a sad, sugary cloud. A floppy cloud? Sounds kinda cool, actually. Is that what a failed Baked Alaska looks like? Cool? Leo, it was a disaster! A sticky, icy disaster. I was trying to recreate one my grandmother used to make. She was a  legend  in the kitchen, Gran. Everything tasted better when she made it. Gran sounds awesome. Did she have one of those little cheese graters with the handle? The really old-fashioned ones? She did! A bright red one. She used to grate the hardest cheddar you could imagine for mac and cheese. Used to say it built character. And strength in your wrists. My Nana has one. It’s a bit rusty though. I tried using it once and nearly took my knuckles off. Oh dear! Be careful with those things. Anyway, back to the Baked Alaska… I think I need to revamp my technique. It’s for the Halloween party, remember? I promised Mrs. Henderson a showstopper dessert. Oh yeah, the party! Are you still needing help setting up? I could do balloons, I guess. Or, like, spooky lighting. That would be fantastic, actually. You’re a whiz with those fairy lights. And maybe… you could help me recruit some older students to help with the younger ones?
