Just to keep an eye out, you know. It’s getting pretty big. Recruit? Like, get people to  work  at our Halloween party? That’s a bit mean. No, not work! Just… assist. The seven and eights get a bit wild. It’s about responsible supervision, darling. It’s something I’m dealing with constantly at the programme, actually. Finding good, reliable young people. It's harder than you think. What kind of programme? You never really talk about your job. It's… complicated. I’m a Programme Director for a youth outreach scheme. We work with kids who are, well, having a tough time. Making sure they’re safe, helping them get into education or training. It's rewarding, but...it can be difficult. You see things, you know? Things that make you angry. Like what? Oh… things. Instances of discrimination, unfairness. Little things piling up. It reminds me… when  I  was a teenager, a teacher actually told me I wouldn't get into university because I wasn't ‘the academic type’.

…and honestly, the bagels weren’t  nearly  as good as they make out. All hype, I tell ya. Hype! Mind you, the sheer scale of everything… Times Square, Central Park… it just dwarfs anything we’ve got here, doesn't it? Proper overwhelming. You sound like you survived it, rather than enjoyed it. New York isn't for everyone, is it? I’ve always fancied it, but the thought of all those people… gives me the willies. More of a quiet coastal town girl myself, clearly. This, though, this is a lovely start to the day. Toast and a proper brew. Much better than a lukewarm hotel coffee. Aye, this  is  good. Proper strong brew, this. And a full English, you can't beat it. Though I was having second thoughts about the black pudding… still, I had to give it a go. Though, you know, after all that New York excitement, I’m thinking I need something…calm. Calm, you say? You’re finally admitting defeat and giving up on your slightly unhinged ambition? What ambition? Oh, you mean the flying lessons? Don’t be daft. It’s just… sitting in a tiny plane, hurtling through the air… suddenly feels a bit much. Especially after nearly being trampled by tourists in Manhattan. Fair enough. Though I thought you were enjoying pretending to be Amelia Earhart. Did you at least manage a loop-the-loop? Loop-the-loop! I managed a… controlled circuit. And a mild panic attack. The instructor was very patient. He kept saying, “Just remember your training, Maureen!” As if remembering my training would magically stop my stomach from trying to leave my body first. Oh, Maureen. You always did have a flair for the dramatic. Anyway, what are your plans for today then, besides avoiding airborne activities? I thought you were heading back up north this afternoon. Aye, I am. Train’s at four. But I thought I'd potter around Mumbles for a bit first. Maybe get a nice walk along the prom. Unless you’ve got some grand Swansea adventure planned for me? Nothing grand, sadly. Just a mountain of marking to wade through. Honestly, the students think essays write themselves. Keeps me in a job, I suppose. Have you seen what's trending on that… what's it called… TikTok? Apparently, university lecturers are becoming a thing. TikTok? Good heavens, no. I actively avoid social media.

Right, ‘quixotic’ for a triple word score! Take  that , Amelia. Though honestly, you were staring into space. Again. I was  strategizing . It’s a complex game, you know. Unlike some people who just throw letters at the board hoping for the best. And it's not my fault you happen to have all the vowels! Strategizing looks suspiciously like daydreaming about daffodils, if you ask me. You were practically smelling the roses. Reminds me of the Chelsea Flower Show… bit early to be thinking about that, though. You going this year, Ben? Last year was…intense. So many hydrangeas. Felt like I was drowning in blue. Nah, probably not. Too much fuss. Gives me the willies, all that perfectly arranged greenery. I prefer a bit of chaos, like this Scrabble board. Although, I’m still stuck with a Q, a Z and a double X. This is hopeless. That's because you’re trying to make ‘xylophone’ again. It’s not going to happen. Honestly, Leo, we discussed this. Think smaller. 'Quiz'? 'Xerox'? Speaking of spelling... I was reading an article about the origins of words the other day. Did you know ‘awkward’ originally meant ‘turned aside’? Like, physically turned away. Isn’t that weird? That  is  fascinating! Language is just… layers and layers of history. It’s why I love linguistics. Though, honestly, sometimes I question my life choices. Another essay on Proto-Indo-European phonology? Send help. Tell me about it. I’m drowning in dissertation research. My supervisor keeps asking for ‘greater nuance.’ What even  is  greater nuance when you’re writing about Victorian sewage systems? Sounds… fragrant. Seriously though, try not to stress. Remember when you were late for your A-Level History exam because your alarm didn't go off?  That  was a stressful morning. Don’t remind me! Mum still brings it up. “Richard, you’ve always had a talent for dramatic entrances.” She thought I’d deliberately missed the start to build tension! The teacher just gave me a patronizing look and told me to get on with it. Classic Mum. She always finds a silver lining. Mine would have had a full-blown meltdown. She's surprisingly competitive, even about things that don’t matter. It's probably why she's so good at Scrabble. She is a Scrabble  fiend . Remember Christmas? She practically interrogated Ben about his tile placement. She did! And then tried to convince me ‘zucchini’ was an acceptable word, despite me pointing out it’s Italian.

…and honestly, Doreen, I still reckon they overcharge for a packet of biscuits these days. A  packet ! Used to be you could get a good, solid biscuit for pennies, now it’s… well, it’s daylight robbery, it is. Oh, Arthur, you say that every time you go to the shop. You’ve been saying it for thirty years! It’s inflation, dear. Everything goes up. Though I do agree, the quality’s gone down. Remember those Garibaldis? Proper biscuits. Garibaldis! Now  there  was a biscuit. Proper ginger, bit of a snap to ‘em. These new ones… they crumble to dust in your mouth. Dust, I tell ya! Makes a man feel old, it does. Reminds me of me own teeth, practically. Don’t be silly, Arthur. Your teeth are fine. A little wobbly maybe, but fine. You had that dentist appointment last month, remember? He said you were doing well for your age. He  said  that, didn't he? Doctors always say that, don't they? Keeps you comin’ back for more poking and prodding. Still, at least he didn’t try to sell me electric toothbrush again. Nasty things, electric toothbrushes. Well, they  are  supposed to be better for cleaning. But you're a stubborn old mule, Arthur. Nothing anyone says will convince you to change your ways. Stubborn? I’m… traditional! There’s a difference. I like my things done the way they always have been. A proper brush, a bit of bicarbonate of soda now and then…works a treat, it does. Bicarbonate of soda? Oh, Arthur! You and your old wives’ tales. I swear, you’re living in the nineteen fifties. Well, the fifties weren’t so bad, were they? Things were simpler then. People knew their place. Less fuss. No one glued to these blasted… whatchamacallits… smartphones. Here we go again. You hate the technology. Honestly, it's not so bad. It keeps us connected with the grandchildren. Did Emily send you that photo of little Leo with his new dinosaur? Dinosaur, eh? Big one? They’re always sendin’ pictures of dinosaurs. That boy’s obsessed. Though, I must admit, it’s nice to see ‘em. They don’t visit as often as they used to. They're busy, Arthur. They have their own lives now. You know that. But they do call. And the pictures are a good way to see them, even if it’s not the same.

…and honestly, the rosemary in this lamb is just  chef’s kiss . Where did you get it, actually, Sarah? It smells far more…robust than anything I’ve managed to grow, even back in Southend. Oh, that’s from Old Man Hemmings at the farmer’s market, Dad. He’s got a little patch dedicated solely to herbs. Says it’s his retirement project. You’d like him, he’s a bit of a character. Always has a story. He does. And the lamb is lovely, Anthony. Really lovely. You've outdone yourself with the Yorkshire puddings too. They're not usually my favourite, but these are perfect. Light and crispy. Well, I’ve had a lot of practice, haven't I? Retirement allows for dedicated pudding-making. Though I did nearly set the smoke alarm off attempting to get the fat hot enough. Still, a small price to pay. Speaking of practice, are you two still keeping up with that horrifying fitness app, 'Stride & Grind'? Don’t remind me. It’s…motivating, in a deeply unpleasant way. It keeps badgering me about my step count. Apparently, marking essays doesn’t count as ‘active recovery’. It's ridiculous, isn't it? I ignored half the challenges this week. Honestly, five thousand steps a day is quite enough for a teacher. We’re on our feet all day! Though, I did manage that virtual hike up Snowdon. Snowdon! Good grief. You two are pushing yourselves. I’m sticking to gentle strolls to the village shop for biscuits. That’s my cardio. Did you see in the  Devon Echo  they’re finally,  finally , putting the finishing touches on the new train station in Kingsbridge? Oh, yes! I saw that. It’s been delayed for – what – nearly two years? It’s a joke, really. More than a joke. It's been impacting the whole area. People relying on the bus service, prices going up… It’s good they're finally getting it sorted though. It'll be a real lifeline for a lot of people, especially those commuting to Plymouth. Absolutely. Remember when they said it'd be open last spring? Classic. Still, better late than never, I suppose. It might even encourage me to venture further afield. A day trip to Exeter, perhaps. Though the thought of navigating a train station fills me with dread. You'll be fine, Dad. I can go with you.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of him, claiming he’d  read  all of Shakespeare. Like, really? All of it? When we were dissecting  Hamlet  in the seminar, he just kept nodding along, saying “Oh yes, the melancholy Dane…” He clearly hadn't cracked a spine. Classic. You get those in every uni group, don’t you? The posers. I’m still trying to get my head around the essay question for next week. ‘The enduring relevance of tragedy in a post-modern context’… honestly, sounds like something they made up to sound clever. Tell me about it. Mine’s on the political subtext in  King Lear . Feel like I’m wading through treacle trying to make it interesting. How’s sixth form going, by the way? Still enjoying it? It's alright. A bit…less weighty than what you're dealing with, I guess. Mostly prepping for A-Levels. Though, everyone's talking about Ben’s stag do. It’s going to be  mental . Prague. Prague?! Seriously? That's ambitious. My cousin, Liam, had his in Brighton. Ended with him accidentally proposing to a seagull with a chip. True story. No way! A seagull?! That’s brilliant. Ben's trying to keep it all very ‘cultural experience’ though. Art galleries and…classical music concerts. Which is terrifying because that's not Ben  at all . He's a FIFA addict. The man's a fraud then! Speaking of FIFA, have you seen the Premier League lately? Arsenal are actually looking…good. Properly good. Don’t jinx it! I’m a Man United fan, so I’m contractually obligated to be pessimistic. Though, even I have to admit, Arteta’s doing something right. It's less painful to watch, anyway. What are you playing at the moment, aside from avoiding Shakespeare-pretenders? I’ve been hooked on  Elden Ring  again. It’s brutal. Absolutely brutal. I swear, every enemy is designed to crush your soul. But it's so rewarding when you finally beat a boss. It’s like…a micro-achievement in the face of overwhelming existential dread. Very university, really. You always manage to make things sound profoundly depressing. I’m sticking with  Overwatch 2  at the moment. Easier to digest when you’ve spent the day trying to understand post-structuralism. Have you been following any of the political stuff in Europe? It’s a mess, isn't it? It’s…complicated.

…and honestly, the presentation just  died . Completely flat. Old man Hemmings, you know, the Head of Department? He just stared at me like I’d presented him with a plate of slugs. Oh no! Hemmings is…intense. What happened? Technical glitch? You always rehearse, don’t you? Rehearsed to within an inch of my life, honestly. It was the data. Apparently, the projections I was using were ‘optimistic’. Optimistic! As if I  made  the sales figures tank. It's just… frustrating. Project coordinating is supposed to be about keeping things  on  track, not magically fixing a downturn in the market. Ugh, sounds stressful. You’re too good at your job to be getting flak for things you can’t control. How did you manage to salvage it? I didn’t, really. Just a lot of apologising and promising a revised report. It’s fine. I just needed to vent. God, it’s good to actually  talk  about it. How’s life at Pearson going? Still battling the marketing world? Battling is a good word for it. It’s… a lot. We’re launching this new online learning platform and the pressure is on. It's all KPIs and target demos and… honestly, half the time I feel like I’m speaking another language. At least the coffee here is good. This carrot cake is heavenly. Oh, you are right! Greens do a good cake. It's a necessary fuel source for dealing with tyrannical bosses, I reckon. Speaking of necessary fuel, how’s your mum doing? I haven't seen her since… Christmas, was it? She’s alright. Still gardening obsessively. She reckons it's the only thing keeping her young. She asked about you specifically – wanted to know if I'd dragged you kicking and screaming to Oxford for university and effectively ruined your life. Classic Mum! Tell her I'm thriving, despite everything. Oxford was brilliant, and honestly, it prepared me for Hemmings and his slugs. It's just… starting to feel like I need a bit of a plan, you know? Everyone's getting engaged or buying houses… I feel slightly behind. Don't even. I saw Sarah from uni announced her engagement on Instagram. With  Mark . Mark, who she swore was the human embodiment of beige. People are weird. And houses? Don’t even get me started. The housing market is a joke. Exactly! So, you’re not feeling the pressure, then?

…and honestly, the basil’s looking a bit peaky, isn’t it? I thought I was being a good plant mum, watering it regularly and everything, but it just seems…sad. Like it’s given up on life. Sad basil. That’s a new one. You've got a knack for anthropomorphising botanical specimens, you know that? Probably needs repotting. They get rootbound pretty quickly, especially basil. You were using that tiny pot from the garden centre, weren’t you? Aye, the little terracotta one. Thought it was cute. Maybe ‘cute’ isn't conducive to thriving. Gran always said plants like to feel spacious. She had a jungle in her back garden, honestly. Roses climbing everything, dahlias the size of dinner plates… and she could coax anything to grow. Even Auntie Brenda's notoriously difficult orchids. Brenda and her orchids. A saga, that was. She’d phone my mum every other week demanding advice, then ignore it completely and wonder why they keeled over. Speaking of Mum, did she mention anything about coming down for the weekend? She said something about needing a break from Dad’s experimental cooking. She did! Apparently, he’s decided he’s a master of Moroccan tagines. Last night’s involved fifteen different spices, a whole chicken, and according to her, tasted vaguely of cinnamon and regret. She said the kitchen smelled like a souk for three days. Oh, bless him. He means well. Remember when he tried to make sourdough during lockdown? The starter nearly took over the fridge. It had a name, didn't it? Bartholomew, or something equally ridiculous. Bartholomew! Yes! And he treated it like a pet. Talking to it, feeding it…It was genuinely unsettling. I think Mum secretly enjoyed the chaos, though. It kept him occupied. Honestly, she's a saint. She is. And a phenomenal cook, which is why Dad’s attempts are so… bravely ambitious. I’m making biscuits later, actually. Trying out a new recipe – lavender and lemon shortbread. Want to be a taste tester? Lavender and lemon? Ooh, that sounds lovely! Is it fiddly? I attempted macarons last month and nearly had a breakdown. Hundreds of bits of almond flour everywhere. It looked like a blizzard had hit the kitchen. Macarons are notoriously evil. Don't beat yourself up about that. This is fairly straightforward, thankfully. Just a lot of chilling the dough. Which gives me time to… procrastinate on my thesis, naturally.

… honestly, appalling. Absolutely appalling. They gave him a penalty for  that ? It was a clear dive. Clear as day! You’re still on about the football then, Alistair? Thought a Professor of Ancient History might find more pressing matters to occupy his mind on a Monday morning. Pressing matters, Gwyn? My blood pressure is a pressing matter! The injustice of it all! And don’t patronise me, I appreciate a good game. It’s a perfectly respectable pastime. Though frankly, the modern game is going to the dogs. And these players… all flash and no substance. Did you see young Bellingham’s son getting escorted off the pitch after the final whistle? Apparently threw a tantrum because his dad didn’t wave at  him  enough. Oh, I did hear something about that. Celebrity offspring, eh? Always a bit… entitled. Though, you know, their childhoods must be odd. Never a normal experience. Reminds me of hearing stories about the snooker players' kids back in the 80s. Constantly travelling, hotels, no school friends… Exactly! It’s not healthy. It breeds a certain… lack of perspective. Different world entirely. Speaking of perspective, how was  your  weekend, Gwyn? Anything more stimulating than questionable refereeing decisions? Relatively peaceful, actually. Spent most of it in the garden. Trying to wrestle the weeds out of the rose bushes. They’re winning, I think. It’s becoming a full-scale war. You wouldn't believe the bindweed – it's like a green python, wrapping itself around everything. Ah, gardening. A noble pursuit. I dabble, but I lack your… dedication. Cairo wasn’t exactly conducive to cultivating prize-winning roses, you know? Mostly sand and the occasional stubborn date palm. Though my mother had a spectacular bougainvillea. Sounds lovely. You miss Egypt then? After growing up there? In parts. The heat, certainly. And the smell of jasmine… But I’m a British man through and through, Gwyn. Always was. Even born under the Egyptian sun. Which brings me to something slightly less fragrant: the student essays. Have you started marking yet? Don't even mention it. I've got a pile the size of Snowdon looming over me. The standard is… variable, to say the least. One young man argued that Julius Caesar was a proto-socialist. A  proto-socialist ! Good Lord. They do say remarkable things, don't they? I had one who insisted that Cleopatra was an alien.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had waiting for me this morning was just… demoralising. It’s like everyone decided to save all their problems for Monday. Honestly, did nobody do  anything  while I was off? Mummy, can we build a fairy house in the garden after lunch? Please? A really, really sparkly one? Oh, sweetheart. Maybe later, darling. Mummy needs to just… clear her head for a bit. We’ll see, okay? It depends how quickly I can wrestle this inbox into submission. Sounds rough, Mum. Honestly, some people treat out-of-office replies as a personal challenge to ignore. What’s the worst one been so far? Oh, don't even ask. Old Mr. Henderson. Sent me a three-paragraph complaint about the quarterly report,  demanding  a revision, and copied in the CEO. The CEO, Freya! It was sent at 6am! Who thinks of that? Is Mr. Henderson grumpy? Like Grandad when his football team loses? A bit like that, yes, poppet. A little bit grumpy. Now, let's talk about something more cheerful. How are we doing with Lily’s Christening plans? I’ve booked the room at the Plough, have you spoken to your Auntie Carol about the cake? I did! She’s absolutely thrilled to be doing it. She's already brainstorming designs - apparently, it's going to involve sugar roses and everything. She’s sending me some pictures to show you this evening. Oh, that’s lovely! Carol’s cakes are always stunning. It will be such a beautiful day. Are we still aiming for the 18th? It feels like it’s creeping up so quickly. Will Grandma and Grandpa be there? And Cousin Thomas? Yes, sweetie, everyone will be there! Grandma and Grandpa are really excited. Thomas is… well, Thomas is trying to decide if he can get out of a football match. Typical. Honestly, that boy. It's always something. We need to pin him down soon. And what about decorations? I was thinking pastel blues and yellows? Sounds nice. I can do a quick trip to that shop in town – the one with all the party bits – on Wednesday, if you like? I've got a lecture in the morning and then a free afternoon. That would be amazing, thank you, Freya. You’re a lifesaver. Oh, and don't forget to ask them about balloons. Lily loves balloons.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is just…criminal. They expect us to be proactive  and  document every single breath we take? It’s ridiculous. Sounds awful, Mum. Still stuck with that new system then? I thought they said it was supposed to streamline things. Streamline? It’s added about five hours to my week, minimum. Honestly, I’m starting to dream in spreadsheets. Speaking of dreams, have you properly started looking at flights for New York? I have! Sort of. I’ve been browsing, mostly. It’s…expensive. Even with booking well in advance. And deciding  where  to stay is a nightmare. Everything’s either tiny and cheap, or massive and costs a fortune. New Yawk! Can we see the Statue of Liberty? And the dinosaurs! Yes, darling, we can see the Statue of Liberty. And maybe some dinosaurs, though I think the really big ones are in museums. We’ll have to look. You're very keen on dinosaurs at the moment, aren’t you? Uh-huh! T-Rex is the best! He  roars!  Okay, okay, settle down, little monster! Mum, about New York…I was thinking maybe we look at AirBnBs? Might be a better option for space and value. That’s a good idea. We definitely need a kitchen, even just for breakfast. Remember that holiday in Italy, when we were completely reliant on overpriced hotel breakfasts? Never again. Oh,  that  Italy trip! The one where Dad tried to order pasta carbonara with ketchup? Don't remind me! The waiter looked like he’d seen a ghost. Honestly, your father… he’s a good man, but his Italian is…creative. He still insists he was trying to clarify the sauce. Grandpa's funny! He is, isn’t he? He really is. So, New York… when are  you  free to really sit down and hammer out some details? I can’t spend my evenings buried in travel websites after the day I’ve had. This weekend is pretty clear. Saturday afternoon, maybe? We could order pizza and make a proper plan. I was also thinking, have we discussed what we actually  want  to do there? Beyond the Statue of Liberty and dinosaurs, obviously. Good point. I've always wanted to see a Broadway show. And maybe visit a museum or two, although Lily might get bored quickly. It's been ages since I've been to a proper art gallery.

…and then, right, the methodology section. This is where it gets a bit hairy, honestly. Professor Davies really wanted us to be granular about  why  we chose a qualitative approach over, say, a quantitative one. It wasn’t enough to just  say  it suited the research question. Granular, huh? Sounds about right for Davies. He loves a good justification. So, what did you go with? Something about needing nuanced understanding of lived experiences? That’s the usual spiel. Aye, something along those lines. But I had to really spell it out. See here? I basically argued that statistical analysis would’ve flattened the complexities of the narratives we were collecting. Like, reducing people’s actual experiences to numbers would’ve missed the whole point. It’s about understanding  how  they feel, not just  how many  feel a certain way. Makes sense. You're doing the oral history project on the decline of the mills, right? You need the stories, the feeling of it. Numbers wouldn’t capture that. I’m wrestling with something similar for my dissertation. It's on gentrification in Hackney, and I'm trying to decide if I need to include a section fully detailing the ethical considerations of interviewing displaced residents. Oh, that's a big one. Definitely. You  should . Especially with something sensitive like displacement. Think about power dynamics, informed consent… all that jazz. You don’t want to be re-traumatizing people just for the sake of your research. Exactly. My supervisor hinted at it, but said it could be "too much for a Masters dissertation." I’m thinking "too much" is better than being ethically questionable, yeah? A hundred percent. Davies would tear you apart if you skipped it. He’s got a real conscience, that man. Though, ironically, he’s notoriously brutal when marking. Speaking of brutal, have you looked at the referencing requirements for this module? It’s… biblical. Chicago style, apparently. Chicago?! Seriously? That's American, isn't it? We're meant to be doing Harvard! Absolute madness. It’s going to take me a week just to format the bibliography. It's already a mess. Tell me about it. I spent three hours last night just trying to figure out the correct formatting for a newspaper article. A  newspaper article ! It’s like they design these things to make you suffer. This bit here is where I’m particularly worried.

…and then, honestly, I was  flying . Not in a plane, mind you, but properly flying, like a bird. Over… well, I think it was Comberton, actually. Everything looked so small. And Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses were… glowing. Glowing roses? That’s a new one, even for your dreams. You always have bizarre ones. Remember the time you were arguing with a badger about the correct way to file tax returns? Don’t remind me. That was a stressful dream, even  in  the dream. This one was… peaceful, though. Just soaring. It made me think, you know? About wanting more freedom, I suppose. Did you see a unicorn? I dreamt about a unicorn last night. It had a sparkly horn. Did you now, love? A sparkly horn? That sounds brilliant. No unicorn in mine, unfortunately. Just glowing roses and a very small Mrs. Higgins. I dreamt I was a dinosaur! A really big one that ate all the broccoli. Good work, darling. Broccoli deserves to be eaten by dinosaurs. So, flying over Comberton… anything else happen? Were you escaping something? Because that’s usually the root of your flying dreams. No, not escaping. Just… observing. And thinking about getting a dog. A dog? Out of the blue? What brought  that  on? I thought we agreed a dog wouldn’t work with both of us working. I know, I know. It's just… seeing everything from up high, it felt… complete. Like something was missing. A furry, four-legged something. Imagine coming home and having a proper welcome, a wagging tail instead of… well, you. Don’t get me wrong, you’re a wonderful welcome, but it’s not  quite  the same. Oh, I see. So I’m lacking in enthusiastic tail-wagging? Right. And what breed of this dream-dog are we talking about? A golden retriever to match the pastoral vibe of your flying dream? Maybe. Or a scruffy terrier. Something that needs rescuing. That’s what the dream made me think about, needing to look after something. It's ridiculous, I know. We could name him Sparkle! Like my unicorn’s horn. No! Dinosaur! We should get a dinosaur. Definitely no dinosaur, sweethearts. Look, it’s a lovely thought, but realistically… it's tricky. We barely have time to breathe, let alone walk a dog properly. Unless… Unless what? Don't lead me on, Sarah. Unless we won the lottery.

…and honestly, the waiting room was  packed . Packed, I tell ya. Looked like half of Newcastle had decided to simultaneously injure themselves. Right, so you were there for ages then? After falling off that… what was it, a wonky paving slab? Sounds like something straight out of a sitcom. Wonky is an understatement! It was more like a miniature cliff face disguised as a pavement. I didn’t even see it. One minute I’m happily walking along, thinking about that new data set I need to clean, the next I’m airborne and tasting grit. Ouch. And your ankle? How bad is it, really? You sounded pretty nonchalant on the phone. Nonchalant is a coping mechanism, alright? It's throbbing, okay? Throbbing like a disco. And it’s properly swollen. The nurse said it  could  be sprained,  could  be fractured. They wanted an X-ray, but then said the wait would be another three hours, minimum. Three hours?! That’s ridiculous! You should’ve kicked up a fuss. I did! I said, “Look, I’m a responsible adult, and my ankle is clearly not enjoying life right now!” The nurse just smiled sympathetically and said they were prioritizing life-threatening injuries. Fair enough, I suppose. Though honestly, the pain  feels  life-threatening. Seriously. A&E is just… a mess these days. Remember when I sliced my hand open building that ridiculous flatpack bookshelf? Took nearly six hours to get stitched up. Oh aye, the bookshelf of doom! You were bleeding everywhere. I thought you were reenacting a scene from a horror movie. Dramatic license. The point is, it’s completely overwhelmed. They’re understaffed and everyone’s using it as their GP these days. Exactly! Old Mrs. Henderson was complaining about a cough she’d had for  two weeks . A cough! In A&E! I wanted to shake her gently. You wouldn’t dare ruffle Mrs. Henderson’s feathers. She’d have the whole street talking. Anyway, did they at least give you any pain relief? Any crutches? They gave me paracetamol. Paracetamol! Like that’s going to touch the sides. And a flimsy bandage. Honestly, it felt like a token gesture. No crutches. They said I  could  have used a wheelchair, but I'm not quite at that stage yet. I hobbled to the car. Right. Well, we’re nearly back at yours now. I'll help you get settled. We can get some proper ice on it.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the Suez Canal blockage again? Utter chaos. Reminded me of when that Ever Given got stuck – felt like the world was holding its breath waiting for a toy boat to be unstuck. Did you see the reports about the insurance claims, Arthur? Astronomical, they were. Good heavens, yes. Read a bit about it. Always something, isn’t there? Seems like global trade is held together with string these days. Though, frankly, I’m more concerned with what’s happening closer to home. Business is… slow. Terribly slow. Slow? Still? I thought after Christmas things might pick up for your little antique shop. People always seem to have a bit of disposable income after the holidays, looking for something unique. You'd think, wouldn't you? But it's been dreadful. Everyone's tightening their belts, I suppose. Fuel prices are ridiculous, and the talk of another recession… it makes people hesitant. I’m starting to wonder if I should just pack it all in, honestly. Pack it in? Arthur, you’ve built that shop up from nothing! Years of work, scouring auctions and boot sales. You can’t just throw that away. Easy for you to say, Richard. You’ve got a pension. I’ve got a shop full of mahogany and chipped porcelain and a rapidly dwindling bank balance. Honestly, I've been toying with an idea… a bit mad, perhaps. Oh? Do tell. You know I'm a sucker for a mad idea. Especially when paired with a good cuppa. More tea? Yes, please. Milk, no sugar. Right. Well, I was thinking…online auctions. But not just any online auctions. Specialist, curated auctions. Focusing on maritime antiques. Brighton’s a seaside town, massive naval history, and there's a surprisingly big collector base internationally. I’ve been doing some research. Maritime antiques, eh? That's… actually quite clever. A niche market. Less competition. You always did have an eye for spotting a good piece, even if you  did  pay too much for that hideous Victorian hat stand all those years ago. That hat stand was a steal! You just didn’t appreciate its… rustic charm. Anyway, I've been looking at setting up a website, getting professional photography done, learning about digital marketing. It’s a whole new world, to be honest. It is. Daunting, even. But you're a resourceful chap, Arthur.

…and honestly, the chips were swimming in grease. Swimming! I mean, it’s a pub, not a deep-fat fryer convention. You’re dramatic, you know that? They were perfectly acceptable chips. Though, I will admit, they did look a bit… enthusiastic. So, are we doing food here, or just sticking to drinks? I’m feeling a bit peckish. I think just drinks. I’ve had my chip-related near-death experience for the week. This place is actually quite nice, though. Have you noticed the stained glass? It’s a bit…unexpected for Woolwich, isn’t it? More something you’d find in a little village pub in the Cotswolds. It  is  rather good, actually. And look at those old photos on the wall. Proper historical stuff. Makes a change from the usual football memorabilia. Though, speaking of unexpected things, did you see Sarah Phelps is writing the new  Happy Valley ? No way! Really? That’s…actually brilliant. She’s  so  good at that gritty, psychological stuff. I was worried they’d try and soften it, make it all glamorous. But Sarah Phelps? She'll keep it real. I’ve been rewatching the first series, actually. Catherine Cawood is just phenomenal. Absolutely. And the way the landscape contributes to the mood. Yorkshire, bleak and beautiful. Reminds me a bit of Scotland, actually. Though Edinburgh’s got a bit more… bustle. Oh, you and your Edinburgh. You always find a way to bring it back to Edinburgh. Even when we’re talking about a fictional Yorkshire police sergeant. Well, it’s a fantastic city! And it’s where I formed my discerning taste in pubs, thank you very much. Speaking of which, this is a good ‘un. Nice atmosphere. What are you drinking? Just a gin and tonic. Trying to be sensible. Though, after those chips… I might need something a bit stronger. You? Pint of bitter. Old habits die hard. Reminds me of uni, actually. Spending evenings like this, arguing about film theory and pretending to understand post-structuralism. Oh god, don't remind me. All that navel-gazing. Though, I do miss the long conversations. We never have time for those anymore. Life gets in the way, doesn’t it? It does. Though we manage alright, I think. And at least we don't  have  to write essays about Derrida anymore. Brrr, it's getting chilly in here. I should have worn my heavier coat.

…aye, and the light was just  perfect . Hit the Old Man of Storr just right. Like somethin’ outta a film, honestly. Did ye see any o’ the photos I put up on Facebook? Aye, I did! Stunning, Hamish. Truly stunning. You've really gotten good with that camera, haven't ye? Remember when you were usin’ yer phone for everything and complainin’ about the blurry pictures of yer niece? Don’t remind me! That was a dark time for my photographic ambitions. No, honestly, it’s been the courses, ye know? And gettin’ oot there, actually  doin'  it. It’s not just the gear, though that helps. That new lens… a wee investment, mind ye, but worth every penny. It shows. You've a real eye for composition now. I was thinkin' actually, since you're gettin’ so into it, have ye considered goin’ further afield? Beyond Scotland? Further afield? What d'ye mean? Like, abroad? Aye, exactly. Think of the landscapes in Iceland, or even Patagonia. The light there...it's supposed to be incredible. I’ve always fancied both, though my work keeps me chained to a desk, unfortunately. Still get to travel a bit for conferences, but it's rarely for pleasure. Och, Iceland… now  there’s  an idea. I’ve seen some photos online, it looks… otherworldly. But a bit pricey, isn’t it? And Patagonia… that’s the South American place, right? A long haul! It is a bit of a commitment, aye. Iceland’s manageable though, especially if you go in the shoulder seasons – April/May or September/October. Flights aren't too bad, and you avoid the peak tourist rush. Patagonia's a different beast altogether, need proper planning and a fair bit of cash. But imagine the photos, Hamish! The mountains, the glaciers… I am imaginin’. I'm imaginin' the rain, mind ye. Always seems to be chuckin’ it down wherever ye go. We've had a proper spell of it here, haven't we? This Edinburgh weather is relentless. Tell me about it. Torrential all week. I practically swam to work this mornin’. Still, even the dreich days have their charm, don’t they? You can get some amazing moody shots when the light's like that. Aye, that’s true. I did a wee shoot down at Portobello beach yesterday, with the clouds rollin’ in. Turned oot alright, actually. Though I nearly lost the tripod in the waves!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I got over the weekend was ridiculous. Just… endless. I barely touched my book. You know, the one I was  so  excited about? Oh, Mum, that sounds awful. Work still chasing you even on your days off? It's not fair. What about the nursery open day? Did you manage to book a slot? I’ve been meaning to ask. That's what I was getting to! It’s a complete shambles, honestly. They only released the slots online last night, and by the time I logged in – because of course, I was dealing with this email avalanche – everything sensible was gone. Like, 8:30 am on a Tuesday? Who has a Tuesday morning free? Oh no! Seriously? That's so typical. Did you try refreshing? Sometimes it throws up cancellations. Refreshing until my eyes bled! Honestly, it was like the Hunger Games. I managed to snag a slot for Friday afternoon at 3, but it’s absolutely rammed. They said you barely get a proper look around with so many people. I wanted to really  feel  the place, you know? See how the staff interact, see what the garden is like… this sounds stressful. Ugh. It’s the most important decision, isn't it? Finding the right place for little Leo. Maybe we could go together on Friday, even if it's chaotic. Two sets of eyes are better than one. I can take half a day, I think. It wouldn't be the end of the world to miss planning. Oh, that would be lovely, actually. Thank you, darling. It's just… all this responsibility. And your dad's been on about fixing the guttering all week. It’s dripping right outside the kitchen window, driving me mad. It's  always  something. Dad and his guttering! It's a constant battle. He’ll get round to it eventually. He just likes to make a fuss. And honestly, the weather’s been so unpredictable. One minute sunshine, the next it’s pouring. Exactly! He's threatened to get on a ladder three times already, and each time I’ve had to veto it. I don’t trust him up there anymore! Honestly, I spend half my week being a health and safety officer. Well, you  are  very good at bossing people around, Mum. It's a gift. Speaking of things needing attention… I was watching ‘Great British Bake Off’ last night, and they were making choux pastry.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of beige at that corporate away-day was criminal. Beige carpets, beige walls, beige… everything! You’d think a company rebranding as ‘dynamic and innovative’ would understand the power of colour. Beige, eh? Sounds… relaxing, I s’pose. My day’s usually just whatever colour the dust is, if I’m honest. Building site ain’t exactly known for its interior design flair. Just tryin’ to get the job done, y’know? Right, Leo. Completely different worlds, aren’t they? Anya, that sounds dreadful. I spend enough time looking at spreadsheets to have my colour vision fading as it is. I don’t need a beige immersion experience. Is that why you looked so frazzled on the phone earlier? Frazzled is an understatement, Liv. It wasn’t just the beige. Old Mr. Henderson decided  he  wanted to micromanage the buffet layout. Apparently, the mini quiches weren’t ‘strategically positioned’ enough. Strategically positioned quiches! I nearly lost it. I mean, I’ve got a degree, I’m coordinating logistics for hundreds of people, not curating a miniature pastry landscape! A degree in… what was it again, Anya? Events, right? Sounds stressful, loads of stuff to remember. Event Management. And it  is  stressful. But usually in a fun way. This was just… exhausting. How’s the building site going, Leo? Anything exciting fall off a truck lately? Nah, nothin’ like that. Just the usual graft. Long days, bad weather… Met a lass though. Sarah. She works in the café across the road. Proper nice. Oh, brilliant! That’s lovely, Leo. Is she… local? Yeah, Cambridge born and bred. Been seein’ her a couple of weeks now. Took her to the cinema last Friday. Bit awkward, really. Forgot to take my high-vis jacket off when we went in. Oh, Leo! You didn’t?! I did! I only realised halfway through the film when a kid kept pointing and askin' his mum if I was a security guard. Mortifying. She thought it was funny though, thankfully. That’s a good sign. She’s got a sense of humour. You need that. Building sites and blokes in high-vis jackets… it's a recipe for amusement. Speaking of which, Anya, you’ve got to tell me about that dress you were wearing at the charity gala photos you posted. Stunning! Is it new? Oh, that. Yeah, it’s new. Found it in a little boutique in Doncaster when I was home last weekend.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the state of the biscuits. Soft as butter, they were. Absolutely no snap at all. A biscuit needs snap, doesn’t it? It’s fundamental! Oh, Reginald, you and your biscuits! Always a drama. I told you, I’ve been a bit distracted. Little Timmy was trying to build a fort out of the sofa cushions this morning. A right palaver it was. Sounds like a typical Tuesday with Timmy. Though, I’d argue a slightly soft biscuit is preferable to a rock-hard one that breaks your teeth. A balance, you see. A balance is key. Just like a good lesson plan. Honestly, you two! Bicker, bicker, bicker. It's always something. Reginald, you know Doreen always prioritises the children. And Arthur, you’re always drawing parallels to teaching! Though, you  are  right about balance. This tea is lovely, Doreen. Exactly how I like it - milk before water, naturally. Milk before water, aye. A proper cuppa. Though it ain’t the tea that’s the problem, Mary, it’s the accompaniments! Speaking of which, did anyone bring any of those nice ginger nuts? I’ve been craving a ginger nut. I did, actually. In the tin, Reginald. But be warned, Timmy had a little…investigation… earlier. He wasn’t  eating  them, thankfully, just trying to see if they’d fit into his fort. An architectural assessment, you mean? Typical boy. They see everything as a building opportunity. Reminds me of young David back in ‘87…built a scale model of the Houses of Parliament out of sugar cubes. The mess…! Oh, Arthur, you always have a story! It's good for us, keeps the mind ticking. Though I do sympathise with your cleaning bill. It sounds dreadful. Doreen, another slice of that Victoria sponge? It's truly divine. Of course, Mary. Help yourself. I made it extra light this time, thinking of your digestion. It’s a silly age, isn’t it? Constantly thinking about what you  can't  eat. Don't I know it! My knees complain if I so much as  look  at a hill. This weather doesn’t help, damp as a sponge it is. Reminds me of Costessey when I was a lad. Always damp. Dampness is the story of England, isn’t it? Shaped our history, influenced our literature…and our biscuit storage. Though, speaking of history, I was reading an article about the decline of the afternoon tea ritual amongst younger generations.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of beige in that hotel room was depressing. Beige walls, beige carpet, beige furniture. It felt like being inside a digestive biscuit. Oh, you’re awful, Eleanor! But I know exactly what you mean. Some hotels just suck the life out of you. Remember that one in Birmingham, the one with the… aggressively floral wallpaper? Birmingham? Oof. I had a work conference there once. The hotel was fine, but the traffic… absolute nightmare. Took me three hours to get to the NEC. Three hours? Crikey. You’re lucky. Last time I was navigating Birmingham, I ended up going around a roundabout five times. Felt like a particularly cruel form of modern art. Speaking of art, did you see that Banksy thing that popped up in London? Apparently, it was on a wall in Hackney for about five minutes before someone tried to sell it. I did! It was brilliant. The audacity of it all! Though, honestly, I’m starting to think half these ‘Banksy sightings’ are just someone with a stencil and a can of spray paint. Probably. It’s the principle, innit? Making a statement. Though I was reading about that protest in Cardiff last weekend. Bit… heated. Some arrests, apparently. They’re getting more frequent, aren’t they? People are rightly angry about a lot of things, but it’s a slippery slope. Where does legitimate protest end and causing actual harm begin? It’s a complex question. One I try to unpack with my students, actually. We were discussing the ethics of civil disobedience earlier today. Went on a rather lively tangent about suffragettes and… well, circumcision, surprisingly enough. Circumcision? Eleanor! At a university lecture? It came up! It was a discussion about bodily autonomy and cultural practices. One student brought it up, and honestly, it opened up a really important conversation. A bit awkward at first, though. I can imagine. Those things tend to happen. You never know where a seminar will lead. I had one go completely off the rails because someone mentioned pigeons. Pigeons! Pigeons? Now  that’s  a conversation starter. My nan used to be convinced pigeons were government spies. She’d chase them with her umbrella. Oh, bless her. She was a character, your Nan. Remember when she tried to teach Dad to drive? He nearly went through Mrs. Higgins’ rose bushes. Oh,  God  yes. And the shouting!

…and honestly, the paella was just  sad . Like, barely any seafood, mostly just rice and regret. You would have been appalled, knowing how much you love a good Spanish dish. Oh, no! That  is  a tragedy. You went all that way and got a mediocre paella? That’s grounds for complaint, honestly. Here, this will help. Earl Grey, just how you like it. How was the rest of Spain, though? Beyond the paella disappointment? Much better! Barcelona was amazing. Really vibrant, loads of street art, and the Sagrada Familia… wow. Photos don’t do it justice. But it was good to be back too, I won’t lie. This flat feels…safe, you know? And peaceful. Did you have a good week looking after Nana? It was…Nana. A mix of lovely moments and needing to gently redirect her from trying to ‘reorganize’ the hospital ward. She kept trying to give the patients her digestive biscuits! Honestly, the things she comes up with. But yeah, she was mostly okay. It’s good to have a routine, I think, for both of us. She really perks up when I visit. She always does. You’re a saint, honestly. Dealing with Nana and a demanding ward…how  is  work? Still utterly chaotic? Utterly. We’re incredibly short-staffed. They keep talking about hiring, but it’s all talk. I had a particularly difficult case last week – a young lad, really struggling, and the resources just weren't there to give him what he needed. It’s frustrating. Hence the Nana biscuit distraction, probably. That sounds awful. You absorb so much of that, don’t you? No wonder you needed a break. Speaking of breaks, Liam texted. He asked if I wanted to meet up for a drink on Friday.  Liam ? As in… the  Liam? The one who couldn’t commit to ordering a pizza, let alone a relationship? Don't remind me. Yes,  that  Liam. Apparently, he’s “back in town” and “doing really well.” It’s probably a performance, honestly. He probably just wants to show off his slightly nicer car. Definitely a performance. Honestly, you deserve better than a man who equates success with vehicle acquisition. Say no. Absolutely say no. Have you heard from Chloe about Saturday? She mentioned wanting to go to that new Thai place. Oh, yes! I completely forgot. That sounds brilliant. I’m in. We should rope Mark in too, he’s been looking a bit glum lately.

…and honestly, the way she talked about the new immunotherapy, it sounded… hopeful. Properly hopeful, not the ‘brave face’ hopeful she usually puts on. Though honestly, five years ago I wouldn’t have even  understood  half of what she was explaining about her treatment. It’s terrifying how quickly you pick up a specialist vocabulary when someone you love is ill. It is. It feels…invasive, doesn’t it? Like the illness is leeching into  you , forcing you to learn all this horrible stuff. I still get completely lost when Mum tries to explain her medication. Is Sarah still managing to get to her painting classes? That always seemed to be her lifeline. She is, thankfully. Just once a week now, and she gets a lift, but she says it’s the only time she doesn’t  feel  like a patient. Which is good. It's just… watching her. She looks so tired. And she's trying so hard to shield us from it, you know? She always was fiercely independent. Remember when she broke her wrist skiing and insisted on making us all breakfast the next morning with one arm in a cast? Oh god, yes! The absolute state of the kitchen. Right, well. Distraction tactic engaged. Let’s talk about something marginally less depressing. Have you had a proper look at those houses in Little Puddleton yet? The ones we were talking about? I’ve scrolled through Rightmove, yes. Nothing’s really leapt out. Too much garden, not enough space, wonky ceilings… you know the drill. It’s the Little Puddleton premium, I think. Everyone wants the ‘village life’ and they’re charging accordingly. Exactly! But we  need  to look properly this weekend, don’t we? We've been saying we want a bigger kitchen for… how long? Three years? And a garden that doesn’t resemble a postage stamp. Plus, a spare room would be amazing, thinking ahead for visiting family. True. And the schools are good. That’s a big factor, even if we’re not actively planning… you know. But just in case. I liked the look of that one on Mill Road, the detached one. Bit of a fixer-upper, apparently. Oh, the one with the overgrown wisteria? I saw that one. It looked… structurally questionable. And probably full of spiders. Spiders are a given. But it has potential. And a huge garden. We could finally get a dog!

… honestly, it’s the noise, isn’t it? Always the noise. Last night it was some lad blasting out grime 'til three in the morning. Three! I had to go up there, didn't I? And he just gives me this blank look, like  I’m  the one being unreasonable. Tell me about it. I had a complaint this morning about someone microwaving fish.  Fish , Liam! At 8 am! The whole corridor smelled. Ms. Davies nearly lost her breakfast. She's a delicate soul. Fish. Right. That's… dedicated. Worse than the vape clouds though, isn't it? They set the fire alarm off  again  last week. Honestly, you'd think they’d learn. It’s not a vape lounge, it's student accommodation. Oh, the vape clouds are a perpetual issue. And they always deny it. “Must have been the steam from my shower, yeah?” Like we’re all idiots. I spend half my day mediating between people who can’t just… coexist. It’s exhausting. What really gets on my nerves though, is the passive aggression with the communal kitchen. Oh, the kitchen. Don't even get me started. Dirty dishes piling up, someone always leaving their food out… It’s like living with a pack of feral students. Exactly! And the notes. The  notes  they leave. “Please wash up your dishes” written in capital letters and stuck to the fridge with aggressive sticky tape. It’s amazing how much vitriol can be squeezed into a single passive-aggressive kitchen notice. Haha, true. I found one once that just said “Seriously?” underlined five times. Didn’t even state what they were being serious about! Just pure, distilled annoyance. I think it was about someone using all the milk. Oh, milk thief is a classic. We had a whole investigation last semester. Turns out it was old Mr. Henderson from 304, using it for his tea. He insists he pays rent and therefore is entitled to the communal milk. Henderson? Blimey. He’s… a character. But yeah, I can see his logic, sort of. Still, could’ve just bought his own. What I can’t stand, though, is the laziness. I walked past a room last week, door wide open, and there were empty pizza boxes stacked to the ceiling. Like a cardboard monument to bad decisions. Ugh, that’s horrific. It impacts my job too, you know? When the fire risk assessments come around, I'm the one explaining the potential hazards.

…and honestly, the sheer  number  of Brits in Bruges was astonishing! Like, you couldn’t swing a cat without hitting someone from Kent. It was almost comforting, but also a bit… depressing, you know? Like we hadn't actually  escaped  England. Bruges, eh? Full of lace and chocolate and… us. That’s the way it is with those package tours, isn’t it? They herd us all together like sheep. My Doris and I tried a Christmas market one year, Colmar in France. Same thing. More accents from Surrey than actual French! Oh, Christmas markets! I'm taking little Maisie to the one in Canterbury this year, if her dad doesn’t mess things up again. It’s a bit pricey, but she's been going on about the gingerbread houses for weeks. She’s seven now, can you believe it? Seems like yesterday she was a babbling mess. Seven! That's lovely, Mum. Time flies. I’m still trying to figure out what I'm doing with myself, let alone thinking about little ones. Uni was exhausting enough. Honestly, half my cohort were just trying to survive on instant noodles and regret. University… that’s all a bit of a blur to me now. Still, you’ve done well, love. A proper degree. Me? Left school, got a job, that was that. Now I mostly potter about. Though, retirement isn’t all it's cracked up to be, you know? Days stretch out… long. Don't I know it, Dad. Still, at least you don’t have to deal with the traffic anymore. Honestly, Brighton seafront on a Saturday is just  mad . Trying to get a parking space is a nightmare. And then all the tourists… Tell me about it! I had a student placement doing research for the council on pedestrian flow, and seafront traffic was the bane of my existence. They were talking about pedestrianizing more sections, but the shop owners were having none of it. Shops. Used to love a good wander round Herne Bay, back in the day. Used to be a proper little seaside town, Herne Bay. Now it's all charity shops and… well, not much else. Good for a bit of a poke around though, if you're looking for a bargain. Speaking of bargains, Christmas shopping is looming. I’ve barely started. I saw a gorgeous little puppy at the pet shop last week.

…and honestly, Miss Davies just kept going on about the potential ramifications. Like, it's  history  happening, isn't it? Shouldn't we be learning about  why  it's happening, not just worrying about what it  might  do to…well, to everything? Right, well, Miss Davies is a product of her generation, love. She probably remembers a very different Ireland. It’s good they’re having the debate in school, though. It’s important you lot understand the details. This equality vote… it’s really quite something. Dad says it’s about making sure everyone is treated the same, like in the law. But Liam O’Connell said his grandad thinks it’ll “ruin the country.” Ruin it! How can wanting everyone to be equal ruin a country? Oh, Liam’s grandad. He's a bit… traditional. Bless him. It's about recognising families, Matthew. Families that aren’t just a mum and a dad. It means things like same-sex couples having the same rights when it comes to marriage, and carers being recognised for the work they do. It's more complicated than just ‘everyone being equal’, though it  is  fundamentally about that. Marriage? Oh, like, actually getting married? Like, with the cake and everything? Yes, exactly. Though I suspect most couples these days are more concerned about the legal stuff, like tax benefits and inheritance. Still, a cake's nice. Speaking of which, your birthday is coming up, isn't it? Any ideas for a party? I was thinking maybe laser quest. But Mum's already saying it’s too expensive. She wants me to have a 'quiet gathering' with just a few mates. A ‘quiet gathering’ is code for ‘a really boring evening’, obviously. Your mother… she's a force of nature, isn’t she? Last week she tried to tell  my  mother how to make scones. My mother! Who's been making scones for sixty years! No way! What did she say? Oh, something about needing to add a pinch of bicarbonate of soda. My mother nearly choked. Said she’d been making them perfectly fine without bicarbonate of soda since before your mother was born! It was glorious. That’s brilliant! She’s so embarrassing sometimes. But… she’s got strong opinions, I’ll give her that. Like with this vote, she’s totally for it. Says it’s about time Ireland caught up with the rest of the world.

…and I’m tellin’ ya, Doris, that sweep wasn’t right for the job. Too much rake angle, see? Just dug in and chattered all over the place. Old Man Hemmings, he’d have known. He could sharpen a tool blindfolded. Proper craftsman, he was. Oh, Arthur, not the lathe tools  again . Lovely sausage roll, by the way, Margaret. A bit spicy, though, isn't it? It’s a Cumberland, Doris. They  are  meant to be a little kicky. And Arthur, you’ve been going on about Old Man Hemmings’ tools since breakfast. Honestly, you’d think you were still running a workshop, not just… reminiscing. Reminiscing? I  was  a dab hand, you know. Could turn out a beautiful spindle, I could. This new fangled stuff, it's all computer controlled, no feel for the wood. Where's the artistry in that, eh? It’s a dying art, that’s what it is. Dying art or not, Arthur, you haven't touched a lathe in twenty years. Perhaps you’re remembering it through rose-tinted spectacles. Though, I must say, you always did make a rather nice little bird table. That bird table was a masterpiece! Mahogany, it was. Honestly, though, getting good tools these days… it’s a nightmare. All plastic handles and flimsy steel. Not like the high-carbon stuff we used to get. Speaking of things being a nightmare, did you two see what little Timmy tried to do yesterday? Oh, don’t tell me… He didn’t! Not again? He did. Apparently, he thought Hammy – you know, the hamster – was cold. Cold? What’s that got to do with… Oh, don’t tell me he… He put Hammy in the microwave. Arthur! Don't choke on your sandwich! Timmy! In the  microwave ? Honestly, that boy… Well, I'll be… The cheek of it! A perfectly good hamster… though why anyone would want a hamster is beyond me. Always squeaking and stinkin’. Thankfully, I caught him just before he pressed start. Apparently, he thought “warming Hammy up” was a good idea. I had to explain, very carefully, why that was a  very  bad idea. He was convinced Hammy was shivering. Shivering? In August? That boy's imagination runs wild. He gets it from your side of the family, I suspect, Margaret. Your father used to try and build a boat in the garden out of washing up liquid bottles.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! Charging five pence for a plastic bag. Five pence! Like it’s going to solve anything. It just feels… punitive. It’s behavioural economics, isn’t it? Nudge theory. Make people think twice before grabbing one. It’s worked, apparently, reduced usage significantly. Though I do forget my reusable ones half the time. Oh, you young ones and your ‘behavioural economics’. Back in my day, we just  didn’t  ask for a bag if we didn’t need one. Common sense really. Though, I suppose things are different now. Everything’s about a system. It’s just another layer of hassle, that’s all. Reminds me of dealing with the bank, actually. Tried to sort out a direct debit today and it was like navigating a maze. Automated this, online that… I just want to speak to a  person . Tell me about it. I spent an hour on hold with them last week, trying to understand why our mortgage rate jumped up. Turns out it’s some tracker thing linked to… well, honestly, I lost track. It felt designed to confuse you. With house prices the way they are, it’s a terrifying thought owing so much money. House prices! Don't get me started. When Alistair and I bought this place, it was a fraction of what similar properties go for now. Utterly ridiculous. Of course, Alistair always said I was a shrewd negotiator. He wouldn’t believe the prices now. Speaking of Alistair, did you see that article about the man who wrote everything backwards? Like, mirror writing. Oh, yes! The one in the paper? Apparently, it was a neurological thing, often linked to being left-handed. Fascinating, isn’t it? Makes you wonder what's going on inside the brain. I'm transcribing an interview with a linguist tomorrow - she's researching how language shapes thought. It's going to be a dense one, I suspect. That  is  fascinating. It’s all interconnected, isn't it? Thinking, writing,… even the way we manage our finances! It’s all mental processing. Speaking of mental processes, have you tackled the cryptic crossword today? I'm stuck on 17 across. "Treacherous journey, briefly ." Ah, a classic. "Perilous". It's a double definition. Perilous meaning dangerous, and referring to 'Peril' being a short journey. Of course! Perilous! I completely missed that. Thank you, headmistress. You still have it.

… honestly, Leo, another hour on that Lego Ninjago game and your eyes will be square. Honestly! It’s a beautiful Saturday afternoon. But Mum! Zane’s frozen prison is  really  hard to build! Kai keeps getting stuck! I know, darling, it sounds very dramatic. But remember what we talked about? A bit of balance? You haven’t even  looked  at your new book. The one about the Roman soldiers? I’m building a mega-base in Minecraft. It’s going to have lava moats and everything! And redstone traps! And  you , my little engineer, are constructing a fortress of solitude? Is that right? It’s not solitude, it’s defence! Creepers are always trying to get in. They explode, Mum! Explosions! Ninjago has villains too! The Overlord! He’s super scary. I’m sure they are frightfully scary. But even ninjas and Minecraft heroes need to recharge their brains with a good book sometimes. Reading lets your imagination build things  even bigger  than you can on a screen. But… the game  is  building. I  am  using my imagination. I’m designing the whole temple! That's true, you are, and I’m not saying it's a bad thing. It’s really clever. But it's a different kind of imagination, isn't it? Like… the game gives you the pieces, and you put them together. A book gives you nothing, and  you  have to create everything in your head. The temple, the characters, the sounds… everything. But in Minecraft, I  can  make anything. I can even make a working clock! Well, almost working. You can, and that  is  amazing. I’m genuinely impressed with your redstone work. But think about it. When you read, you create the clock. You design it. You decide what it looks like, how it sounds, even who made it and why. No limits! So… like I build Zane, but in my head? Exactly! It’s like building Zane, but he’s even more  you . You get to decide his personality, his backstory… everything. Plus, you learn loads of things without even realising it. About history, about different cultures, about… well, everything! Does the Roman soldier book have explosions? Not exactly explosions, darling. But it has battles! And courage! And sieges! They built amazing things, too, you know. Roads and walls and… well, you'll find out if you read it! Mum, can Zane have a Roman soldier friend in my head?

…and honestly, the traffic getting back from Cornwall was  brutal . Four hours to get from Newquay to Bristol. Four! I thought we’d be stuck there forever. Did either of you manage to get any sleep in the car? A bit. Mostly just tossing and turning and trying not to squash myself against the window. You drive like a rally driver, Mum, even on motorways. It's impressive, but not conducive to rest. I was surprisingly out for most of it. Headphones in, playlist on…totally conked. Though I did wake up once and saw Dad attempting to navigate using a map. A paper map! In 2024! It was a sight. He insists he knows how to read a map! Says SatNavs are “the downfall of civilisation.” Honestly, the man. But the weather was lovely, wasn’t it? Absolutely glorious. Worth the drive, even with the gridlock. Definitely. Porthcurno beach was stunning. And that little pasty shop in St. Ives… I’m still dreaming about those pasties. I think I gained about half a stone just on pasties and cream teas. Well, we  were  on holiday. No harm in indulging. Though you’ll be back on your salads tomorrow, I suppose, being the healthy one. What about you, Chloe? What was your highlight? For me, it was probably Land's End. It felt…epic, you know? Standing right at the edge of the country. A bit touristy, admittedly, but still. Plus, the ice cream was pretty good. It is a bit of a cliché, isn’t it? But a good cliché. Right, enough reminiscing about sunshine and sea air. What are we doing today? I thought we could potter around Lichfield, maybe look at that new art gallery? The art gallery sounds nice. Though I’ve got a bit of a nightmare situation at work. Old Mr. Henderson called in sick, and I’m the only keyholder who can get into the stockroom. I might need to pop back to Burton at some point today. Oh, dear. That’s a pain. When do you need to go? Hopefully not until after lunch. I’ve arranged for Sarah to cover for the first few hours. But if it drags on, I’ll have to leave early. It’s just…Henderson always picks the busiest days to be ill. Classic Henderson. He's a professional sick-day taker, isn't he? No offence.

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  stared  at me. Like I’d insulted his mother or something. All I said was the homework was a bit…ambitious. Ambitious? Mate, it was a full essay on the socio-economic impact of the Corn Laws! We’re doing GCSE History, not a university module. He's lost it, I swear. Did you see him yelling at Chloe about her referencing TikTok in her presentation? Oh, God, Chloe was mortified! It was classic Davies though, wasn’t it? He thinks anything pre-2010 is the height of civilisation. Speaking of civilisation… this sandwich is surprisingly good. Proper crusty bread. It is, yeah. Mum packed it. She’s weirdly proud of her sandwich-making skills. Says it’s a life skill. Honestly, a life skill for what? Winning sandwich competitions? Better than my packed lunch, that's for sure. Another cheese and pickle. I swear my mum thinks I’m five. I tried to suggest a baguette with salami and rocket and she looked at me like I’d asked for a live badger. A badger! You’re pushing it, Arjun. Anyway, are we still on for Cards Against Humanity tonight at Leo’s? It's been ages since we properly played. Yeah, definitely. My little brother’s been obsessed with this new war documentary he found on iPlayer. He keeps trying to make me build miniature trenches in the garden. It’s… unsettling. All he talks about is strategy and logistics. Seriously? What documentary? It sounds…intense for a kid. My cousin’s lad is obsessed with that show,  SAS: Who Dares Wins . Keeps trying to do press-ups on everything. It’s a phase. Though, it’s a weird phase. It’s probably all that stuff happening in… well, everywhere. You see it on the news, even avoiding it is hard. Makes you think. My auntie was saying her friend's son signed up. Said he wanted to “make a difference”. That's…heavy. It’s just…sometimes I think people romanticise it. Like it’s some grand adventure. My grandad fought in the Falklands, and he  never  talked about it. Just always said it was awful. That’s true. My nan’s brother was in WWII. She said he came back a completely different person. It’s not some game. Speaking of games, anyone seen that new Marvel movie?  Eternals ? I did! It was…long.

…and then Mr. Davies  actually  said, "Newton would be turning in his grave!" Honestly, it was over a slightly wonky graph. A  slightly  wonky graph! Like, it wasn't even drastically off. No way! Davies is proper intense about physics, isn’t he? More intense than Mrs. Peterson, even. And she practically  lives  in the lab. You have  no  idea. He was going on about the precision required for scientific observation. Precision! We're fourteen, not research scientists! It’s just homework. Exactly! It’s not like we’re building the Large Hadron Collider in the shed. Speaking of homework… did you understand any of that stuff about potential energy? I honestly zoned out halfway through. It all just blended into Greek to me. A little bit. I think. It’s just… so many equations. And he doesn't explain  why  they work, just  that  they do. It's just memorize, memorize, memorize. It’s rubbish, really. Tell me about it. It's completely different to Miss Davies’ English lessons. Remember how she made us dissect poems like… like we were surgeons? It was weird, but at least it made sense. You actually understood  why  Shakespeare wrote what he did. Oh god, yes. She’s brilliant. Though, honestly, after a whole lesson on iambic pentameter, my brain feels like mush. Did you hear she’s setting us that extra reading assignment?  Great Expectations ? Seriously? Ugh,  Great Expectations ? That’s…thick. I started it over the summer and gave up. Too many descriptions of marshes. I’d rather be watching ‘17 Again’. Ooh, ‘17 Again’! Have you seen it? Matthew Perry is hilarious. I keep thinking what it would be like to be seventeen again, knowing what I know now. You could just… fix all your mistakes. Exactly! Although, knowing me, I’d probably just spend the whole time trying to avoid embarrassing moments. Like that time I tripped over my own feet in front of Leo in Year 8. Still cringe thinking about it. Oh, don’t even  start  on Leo. He's… Leo. Completely oblivious. Remember how he asked Chloe what ‘photosynthesis’ meant  during  the biology test? Oh my god! I’d completely forgotten about that! She looked like she was going to explode. And then Mr. Harrison had to explain it, which meant  everyone  lost valuable test time! He’s such a sweetie, Mr. Harrison, but seriously. He’s the best form tutor, though.

… honestly, the library's been a  nightmare . Everyone’s cramming for finals, it’s like Piccadilly Circus in there. Seriously considering just writing my dissertation from my bed, even if it means being surrounded by dirty laundry. Sounds about right. Uni life, eh? At least you’re nearly there. Though, speaking of escaping… Transylvania is still on for August, yeah? I've started looking at flights again. They’re getting a bit pricey. Ooh, Transylvania! I’m so excited. I’ve already started mentally packing – mostly black clothes, obviously. Gotta fit in with the whole Dracula vibe. Are we definitely hitting Bran Castle? I’ve seen photos, it looks incredible. Strewth, Transylvania! That's a fair hike from Brum, isn't it, Loz? Sounds…intense. Though, good on ya for going. I'm just hoping to actually  have  a summer this year. Last year was all work, work, work at the café. Yeah, Bran Castle’s a must. I'm also hoping to find some proper hiking trails. Not just tourist traps. Want to really get lost in the Carpathian Mountains, you know? And yes, Loz, it  is  a fair hike. Hence the flights. I’ve been meaning to ask, how’s the café going, Rach? Still battling the hordes of caffeine addicts? Constantly! Honestly, sometimes I feel like all I do is pour lattes and listen to people complain about their Mondays, even on a Sunday. It’s alright though, pays the bills. Speaking of bills… have you heard anything from Leo? He was talking about getting that laser eye surgery. Oh, Leo! No, not since he mentioned it last week. Said he was terrified but finally booked it in. He’s such a drama queen. Always exaggerating everything. He probably convinced himself he was going blind. Sounds like Leo, alright. We all have one of those mates. What about Sarah? Haven’t seen her in ages. Last I heard she was applying for that gallery internship in New York. She got it! I saw her post on Insta. Officially a fancy art world person. She's flying out next month. Proper jealous, I tell ya. New York… I need to get my act together. Transylvania is good, but it's not  New York . Sarah always was ambitious. Bet she’ll be amazing. Right, back to Transylvania. I'm thinking we should book accommodation soon. Airbnb or hostels? I'm leaning towards Airbnb for a bit more space and a kitchen, so we can at least attempt to cook a proper meal instead of living on pastries.

…and honestly, the playlist is the biggest stress. Leo keeps requesting death metal, which, lovely for him, but not exactly party vibes for Grandma and Grandpa, is it? But death metal  is  good, Mummy. It’s got… energy! It does, darling, it definitely has energy. But maybe we save the energy for dancing to something everyone can enjoy? How about some 80s classics? Everyone likes a bit of Madonna. Can we play the ‘Alice in Wonderland’ soundtrack? The Queen of Hearts song is funny! Ooh, good shout, Arthur! We can definitely add that in. Right, playlist… almost sorted. More pressing, though – photos. Auntie Carol is bringing her “professional” camera. Does that mean lots of poses? I hate poses. Well, a few, maybe. But mostly, she wants nice family pictures. You and Arthur looking adorable, me and your Dad not looking too tired… the usual. And she’s suggested a photoshoot beforehand, themed around… wait for it… ‘Alice in Wonderland’! Cool! Can I be the Mad Hatter? You absolutely can be the Mad Hatter! We already talked about that. Lily, you can be the White Rabbit, though you might have to practice hopping. Hopping is silly. It  is  a bit silly, but that's the point! Look, the important thing is we all cooperate for five minutes for Auntie Carol. She gets very upset if we don’t. Remember last Christmas? And the ‘forced smiles’? Oh yeah. Dad’s face was really funny last Christmas. He looked like a grumpy gnome. He did, didn't he? Okay, no repeating that this year. Speaking of funny faces, did you two eat all the biscuits I left for the party? Maybe… a couple. I just had one! Lily had, like, five! Five?! Lily! Honestly! We need those for guests. And  no  swearing, Arthur. Remember what we talked about? “Darn” and “Blimey” are acceptable substitutes. But "like" is a proper word! It’s a filler word! You use it too much. Anyway, biscuits aside, we need to finalise the food. I was thinking sausage rolls, mini quiches… your Dad’s doing the barbeque. Can we have those little chicken things with the pineapple? Chicken satay? Yes, of course. Those are always popular. Right. And after the party, I promised Sarah I’d show her my aerial hoop. The shiny circle thing? Is it hard? It is tricky, yes. It takes a lot of practice. But it’s really good fun.

…and honestly, the state of that rhubarb crumble Mrs. Higgins brought round last week! All soggy bottom and not enough ginger. Honestly, you'd think after all these years she'd have mastered a simple crumble. Still, polite I was, said it were lovely. Didn’t want to hurt her feelings, did I? Oh, Arthur, you always were a soft touch. Though I do agree, her crumble  is  usually a bit of a disaster. More like a rhubarb soup, really. Anyone want another slice of this roulade? It's divine, honestly. Much better than Mrs. Higgins’ efforts. I’m good, thanks. This pizza’s hitting the spot. So, Lily, Maisie, how are we feeling now the dust has settled on the exams? Any initial thoughts? Don't tell me you've already checked results a dozen times online. Mr. Davies! Don’t even  ask . I’ve refreshed the page like, a million times. Still nothing. It's just... waiting is the worst. Me too! I keep looking at my phone, hoping something will pop up. Mum keeps saying to relax, but how can you relax when your whole future hangs in the balance? It’s so dramatic. Dramatic is right, darling. It feels like a lifetime ago when  I  was sitting exams. Though we didn't have the internet back then, so no refreshing pages every five seconds! It was just… waiting for that envelope. Agonising. Aye, waiting. That’s the killer, eh? Reminds me of waiting for my call-up papers. Now  that  were a worrying time. Though, truthfully, I wasn’t keen on the idea of marching about in the mud. Different pressures, Arthur. Though equally real at the time, I’m sure. Speaking of pressures, Lily, you were saying you’ve started thinking about driving lessons? Yeah! Chloe started hers last week and she says it’s really good. Gives you so much freedom, you know? I’m hoping to save up over the summer and start in September. It’s just… expensive. It is. But worth it in the end. Imagine, driving yourselves to school! No more relying on buses. Though, Arthur, don’t even  think  about letting them drive your vintage Morris Minor! Don’t be ridiculous, Brenda! I wouldn’t trust anyone with Bessie! She's a lady, that one, needs a gentle hand. Speaking of gentle hands, I was reading about these pressure points...apparently, you can relieve a headache by pressing  here … .

…and honestly, the raspberries are looking remarkably good this year. Despite all this rain. You wouldn’t think it, would you, considering how much we grumbled about the lack of sun in May? Remember that, David? You were threatening to move the whole patch indoors under grow lights. I might have been exaggerating a  little . It was looking bleak for a while there. But you were right to keep faith, Mum. They’re thriving. Though I think Dad’s been sneaking them. I saw a suspiciously red-stained beard this morning. Guiltily? Me? Never! Just… tasting for ripeness, naturally. A quality control check. You have to ensure the standards are maintained. Besides, the berries were calling my name. Speaking of which, anyone else fancy a bit more breakfast? I made a fresh pot of tea. Oh, lovely! Yes, please. I skipped the toast, feeling a bit peckish later. Though I did have a rather large grapefruit. Trying to be healthy, you know. Seeing as how much gardening I've been doing. It's hard work, but rewarding. David, how’s the new Korean drama going? You were glued to it last night. It’s fantastic! It’s a historical one, based on a real princess. The subtitles are a bit of a workout, but the cinematography is stunning. It’s making me want to brush up on my Korean, honestly. Though I’m already overstretched learning about the pronunciation nuances for my students. Honestly, some of them struggle with the ‘th’ sound. Sounds complicated. Reminds me of trying to understand my grandson explaining some computer game to me. It’s all jargon. He’s at university now, isn’t he? Still enjoying linguistics? He is! He’s completely obsessed. Says he wants to specialise in sociolinguistics. He was asking me about regional dialects the other day, specifically Scottish. He’s got this whole thing about the possibility of Scottish independence affecting language evolution… it's a bit much for a Sunday morning. Oh, that’s… a complex one. I always think of Winston Churchill and his speeches when it comes to the power of language. Such a master orator. Although, no doubt, terribly flawed as a man. He was a character, alright. Powerful.
