…and then, honestly, the lag was  terrible . Like, I was firing, and it registered three seconds later. No chance against a coordinated team, you know? Yeah, lag is the worst. Did you try restarting your router? That usually works for me. Aye, of course, I did. Everything. Multiple times. It’s their servers, I reckon. They’re overrun with people since the new season started. Sounds stressful, Liam. You were getting quite animated there for a minute. Daniel, darling, eat your peas. No pees! They’re green! He’s got a point, love. Peas  are  a bit suspect. Listen, did you have a good walk with him earlier, Sarah? He seems full of beans. We did. It was… eventful. He insisted on “rescuing” every single leaf that fell off the trees. Each one needed a proper burial with a little stone marker. It took  ages . Sounds like fun, actually. Reminds me of when I used to build LEGO fortresses in the garden. Serious business. He’s already a planner, that one. Always arranging things. Speaking of arranging, he was building a little house for Buster this morning. Honestly, it was quite impressive, for a two-year-old. All the soft toys were invited. Oh yes! He spent a good half hour meticulously placing them all. Buster, the bear, was definitely the guest of honour. He kept making Buster ‘talk’ in this tiny little high-pitched voice. What did Buster say? “Want honey! Wanna play!” Everyone laughs. Ah, that's priceless. He picks up everything, doesn’t he? Even the way I try to do Buster’s voice. He's a little mimic. He was pretending to be you on the phone earlier, going on about “important computer things”. Important computer things! That’s my entire professional life you’re mocking, young man! You should’ve heard him trying to explain coding. He was flailing his arms and saying “algorithms!” It was hilarious. Algorithms, eh? He's a bright spark, that boy. Though I'm starting to think all this time with soft toys is slowing down his reaction time. He won’t stand a chance against me in a game of FIFA when he's older. Don’t even  think  about corrupting him with FIFA, Liam. He needs imaginative play. It’s good for his development. I’m just saying, a little competitive spirit…it's healthy. Besides, I could teach him a thing or two.

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘is cotton socks, he goes and puts a whole tin of Quality Street  in  the gravy! Honestly, Doris, I thought you’d ‘eard everything. Christmas dinner was ruined, absolutely ruined. Oh, Arthur! You  always  tell that story. It seems to get more dramatic each year, though. A whole tin? Really? Every single one! Well, nearly. He left the toffee ones, mind you. Always ‘ad a sweet tooth, that boy. Though he’s a right businessman now, runs ‘is own plumbing firm. Imagine! Sounds like a lively Christmas. We usually have a slightly more subdued affair. The kids are getting older, less inclined to chuck sweets in the gravy, thankfully. Though last year, the debate over Brussels sprouts nearly escalated into a full-blown argument. Oh, Dad! You’re exaggerating. It was just a disagreement. I happen to  like  Brussels sprouts! Only because you smother them in honey, Lily. Honestly. Honey on sprouts? Now  that’s  a new one. Never ‘eard of such a thing! Back in my day, sprouts were just boiled to within an inch of their life and served with a hefty dollop of resentment. Arthur, you're terrible! Though, you're not wrong about the boiling. Mothers back then thought everything needed to be…well, grey. It wouldn't be Christmas without it! Speaking of which, are we all agreed on the timings for the journey tomorrow? I rather fancied leaving around 9, to avoid the worst of the traffic. 9 is good. That gives me time to finish marking a few essays. And it avoids the school run chaos. Are the girls packed? Nearly. I still need to find my sparkly headband. It’s essential Christmas dinner attire. It absolutely is. And I'm still deciding which jumper. The reindeer one or the snowman? Difficult decisions. Headbands and reindeer jumpers! Times ‘ave changed, I tell you. We just ‘ad a clean shirt and a pair of shoes we didn’t usually wear. Luxury, that was. You always make us feel so ancient. Remember when you used to go horse riding, Arthur? You were quite the equestrian, weren't you? Oh, aye. Old Bess, she was a good mare. Steady as a rock. Used to take me down to the marshes. Haven’t been near a ‘orse in… well, decades now. Knees aren't what they used to be, you see. Lily’s been getting really into her art lately.

…and honestly, the state of the night shift is just getting worse. Old Mrs. Higgins demanded  specifically  warm milk with two sugars, then complained it wasn’t warm  enough ! Two sugars, honestly. It's like dealing with toddlers sometimes. Sounds about right, love. You always get the demanding ones on nights. I had a similar issue with the procurement budget this week. Dave from accounts thinks we can run the entire department on enthusiasm and biscuits. Biscuits, Margaret! Biscuits? That’s…ambitious, even for Dave. You know, my boss tried to suggest we brainstorm using only emojis the other day. Said it would be “more engaging.” I nearly lost it. Oh, the youth of today! Emojis! It's all a bit much, isn’t it? Still, at least you’ve got a boss who  tries  to be innovative. Mine just blames everything on staffing levels. Speaking of trying, I’m attempting a paella for your birthday, pet. It's not my usual repertoire, but I saw it on that cooking show you like. Hopefully, it won’t be a disaster. Oh, you shouldn’t have! Honestly, I don’t need a fuss. A nice quiet evening is plenty. But paella…that's ambitious, even for you, John. You usually stick to roast chicken. Paella sounds amazing! I'm officially volunteering as taster. Though, knowing Dad, it'll either be perfect or slightly charred. There's no in-between. Slightly charred is a generous description, Chloe. Remember that attempted soufflé? It resembled a deflated football. Oh, don't remind me! The dog wouldn’t even touch it. But you’re a good cook, honestly. And I appreciate the effort. You know, it’s nice to just…be here, chatting. Work’s been so stressful. Totally. I've been drowning in copy for this new organic dog food brand. “Introducing Bark Bites - the ethically sourced, paw-sitively delicious treat your discerning canine deserves!” Honestly, I’m starting to bark. Oh, you are awful. But good! That's a terrible line, but good awful. Right, so, birthday presents. I’ve got something, but Chloe's been suspiciously quiet. What have you been up to, young lady? Don't tell me you left it to the last minute again? Me? Never! I’ve been…researching. Very thorough research. It’s a…unique gift. Let’s just say it involves a voucher and a very large map.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the price of a loaf of bread these days. Went down to Costessey Co-op yesterday, and it's nearly three quid! Three quid for a white slice! Back in my day… well, you remember. Everything was affordable. Oh, don't start, Arthur. Everything was affordable when  you  had your mum doing all the shopping and a pension that actually meant something! It’s the same everywhere, dear. I popped into Harrow town centre last week, same story. Though I did find a lovely little shop selling those lavender sachets you like, near the market. Lavender sachets? That's nice, Doreen. Very thoughtful. Still, a loaf of bread… it bothers me, it does. It's a sign of the times, innit? Everything going to pot. Speaking of signs of the times, have either of you seen that new series of  Big Brother ? Utterly ridiculous. The casting is awful. They’re just looking for conflict, not interesting personalities. Dad, honestly? You’re still watching  Big Brother ? I thought you were above all that. You’re a Professor Emeritus for goodness sake! Don’t you get smart with me, David. It’s a guilty pleasure! Besides, it tells you a lot about society, doesn't it? The narcissism, the attention-seeking… All those young people. Sounds exhausting just listening to you describe it. I'm happy with my jigsaw puzzles and a nice cup of tea, thank you very much. Remember that party we had last month, Arthur? That was a good bit of fun. Aye, that was a good do. Though young David here kept going on about the heating being too high. Said it was carbon footprint this, and energy crisis that. Well, it  was  stifling, Dad. And we’re trying to be mindful, aren't we? It's a bit different when you're not on a fixed pension. Mindful of what? Suffering in silence? Honestly, David, a little warmth is hardly the end of the world. I built this house, I’ll heat it as I see fit. Now, now, let's not squabble. It's lovely and cosy in here. Arthur, have you taken Winston for his walk yet? He’s been looking at the door all morning. Not yet, Doreen. Got a bit of a twinge in my hip. Silly dog knows when I'm feeling it. He just sits there, looking mournful.

…and then Grandad, bless ‘im, tried to explain NFTs to Auntie Brenda. You should’ve  seen  her face. She thought he was talking about a new type of fertiliser! Honestly, it were reet funny. Oh my god, that sounds  exactly  like something he’d do. He's still convinced the internet is a series of tubes, isn't he? How’s Doncaster treating you, by the way? It feels like ages since I last properly spoke to you, not just rushed texts. Aye, it is a bit of a distance, isn't it? Doncaster’s…Doncaster. Same as ever. Still grey, still a bit rough around the edges, still full of folk who’ll talk your ear off if you let ‘em. Work's good though, finally getting a handle on organizing the regional plumbing conference. Honestly, plumbers are a  demanding  bunch. I can imagine! Sounds stressful, but at least it’s interesting. My job is…predictable. Production Controller. Sounds fancier than it is, really. It's mainly spreadsheets and making sure things arrive on time. Exciting stuff. But at least it pays the rent in Cambridge, which is a small miracle in itself. Speaking of which, is your Mum still nagging you about finding a “nice young man”? Don’t even  start  me. Every phone call is a barrage of ‘When are you gonna settle down?’ and ‘Poor Doris next door’s granddaughter met a doctor!’ It’s exhausting. I’m twenty-six, not sixty! What about your Dad? Is he still trying to set you up with every eligible bachelor in South London? He’s… toned it down, slightly. After the fiasco with the ‘entrepreneur’ who was apparently selling NFTs… legitimately this time. He still tries discreetly, though. Leaving articles about successful couples around. It’s suffocating. Anyway, dinner is almost ready. I made that lentil dahl you like, and I attempted a naan bread. Don't judge it too harshly, it’s my first go. Oh, brilliant! I’m starving. And don’t worry, I'm no Paul Hollywood. If it’s edible, I’m happy. I brought some Yorkshire cheeses with me, thought they might go nicely. So, change of subject – have you seen that new Wes Anderson film?  Asteroid City ? Not yet, but it's on my list. I’m a sucker for his aesthetic. It’s just… sometimes his films feel a bit… detached, you know?

…and honestly, lad, I just don’t see what all the fuss is about, not  again . Another referendum? Honestly! It's like a bairn throwing a tantrum, wanting something, being told no, then demanding it again five minutes later. But Gran, it's not just a tantrum. People in Scotland feel…different. They want to make their own decisions. Mr. Henderson in history said it’s about self-determination. Self-determination, aye, that’s a fancy word for wanting to run your own show. And look at the mess they nearly made last time! All that uncertainty. Remember your Grandad Arthur? He nearly had a fit worrying about his pension. He worked hard all his life, and the thought of it all being up in the air… He worries about everything, Gran. Even if the kettle whistles too loud. Aye, a worrier he was. But he had a point! It’s not just about money, though, is it? It's about history. My own great-grandfather fought  with  Scotsmen in the Boer War. We've been intertwined for centuries. Look at the Union, how strong we are together. But hasn’t the Union…changed? Mr. Henderson was saying how Scotland used to be really powerful, and then it got sort of…absorbed. And the oil money, he said, a lot of that goes to London. Oil money… now there's a can of worms. It did bring a lot in, aye, but it’s not as simple as that, is it? And “absorbed”? That’s a bit strong, isn't it? It’s a partnership, a union. And remember, they voted to stay last time. A clear majority. What makes you think it’ll be any different this time? Because things  are  different now. Brexit’s changed everything. Scotland voted to stay in Europe, didn’t it? And now they’re being dragged out against their will. It feels unfair. That's a fair point, I’ll give you that. Brexit certainly stirred things up. I didn’t vote for it myself, mind you. Never could see the benefit. But to throw everything away again over Brexit… It feels a bit drastic. I remember when we joined the Common Market - your grandfather and I thought it was a good thing, opening up trade and all. Never imagined it’d all unravel like this. So, you understand  why  they might want independence, even if you don’t agree with it?

Oh, honestly. Look at ‘em, goin’ at it ‘ammer and tongs already. It’s barely 9:30! This is  why  I don’t usually watch this. Proper stressful. Ah, come on, Liv. It's entertaining, innit? You know exactly what you're gettin' with Jeremy Kyle. All the drama, none of the intelligence. It's a guilty pleasure. Honestly, it’s fascinating how readily people air their dirty laundry on national television. It’s…sad, really. And the accents! They compress everything, don’t they? Like, every syllable gets squished. Aye, it does, doesn’t it? It's like they’re tryin’ to fit a whole essay into one breath. Listen to that fella – ‘I didn’t  do  nuffin’!’ It’s all run together. Proper elision, that is. My linguistics teacher would have a field day. Elision! That’s exactly it! I noticed it ages ago. Everyone speaks a bit like that when they’re proper stressed or excited, but they’ve all cranked it up to eleven for Jeremy Kyle. Makes it hard to understand half of what they're sayin’. It's worse because it highlights the differences even more, like. You can tell where everyone’s from, but it’s all… distorted. It makes even  my  accent sound posh! I mean, I'm from Doncaster. It’s not exactly the Queen’s English, is it? Posh? Liv, you've got a proper Yorkshire drawl! Don’t be daft. Mine sounds even more…scouse, I suppose, when I’m riled up. My nan always says I sound like a market trader. I can hear it slightly, actually. It’s the way you pronounce your vowels. Mine's pretty neutral, I think, being from Derby. Midlander problems – we just blend in. Nobody ever asks where I'm from. It’s tragic. That’s rough! I get people askin’ all the time. “Ooh, you’re from Yorkshire, are ya?” They’re usually tryin’ to guess if I can yodel or wrestle sheep or somethin’. Don’t encourage them, Chloe! You’ll be gettin’ requests for a demonstration at every party. Speaking of stereotypes… this bloke on the TV thinks ‘lie detector’ is a legitimate way to sort out relationship problems. Honestly! It's just a man with a voltmeter and a lotta opinions. And his accent's so thick, I can barely understand a word he's sayin'. They  know  it’s not admissible in court, right?

Honestly, that was a  terrible  tackle. Absolutely reckless. They’ll be lucky if he doesn't get a red card. Reckless, maybe. Desperate, definitely. They're getting hammered, love. They’ve gotta try  something . Though I agree, that was bordering on criminal. Who are you even rooting for? I thought you didn’t follow football properly? I don’t, not really. But my dad’s a massive Sunderland fan, and he’s been badgering me all week to watch this one. Said it's a 'must-win’ for morale. So I’m, like, spiritually supporting them. Plus, it's good to have something to moan about, innit? It’s a North East tradition. A tradition, aye. Right up there with flat caps and parmos. Speaking of traditions, how’s the knitting going? Still aiming for a scarf long enough to wrap around Cambridge? Progress is…slow. It's surprisingly relaxing though. Mum always used to knit. Said it kept her hands busy and her mind calm. I can see what she meant. Trying to pick a colour scheme is the hard bit. I'm thinking something for the little one… if we ever decide on a name. Oh, don’t get me started on names! We were having  another  debate about it last night. I'm sticking with Arthur. Classic, solid. You’re still obsessed with… what was it? Bronwyn? Bronwyn is beautiful! It's Welsh, you know. And it means 'white breasted'. Elegant. Arthur sounds like a grumpy old man. No offense. None taken. Though I suspect our Arthur will be a grumpy old man in training. Seriously though, we need to narrow it down. The Olympics are coming up and I'm envisioning us frantically googling athletes' names for inspiration on the way to the hospital. You're probably right. That’s precisely what will happen. Remember when we were trying to come up with dog names? It took us a week and we ended up calling him Winston, because it was the only thing we both agreed on. Winston was perfect. A truly dignified name for a slightly ridiculous pug. Actually, talking of the Olympics... do you think they’ll actually  happen  properly this time? After the last one... I hope so. It needs a bit of…  something , doesn't it? A collective boost. Everyone needs a bit of cheering up. Plus, I’m a sucker for the gymnastics.

…and honestly, the whole premise of the Bee Movie is just  bonkers . A bee suing humanity? It’s brilliantly silly, isn't it? Though, honestly, I think Barry B. Benson had a point about pollen exploitation. Bees can't  sue  people, Mummy! That's daft. Yeah! They just… sting them! Well, in the movie they can. It’s a film, darling. It’s meant to be a little bit fantastical. It got me thinking though, about Kings and Queens. All that power… It's a bit like the bees controlling all the honey, isn't it? But Kings and Queens are nice! Princess Charlotte waved at me on the telly! She did? That's lovely. They  seem  nice. But it’s funny, isn’t it, that we pay to go and look at where they live? All those palaces… Windsor, Buckingham… paying just to walk through rooms where people are… just living. We went to Warwick Castle! That had a dungeon! That’s different, isn't it? That’s history! Palaces feel… a bit much sometimes. I mean, don’t you think it’s a bit odd, in a supposed democracy, we’re essentially admiring people just because of who their parents were? But they wear sparkly crowns! They  do  wear sparkly crowns. It’s a very good tactic, actually. Speaking of things royalty eat… remember Granny’s garden? All her lovely fruit? She always said she grew ‘Royal fruits’ for the Queen. What’s ‘Royal fruits’? Well, she meant the best plums and peaches. She was a bit of a character, your Granny. Always convinced she had a direct line to the palace. She’d send them letters, complaining about the price of sprouts, honestly. Did the Queen write back? Never. But Granny didn't let that stop her. She said it was because the Queen was too busy… making important decisions about… well, plums, probably. Honestly, I sometimes wonder if I should have gone into politics. Or become royalty. You get to live in a palace! You could be Queen! You’re good at bossing us about! That’s not quite the qualification, darling. It's more complex than that. Though, I  am  good at organising. Maybe a Prime Minister then? No. Too much arguing. Teaching is less… politically fraught, usually. Are you both taking your vitamins? I put them by your breakfast plates. Yuck! They taste like feet!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of things your father has accumulated! It’s like he was preparing for the apocalypse, not just downsizing for a smaller place. Did you see the five different types of sandpaper? Sandpaper, lad! What does one man  need  with five different grits? Aye, he's always been a bit of a hoarder, your brother. Remember when he tried to convince us he needed every single issue of ‘Practical Poultry’ from 1987 onwards? Said it was “historical documentation.” Historical documentation of… chickens? Seriously? It was a phase. A very…involved phase. Though I think he secretly still misses Henrietta. Henrietta the hen! Goodness me. And the garden gnomes! Honestly, there were more gnomes than plants. I swear, each one had a little personality your father had  given  it. “This is Bertram, he supervises the tomatoes.” Utterly bonkers. He’s just…sentimental, Elsie. You know that. Everything has a story. Though I agree, a lot of those stories need a good edit. This coffee is lovely, by the way. Just what I needed after wrestling a rusty lawnmower out of the shed. I helped with the lawnmower! It was heavy. And smelled bad. You were a star, lad. Really. Saved my back. We’d still be there if it wasn’t for you. It’s amazing what people hold onto, isn’t it? I was sifting through some old boxes at Mum's yesterday and found a complete collection of "TV Times" from 1978. Apparently, it was crucial for planning viewing. Crucial! Back then, you  needed  the TV Times. There weren't hundreds of channels and on-demand everything. It was all about knowing what was on, and when. “Doctor Who” on Saturdays, “Coronation Street” on Wednesdays… Life was simpler. Though the picture quality was dreadful! Simpler, perhaps. Though I remember my Aunty Mabel complaining incessantly about the limited choice. She was convinced the BBC was deliberately trying to offend her. What’s the BBC? Oh, lad! The British Broadcasting Corporation! It’s…well, it’s television, but it’s more than that. It’s a national institution. It used to be the only channel. It still produces some fantastic things. Though I do worry about its future, with everything changing. Speaking of changing, have you thought anymore about the colour scheme for the living room, Mum? We  are  trying to make this new place feel like home, aren’t we?

… honestly, the Walker Art Gallery’s parking is a joke. Absolute daylight robbery. Fifteen quid for two hours! You’d think for a cultural institution they could sort something better out. Fifteen quid?! Seriously? I thought it was bad at the Maritime Museum, but that was only eight. We walked from James Street, remember? Luckily it wasn't raining  too  hard. How was the exhibition anyway? Worth the extortionate parking fee? The exhibition was decent, yeah. The Pre-Raphaelites. Really beautiful stuff. But fifteen quid… it kinda soured it a bit, didn't it? It felt like they were penalising people for wanting to experience art. And it’s not like it’s easy to find a spot anywhere else nearby, is it? No, it's a nightmare. Listen, speaking of nightmares, I had a really strange session with old Mr. Henderson today. He was convinced his cat was judging his life choices. Proper existential crisis, apparently triggered by a feline stare. No way! That's brilliant. Animals are brilliant at making you question everything. Remember when our Nan’s budgie used to just  stare  at you? Felt like it knew all your secrets. Exactly! It’s the unblinking judgement, isn’t it? Anyway, he’s referred himself for some CBT. Hopefully, that’ll help him differentiate between genuine self-reflection and a cat’s disinterest. Busy week at work generally though, that referral load is just… increasing. How’s the teaching going? Any unruly scousers causing havoc? It's alright. Year 10 are driving me insane with their TikTok obsession. Every lesson it’s like pulling teeth to get them to focus on Dickens instead of dances. But I’ve got a good head of department, she's really supportive. Actually, I was thinking... about that Masters. The interview’s next Tuesday. Oh, amazing! That’s fantastic, Liam. Have you been prepping? You’ll be brilliant. What kind of questions do you think they’ll ask? I’ve been going over my personal statement a million times. I think they’ll want to know about my research interests, and specifically why  that  uni. It's just... the money, innit? Even with the potential scholarship, it's a hefty expense. Well, we’ll figure it out. We always do. Maybe we could look at tightening the belt a bit? Less takeaway, more cooking? And I've got that bonus coming next month, we could put some of that towards it.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the hype around this new Harry Styles album. Everyone's losing their minds, and it's… fine. Just fine. It all sounds the same, innit? A bit beige, if you ask me. Beige?! Elsie, that’s harsh! I actually really like it. It's a vibe, you know? Like, perfect for driving with the windows down, pretending you’re in a music video. And he’s actually a decent actor now, have you seen  Don’t Worry Darling ? I tried to. Honestly, Florence Pugh carried that whole film. Harry just… existed. And a “vibe” is a bit vague, don't you think? Give me something with a bit of…grit. Like, I’ve been rewatching early Arctic Monkeys videos and that's a vibe. Properly a vibe. Ooh, Arctic Monkeys! Classic. Though, Alex Turner’s gone a bit… abstract these days, hasn’t he? It's like he’s actively trying to confuse everyone. Speaking of confusing, have you seen what’s trending on TikTok? It’s all about recreating childhood photos. Oh god, don’t even. My mum keeps sending me links to ones she wants  me  to recreate. With the same outfits. She dug out my Spice Girls dress from, like, 1997. It does  not  fit. And it’s… questionable. Oh no! That’s amazing and tragic all at once. My nan is obsessed with TikTok too. She keeps trying to do those dance challenges. It's brilliant. It's just… her knees, you worry about her knees. Bless her. At least she's keeping busy. I’m just completely overwhelmed with uni work. This essay on post-structuralism is killing me. I’ve been living on coffee and sheer willpower. Tell me about it! I’m drowning in research for my psychology project. It's all about the effects of social media on self-esteem. Which is ironic, considering I’ve spent the last three hours scrolling through Instagram comparing myself to influencers… The irony! It’s brutal. You should probably stop for the research, though. You'll end up needing a therapy session  about  the research. Fancy going to that new Italian place on Friday? Proper pizza, not that student canteen stuff. Ooh, yes! That sounds amazing. I've been craving a proper Margherita all week. Is Liam coming? I haven't asked him yet. I'm trying to gauge whether he’s still trying to impress that girl from the football society.

…and then, like, the Charizard absolutely  destroyed  his Blastoise. It was epic. Honestly, Leo, you wouldn’t believe the critical hit ratio I’ve been getting lately. It's all down to the new EV training method, apparently. Sounds…intense. More intense than your dinner, judging by how little you’ve eaten. Honestly, Finn, you’ll turn into a pixel yourself if you spend all your time staring at that screen. ‘Zard! ‘Zard! Fire! He likes Charizard too, Mum! See? He gets it. It's a classic. Although, technically, it's a Fire/Flying type… Right. A Fire/Flying type. You know, when I was your age, “types” meant what kind of music you liked. Now it’s…Pokémon attributes. Different times. Speaking of different, did you Skype Gran today? She was asking about you. Yeah, briefly. She wanted to know if I was still obsessing over Pokémon. She doesn’t  get  it, does she? She thinks it's a waste of time. She worries about you, love. She’s old school. We're going to call her properly tomorrow, after Oisin’s nap. Honestly, that boy… he sleeps for approximately five minutes at a time these days. Up! Up! ‘Zard ride! Alright, alright, ‘Zard ride it is! Just… maybe not while I’m trying to explain the intricacies of Pokémon battling. Listen, Mum, about Friday…are we still on for ramen? I was thinking that new place downtown, the one everyone’s talking about? Oh, yes! Ramen sounds amazing. I haven't been out for a proper meal in… well, ages. Just need to make sure Oisin behaves. He's been a little handful today. And I need to find decent clothes to wear. Everything feels…tight. Tight? What do you mean? Well, you know. Having a baby does things. And I haven't exactly been prioritising fashion. Plus, all my comfy clothes are covered in… you know. Baby stuff. Fair enough. Don’t worry about it. You always look good. Besides, it's ramen, not a fashion show. I'm just wishing I had some new jeans. All mine are starting to get… well, they're falling apart. And everyone’s wearing those ridiculously skinny ones now. Skinny jeans? Oh, Finn. Honestly. You look perfectly presentable in your regular ones. Don’t fall for those trends. They’re uncomfortable and impractical. But… everyone at school has them! Even Leo’s got a pair.

… honestly, I don't know  why  I kept it all this time. It's just… stuff. Mountains of stuff. And dust. So much dust. Well, you always were a bit of a hoarder, weren't you, darling? Not in a bad way, mind. More of a 'might-need-it-one-day’ kind of way. Is that the gardening set? The little plastic one? It is! Oh, goodness. Look at this. It’s all faded now, the colours. Remember how obsessed we were with it? We spent  hours  pretending to grow things. Mostly weeds, if I recall. We did! And arguing over who got the watering can. You always wanted the watering can. I wanted the little trowel. Strategic digging, that was my aim. More effective than endlessly splashing water about, I always said. You were always the pragmatic one. I just liked the  idea  of making things grow. We had a whole garden planned, you know. For the patio. A miniature herbaceous border… With pebbles for stepping stones! Don't forget the pebbles. And we meticulously arranged the little plastic carrots and radishes. Honestly, looking at this, it’s a wonder we ever had time for proper schoolwork. Proper schoolwork? A distant memory. Speaking of distant memories, is that… oh, heavens. The Bako set! Oh,  Bako ! Now that was something else. Hours and hours building fantastical castles and things. They didn't make toys like that anymore, did they? Everything's all screens and buttons now. No. It was… tactile. Real. You actually had to  think  about how to make things stand up. And then they’d inevitably collapse, and we’d blame each other. You always blamed me. Said my structural engineering skills were lacking. You were the architect, naturally. I was just… the demolition crew. I wouldn't say  always . Though, you did tend to favour overly ambitious towers with very narrow bases. It was a design flaw. A calculated risk! It added drama. Look, all the little windows and doors are still here. And that bright yellow scaffolding. God, this takes me back. But… it’s just… overwhelming, isn’t it? All this. It is. And it’s making me realise how much of our past we’ve just… accumulated. I thought it would be nice, a little trip down memory lane. But it's harder than I thought, actually letting go. It’s not just the toys, is it?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it! Just buzzing around my head as I was marking essays. You’d think after all these years living in this house, I’d be used to the Norfolk midges, but this felt… different. More aggressive. A mosquito, was it? Probably hitched a ride in with all the plants you brought back from the garden centre. You’re turning our living room into a jungle, you know. A very aesthetically pleasing jungle, admittedly. It  is  rather lovely, isn’t it? But yes, probably. It’s just… I swear it was a particularly large mosquito. And determined. Anyway, Baby Leo barely stirred through the whole thing, which is a blessing. He's a surprisingly sound sleeper, even with miniature vampires trying to feast on his mum. He gets that from you. Stubbornness, I mean. Not the vampire attraction. Though, he  does  have your rosy cheeks. Right, park bench achieved. He’s properly settled now, gazing at the trees. This is nice. Proper quiet for once. It is. Blissful, actually. Though I’m already dreading the drive back. Did you see the traffic on Unthank Road earlier? It was absolutely horrendous. Took me nearly forty minutes to get to the University and it's usually a twenty minute drive. Don’t even  start  on the traffic. I’m still reeling from trying to navigate it yesterday evening. Apparently, there was a broken-down van near the A47. It just ripples outwards, doesn't it? One van and the entire city grinds to a halt. It's ridiculous. They really need to look at improving the infrastructure. I mean, Norwich is a lovely city, but its road system is… Neolithic. Speaking of things that are a bit behind the times, have you seen what gigs are on at the Waterfront next month? Ooh, go on. I haven’t checked in ages. Last time I looked they were playing some sort of… death metal ukulele band. Which, while intriguing, wasn't exactly our vibe. No, thankfully not. There’s a band called ‘Indigo Bloom’ – indie-folk, very mellow. Reminds me a bit of that stuff we used to listen to when we first met. And then ‘The Static Waves’ are playing the week after. Bit more upbeat, electronic sort of thing. Indigo Bloom sounds perfect for a chilled night out. Though, 'The Static Waves'… I'm surprisingly up for that.

…and honestly, the putting green was  brutal  today. Felt like trying to roll a marble uphill in treacle. Honestly, Gareth kept moaning about the rough being too long, but I think the real issue was just everyone’s heads were gone after that early frost. Ugh, sounds grim. You’d think professional golfers wouldn't let a bit of frost throw them off. Though, I suppose it’s different when your livelihood depends on it. My day was… less stressful. Mostly spent applying for jobs and staring at my phone. Which, by the way, is about to die. Again. Another dead phone, eh? You go through those things like I go through golf balls. What’s the issue? Battery, charger, you just…  use  it too much? I think it's the battery. It barely holds a charge anymore. I’ve been meaning to get it replaced, but it feels like such a faff, and then I'll probably just break the new one somehow. It's a vicious cycle. Speaking of faff, I had a letter today. A  real  letter. Not a bill, not junk mail, an actual handwritten letter. From Aunt Carol. No way! Aunt Carol still writes letters? That’s… quaint. What did she want? Another update on the ‘suitable young men’ in my orbit? Worse. She's been to this ghost tour in High Wycombe Old Town, swears it’s haunted by a Victorian theatre performer. Apparently, she felt a cold spot and heard a whisper. She wants me to go with her next time. A ghost tour? Seriously? Your Aunt Carol’s letting her imagination run wild. Look, I deal with pressure all day, every day, and I  still  wouldn’t fancy wandering around in the dark hoping for a spooky encounter. Exactly what I said! But you know she is. She’s convinced the old theatre's toilets are a hotbed of paranormal activity. Apparently, someone died in there in the 1880s. Right. Well, I’m sticking to 18 holes and hopefully a decent score. Did you manage to get any actual application progress done, or was it all Aunt Carol and ghosts? A bit of both. Sent off three applications. One for a marketing assistant role in Manchester, which is a long shot, but… Manchester’s Manchester. Keeps cropping up. And two for graduate schemes with that recruitment agency, Stellar Solutions. They sound pretty intense, though.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the cloud migration has been a nightmare. They promised seamless, they delivered… chaos. Three servers down yesterday, lost a whole morning untangling it. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I bother. “The wheels on the bus go round and round, round and round, round and round…” Leo, darling, maybe a little quieter during Daddy’s explaining about work? It sounds complicated. And a bit stressful, actually, Liam. It  is  stressful, love. It's not just the tech, it's the management. No understanding of the real world implications. Anyway, enough about work. What are we having for dinner? I'm starving. I was thinking spaghetti bolognese. Quick, easy, and Leo will actually eat it. Though he mainly seems to enjoy flinging it. Wee! Bolognese is good! Can I have garlic bread with it? Proper garlic bread, not just buttered bread. Garlic bread is a yes. Although, you’ll be breathing fire all night. You know that. Liam! Don't encourage him. He already has enough energy. He was bouncing off the walls at soft play this morning. He’s a whirlwind, our Leo. A precious whirlwind, but a whirlwind nonetheless. Did you manage to sort out the arrangements for Saturday? Auntie Mary’s birthday? Nearly. I’ve booked the restaurant, but I’m trying to get a babysitter. Everyone is booked solid, naturally. It’s a Saturday night in Ballincollig, apparently the height of social activity. I can look after Leo if you want! I’m pretty good at building Lego and reading stories. You're a good lad, Jamie, but your mum and I wouldn’t want to impose. It’s a bit late for you. And Auntie Mary’s house… well, let's just say it’s not exactly geared towards a rambunctious teenager. Exactly. It’s a small space, and Mary has that antique china she’s terrified of breaking. I feel bad leaving her on her own though, she gets lonely. We’ll figure it out. Maybe we can ask old Mrs. O'Malley next door? She adores Leo. Actually, that’s a brilliant idea! I’ll ring her now. Fingers crossed. It would be a weight off my mind. While you’re doing that, can we maybe watch a film later? I was thinking that new superhero one? The one with the glowing suit? We’ll see. Depends on how much chaos Leo creates before bedtime.

… honestly, I still can’t believe he slept in just his pants last night. And not even  nice  pants, like, the grey marl ones with the hole near the waistband. Oh, bless him. He was proper knocked out after building that Lego fortress with Leo. It’s a miracle he even  found  his pants, let alone put them on. Honestly, it’s the countryside air. Makes them wild. Daddy? Why does ANON only have pants on? Is it a pirate thing? No, sweetheart, it’s not a pirate thing. He was just very, very tired. Sometimes when people are really tired, they don’t bother with all the clothes. I sleep in my pyjamas! Pyjamas are much better than just pants. They have dinosaurs on mine! They  are  much better, aren't they? Though, your dinosaur pyjamas do seem to end up on the floor more often than on you... Anyway, speaking of comfortable things, I was thinking… while we're here, escaping to this lovely little house, maybe we should  actually  start properly planning that extension. Oh, here we go. The planning committee is in session. What’s sparked this now? Is it the lack of central heating reminding you how much space we’d need for a proper boiler, or…? Don’t be cynical! It’s… inspired. We've got space in the garden, a vague idea of what we want, and, crucially, no builders actually  here  to tell us it can’t be done. I was picturing extending the kitchen, knocking through to create a bigger family room. Think: Aga, huge table, somewhere for the kids to do their homework without driving us insane. An Aga? Right. Because a wood-burning stove in Suffolk isn’t enough rural charm for you. And forgetting the small detail of, oh, I don’t know… the budget? We’re account executives and a teacher, not lottery winners. We could look at financing options! And it wouldn’t be a  huge  Aga. Maybe a… medium Aga. Or a very enthusiastic electric Aga. Look, I’ve been sketching. Ooh, can I see?! Is there a slide in the new kitchen? Not a slide, darling, but maybe a breakfast bar you can spin around on. Here, look. I was thinking if we moved the utility room… and knocked down this wall… You want to turn the back garden into a glass atrium? It looks like a botanical garden.

…and honestly, the magnolia was a crime against interior design. Simply dreadful. My wife, bless her, she has  ideas . Bold ones. We’ve gone for a Farrow & Ball ‘Railings’ now. Very sophisticated. Though getting the painter to understand the nuance between ‘Railings’ and ‘Corvedale’ nearly caused a marital incident, I assure you. Oh, the shades of grey! A dangerous world, that. My wife’s a staunch believer in ‘feature walls’. Last one was a sort of… aubergine. Looked like someone’d left a bruise on the living room. I fought hard for neutral in the study, though. Needed a calming space for the funding applications, you see. Funding. Don’t even  mention  it. I’ve just had another rejection. The Rutherford Project. Apparently, “lacks innovation” according to the panel. Lacks innovation! We're proposing to refine the data analysis from the Hadron Collider! What more innovative can you get? They’re all the same, aren't they? Buzzwords and checklists. I put in for a small grant to continue the work on pre-industrial Welsh ironworking – vital stuff, you know, understanding the origins of heavy industry – and they said it didn’t align with their ‘strategic priorities’. Strategic priorities! They funded a project on the social impact of competitive dog grooming! Competitive dog grooming?! Good heavens. The world has gone mad. Honestly, I’m seriously considering retiring early and just… growing orchids. Less stressful. Have you had your coffee refilled, Alun? I'll get you another. That’s kind of you, David, but I’m alright for now. Though it  is  a bit weak today, isn't it? They’ve changed suppliers again, I suspect. It’s always something with these office coffee arrangements. Like the water companies, always fiddling with the pressure, claiming it’s for ‘improvements’. It's always a price hike disguised as progress. Exactly! They claim the chlorine levels are optimised for ‘customer experience’. As if anyone enjoys tasting chlorine! It's daylight robbery. It reminds me of a trip I took to Italy a few years ago. The water… magnificent. Served in carafes, sparkling, tasted of the mountains. Completely different. Italy. Now you’re talking. Tuscany, wasn’t it? You were presenting at that conference on particle physics, if I remember correctly. Florence, actually. And yes, a small symposium. Though frankly, the food was the highlight. I spent more time researching  gelateria  than I did the Higgs boson.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Lego is astonishing. It’s like it  multiplies  when you’re not looking. Right, Lily? Are we aiming for colour-sorted, or theme-sorted today? Because theme-sorted will take until Christmas. Colour-sorted! Definitely colour-sorted. It’s easier. And then we can make a rainbow tower! A really,  really  tall rainbow tower! But the Ninjas need their own pile! They can’t be with the pink bricks! That’s silly. Well, the Ninjas  could  have their own special section  within  the colour-sorted piles, Leo. Compromise. Green bricks are for Ninjas, mostly. Is that acceptable? Hmm… okay. But I get to build the tower first! With all the green ones! No fair!  I  want to build it first! Right, okay, potential meltdown averted. How about we each build a  section  of the rainbow tower? Lily can do red and orange, Leo can do green and yellow… And I get Leonardo! He's the best Ninja! Michelangelo is! He’s funny! He says “Cowabunga!” They’re both excellent, darling. They each have their strengths. Honestly, you two are exactly like Harry, Ron and Hermione arguing over Quidditch. What’s Quidditch? Is it like…magic Lego? Not exactly. It’s a game from Harry Potter. You fly on broomsticks and try to score goals… it’s a bit complicated to explain right now. We can watch one of the films later if you like. Actually, thinking about films, do you fancy going to the cinema this weekend? There's that new animated one – the turtle one? Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles! Yes! Can we get popcorn? A big bucket! And sweets! And a drink! A really fizzy one! We can discuss the exact caloric intake later. Right now, Lego. Speaking of sorting, did you know Granny’s having the kitchen completely re-done? Granny’s kitchen? But it's always smelled of biscuits in there! It will still smell of biscuits, just in a  newer  kitchen! They’re knocking down a wall, apparently. It's going to be chaos. Mum’s been helping her choose colours, it's all very stressful. Is it like building with Lego but really big? In a way, yes. Except you can’t just pull it apart and start again if you make a mistake! Which brings me back to this mountain of plastic… Honestly, I swear I stepped on a rogue brick earlier.

…and honestly, the paella was just  sad . Like, barely any seafood, mostly just rice and a really aggressive amount of paprika. You know how much I love a good paella! Oh no! That  is  a tragedy. Spain should be illegal if they serve bad paella. How was everything else? You seemed to have a good time on Instagram, at least. Loads of sun and sangria. It  was  amazing, don't get me wrong! Barcelona was incredible. Just… the paella. It’s a sticking point. And the heat! It was proper scorching. I feel like I've aged ten years just from sun exposure. How was your week with your mum? Did she manage to avoid lecturing you about needing a husband? Oh, you know Mum. The lecture happened, naturally. It was a brief but intense campaign about my 'biological clock' and how all my friends are 'settling down'. I deflected by telling her about a particularly challenging patient at work. She doesn’t handle that stuff well. Smart move. Changing the subject to ward politics is always a winner. Speaking of challenging… work’s been a nightmare since I’ve been back. Mr. Henderson decided  during  my holiday that he wanted the entire project scope changed. Seriously? He does that  every  time, doesn't he? The man lives for last-minute chaos. What’s changed now? Basically, the entire marketing campaign needs to be reworked. It’s like, we were aiming for a younger demographic, and now he wants something… ‘classic’ and ‘sophisticated’. Which translates to beige and boring, probably. Honestly, I just want to scream. Ugh. That sounds awful. I’m so sorry. It’s so disrespectful to change things while you’re away. You’re supposed to be able to switch off. I had a similar thing happen last week, actually. Old Mr. Davies was having a really rough patch and I was covering for Sarah on her leave, so it was just…constant crisis management. Made me appreciate a week with Mum and her anxieties, honestly. That sounds exhausting. You're a saint, dealing with that every day. I sometimes wonder if I'm cut out for project management. It's all meetings and spreadsheets and people constantly changing their minds. You're brilliant at it, though! You just need to learn to say ‘no’ more. And maybe threaten Mr. Henderson with a strongly worded email. Maybe. Or just move to a remote island and become a paella chef.

…and honestly, lad, I don’t know  why  they keep changing the mark schemes. It’s a nightmare! Last year it was all about ‘showing working’, this year it’s ‘elegant solutions’. What  is  an elegant solution to a simultaneous equation for a fifteen-year-old, eh? It’s just maths, not a blooming art competition! Sounds stressful, Mum. I’m just glad I’m nearly done with GCSEs. Though Physics is… well, Physics is still Physics. Aye, Physics. Always a tricky one. Your Grandad here barely scraped through it, didn't you, Arthur? More interested in tinkering with engines than triangles, he was. She’s not wrong. Triangles never fixed a Ford Anglia, let me tell you. Though I reckon I could build you a mark scheme for that, Doreen. Plenty of steps involved! Oh, you would, wouldn’t you? You always were a practical man. Now, are you two comfortable enough? Can I get you another cuppa? I made Brenda’s shortbread, you know, your favourite, Arthur. Don't mind if I do, lass! Brenda always made a cracking shortbread. Better than anything you get in the shops. And comfortable as can be, thank you. This armchair is a godsend for these old bones. Me too, dear. Lovely and warm in here. Not like that draughty old house we had in Hull, eh Arthur? Remember the winter of ‘63? Frozen pipes for weeks! Don’t remind me. Had to melt the ice with a camping stove! Nearly burned the kitchen down. That was a bit of a panic, that was. Wow, really? Sounds…intense. Intense is one word for it! Your Gran was a force of nature then, she was. Always had a plan, even if it involved a camping stove and a potential house fire. Speaking of plans, I was thinking, Michael – that’s you, love – maybe you could give your Grandad a hand with the garden next weekend? He’s been moaning about the weeds. Ugh, weeds? Mum! Now, now, be polite. It’d be lovely for both of them. And a bit of fresh air would do you good, glued to that computer screen all the time. He’s a good lad, Michael. Always willing to help. Unlike some! Now, now, Doreen. I  helped  with the garden. I pointed out where the weeds were. That's a crucial contribution, you know. Strategic weed identification. Strategic weed identification?

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…dark. Not in a good, Disney-villain dark, but just…sad. Even for a story about a boy who doesn’t grow up. But Tinkerbell was pretty! She sparkled  lots . She  was  pretty, wasn’t she, sweetheart? A proper little firework. Though, the newer Tinkerbell films, the animated ones… they’re quite different to the original story, you know? Very…pink. Pink is cool! Like my red car! Vroom vroom! It  is  cool, Leo. And your red car definitely goes vroom vroom. But in Peter Pan, Tinkerbell’s magic wasn’t just about making everything glittery. She was fiercely protective of Peter, and a bit…jealous. Remember that? She tried to get Wendy shot! Well, she  tried  to. She didn't want Peter looking at anyone else. It wasn't very nice of her, was it? It's funny, thinking about it, my Great Aunt Millie used to work at Great Ormond Street Hospital. Great Ormond Street? Is that where sick people go? That’s right, darling. And J.M. Barrie, the author of Peter Pan, he gave the copyright of the story to Great Ormond Street. So every time someone makes a Peter Pan film, or sells a book, or anything like that, money goes to the hospital to help sick children. Isn’t that lovely? He gave them  all  the money? Not  all  of it, but a massive amount. He didn’t have any children of his own, you see, so he wanted to do something to help children who were poorly. He used to visit the hospital a lot too, and tell stories. Did he dress up as Peter Pan? I don't know if he dressed up! That would be amazing, wouldn’t it? Though, I imagine the nurses and doctors were busy enough without a grown man running around in green tights! I think he just told them the story. I liked the  Pan  film. With the fairies. Oh,  Pan . That was…a bit of a different take, wasn’t it? Honestly, it felt like they’d taken bits of Peter Pan and then added a whole load of other adventure stuff. Was Captain Hook in it? He was! But he wasn’t quite the same Captain Hook, was he? He wasn’t as…scary. In the original, he’s absolutely terrifying! He lost his hand to a crocodile, you know.

…and honestly, the M5 this morning was a nightmare. Absolute gridlock near Taunton. Thought we’d be stuck there for hours. Glad we left when we did, even with the early start. You’re telling me! I checked the traffic app just before we left, and it was already predicting delays. Still, good job anticipating it, Dad. Mum, are you comfy back there? You seemed a bit restless when we stopped for coffee. I am comfy, dear, just…thinking. This is all a bit emotional, isn’t it? Seeing Sarah off to Australia for so long. It feels like only yesterday she was learning to ride her bike in the garden at our place in Totnes. Totnes, now  that  was a nice little town. Much quieter than Exmouth. Remember Mrs. Higgins and her prize-winning roses? She used to try and give me cuttings, said I had “gardener’s hands.” I told her my hands were better suited to spreadsheets. You and spreadsheets. A love story for the ages. Though, you did finally grow those tomatoes last year, didn’t you? After years of failure. A fluke! A complete fluke! All down to the weather, I tell you. This Devon sun is something else. Though, it’s a long way from Southend, isn’t it? Used to be able to smell the sea air, even in the house. Miss that sometimes. Southend was…bustling. Very different pace. We wouldn’t have swapped our time in Wellington for anything, though. That little cottage, the village pub… lovely memories. And much better for bringing up the children, wouldn't you agree? Definitely. More space, safer, and the school was brilliant. It’s funny how quickly you adapt, isn't it? I remember feeling so anxious about leaving Hampshire, but Devon feels like home now. It does. Though, getting to the airport is always a pain. This journey always feels longer than it is. You’d think after all these years I’d be used to it. It’s not even as far as driving to Taunton used to be when I was working! Speaking of Christmas, have we finalised plans? Are we all at your place this year, Sarah’s absence aside? I think so. We said we’d rotate, and it’s your turn, Mum. Unless you’d rather we came to mine? It's a bit smaller, but… No, no, yours is perfectly fine, dear, but it’ll be nice to have everyone at ours.

…and honestly, the whole thing’s a bit fiddly, isn’t it? All these little track sections. My hands aren’t what they were, you see. Used to be able to mend anything, delicate porcelain, grandfather clocks… now a bit of gravel gets under my fingernails and I’m complaining like a child. Tell me about it. I’ve spent my life managing buildings, you’d think I’d be handy. But bending down, fiddling with these sleepers… my knees are screaming. Good to have a breather, though. This ticket office is surprisingly comfy. It is, isn’t it? A bit reminiscent of my gallery, actually. Small, enclosed, a certain… stillness. Though the clientele were usually a bit more interested in price tags than railway lines. You local to these parts? Birmingham originally, but moved around a bit with the Nationwide. Now I live just outside Taunton. You? Well, Somerset born and bred. Near Wells, actually. Used to be proper countryside, you know. Now it's all holiday lets and avocado farms. I was an artist, mostly landscapes, and ran a little antique shop too. Bit of everything really – furniture, paintings, bits and bobs. Lovely. My wife, God rest her soul, used to adore antiques. She always said I didn’t appreciate them enough. Too practical, she said. Always wanted me to buy a mahogany sideboard. Never did. They are… acquiring things. It’s a habit. My late husband, Geoffrey, was the same. Always bringing home ‘rescue’ furniture. The house was groaning under the weight of it. Speaking of rescues… I volunteered at the hospice for a while, you know. Terribly sad, but rewarding. The people there are angels. That’s good of you. My wife was in one for the last few weeks. The care they gave her was… well, it was everything. Brings it all back, though, even talking about it. It does. Changes your perspective, doesn't it? Makes you focus on what's truly important. It’s funny, isn’t it? All this talk of equality, and women still generally end up doing the bulk of the caring. It was Geoffrey who ended up needing full-time care with his emphysema, and I was the one who stepped up. No one even  asked  if I had other things I wanted to do. That’s the truth of it. My daughter’s a nursery teacher. Absolutely brilliant with the little ones.

…and honestly, the photos online don’t  do  it justice. It looks…beige. Like a really expensive beige box. I was hoping for a bit more charm, you know? Something with character. Beige? Oh dear. That's not a good start, is it? You’re paying a fair bit for that villa, aren't you, love? I thought you said it was supposed to be overlooking the sea? It is, technically. It’s on a cliff, so you can  see  the sea, but you’re looking down on a car park mostly. And the beige…it’s pervasive. The website said ‘modern minimalist’ but I’m getting ‘drab and depressing’. Minimalist can be nice, but not when it comes across as just…unfinished. Right. Well, we've paid the deposit, haven't we? Can you not change it? Speak to the agency? I spoke to Sarah at 'Sunshine Escapes' this morning. She said everything is fully booked for August. Apparently, everyone and their dog wants to go to the Algarve this year. She did offer me a different place, further inland, with a ‘rustic charm’ – which I suspect translates to ‘no air conditioning and spiders’ – but it’s miles from the beach. And you know I was really looking forward to swimming every day. Spiders are a definite no-go. You know my history with eight-legged creatures. And swimming is important. You  need  a break, El. Teaching those teenagers all year round must be draining. Remember last summer? You were running on fumes by September. I do remember. It was…intense. That’s exactly why I booked this! I was picturing myself with a book, a glass of vinho verde, the sound of the waves…not staring at concrete. I'm starting to wonder if we should just cancel and stay in Devon. We could do day trips to Salcombe, maybe even a little staycation in Dartmoor. Now, hold on. Don't throw the baby out with the bathwater. Cancelling now will probably lose you a good chunk of money, won't it? And you deserve some sunshine. Let’s think. Have you tried asking Sarah if they have  any  other options, even if it’s not on their website? Sometimes they hold things back. I did. She said she’d check, but didn’t sound hopeful. She said the Algarve's incredibly popular with families this year, and anything with a sea view is snapped up instantly.

…and honestly, the delivery driver just left it on the doorstep! A brand new telescope, just  sitting  there. Anyone could’ve nicked it. Lincoln life, eh? Not exactly Fort Knox out there, is it? You expecting a meteor shower or something, lad? That’s a proper investment. Nah, not a shower. Just…clear nights. I've been reading about astrophotography. Proper nerdy, I know. It’s a bit of a distraction, to be honest. Uni’s been… intense. Distraction's good. You need 'em. Remember when you got obsessed with collecting bottle caps for, what, a month? Drove your mum mental. Okay, okay, low blow! That was different. This is…productive-ish. Anyway, did you see the football last night? City absolutely rinsed United. Haaland’s a machine, innit? I caught the highlights. Haaland  is  something else, proper goal-scoring animal. But you know I’m a Liverpool man through and through. Still reeling from that defeat against Tottenham, though. Klopp looked proper gutted. Ah, gutted is an understatement. Speaking of gutted, Mum was giving me an earful earlier about Auntie Carol. Apparently, she's convinced she saw Idris Elba at the supermarket. Idris Elba?! Carol and her celebrity sightings! Last week it was Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson buying bananas. She needs to lay off the sherry, that woman. Tell me about it. She was absolutely convinced. Said he winked at her. Honestly, it's more likely to have been a shopper who  looked  a bit like him. Likely is the operative word. How's work been, by the way? Still juggling all those spreadsheets and impossible deadlines? You have no idea. My manager, Sarah, is a whirlwind. She expects miracles, then gets annoyed when they happen too quickly. I swear she thrives on chaos. I'm thinking of applying for that internship at the observatory, though. It’s a long shot, but… Observatory internship? That’s brilliant! That ties in with the telescope then. Go for it, man. You're smart, you'll get it. Anything's better than being a spreadsheet slave, eh? Definitely. That’s what I'm thinking. It's just…scary, you know? Leaving the relative safety of a guaranteed job, even if it's soul-crushing. Scary is good. Scary means you’re stretching yourself. Remember when I left Barbados to come to England?  That  was scary. Leaving everything I knew behind, starting all over.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the clarity on this new screen. Nigel’s been fiddling with it all morning, bless ‘im. Makes you feel like you’re right here in the room, doesn’t it? Though a proper cuppa in person’s always best, mind. It  is  lovely, Arthur, truly. Much better than that grainy picture we had last month. And yes, a real biscuit with my tea is preferable! It’s just so good to  see  you both. Nigel’s well, is he? He seemed a bit off last time. He’s alright, Mum. A bit achy in the leg, the usual. The weather’s been playing havoc with it. He gets all…philosophical when it flares up, rambles on about the old days. Now, now, David, don’t you go making me sound like a dusty old relic! I just appreciate a bit of contemplation, that’s all. Reminds me of when I used to spend hours with that globe Grandad gave me. You remember that, Doreen? The one with all the raised bits? Oh,  that  globe! Yes! You used to trace your finger around it, pretending to sail to all sorts of exotic places. Remember when you were convinced Siam was made of chocolate? Did I really say that? Goodness me. Always had a sweet tooth, I suppose. We never  did  get to Siam, did we? Or anywhere much further than Blackpool, come to think of it. Blackpool was good, though! Remember building those sandcastles? And Dad nearly losing his wallet on the pier? Don't remind me! Spent half an hour searching, I did. Right, a right palaver. We talked about going to Yorkshire once, didn’t we, Doreen? You always said you wanted to see the Moors. We did. But then your leg started acting up, and we thought it would be too much. Walking the Moors isn't easy. We considered youth hostels, remember? Trying to be all adventurous. Adventurous! Me? I liked me comforts. Youth hostels… far too many shared bathrooms. No thank you. Still, I suppose it’s better than not travelling at all. I always thought it was a shame you weren’t able to do more of that sort of thing, David, with school. All those projects. It was alright. We did a project on the London Underground once. Had to draw out the whole system. Took weeks.

…and honestly, the website kept buffering! I was  this  close to just phoning up British Airways and getting someone to do it for me, but I thought, ‘No, you’re a graduate, you can handle booking two flights!’ Apparently not. Oh, relax, love. Websites are the devil. Especially when you’re trying to find a decent deal. Did you at least manage to get something sorted for Venice? Eventually. It took me nearly two hours. Two hours, I tell you! And it's not even a direct flight. We have to go through… Luton. Luton! Honestly, like adding insult to injury. Luton? Ugh. That's… optimistic. Still, Venice will be worth it, right? Imagine the gondolas, the little bridges… all that pasta. This is actually really good pasta, by the way. Did you make this from scratch? Nah, supermarket job. I’m a professional event planner, not a chef! Though I  could  plan a Venetian themed gala dinner… Hmm, idea. No, focus, focus. Venice. It's just… flying from Doncaster to Luton to Venice feels unnecessarily complicated. I could practically walk to Venice quicker. You and your walks! You’d need a passport for that one, wouldn’t you? Look, Luton is a pain, yeah, but it's cheaper, isn't it? You were moaning about the prices earlier. And honestly, you're from Yorkshire. You're practically built for airport transfers. You’re used to trekking. That's a low blow, Chloe. Just because I'm from Doncaster doesn’t mean I enjoy spending half a day in airports. And it wasn't  that  much cheaper. Fifteen quid. For the emotional distress, I think I deserve more than fifteen quid off. Fifteen quid is fifteen quid! I’m saving for that pottery class, remember? Every little helps. Besides, think of it as…pre-holiday adventure building. You and Gran will have a story to tell. Don't remind me about Gran. She's already started compiling a list of things she 'absolutely must see' which currently includes seventeen churches and a pigeon sanctuary. Seventeen churches? She's committed, I'll give her that. Is she packing her binoculars for the pigeons? Probably. And her walking boots. She's convinced she's going to climb the Campanile. I’ve warned her, but you know what she's like. Determined. She's a force of nature, your Gran. A lovely, church-visiting, pigeon-observing force of nature.

…and honestly, the price of a loaf of bread now! It’s criminal, I tell you. Criminal. When I started out, you could get a decent loaf for… well, I can’t even  remember  how much, it was so long ago. But it certainly wasn’t nearly three pounds! You’re sounding like Grandad, Arthur. It  is  expensive, though. I’ve started making my own. It’s surprisingly therapeutic, actually. And cheaper, obviously. Though the electricity bill… that’s another story. Therapeutic? Honestly, Emily? You’ve been teaching French for too long. Sounds like something you’d tell your students to cope with verb conjugations! I just switch to own brand. Does the job. Though the quality… well, you get what you pay for, don't you? Own brand’s not bad, Doreen. Not bad at all. Though I like a bit of Hovis, myself. A bit of tradition. Speaking of which, have either of you checked your pensions lately? I had a nasty shock. They’ve… adjusted something. Said it was to do with inflation, but it feels like they’ve taken more than they’ve given. I did, actually, just last week. And you’re right, Arthur. It's… minimal, the increase. They said roughly 3.1%, but with everything going up, it feels like a cut. Honestly, I'm thinking about going back to my bank and having a proper word. The customer service is appalling. Last time I called, I was on hold for forty minutes listening to dreadful music! Forty minutes? You’re lucky! I tried to dispute a charge on my card - a completely fraudulent transaction, someone using my details - and they put me through the robotic wringer for  hours . Kept saying “your call is important to us” while clearly demonstrating it wasn't. In the end, I had to go into the branch, and even then, it was a nightmare. The whole system feels rigged against us, doesn’t it? Rigged is the word. Banks used to be… well, they were reliable. You knew where you stood. Now it’s all algorithms and call centres in India. It makes my blood boil. I remember when Mr. Henderson at the local branch knew everyone by name. It's just so impersonal. And it’s not like you can threaten to take your business elsewhere, either. They all seem to be the same these days. Have you seen what Vodafone are charging now, Arthur?

… honestly, I just need a week where I don’t have to  think  about essays. Like, proper sunshine, clear blue skies… South Africa feels a million miles away right now, even though Mum and Dad still live there. I’m dreaming of braais and proper heat. What about you, Chloe? Any holiday plans bubbling? Ooh, South Africa sounds amazing, Anya! Jealous. I’m heading back to Bishop Auckland for a week with me mam and dad. Not exactly exotic, but it’ll be nice to just chill. Dad’s promised to make his famous Sunday roast – it’s the one thing that gets me through placement sometimes, honestly. And Mabel needs a good cuddle. Mabel? Is that a person, or…? No, Mabel’s me dog! She's a golden retriever. Absolute fluffball. She's the best at giving judgemental looks when I'm eating biscuits, you know, the "share with me" kind of look. Oh, a dog! I miss having a dog. We had a boerboel back home, massive thing, called Brutus. He was a gentle giant, though. Could nap for sixteen hours a day. What about you, Saoirse? Anything planned? Heading home to Ireland? I am, actually! I'm going back to County Clare next week. Me auntie has a little farm, loads of sheep, a few cows… it’s proper countryside. It’s not glamorous, but the air is just…different. And Auntie Bridie makes the best soda bread in the world. Trust me, it's life-changing. Forget your fancy breads, this is proper stuff. Oh, soda bread! I love a good soda bread. Though, nothing beats a warm Welsh cake with a bit of butter, does it? I'm going to Penarth to see me nan. She always has a stack waiting for me. She’s convinced I’m wasting away on hospital food, so she tries to fatten me up. Sounds like you’re in good hands, Rhiannon. I’m stuck here working extra shifts to save up for… well, I haven’t  decided  where to go yet. I’m thinking maybe a weekend in the Lake District? It's a bit closer to home - Hartlepool - and I could take Buster. Buster? Another dog! This flat's turning into a zoo! What is he? He's a staffie. A proper little character. Gets into  everything . But he's a cuddle monster. Needs a lot of walks, though, which is why the Lakes are appealing.

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels a bit… pointless, doesn’t it? Like, dedicating three years to writing essays about things nobody will remember in five minutes. Especially when I’m already picturing myself with a bad back and sensible shoes. Sensible shoes? You, Lyra? Never. Though I get what you mean about the essays. This Derrida bloke is actively trying to confuse me, I swear. But pointless? Bit harsh, isn’t it? It's building skills, innit? Critical thinking and all that jazz. That's what everyone  says . But what are we critically thinking  towards ? A lifetime of spreadsheets? I keep imagining us both, like, seventy, stuck in a retirement home arguing over bingo numbers. Real glamorous. Oi! I’ll have you know I’m a formidable bingo player. My nan taught me everything. And we won't be in a retirement home. We’ll be eccentric artists living in a rambling cottage somewhere. You, painting moody seascapes, me sculpting… well, I haven’t worked out the sculpting bit yet, but something artistic. Moody seascapes, huh? You reckon I’ve got it in me? All my attempts look like a toddler attacked a canvas with a particularly vibrant shade of blue. Remember that abstract piece I did last term? Professor Davies looked genuinely scared. He’s just got no vision, that's all. It was…bold. Intense. Anyway, that's why we need to actually  do  the art, not just think about doing the art. Got that life drawing class booked for next week? Yeah, Tuesday. I’m dreading it. Being stared at by a room full of art students whilst trying to look vaguely artistic is not my idea of fun. It’s terrifying! What about you? Still obsessed with building that virtual world? Obsessed is a strong word. Dedicated. I’m dedicated. I’ve nearly finished the market square. Trying to get the cobblestones to look  just  right is driving me insane, though. It’s all about the texture, see? And I'm adding NPCs with proper Scouse accents. Gotta represent. You are a menace. They’ll be selling stolen tellys and offering cut-price hair extensions within five minutes. But seriously, that sounds… amazing. So much more tangible than these essays. It feels like you're creating something real, even if it  is  only digital. Exactly! And think about it, in fifty years, people might be exploring  that  world, rather than reading about post-structuralism.

… honestly, I just don’t get why she keeps doing it. Every single time we go out, she has to one-up everyone's stories. It's exhausting! Right, Chloe and the competitive anecdotes. Still going strong then? I thought you’d managed to navigate around that. Navigate? It’s like navigating a minefield! Last night, Liam was telling a funny story about getting stuck in the rain, and she  immediately  jumped in with a tale about being caught in a monsoon in Thailand, nearly being swept away by a river… It felt deliberately dramatic. Oh, Chloe. She’s definitely a… character. Is it the attention thing, do you think? Or genuinely believing her life is more exciting? I honestly don’t know. I used to think it was just insecurity, but it feels more…pointed now. Like she actively  wants  to diminish other people’s experiences. Anyway, enough about Chloe’s need for validation. What are you making? Smells amazing in here. Just a quick lentil dahl. Needed something warming. Long day at work, you know how it is. Mr. Henderson was particularly…verbose today. Kept recounting his childhood in excruciating detail. Oh, bless him. He sounds like he needs a friend, not a nurse. Though I imagine listening to life stories is part of the job. It is, but some stories are…epic. He spent a good twenty minutes describing the precise shade of green of his grandmother’s garden fence. Anyway, distracting myself with lentils. You having a rough week too then, judging by the Chloe venting? It’s not just Chloe, actually. Work’s been a bit mental. Mr. Davies is breathing down everyone's necks about this new project deadline. It’s completely unrealistic, and he’s refusing to listen to any reason. I spent half the day collating data he  already  had access to. Classic Davies. Always needing to feel in control. You should tell him to get his head out of…well, you know. But realistically, you probably need to document  everything  and then subtly show him he was wasting everyone’s time. I’m trying! It's just draining. Honestly, sometimes I think about just giving it all up and opening a little bookstore. No deadlines, just books and quiet. That actually sounds lovely. You’d be brilliant at that. You always know exactly what book to recommend. Although, you'd probably end up with a regular customer who wants to debate the merits of Dickens for three hours.

…and honestly, Patricia, I still think the phrasing on section three is a bit leading. "Do you believe cultural sensitivity is paramount in international business?" Well,  of course  they do, or they wouldn't be signing up for this seminar, would they? It feels like we're nudging them towards a specific answer. Oh, come on, Brenda. It's just establishing a baseline understanding. We need to know their starting point. It’s a consent form, not an interrogation. It's about verifying they understand  why  cultural sensitivity matters before we delve into the practicalities. I’m with Patricia on this one, Brenda. It’s not necessarily about leading, it’s about the potential for response bias. People will say what they think you  want  to hear, especially in an academic setting. It skews the data, even if it’s just for our internal assessment. Should we maybe rephrase it to something like, “How important do you consider cultural sensitivity to be in international business?” with a scale? Aye, that’s better, Sarah. A scale’s much more sensible. “Very important, important, neutral, unimportant, very unimportant.” Something like that. Less…judgmental, like. I just worry about the ethics of it all. We’re academics, we need to be rigorous, even with a little consent form. Remember Professor Armitage and the debacle with the student surveys? Oh, don’t even mention Armitage. That was a mess. And a complete overreaction by the university, if you ask me. But fine, a scale is a good compromise. We can change it. Anything else bothering you about the form, Brenda? Let’s get this sorted. The Vice Dean's breathing down our necks about getting everything finalised. Just the data protection bit. Is it clear enough that their responses are confidential and only for the purpose of improving the seminar? I've had students in the past get twitchy about that sort of thing. I reviewed that section, Brenda. It specifically mentions anonymisation and data storage protocols. It's pretty standard, complies with all the GDPR regulations. I even added a line about data destruction after six months. Good, good. Right. Form's…mostly sorted then. Now, the seminar itself. I've been thinking about the structure. I was envisioning starting with a broad overview of Hofstede’s cultural dimensions, then moving onto more specific communication challenges. That sounds reasonable. I think we need to emphasize the practical application though.

…and honestly, the student feedback was brutal. Brutal, Daniel. Apparently, my enthusiasm for post-structuralism is ‘intimidating’ and my lectures are ‘too dense’. Can you  believe  that? Intimidating enthusiasm? That’s a new one. Sounds like they just don’t want to work, love. It’s always easier to blame the lecturer than to actually engage with the material. Which university are we even passing now? Everything looks the same here. This is Tsinghua, actually. We’re cutting through the back routes to avoid the main traffic. And it’s not that they don’t  want  to work, it’s just… the cultural difference, I suppose. They’re so used to being spoon-fed information. I want them to  think ! It’s infuriating. I spent six years doing a PhD, I’m hardly going to dumb things down. I get it. My lot aren’t much better, to be fair. They’re just… quieter about their complaints. More polite. Still don't understand why I need to explain basic econometric modelling three times in one lecture. Worse, though, is the admin. They’ve changed the grant application process  again . It’s a complete farce. Oh, don't even get me started on admin. It’s the bane of my existence. It's like they actively try to make everything more complicated. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I made the right decision coming here. It’s amazing, the opportunity, the research… but the bureaucracy… We both knew it wouldn't be all noodles and academic freedom. Remember all that research  we  did before we committed? Still, it is tiring, isn't it? Especially with… the house situation. Don’t remind me. Mrs. Chen is convinced that installing more gold trim will somehow increase the flat’s value. Gold trim, Daniel! It looks like something out of a… a slightly garish palace. And she keeps offering me tea with what I suspect is a truly alarming amount of sugar. She means well. It's just… her sense of aesthetics is… different. And the entire building smells perpetually of incense and something vaguely medicinal. Medicinal is putting it mildly. It smells like a pharmacy exploded. And the noise! The constant stream of mahjong tiles clacking… It’s charming, in a way, but also incredibly distracting when I'm trying to mark essays. I'm starting to think we should have pushed for something a little further out, even if it meant a longer commute.

… honestly, I just feel awful throwing away perfectly good broccoli stalks. Gran would have made soup with those. Everything was used. Nothing wasted. Remember how she used to pickle everything? Even the beetroot leaves! Oh god, the beetroot. The whole house smelled of it for weeks after she’d done a pickling session. It wasn't a  bad  smell, just… pervasive. Though, she was right about not wasting things. It feels almost offensive now, with how much food gets chucked. This lasagne is amazing, by the way. Did you use that ricotta from the farmer’s market? I did! It made all the difference. And yes, Gran’s philosophy is definitely rubbing off on me. I was watching that documentary about food waste last night, and it’s horrifying. We’re so disconnected from where our food comes from. It’s all neatly packaged in plastic at the supermarket… speaking of which, the 5p charge for plastic bags actually  does  make a difference, doesn’t it? I find myself remembering them now. It does, a small one. Though I still see people just buying a new one every time. It’s frustrating. It's like they haven’t grasped the concept. Speaking of things needing a shake-up, have you seen the latest series of ‘Severance’ on Apple TV? Completely mind-bending. They’re exploring the whole idea of work-life balance, or rather, the complete lack of it, in a really unsettling way. No, not yet. It's on my list! Everyone’s raving about it. It sounds a bit… intense though? I've been re-watching ‘Great British Bake Off’ for comfort. Pure escapism.
