Anyway, back to more serious things… I was talking to a Year 10 student today about careers, and he wants to be an engineer, like you. But he's worried about finding work experience. Everything feels so… ‘closed’ off. That’s a common problem. A lot of industries are still gatekept. It's easier if you know someone. I was lucky, Dad knew a guy at the power station. But even then, it was competitive. Honestly, I think schools need to do a better job of forging links with private companies. They’re the ones with the resources, you know? It's not fair that some kids are starting the race already miles ahead. Exactly! And it’s not just engineering. It's everything. Then they wonder why there's a skills gap.

…and honestly, the funding application just feels like shouting into the void. Three months of work, meticulously crafting every sentence, justifying every methodological choice… and for what? A polite ‘thank you, but no’ email. Oh,  don’t  start. You say that every time, and then six months later you're beaming about a new grant. It’s your dramatic flair, darling. Though, I do sympathise. It’s the same with Ofsted reports. Hours poured into preparing, then someone comes in for a day and decides the future of the whole school based on… well, who knows what sometimes? It’s not flair! It’s… frustration. It's the principle! They ask for innovative approaches, then penalise you for anything that deviates from well-trodden paths. It's completely paradoxical. Did I mention Professor Davies wants me to re-analyse the data using a completely different statistical method? He thinks the initial findings aren’t ‘significant’ enough. Davies, eh? Always a joy. What's he suggesting? A t-test when a MANOVA would be far more appropriate? He has a habit of that, doesn't he? Worse. He wants me to run a regression analysis, claiming it will ‘reveal hidden correlations’. It’s practically data dredging! And it will completely undermine the original research question. I feel like I’m being asked to… fabricate something. Right, that’s… ethically challenging. Have you explained that to him? Gently, of course. Trying to reason with Davies is like negotiating with a particularly stubborn toddler. I tried. He just brushed it off with a ‘trust me, I’ve been doing this for thirty years’. Thirty years of potentially flawed methodology, more like. Ugh. How was your day? Anything less infuriating happening at work? Comparatively peaceful, actually. We had a mock Ofsted inspection. It wasn’t the real thing, thankfully, but it helped iron out some wrinkles. Turns out, the new reporting software is even more clunky than we feared. Spent most of the afternoon battling spreadsheets. Spreadsheets. The nemesis of modern existence. At least no one’s asking you to fabricate data. True. Though some of the data  is  a little…optimistic. A few teachers are overly generous with their self-assessments. I have to gently nudge them towards realism. It's basically diplomatic data adjustment. Diplomatic data adjustment. I like that. Sounds far less sinister than what Davies is suggesting. How are your mum and dad doing, by the way?

…and honestly, Doreen, it’s just the grey. Everything’s grey. Not just the sky, mind you – though it  is  a bit drizzly today - but in here, too. Feels like it’s seeped into the walls. Even the telly isn’t cheering me up, and you know I can watch anything. Oh, Arthur. I know, dear. It  is  grey. It’s February, after all. Though I do think you’re letting it get to you a bit more than usual. Remember that week we had in Cromer last August? Proper sunshine, that was. You were like a different man, skipping along the beach like a boy. Speaking of Cromer, Arthur, you were telling me last week about that lovely little house you spotted there. The one with the blue shutters? Still thinking about it? Thinking about it? What’s the point of thinking about it, David? It’s a pipe dream. A nice little place, close to the sea… costs a fortune. More than a fortune, probably. And even if I  could  somehow magic up the money, what good would it do? Just a different four walls to feel sorry in. Now, now, don’t talk like that. David’s right to ask. Sometimes just  having  something to look forward to, even a distant possibility, can make a difference. Remember when we were saving for that little trip to Spain? Even the scrimping and saving felt…positive. It's understandable you're feeling low, Arthur. It's been a tough few months. Losing Margaret... and then with the issues with the benefits… it’s a lot to take on. And you’ve never been one to readily ask for help, have you? Help? Who’s going to help? The government? They seem determined to make life as difficult as possible. And as for family… well, they’ve all got their own lives, haven’t they? Can't blame 'em. That’s not fair, Arthur. Your granddaughter, Emily, called just last week. She was very concerned. And your son, Peter, he’s always offering. You just brush him off. He means well, Peter does. But he doesn't understand. He's got his fancy job, his nice house…he doesn't know what it's like to just… be  without a purpose. Not anymore. Used to enjoy my garden, you know. Even a bit of bird watching. You were telling me about the blue tits nesting in your apple tree.

…and honestly, the difference is  night and day . I used to spend ages trying to curl my hair, and it would just…flop. This stuff, though, honestly, holds it all day, even in this humidity. You wouldn’t believe. Wow, seriously? Because mine is just… hopeless. I tried one of those heated rollers last week, saw an ad online, looked amazing on the woman in the video. Disaster. Just gave me weird kinks and didn’t hold  anything . Oh, heated rollers. They're a minefield, aren’t they? I think it really depends on your hair type. Mine’s quite fine, so the heat just… doesn’t really take. What about you? Is yours thick, or thin? It's… a bit of both, actually? Thick at the roots, really stubborn, then kinda gets thinner towards the ends. And frizzy. Always frizzy. That’s why I was hoping the rollers might work. I was aiming for that bouncy, 40s Hollywood wave look. Ended up looking like I’d had a fight with a sheep. Oh, no! Right, okay, stubborn roots and frizz… this stuff is a mousse, so it gives a really good hold  at  the root, you see? And it’s not sticky. It’s one of those airy ones. Let me show you. It’s called ‘Cloud Volume’ – completely ridiculous name, I know, but it actually delivers. Cloud Volume? Sounds… optimistic. Is it expensive? I’m a bit strapped this month, what with little Alfie needing new trainers and everything. Not  terribly  expensive, about a tenner from Boots. And a little goes a long way. I’ve had this bottle for ages. Actually, speaking of Boots, did you manage to get that new foundation I told you about? The one with the hyaluronic acid? Oh, the one for dry skin? No, they were completely out of my shade. The girl at the counter said they’d had a massive rush on it because some influencer recommended it on TikTok. Honestly, it's ridiculous the power those people have. It  is  mental, isn't it? You'd think people would try things for themselves. But yeah, that foundation is amazing. It actually feels hydrating, not like you’re covering your face in plaster. I'll keep an eye out when I'm next in. I'm going Saturday for shampoo. You're a lifesaver. I'm thinking of trying nail varnish again.

… honestly, the parking situation around the Walker Art Gallery is mental, isn’t it? I was trying to take a class there last week, showing them some of the Pre-Raphaelites, and nearly had a breakdown just  finding  a space. Ended up ten minutes walk away. Ten minutes! In November! Tell me about it. Tried to get to the Tate last month. Forgot about football at Anfield. Absolute chaos. You’d have had more luck finding a unicorn. How were the kids, though? Did they actually  get  the Pre-Raphaelites or were they mostly scrolling on their phones? Surprisingly engaged, actually! A few were a bit “what’s the point of all this flowery stuff?” but once I started talking about the symbolism, the stories behind the paintings… they perked up. It’s the storytelling aspect, isn’t it? They connect to that. Anyway, enough about work. How’s things with young Liam? Still causing mayhem? Mayhem is an understatement. He’s decided he’s a dinosaur. Roaring, stomping, demanding “leaves” for his nest… which means scattering my houseplants everywhere. It’s exhausting but, you know, adorable. It’s just… different, now he's properly mobile. Speaking of exhausting, how’s the interview prep going for your Masters? You sounded stressed last time we spoke. It’s… looming. It's next week. I’m revising like mad. All those theories about second language acquisition… it’s a lot to cram. I’m worried about the practical bit, you know, the teaching demo? I can explain the concepts, I just don’t want to look like a proper idiot actually  doing  it. And it’s expensive, isn’t it? Even if I get in, the fees are… substantial. You'll be brilliant, honestly. You’re a natural teacher. Everyone says so. And yeah, the fees are ridiculous. I’m looking at doing some extra bits at work, trying to pick up some supervisory hours. Gotta boost the income somehow. We're still saving for the house, and it’s moving at a glacial pace. Saving… that’s the dream, innit? Everything costs a fortune these days. We’re trying to put a bit away for Christmas, but it feels hopeless. My Nan keeps asking what I want. I haven’t a clue. Honestly, just a quiet Christmas with a few beers down the pub would be ideal. What about you? Any present ideas for Liam?

…and honestly, the whole thing with Mark’s son, Leo, refusing to even  look  at the Christmas present I got him… it just felt… pointed. Like I'm deliberately trying to replace his mum, which, honestly, isn't the goal at all. It's exhausting, this tiptoeing. Oh, darling, that sounds awful. Leo’s still massively processing everything, isn't he? It’s only been just over a year since his mum and Mark separated. A year isn't long for a child, especially not one who was very close to her. Don’t take it personally, even though it  feels  personal. It absolutely does, I know. I  know  rationally, you’re right. Mark says the same thing. But rationally doesn’t stop the little stab of hurt, does it? Especially when you’ve spent ages trying to find something you think he’d genuinely like. I got him that astronomy kit, remember? He’s been talking about space for months. You did! That was a lovely idea. He’s a sensitive little boy, though. Mark always said so. He's probably just… wary of new things, new people stepping into that role. It's hard for them. Easier for us, observing it all. Easier for us, definitely. You’ve navigated this before, haven't you? With Daniel and his kids, even though that was a different dynamic. You always seem to have such a calm perspective. Calm on the surface, maybe. Beneath it, I was a mess! Honestly, those first few years with Daniel’s two… chaotic doesn’t even begin to cover it. And it wasn’t like this. With Leo, you’ve got Mark actively wanting you to be part of his son’s life, which is a huge difference. With Daniel, well, let's just say his ex wasn’t keen on me being anywhere near her children. Constant battles. Right. That sounds… draining. This feels more subtle, and in some ways, harder because of that. It's the unspoken things, the little rejections. I just want Leo to know I’m not trying to  be  his mum. I want him to feel comfortable around me, you know? Of course. And it will take time. It genuinely will. It's not a quick fix. You’re putting pressure on yourself, trying to force a connection, which will only make it worse. Let him come to you. Focus on just being… a supportive adult in his life.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of that contestant on ‘Great British Bake Off’ to claim a soggy bottom was a 'deliberate textural choice’! Deliberate! It was a disaster, Mark. A sticky, floury disaster. Oh, you’re still on about that? I thought you’d have moved past Prue Leith’s disappointed face by now. You get  so  invested in that show. Invested? It’s a national treasure! And she looked genuinely horrified. Anyway, it’s better than scrolling through Pinterest all day, isn’t it? You’ve been glued to that thing since… well, since Sarah mentioned planning her hen do. Hey, Pinterest is research! Serious research! Sarah wants a ‘rustic whimsical’ vibe. Which apparently means fairy lights, bunting made of hessian, and floral crowns. All things readily available… on Pinterest. Right. And you’re volunteering to  make  the bunting, aren't you? Because your crafting skills are legendary. I said I’d  look into  it. There are tutorials. And Etsy exists. It’s about options, Liv. Options! Speaking of things needing planning, have you thought about what you’re getting your mum for her birthday? It’s next month already, isn't it? Don't remind me! It's always tricky. She says she doesn't  want  anything, which is a blatant lie. Last year’s 'I don't need a thing' led to a detailed list the size of my arm. Remember the garden gnome saga? Oh god, yes. The one that looked suspiciously like a slightly disgruntled Winston Churchill? She was determined to find a place for it. Ended up guarding the compost heap, didn’t it? It did. And she named it Reginald. She genuinely talks to Reginald. I'm thinking a nice experience this year. Maybe a weekend away? Somewhere… not gnome-related. That's a good shout. She’d like that. Have you asked Dad for input? He usually has some devious plan involving a caravan and a coastal walk. Don’t even  go  there. He's already hinting at 'a surprise adventure'. I suspect it involves wellies and questionable seafood. Honestly, they're like a couple of mischievous teenagers sometimes. They are. They've clearly realised retirement means embracing chaos. Have you heard from Ben lately? I haven’t seen him since that awful pub quiz last week. He was so gutted about losing. He texted me earlier. He’s buried under coursework, apparently.

…No, that one's awful. Honestly, it looks like something out of a dentist's waiting room. All chrome and… pointy bits. Definitely not the 'cosy farmhouse' vibe we're going for. You’re ruthless. I thought it was…functional. Though you’re right, ‘cosy farmhouse’ and ‘chrome pointy bits’ don’t exactly gel. Still, we're getting somewhere. We've ruled out anything aggressively modern. How about this one? The brass one with the frosted glass? Mmm, better. Much better. It’s a bit…safe though, isn't it? Doesn’t really  say  anything. It’s just…there. We need something with a bit of character. Remember that one we saw in that little antique shop in Rye? The iron one with the coloured glass panels? Vaguely. Wasn't that ridiculously expensive? And a bit wonky? I remember you saying it would require a structural engineer to hang. Details, details. It had  soul . Anyway, let's keep looking on eBay. There’s bound to be something. Oh! This one's interesting. A vintage schoolhouse pendant. What do you think? Actually, I quite like that. It’s…unexpected. And it wouldn’t clash with anything. Is it…reasonably priced? eBay can be a minefield. Seems to be. And the seller’s got good feedback. We could get a couple of those for the kitchen island? Maybe. We should probably get back to the more pressing issue, though. These light fittings are distracting us from the real task at hand: finding somewhere to  put  them. Have you had a proper look at Rightmove this evening? Yes, and I’m starting to feel even more defeated than I did this morning. Everything's either a tiny cottage that needs a complete overhaul, or a huge, soulless new build that costs a fortune. And the gardens! Everyone wants a garden the size of a football pitch, apparently. I know, it’s frustrating. We just want somewhere with a bit of space, a decent kitchen, and a garden big enough for a vegetable patch and maybe a couple of chickens. Is that too much to ask? Apparently. Look at this one. Near Market Harborough. Four bedrooms, detached, pretty garden… but have you seen the price? It’s ridiculous! And look at the kitchen. Beige. Just… endless beige. Beige is the enemy. Absolutely the enemy. Let's widen the search radius a bit. Maybe Rutland? It’s a bit further, but slightly more affordable.

…and honestly, the state of the communal bathroom at the hospital is just  dreadful . It's like a biohazard zone half the time. You wouldn't believe the things I’ve seen. Oh, bless you, Sarah. Still dealing with that, then? I thought they promised to renovate it, what, six months ago? Promised is doing a lot of heavy lifting, Lynn. They talked about it. There were memos. Someone did a walk-through with a clipboard. And then…nothing. It’s the same cracked tiles and leaky faucets. Honestly, I’m starting to bring my own disinfectant wipes. Eww, seriously? That sounds awful. I’m glad I chose to do home care. Old Mrs. Higgins’ bathroom is spotless, though she does make me wear gloves when I clean the loo, says I’ll “catch something dreadful”. She’s a character. Oh, bless her! Old people are the best, aren’t they? Full of wisdom and…particular habits. How is she doing, actually? Still complaining about the postman? Always! Says he looks shifty. Honestly, he’s a lovely lad, brings her little chocolates sometimes. She just likes a grumble. She keeps asking about Mum, though. Remember how Mum used to take her shopping? Oh, yes. Mum loved a shopping trip with Mrs. Higgins. Always ended up coming home with half a charity shop’s stock, didn’t it? She had a good heart. She did. Speaking of good hearts, how’s the job hunt going, Chloe? Any luck with those care positions in Tunbridge Wells? Not brilliant, to be honest. I’ve had a few interviews, but nothing concrete yet. They all seem to want experience with dementia care, and while I’ve done some training, it’s not the same as having had it hands-on, you know? It’s a tough one. They always want experience, but how do you get experience without…getting experience? I remember that when I first qualified. It’s a catch-22. It is. Perhaps look at agencies, Chloe? They sometimes take on people with less direct experience and offer more support. Plus, you get a variety of placements, so you build your skills up quickly. That’s a good shout, Sarah. I've been avoiding them, thinking they pay less, but I've been looking for so long now, I'm willing to consider anything. Don't dismiss them out of hand. Some are really good.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just a bit embarrassing. Wandering around Rome, looking for the Colosseum, and ending up… well, near a laundrette. Twice. It wasn’t exactly romantic sightseeing. Oh, darling, you and directions. It’s a running theme, isn’t it? Rome, Edinburgh, even Cambridge sometimes! Though to be fair, Cambridge  is  designed to confuse. All those little lanes… Hey! I found this place, didn’t I? Admittedly, after asking three people and consulting Google Maps for an hour, but I  found  it. And look, speaking of finding things… did you read that article I sent you about sleep? The one on chronotypes? The lion, bear, wolf thing? Yes! Fascinating. Apparently, I’m a solid bear. Needs a regular schedule, gets grumpy if disrupted. Sounds about right, doesn't it? Where do you fall? Definitely a wolf. I thrive on chaos, late nights, and then I just… crash. Which is probably why I'm perpetually tired. The article said bears shouldn’t even  try  to be wolves. We’re fighting our natural rhythms. So, less late-night strategising for your next business venture and more early nights? Good luck with  that . Though honestly, the ‘shut down your screens an hour before bed’ thing… I’m trying, I really am. It’s hard! It is. I’ve been using that blue light filter, which helps a little. But I was thinking… you know how we were talking about getting away this summer? I had an idea. Camping. Camping? Seriously? After the Rome debacle, you want to entrust our weekend to your navigational skills in the  wilderness ? Come on! It'll be fun! Proper stargazing, campfires… and I promise, I’ll download offline maps. Triple-check the route. We can go somewhere relatively tame – the New Forest, maybe? I was reading about a campsite there… The New Forest…hmm. That does sound rather nice. As long as you promise me a reasonably flat pitch and palatable coffee. And no getting lost chasing badgers. Deal. Flat pitch, excellent coffee, badger-avoidance guaranteed. Although, speaking of navigation… it reminded me of old man Hemmings, the pilot from Wellington. Remember him? Vaguely. The one who flew those little Cessna planes? The one you used to beg him to take you up in? That’s the one. Always had a story. One time, he told me he got completely disoriented in fog over the Tararua Ranges.

…and honestly, the audacity of him to  bury  sunflower seeds in my sock. A SOCK, Elsie! Like, what was going through his tiny hamster brain? Oh, Barnaby! He sounds a menace. Honestly, they’re all little hoarders, aren’t they? My Winston tried to stuff his cheeks with fluff from the rug yesterday. It was… a look. You think  that’s  bad? Colin tried to build a nest in my hair while I was revising. A  nest . I had to bribe him with a yoghurt drop to get him out. It was a nightmare. Honestly, I’m starting to question my life choices that lead to hamster ownership. You all are just soft. Hamsters are meant to test your patience. Mine, Brenda, just runs on her wheel for twelve hours straight, then sleeps for five minutes and starts again. It's hypnotic, actually. Hypnotic? Sounds exhausting. Barnaby just wants to dismantle everything I own and rearrange it according to his own chaotic logic. It's like living with a tiny, furry anarchist. He also seems to have a vendetta against anything ginger. Against ginger? What do you mean? Like, if I’m eating a ginger biscuit, he’ll actively avoid the cage. Or if I’m wearing anything orange, he stares. It’s proper judgemental. That’s… weirdly specific. Maybe he had a bad experience with a ginger cat? Or someone who smells of ginger? Maybe he's just got taste. Gingers  are  a bit suspect, aren’t they? Joking! Joking! Don’t come at me, ginger friends. Oh, here we go. Don’t start, Chloe. You and your ginger prejudice. My cousin’s a ginger, and he's lovely. He makes amazing sourdough bread. I didn't say anything  against  them! Just… statistically… less melanin… slightly more prone to sunburn… Okay, okay, I'll stop. It's a running joke. It’s just… growing up in Sunderland, you hear a lot of things. Right, well Barnaby clearly got the memo. He won't even  look  at my ginger stationery. I bought a lovely orange pen, and he just turned his back on the cage. It's personal, I tell you. Maybe he's colour blind? I read somewhere hamsters don’t see red very well. So orange might just look… grey and boring to him. That's actually a good point, Ella. It might not be prejudice, it might be a visual impairment!

Right, I’m reinforcing Kamchatka. Honestly, this is a nightmare. Every time I think I’ve got Australia locked down, someone decides to invade. Dad, you  specifically  said you wouldn't attack me there. Didn’t say I wouldn’t  think  about attacking you there, did I? Strategic ambiguity, lad. That’s the key to Risk. Besides, Carol was egging me on. Said you were getting too comfortable. I just suggested a little…rebalancing. You were hoarding troops. It’s not fair to the rest of us. And honestly, looking at this map… Is that supposed to be Siam? You always call it Siam. It’s Thailand now, you know. It's  always  been Siam to me! It just…sounds right. Like calling Liverpool “Liver-pool.” You wouldn’t, would you? And rebalancing? You're allied with Dad, you're practically giving him cards! Now, now, don’t go accusing anyone of collusion. It’s all about tactical alliances. Speaking of which, this new update to the game is rubbish. They’ve nerfed the cavalry. Remember when cavalry were  feared ? Proper Genghis Khan stuff. Now they’re just…slightly faster infantry. I agree. The last version was better. Though, I must say, I’m enjoying the chocolate biscuits. Did you get those from that little bakery on Mill Street, Jamie? They have the best ones. Yeah, Mrs. Higgins made them. She remembers all my childhood misdemeanours, though. “Oh, Jamie, still causing trouble, I see!” It’s exhausting. It’s like she’s filing a permanent report. She’s a lovely woman. You should appreciate being remembered. I’m forgetting where I put my glasses every five minutes these days. It's…distressing. You had them on your head five minutes ago, Dad. Okay, moving on from family history and failing eyesight… anyone fancy a drink? It’s been a  long  game. Just a small glass of wine, thank you. Though, I'm starting to wonder if this game is some sort of elaborate psychological test. All this aggression… Aggression? It’s strategy, Carol! Pure, unadulterated strategy! Though, I did hear Aaron's wife is expecting. Really? Aaron? Wow. That’s…unexpected. Last I heard, they were pretty firm about not wanting kids. People change. It's…a complicated thing. I remember when Sarah was deciding…it was a huge weight. All the ethics, the practicalities… And then there's the whole discussion around choices, faith in doctors, even considering things like Chinese medicine… it's a lot.

…and honestly, the whole archaeology thing is just… fizzling out, innit? Like, I  thought  it was what I wanted, digging up bits of pottery and pretending I was Indiana Jones, but it’s mostly just mud and paperwork. And Professor Davies keeps going on about stratigraphy like it’s the most exciting thing in the world. Stratigraphy? Sounds thrilling. Honestly, you always did have a romantic view of everything. Remember when you wanted to be a marine biologist  just  to swim with dolphins? Hey! That’s different. Dolphins are majestic. Pottery shards are just… broken bits of things people chucked away. It feels a bit pointless, doesn’t it? What are  you  feeling about law, anyway? Still convinced you're going to be the next Amal Clooney? Please. Amal Clooney has a team of people doing all the grunt work. I’m starting to suspect everyone here just picked law because their parents told them it was ‘sensible’. It’s… a lot of reading. And the tutorials are terrifying. Old Mr. Henderson just  loves  to corner you with a question about tort law. Oh god, sounds awful. So, we’re both adrift in a sea of sensible career choices we regret? Wonderful. Maybe we should have both gone to drama school. We could've been famous. I reckon I could’ve pulled off a pretty convincing Keira Knightley, you know, with a bit of effort. You and Keira Knightley? You're more…Rosamund Pike, maybe? All sharp angles and mysterious vibes. And I’d be… I dunno, maybe someone’s slightly sarcastic sidekick. Definitely not the leading lady. Although, imagine us on a red carpet. ‘Two Northern and Southern Girls Take Hollywood!’ I like the sound of that. Though, honestly, the thought of all that attention is exhausting. Makes me want to just… buy a cottage in Cornwall and raise chickens. Chickens? Seriously? You’re going from Indiana Jones to… poultry farming? Don’t judge! It's peaceful! No one asks you about stratigraphy when you're collecting eggs. Plus, think of the fresh eggs! And maybe a goat. Old MacDonald’s is the life for me. Honestly, you're all over the place. Have you thought about, like, actually talking to someone about this? A career advisor? They might have something useful. Ugh, career advisors. They always suggest things like actuarial science. It's just… depressing. And then they start asking about five-year plans

…and then Mr. Davies just  looked  at me, right? Like I’d insulted his mother or something, just because I asked why we were learning about the War of the Roses  again . Honestly, it’s like he thinks history stopped happening after 1487. Tell me about it. He's obsessed. I swear, if I have to write another essay on Richard III, I’m going to scream. At least yours is vaguely interesting. We're doing the economic impact of the Industrial Revolution. Which, okay, important, but dry as dust. Yeah, that sounds…enthusiastically boring. We’re supposed to be doing a project on modern social issues, though. That's the bit I'm stressing about. We have to  research  something and propose a solution. It feels massive. Massive is an understatement. Liam and I are thinking about homelessness. It's pretty visible around Wembley, you know? Makes you think. That’s…heavy. Good, though. A proper issue. I was thinking something like consumerism, but it feels a bit…fluffy? Like, yeah, we buy too much stuff, so what? It doesn't feel urgent like people being on the streets. It’s not fluffy, it’s connected, though, isn’t it? All that advertising, the pressure to have the latest trainers or phone… it’s all part of a system where some people have way too much and others have nothing. It’s all interwoven. My Nan always says, "Waste not, want not." She grew up during the war, so she's seen proper hardship. My grandad was in the war too. He doesn’t talk about it much. Just says it was ‘rough’. It’s weird, isn't it? People thinking about rationing and everything, and now we’ve got food banks. It feels backwards. Completely. And the government just…talks about statistics. Like real people aren’t behind those numbers. It gets me proper wound up. My older brother was going on about politics last night – all about tax cuts for the rich and trickle-down economics… it just felt so detached from reality. Ugh, don’t even get me started. My dad tries to explain it, he's always reading the news, but it still feels like they're speaking another language. It’s all so…manipulative. Plus, half the stuff is just soundbites designed to rile people up. Exactly! It's exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, did you see Ben today?

…and honestly, the whole recording process was a nightmare. Trying to get a decent vocal take when Mr. Henderson next door decides 3 PM on a Tuesday is the perfect time to practice his tuba? It’s beyond belief. He  knows  I do voiceover work! Oh,  him . That man is a menace. Seriously, isn't there some sort of noise ordinance? It's not like it’s a refined hobby, is it? It’s just…  oompah . Exactly!  Oompah  doesn’t sell financial products, darling. It really doesn’t. I had to edit around three particularly enthusiastic bursts. It added hours to the work. Anyway, how are  you  doing? Beyond dealing with the tuba-playing terror, that is. Have you managed to get out at all this week? Not really. Honestly, my knee’s been killing me. I did try to walk to the shops yesterday, and I regretted it instantly. It felt like someone was stabbing it with a rusty spoon. Oh, love. Is it still the same knee? Have you been doing your physiotherapy? You promised you would. I  tried . But it’s so…boring. And honestly, it hurts more  during  the exercises than just, you know, existing. I just end up lying on the sofa feeling sorry for myself. That's counterproductive, though, isn’t it? You need to strengthen it. It’s likely that bad joints are causing the problem, and a bit of effort now will save you a lot of pain later. I have terrible wrists, you know. All that typing over the years. I'm practically held together by elastic bands. See, that’s what I mean! Everything hurts as you get older. It’s depressing! And then people are always going on about diets. Honestly, I saw a woman at the supermarket – she was practically skin and bones – lecturing a teenager about eating a biscuit. It was appalling. Oh, the judgement! It’s relentless. Are you thinking about trying anything new, food-wise? I’ve been experimenting with that Mediterranean diet. Lots of fish, olive oil… trying to avoid the carbohydrates, though that’s proving difficult. I don't know. I just want to eat something comforting. Like, a really big lasagne. Or a whole chocolate cake. Actually, now you’ve said cake, I really want cake. That's the trouble with talking about food, isn’t it? It just makes you hungrier. Speaking of which, I’m planning on making a shepherd's pie later.

…and honestly, the catering company tried to tell me lavender was “on-trend” for a  construction  conference. Lavender! Like, are they expecting a field of wildflowers to grow out of the concrete? It was a right laugh trying to explain why builders are more interested in a solid bacon butty than a floral infusion. Oh, bless ‘em. Some people just live on a different planet, don't they? Lavender. Seriously. You’d think after coordinating events for a year, they’d have  some  idea of your audience. This smells amazing, by the way. Is that rosemary in there? Aye, it is. Mam always said a little rosemary sorts everything out. And yeah, you'd think so, wouldn’t ya? It’s not like I asked for anything extravagant, just… sensible. They pitched me a whole thing about ‘deconstructed sandwiches’.  Deconstructed . Who wants to build their own sandwich at a networking event? You just want to eat and talk, not play Lego with ham. Deconstructed sandwiches. That's… avant-garde. You're a marvel for keeping your cool. I’d have told them to pack their lavender and their disassembled bread and just leave. Though, let’s be fair, my patience rarely stretches that far. Remember that time I had to explain to a supplier that “ASAP” doesn’t actually mean ‘whenever you feel like it’? Oh god, yes! The saga of the delayed labels. You were practically seeing red! Did you ever get those sorted? It felt like it was hanging over you for weeks. Eventually. After a strongly worded email and a threat to go elsewhere. People just don’t appreciate deadlines anymore, do they? It's like they think production just magically  happens . It's all well and good having a Masters, but it doesn't teach you how to herd cats, that's what I say. Speaking of which, how  is  the house hunt going? Still scouring Cambridge? Slow. Really slow. Everything’s either ridiculously small, falling apart, or costs more than a small country. Honestly, I’m starting to think I’ll be living in my childhood bedroom forever. It’s not awful, mind, Mam keeps it spotless, but… I need some space. And definitely need to escape the constant questioning about when I’m settling down and giving her grandkids. Tell me about it. My nan's the same. Every family gathering it’s “So, Chloe, any nice young men then?”

…and honestly, the cinematography was just  chef’s kiss . Like, every shot felt deliberate, you know? Not just pretty, but actually  saying  something. Ooh, which film are we dissecting now, Liv? You get so into this stuff. Was it that weird French one you were on about last week? The black and white one with, like, no dialogue? No, no! That was…an experience. This is ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’. Seriously, you  have  to see it. It’s bonkers. Michelle Yeoh is incredible. ‘Everything Everywhere’? Sounds…intense. I’m more of a straightforward action kinda guy, to be honest. Give me a good Liam Neeson film any day. The Taken franchise? Pure class. Oh, Liam Neeson is your go-to, is he, Ben? Predictable! Although, I can’t deny a bit of ‘Taken’ is good mindless fun. But Liv’s right, 'Everything Everywhere’ is genuinely brilliant. It’s chaotic, emotional, hilarious… it's a lot. Oh my God, I  loved  that film! Seriously. I watched it like three times in a week. The hot dog fingers bit? Iconic. It made me cry, though. Properly sob. See?! Chloe gets it! It's not just about the hot dog fingers, although they  are  amazing. It’s about family, and regret, and…everything. It's deep, man. I’ve heard good things, to be fair. It's been on my watchlist forever. I just keep getting distracted by all the prestige dramas. I’ve been ploughing through ‘Succession’ again. That family is… something else. Utterly awful people, but you just can’t look away. ‘Succession’ is amazing! The writing is just razor sharp. But a three-hour multiverse-hopping film sounds… exhausting. I need something a bit lighter after Uni deadlines. Any recommendations for something less… existential? Honestly? ‘Dungeons and Dragons: Honour Among Thieves’. Proper laugh. Loads of fun. Chris Pine is brilliant in it. It's not gonna win any Oscars, but it's a good time. Oh yeah, that was surprisingly good! I went in expecting total cheesy nonsense, and it was genuinely witty. And the creature design was great. Oooh, I saw a trailer for that! Wasn’t it full of goblins? I love goblins. It is! Loads of goblins. And a dragon. Though not a very scary dragon, mind you. More of a… cheerful dragon. Okay, okay, slowing down the chaos. 'Everything Everywhere' isn’t  mandatory . But genuinely, if you’re feeling up for something a bit different, it’s worth it.

…and honestly, the queue for the Louvre was just  insane . I thought we’d be stuck there all day. Worth it for the Mona Lisa, I suppose, but still. My feet are still killing me. Oh, darling, Paris sounds exhausting! You always do go for the big stuff, don’t you? I’m just glad you both got back safe. I was picturing all sorts of things happening with you two gallivanting around a capital city. Are you sure you didn't try to run a marathon while you were at it, Millie? Mum! No marathons. Just a lot of walking. And a slight… incident. Slight incident is putting it mildly. She tripped over a cobblestone trying to take a picture of a particularly picturesque patisserie. Hey! It was a  very  picturesque patisserie. And the cobblestones were deliberately trying to ruin my life, I swear. Oh, you clumsy thing! Did you hurt yourself badly? I told you to wear sensible shoes. Those little sandals weren’t exactly made for power-walking across historic cities. I’m fine, honestly. Just a really nasty graze on my knee. Leo patched me up with one of those travel plasters, the ones with the cartoon animals. Very dignified. It  was  a slightly embarrassing plaster, I’ll admit. But it stopped the bleeding. And honestly, Millie, you were more upset about ruining the photo opportunity than the actual pain. Well, the light was  perfect , okay? It won't happen again, I assure you. How was your weekend, anyway? Anything more exciting than my Parisian mishaps? Quiet as you’d expect. I spent most of Saturday marking mock GCSE papers, unfortunately. The joys of being an Examinations Manager. Though, Mrs. Henderson brought in some truly lovely lemon drizzle cake. That was a highlight. Did you eat well in Paris? I hope you didn’t just live on pain au chocolat. Oh, the food was amazing! We had escargots – surprisingly good, actually – and steak frites, and this incredible onion soup… and yes, a  lot  of pain au chocolat. Leo’s trying to put me on a vegetable regime now, as punishment. He has a point. You were practically vibrating with sugar when we got back. Although, I did sneak a croissant this morning, so I’m an accomplice. Good! Solidarity in pastry consumption is vital. Did you catch up with Sarah at all this weekend, Mum? I meant to ask.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of essays needing marking is terrifying. I swear, they all suddenly decided to write 5000-word masterpieces the last week of term. Tell me about it! Though retail has its own seasonal surges of… chaos. It's less about complex arguments and more about dealing with twenty people simultaneously wanting the last discounted toaster. Still, draining. Did you have a nice weekend, at least? You mentioned going to Chichester? It was good, yeah. Surprisingly good. My sister lives there now, you know? Didn’t realize Chichester had so much going for it. Quaint, very…historical. We went to a little Shakespeare production. Nothing fancy, but pleasant. How about you? Any adventures in Croydon? Croydon was…Croydon. Mum needed help with her garden, which is code for “I want you to spend eight hours weeding.” Blissful. Though, afterwards, we had a proper family roast. Always good. Speaking of families, still no pressure from your lot about settling down, is there? Remember your aunt grilling you at Christmas? Don't remind me. The ‘when are you going to find a nice girl and give us some grandkids’ routine. It's exhausting. And no, not yet. Though, Mark from the linguistics department keeps…hovering. He’s been going on about the British National Corpus like it’s the eighth wonder of the world. Oh, God, the BNC. Every linguistics student's obsession. Is he trying to impress you with passive voice analysis or something equally thrilling? Worse, actually. He wants to ‘collaborate’ on a paper about dialectal variations in Malaysian English. Apparently he’s done some research. Honestly, I just want to get through marking these essays without accidentally flunking anyone for incorrect referencing. My brain is fried. Pay day can’t come soon enough. Preach! I’m already mentally budgeting. Supervisor wages aren’t exactly…lavish. Especially with my student loan repayments looming. Are you still picking up extra TEFL hours to keep afloat? A couple. It's useful, keeps me sharp on the basics…and the money helps. Honestly though, sometimes I wonder why I bothered with a Master’s. The tuition fees were…a commitment. You did your postgrad, didn't you? What was yours in? Marketing. Which is ironically useful for convincing people to buy things they don't need. It's been handy for getting the supervisor role, though. More responsibility, thankfully more money.

…and then you  really  gotta fluff it with a fork, yeah? Not stir, fluff. Otherwise it gets all sticky. Like when you tried making it last time. Oh, don’t remind me. That was… an experience. Honestly, I thought I’d created some sort of rice concrete. It was inedible. Right, fluffing. Got it. So, one cup of rice to two cups of water, and then fluff. Simple enough. Though, actually, I was thinking… fancy going out for a curry tonight? I’ve got that voucher from Deliveroo. Deliveroo? Again? We had Deliveroo like, three times last week! Plus, I’m trying to show you how to actually  cook  a curry, not just order one. And this rice is going brilliantly, see? Perfectly separate grains. It’s a point of pride, honestly. I know, I know, you’re Chef Jamie Oliver. But honestly, after a day chasing Leo around… the thought of chopping onions and fiddling with spices just feels… exhausting. The Deliveroo voucher is practically begging to be used. It's a good place, that Indian place on Douglas Street. They do a really mild korma, which Leo might even manage a bite of. Mild korma? That’s barely a curry! You gotta have a bit of kick. I was thinking a proper Madras. We could add some jalapenos. Remember those we got from the market? Jalapenos?! Are you trying to set my mouth on fire? Honestly, sometimes I think you deliberately try and push my spice tolerance. And the last time you “added a bit of kick”, I spent the next hour regretting every life choice I’d ever made. Plus, remember what Dr. Bell said about really checking food content? All that salt in takeaway curries… Dr. Bell always says something about salt. She’s convinced everything’s going to give us high blood pressure. And a little salt isn’t going to kill us. Anyway, we can ask them to go easy on it. It's not like we're eating it every day. This rice is almost done. Have you checked the chicken? Is it… questionable? It was looking a bit pale this morning. Oh, the chicken… That’s a good point. I think it’s okay. I put it in the fridge as soon as I got back from the shops. But you’re right, it did look a bit… off. Maybe we should just have something vegetarian then?

…and honestly, the Job Centre just feels like they’re tickin’ boxes, y’know? Another application for a warehouse job I'm completely unsuited for. Like I'm gonna enjoy shift work packin' boxes after gettin' a degree in… well, never mind what I got a degree  in . Doesn't matter now, does it? Oi, don’t be so down, Liam. You’re smart. Something will come up. It’s just… a bit rubbish at the minute, innit? What did you actually apply for today, besides the boxes? Not a lot, to be honest. Saw one for a pub chef, but needed experience. Experience! How am I supposed to  get  experience if no one gives me a chance? It's a right catch-22. It sounds exhausting, always applying. Honestly, sometimes I just wanna chuck it all in and go live in a van, travel around, and paint. Though, then I remember I have student loans looming… Vans are romantic 'til you've got no shower for a week, Chloe. Trust me. I supported a fella last year who tried that. Didn't last a month. How was college today, love? Anything interesting happen in history? Proper hectic, actually. Mr. Harrison finally explained the causes of the English Civil War in a way that actually made sense. Normally he just rambles. Still got that essay due on Friday though. Ugh. Thinking of just hitting the library all weekend. Essay, eh? Wish I was writin' essays. Be a lot more productive than fillin’ out forms for jobs I’ll never get. Sarah, you still enjoying your placement at the primary school? It’s good, yeah. Exhausting, but good. Little Billy Henderson tried to glue glitter to his eyebrows today. Absolute chaos. But genuinely rewarding, seeing them learn. Pays the bills, at least. How’s your mam doing, Liam? I haven’t seen her since… Christmas, was it? She’s alright. Still moanin’ about the council not fixin’ the potholes on Lowther Street. Says her suspension is takin' a right batterin’. She keeps tellin' me I need to "get on with it" and "stop wallowin'," y’know, the usual. Mothers, eh? Always got the right words... or the words that  feel  wrong at the time. Mine keeps asking when I’m going to “settle down” and get a proper job. Like being an artist isn't a proper job! Tell me about it. Mine's obsessed with me becoming a teacher.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of requests for vegan options this year is  mental . Like, three years ago it was a polite enquiry, now it’s practically a demand. It's for the tech conference, right? You’d think coders lived on pizza and Red Bull, not quinoa and kale! Sounds stressful, love. Though, I suppose things change. Everything does. Used to be, people just wanted a decent buffet and a comfy chair. No fuss. Exactly! And then you get the dietary requirements on top – gluten-free, nut allergies, lactose intolerant…it’s like navigating a minefield. This one woman emailed me three separate times just to confirm the hummus was definitely tahini-based.  Tahini-based ! Right. Sounds like you need a holiday. You work too hard, Annie. Always have. Remember when you were a little ‘un, organising the street parties on Elmbridge? You were bossing everyone about even then. Oh, don’t start! I was a tiny dictator. Mum always said I had a ‘gift for logistics’. Now it’s just… overwhelming sometimes. How are  you  keeping, by the way? Still managing to get out for walks? I’ve been trying. My knees aren’t what they used to be, though. Honestly, feels like every step is announcing itself. Doctor said I need to build up the muscles around them, but… well, you know me. Motivation's a bit of an issue. You should join a gentle exercise class! There's that one at the community centre, chair yoga. It sounds a bit tame, maybe, but it's low impact and everyone's really friendly. Keeps you moving, at least. Chair yoga, eh? Sounds… civilized. Not sure I'm quite ready for all that stretching, though. I did try to potter in the garden a bit last week, and nearly ended up face-first in the rose bushes. Oh, bless you! Maybe start with some short walks then? We could go to Grantchester Meadows sometime next week, if the weather holds up. It’s flat, lovely scenery. That sounds… nice. Very nice, actually. I haven’t been to Grantchester in ages. Gets a bit lonely, you know? Just me and the telly. I know. That’s why I try to pop over when I can. It’s good to talk. And stop you from becoming a complete hermit! Speaking of which, how  is  Mrs. Higgins? I haven’t seen her since… Christmas?

…and honestly, the amount of washing up  you  two generate is frankly astonishing. Honestly, it's like a small restaurant in here after every meal. Leo, honestly, did you even  attempt  to clear your plate? Mum, I was telling Ben about the new level I unlocked on Call of Duty. It’s really hard! Priorities, eh? Though, I confess, even I left my mug. Long day at work. Honestly, the systems upgrade is a nightmare. It’s like trying to herd cats. It's not just the plates, Dad. It's all the snack wrappers too. Leo ate, like, five granola bars while we were gaming. Five? Leo! Really? That’s just…excessive. And don’t you two start blaming each other. Right, everyone, five minutes. Plates, wrappers, everything. Then we can properly talk about your tennis results, Ben. I heard you won. Yeah, but I nearly lost! This kid, Harrison, he serves like…like a professional. Seriously. That’s good, lad. A close win feels better sometimes, builds character. Reminds me of a story…back in Korea, my grandfather used to say losing a small battle prepares you for winning the war. Very philosophical man. He also had a magnificent moustache. Your grandfather and his moustache? Is this going somewhere, David? Last time you brought up your grandfather, we ended up discussing the intricacies of Korean fermented cabbage for an hour. No, no, it's relevant! It was a rather striking moustache. Thick, perfectly groomed. Not like some of the bizarre things I’m seeing young men attempting these days. One of your son’s friends had a…a sort of patchy soul patch the other day. It was unsettling. That was Finn! He's trying to look edgy. It looked a bit like…Hitler. Sorry. I didn’t mean to say that. Ben! Honestly! That was…a rather unfortunate comparison. Just don't. Ever. We do  not  make comparisons like that. Ever. It's insensitive and deeply inappropriate. Quite right. Perhaps we should steer clear of facial hair altogether. Can we talk about something else now? Like, I saw Chloe at the skate park today. Chloe? Oh, is that the girl you've been…seeing? Is that the right word? We’re not  seeing ! We just…hang out. She’s really good at skateboarding. And she follows me on Instagram. She likes all your posts. Seriously, she likes  everything .

…and honestly, the state of that sideboard when they delivered it! Scratched to bits. I sent photos straight to the shop, mind you. Said it weren't fit for purpose, not for the money. They offered me fifteen quid off. Fifteen! As if that covers the embarrassment of having it as the centrepiece of the dining room. Fifteen quid? Seriously? You should’ve kicked off more, Mum. You always let them walk all over you. Oh, I did have a word, love. A  firm  word. But what are you gonna do? Drag it back to the van? It's heavy as owt. And then where would we be? Nowhere near ready for Christmas. Aye, fifteen quid is a cheek. Should’ve demanded a replacement. Though, you did get it down from that antique place, didn’t you? They're all a bit… precious. Precious and expensive, that’s them. I thought it would be a good investment, something lasting. It’s going to need a good polish, that’s for sure. Still, better than nothing. Did you manage to get rid of all that stuff at the tip on Saturday, Doris? Oh, aye. A right clear out. Found some of your Dad’s old tools I’d forgotten about. Nearly chucked ‘em, then thought, ‘No, someone might want these.’ Though, honestly, the tip is chaos. People dumping anything and everything. It's ridiculous, isn't it? Saw a full armchair someone just…left by the gate last week. Like, who does that? Lazy lot, the lot of ‘em. Speaking of lazy, have you heard from Sarah about how Lisa is? Still poorly, is she? Yeah, she’s not great. Her husband, Mark, is completely overwhelmed. He’s having to do everything, looking after the kids  and  trying to manage Lisa’s condition. It’s awful. Apparently, it's getting harder to remember things, even simple stuff. It sounds… scary. Poor love. It’s terrible when it starts to creep in like that. My Auntie Margaret, she had it bad towards the end. Didn't recognise anyone. Breaks your heart, it does. It really does. Makes you think, doesn't it? We’re so lucky our families are still mostly with it. Remember old Mr. Henderson on the street? Always moaning about kids kicking his ball into his garden. He started forgetting where he lived about six months before… well. Ugh, don’t remind me.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt so…cold. Like they’d already made up their minds. “Restructuring,” they called it. Restructuring into fewer people doing the same amount of work, more like. Oh, love. That’s awful. Truly. So, you  are  officially redundant then? I thought it was just rumours swirling around the office last week. Officially. Meeting with HR was this morning. They gave me the standard spiel – ‘valuable contributions’, ‘difficult decision’, ‘support with job searching’… you know the drill. It feels so impersonal. I really liked that job, Mum. I was finally getting somewhere with the new marketing campaign. I’m so sorry, darling. It’s a rotten feeling. But honestly, sometimes these things are a blessing in disguise. You're young, talented, you’ll find something even better. Have you started looking already? A little bit. Scrolled through LinkedIn, mostly. It’s just…daunting. Everyone wants three years’ experience minimum, and I’ve only been working for two. Still, I’ve updated my CV and asked Sarah – you remember Sarah from uni? – to look it over. She’s a recruitment consultant now. Good, good. That’s sensible. Sarah’s a clever girl. Listen, don’t dwell on it too much this weekend. We need to cheer you up! Are you still up for coming to Norwich? Your Grandad’s been asking about you. He’s been on a bit of a reminiscing kick lately, talking about when you were tiny and used to steal his biscuits. Oh, God. I’d almost forgotten about the biscuit incidents. Yes, absolutely. I need a proper Mum-and-Grandad hug. And a proper home-cooked meal. I’ve been living on takeaways since everything went south at work. It’s terrible, I know. Don’t beat yourself up about it. It happens. But honestly, your eating habits have been atrocious since you left uni! Remember when you used to practically live at the gym? You haven’t mentioned going in weeks. I know, I know. Gym’s been…low priority. Honestly, finding the motivation is hard when you feel like your life is completely up in the air. I feel sluggish and awful. Maybe Norwich will kickstart me again. Fresh air, walks with Grandad… Exactly! Plus, I've been meaning to ask, have you had any luck with quotes for the house extension yet? I know you were looking at getting a little office sorted out.

…and then Mick was building this massive den, right? Out of, like, everything! Old tyres and branches and this huge tarpaulin. It was brilliant. Better than the one  we  tried to make last week, definitely. That’s nice, love. Hope it inspires you to actually  help  me clear out the shed this summer. It's looking like a health hazard. Mum! Don’t start on the shed already. It’s only the beginning of the holidays! I haven’t even properly  started  being bored yet. Gah! Mick! Mick! Den! See? Even Leo's on the Mick bandwagon. He just wants to build things and make a mess, just like you. Although his construction skills are… limited. Hey! I’m not  always  making a mess. And Leo's just a baby! What am I supposed to  do  all summer though? Tom and Ben are going to Wales with their families, so I won't see them for ages. Well, firstly, you could help with the shed. Secondly, Mrs. O’Malley said she’s running a lifeguard course at the pool. Maybe you’d be interested? They need young instructors. Swimming instructor? Ugh. I’m alright at swimming, but teaching little kids… They’re scary! And I’m not sure I’m responsible enough. Remember when I nearly lost your car keys at the beach? I remember. That was… a moment. But seriously, it’s good experience. And it gets you out of the house. What about your guitar? Have you been practicing? A bit. Mr. Davies gave me that new piece, the Japanese one. It’s really hard. All the different symbols and stuff. I can’t even read the tabs properly. Japanese music? That’s… different. Your teacher's always pushing you. Maybe just stick to the chords you know for now? We could find some easier songs online. It’s not the chords, it’s the  reading  of it. It’s like a different language! I wish I’d paid more attention in languages at school. You never paid attention in languages  at  school. That’s the problem. Anyway, dinner's ready. Leo, no throwing spaghetti! Gah! Fly away! You’ve got spaghetti in your hair, Leo. This is why I need a holiday  from  the holiday. Look, how about we make a list, alright? Write down everything you  might  want to do, and then we can try and fit some of it in.

Honestly, the dialogue in this… it’s just  awful . Like someone wrote it based on watching American cop shows from the 90s. You sayin’ ‘awful’, I’m sayin’ it's…authentically bad. It’s almost impressive how consistently cringe it is. It's providing a valuable service, innit? A lesson in what  not  to do. A lesson I’m already learning the hard way with my own writing, probably. This is exactly the kind of stuff my tutor warns me about - the 'tell, don't show' malarkey. Though, showing a dodgy detective in a car chase is probably more exciting than what I'm showing anyone at the moment - mostly just a bloke staring at a laptop. You’re bein’ harsh on yourself. You were sendin’ me bits last week, that were dead good. Properly atmospheric. Better than this… visual noise, anyway. Reminds me a bit of that dentist I had last year. All shiny surfaces and performative competence, but ultimately, deeply unsatisfying. A dentist analogy for bad filmmaking? That’s… inspired. Was it a bad experience then, the dentist? Proper root canal drama? Nearly. Just…a lot of empty promises about the ‘state-of-the-art’ equipment. And him talkin’ through a mouthful of cotton wool. Sounded like someone gargling pebbles. Speaking of painful experiences, remember that gig we went to in Sheffield last year? The band were… let’s just say they didn’t live up to the hype. Oh,  god , don't remind me. The lead singer sounded like a strangled cat. And the venue smelled faintly of damp and regret. I thought my ears were gonna bleed. I need a holiday after remembering that. Somewhere with no music, no dentists, and definitely no terrible films. Thinkin’ maybe the Lake District? That sounds lovely, actually. Peaceful. We could maybe hire one of those Citibikes they've got now. Cycle round, pretend to be Wordsworth. Though I reckon I'd be more 'struggling up a hill, lookin' a right state' than Wordsworth. Very accurate. You and a Citibike – a comedy waiting to happen. I’d pay to see that. Hey, you've been teaching English for ages now. Do you ever get annoyed by people deliberately doing bad accents? Like, just for a laugh? Are you askin' because you've been practicing your Scouse? And yeah, all the time! It’s infuriating! Especially when it’s a really bad, stereotypical effort.

…and honestly, the traffic on the A38 was  brutal . Took me nearly an hour to get from Curdworth to here. You wouldn’t believe it for a Tuesday morning. Oh, Mum! Seriously? I thought leaving early would beat it. I left Litchfield at 8, thinking I’d be fine. You're right, though, it’s always a nightmare around Spaghetti Junction. Glad you made it, though. Coffee’s brewing. How was your pottery class? Did you manage to finish that vase? It was… frustrating. The clay just wasn’t cooperating. Kept collapsing in on itself. I managed to salvage  something , but it’s definitely wonky. I think I need a lesson on centering again. Never mind, it’s relaxing overall. More relaxing than battling motorway drivers, anyway. So, tell me about this new job. You sounded a bit hesitant on the phone. Hesitant is… a polite word. It's fine, Mum, genuinely. It’s just… a lot. Year 2 is… energetic, to say the least. And Mrs. Davies, the Head, has  very  specific ideas about display arrangements. It's all themed, apparently. This term is ‘Enchanted Forests’. Can you imagine the glitter? Oh, goodness. Glitter  everywhere . Sounds… challenging. But you’re a natural with the little ones, love. You were always brilliant with your cousins, putting on those plays. You’ll manage. It's just a bit of adjusting, isn't it? I think so. I just wish they’d explained the display demands  before  I accepted. I’m already planning my weekends around crafting miniature toadstools. Honestly! But the kids are lovely, genuinely. Little Leo brought me a dandelion this morning. Melted my heart. That's lovely. See? It's all worth it for moments like that. Speaking of little ones… have you given any more thought to Easter cakes for the family? I was thinking a lemon drizzle this year, perhaps? Lemon drizzle sounds amazing! I was planning on doing some, actually. I found a really cute recipe with little chocolate chicks on top. Although, with work being so hectic, I might need to enlist some help. Would you be up for decorating? You're much better at the icing. Of course, darling. Always. We can make a proper afternoon of it. It’ll be lovely to have that time together. And it's almost time to start thinking about Thomas’s christening, isn’t it? Sarah and Ben have finally settled on a date.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I had last week was  criminal . Sixteen year olds, you know? They think a comma is some sort of optional extra. It’s like pulling teeth getting them to understand basic sentence structure. Oh, don’t even  start  me on teenagers. I’ve moved down to Year 8 thankfully, a bit more manageable, though the drama is still…present. Still, at least they haven’t yet decided grammar is a personal affront. How’s little Leo coping with the move to secondary school? Is he settling in alright? He’s… adjusting. It’s a huge change, going from being a big fish in a small pond to feeling like a minnow again. He’s made a couple of friends, thankfully. Mostly through gaming, which, while I’m not thrilled about the screen time, is at least  something . He’s already complaining about homework though. Says Mr. Henderson gives way too much. Henderson… that name rings a bell. Isn’t he the history teacher who’s obsessed with medieval weaponry? That's the one! Apparently, he sets essays on the socio-economic impact of longbow production. On a Friday. Leo is convinced he’s intentionally trying to ruin their weekends. Oh, bless him. Sounds like a typical teenager. My Emily is glued to TikTok, showing me these… dances. Honestly, my hips aren’t what they used to be. Though, speaking of things glued to screens, I finally managed to get my online skincare business properly off the ground. Oh, that’s brilliant, Janet! I knew you’d do it. "Bloom & Glow," wasn’t it? How’s it going? Are you actually making any money, or is it mostly samples and good intentions? Better than samples and intentions, thankfully! It’s slow, but steady. I'm building up a loyal customer base, mostly through Instagram. It’s a lot of work though, trying to take good photos, write descriptions, and then actually package everything up. It's a world away from marking spelling tests! And the competition is  fierce . Everyone's a beauty guru these days. It sounds exhausting, but amazing you’re doing it. You’ve always had such good skin, it makes sense you’d go down that route. I just stick to the basics, really. Though, my mum keeps trying to get me to use her ‘miracle’ face cream. She swears it's the secret to her youthful glow.

…and honestly, the matzah ball soup was a bit… dense. Not light and fluffy like Auntie Sylvia’s. She’s a matzah ball  master . Oh, come  on , Leo. You say that every year! It wasn't  that  bad. My mum puts a good pinch of dill in, it makes all the difference. Though, Sylvia  does  have a secret, doesn’t she? Something about using seltzer water? It’s not a secret, darling, it's just good technique. And a really light hand. She whispers to the matzah meal. Honestly, the woman has a gift. Though, I think we should move swiftly from critique of the soup to a discussion of the charoset. David, yours was… interesting. Date and walnut? A bit adventurous, even for you. Hey! It’s a family recipe! My nan on my dad's side – she was half-Italian, you see – used to add a tiny bit of amaretto to hers. So I just… carried on the tradition. It’s subtle! Subtle like a foghorn, mate. But points for creativity. Seriously though, after this, I feel like I need to book a flight to Italy. All this talk of dates and nuts and… I just want a proper carbonara. Oh, Italy! Remember that trip we took after Uni, Leo? Rome, Florence, Venice…the pastries! I swear I gained half a stone just from cannoli. Thinking about it makes me want to bake. Maybe I’ll try a new babka recipe later. You make a heavenly babka, Clara. Truly. Though it’s a world away from the food of our ancestors, isn’t it? From escaping Egypt and eating hastily baked bread to…babka with chocolate and hazelnut. It’s quite a journey. Speaking of journeys, has anyone heard anything from Ben and Rebecca? They were supposed to be in Paris this week. Last I heard, Ben was trying to order an Ortolan. An Ortolan? Really? That's…intense. All that netting and eating the whole thing, bones and all. Even  I  have standards, and I’ll eat a dodgy kebab at 3am. He’s a bit of a foodie daredevil, your brother, David. I think he saw it on some show and his curiosity got the better of him. Probably ended up just ordering a steak frites. I texted Rebecca earlier. They’re fine. Ben did, apparently, attempt the Ortolan, but the waiter looked at him like he’d grown a second head and suggested something less…rustic.

…and honestly, the pacing was just  awful . It felt like they stretched a novella into a six-part series. All that lingering cinematography, showing us rain on windows for five minutes! I mean, atmosphere is fine, but give me  something  to happen. Oh, you’re talking about ‘The Shadow Bloom’? I actually quite liked it. A bit slow, granted, but I thought the acting was superb. Especially Beatrice Bellwether as Old Man Hemlock. She was chilling. Chilling is one word for it. I found her… grating. Like nails down a chalkboard. And the whole plot hinged on this ridiculously contrived secret. I kept waiting for a sensible explanation that never came. I’m definitely Team-Book on this one. The novel was so much tighter. Exactly! The book had nuance. The series just… wallowed. Honestly, I nearly gave up after episode three. I was knitting a ridiculously complicated cable knit jumper at the time, and I almost unravelled the whole thing in frustration. You and your knitting, Sarah. You  always  knit when you're stressed. What colour is this jumper? Is it for young Thomas? He's growing like a weed. It’s a charcoal grey, and yes, it’s for Thomas. He specifically asked for a “proper jumper, like Grandad used to wear.” Honestly, the pressure! It's got to be perfect. It’s a bit ambitious, even for me. More fiddly than that crochet blanket I made for Lily last year. Speaking of Lily, how are her A-Levels going? She was looking a bit overwhelmed last time I saw her. She is. The pressure is immense. Her mock results weren’t fantastic, she’s panicking about getting into university. We’re trying to tell her it’s not the end of the world, there are other routes, gap years, apprenticeships… but she’s fixated on Oxbridge. Oh, darling. That’s tough. Remember when  I  was freaking out about university? My mum nearly had a breakdown trying to calm me down. Though, to be fair, she was reading Georgette Heyer at the time, so her perspective was slightly skewed. Georgette Heyer? Classic Mum-distraction tactic! My nan was obsessed with Agatha Christie. Any crisis, and she’d immediately delve into a Miss Marple. It's amazing how books can be an escape, isn’t it? Though I confess, I’m increasingly switching to eBooks. Just so much easier to carry around, especially on my commute.

…and honestly, the sheer amount of plastic is ridiculous, isn’t it? They could at least make the boxes recyclable. Right, let's get these bad boys out. So, you went for the… lavender one, yeah? Yep! Lavender. Seemed a bit less… shouty than the other colours. And yes, the packaging  is  obscene. Seriously, it’s like they’re deliberately trying to contribute to the plastic crisis. You got the black one, didn't you? Very you. Predictable, I know. Black’s just…practical. Less likely to show up the fingerprints. Now, right, let’s get these switched on. Feel like we’re back in 2007, unboxing Nokias, only… less robust, probably. Remember when you could genuinely  throw  a 3310 at a wall and it would just bounce? Oh god, don’t remind me. My dad went through about four of those. He swore they were indestructible. This feels… fragile in comparison. Right, powering on… okay, welcome screen. Finnish, Swedish… and English, thankfully. Always English first, eh? Speaking of Finnish, this is weird, isn’t it? Sitting in a pub in Joensuu, unpacking brand new phones practically the moment they’re released. Feels a world away from Liverpool. It does. Makes you think about how much has changed. Remember Nokia  being  Finland? It was massive. My grandad used to work for them, in the factory over on the Wirral, actually. He was so proud. Aye, they were giants. And then… just… not. It’s a fascinating case study, really. From dominating the global market to… well, to what it is now. It's almost poetic, isn’t it? This phone, manufactured by a Chinese company, being set up in a pub in Finland, bypassing the home of the original mobile phone powerhouse. A slightly depressing poetry, maybe. Okay, I'm at the 'select your region' bit. Should I just go with United Kingdom? Yeah, stick with UK. It'll sort out the time zone and all that. You want me to walk you through the settings, or are you feeling confident? Actually, maybe a little help with the privacy settings. I always get paranoid about what data they’re collecting. You’re the tech guru, after all. Plus, you've read all the terms and conditions – something I definitely don't have the patience for. Guru is a strong word. But I do tend to skim read the small print, sadly.

…and then he  jumped  on the sofa! Honestly, Mum, Winston is mental. A complete whirlwind. You wouldn’t believe it. Winston sounds…spirited. Is he still trying to ‘bury’ his toys in the cushions? He did that for weeks last Christmas. Drove me round the bend. Roar! Dino bury! Yeah, pretty much. Only now it’s socks. He’s obsessed with hiding your socks, Mum. It’s a conspiracy, I swear. But still, he’s the best cat ever. Way better than a dog. Oh, now that’s fighting talk! A good dog is a loyal companion. Remember old Barnaby? Your Grandad’s Malamute? He was a gentle giant. Barnaby was…fluffy. And shed  everywhere . Winston doesn’t shed, he’s practically hypoallergenic. And he lets me dress him up in little hats. Try  that  with a Malamute. Hat! Me hat! He does love a hat, doesn’t he? Right, back to the important stuff. Leo’s birthday. Have you given any more thought to what you want to get him? I was thinking… he's really into those red pandas at the moment, isn’t he? Maybe a red panda plushie? Or a book about them? Good idea! A book is always useful. Though he does have a mountain of them already. Maybe something a bit different? He was admiring that little coding game on the iPad the other day. Oh! That’s a good shout! But Dad said no more screen time. He’s been on about getting me to use the laptop more for school stuff. He thinks it’s ‘character building.’ Your father and his ‘character building’. Well, perhaps we could suggest the coding game as a… constructive hobby? And speaking of hobbies, have you remembered to invite Maya to the party? Oh yeah! I texted her this morning. She said she's definitely coming. She's really good at gymnastics, you know. She does that backflip thing. She could maybe do a show-off routine if we asked. Maybe we’ll leave the show-off routines to the professionals! We’re just having a little gathering in the garden, aren’t we? Board games, cake…simple. Cake! We should get a pinata! A red panda pinata! It would be amazing. A pinata…that’s a bit ambitious, darling. We’ll see. We need to finalize the guest list and order the cake. And what about decorations?

…and honestly, the Christmas markets in Lancaster are nothing compared to what you get in Germany, are they? It’s all just overpriced mulled wine and a few dodgy fairy lights. Not the  atmosphere , y’know? Dodgy fairy lights? That's harsh, Liv! Lancaster’s alright. It’s not… Cologne, granted. But it's a good effort. Though I do miss the  Glühwein  from Berlin. Proper stuff. And the markets went on for ages, didn't they? Oh, you youngsters and your European Christmas markets! Back in my day, Christmas was… simpler. We didn't need all these fancy displays. Just a proper tree, carols, and a good Boxing Day walk. Simpler is right, Margaret. Though I do recall a rather magnificent display at Harrods one year. Expensive, of course. Took Arthur – that was your mother, Liv – a good hour just to find a parking space. And then the crowds! Grandad, Harrods at Christmas sounds like my worst nightmare. Too many people. I prefer a quiet Christmas, to be honest. Like the ones we had up in the Lakes, remember? Just us, Nana and Pop, and a roaring fire. No fuss. Yeah, those were the best. Pop always used to tell the same awful jokes, though. Remember the one about the snowman? Oh, I do. “What do snowmen call their parents? Ice-bergs!” He told it every single year. And every single year, we pretended to be surprised. He had a talent for terrible puns. A true talent. It’s a shame humour seems to have changed so much. Everything’s got to be… sarcastic now, hasn’t it? No genuine, good-natured silliness. Not always, Grandad. It’s just… different. Things change. Speaking of different, Emilio, you never had proper snow Christmases in Manila, did you? Nope. We had… different traditions. Less about the cold and more about the heat, obviously.  Simbang Gabi  – nine days of dawn masses leading up to Christmas. It’s… a big deal. Everything's brightly lit, really colourful. And the food! Lechon,  bibingka ,  puto bumbong ... you wouldn’t believe the feasts. Sounds lovely! We always had turkey, of course, with all the trimmings. And Christmas pudding, naturally. Though I always suspected your grandmother secretly hated making it. So much effort for something nobody really enjoys. Nonsense, Margaret! The Christmas pudding is a cornerstone of the British Christmas. A symbol! Although, I do agree, the brandy butter is the best part.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of audio I had to transcribe this week was  insane . It was all police interviews, really grim stuff. One was a detailed account of a burglary gone wrong, the other… well, let’s just say it involved a very angry neighbour and a garden gnome. Garden gnome violence? Good Lord, Brenda. You really do get the best of it, don’t you? My week was remarkably…beige. Spreadsheet mostly. Old Man Hemmings decided he wants a report on paperclip expenditure. Paperclips! Oh, Hemmings. He’s a classic. Honestly, I sometimes think he invents these tasks just to feel important. Speaking of important, anyone fancy another slice of this Victoria sponge? I used a new raspberry jam, it's divine. Don't mind if I do, Margaret. It  is  rather good. And beige sounds…safe, David. Though, honestly, after listening to people detail their worst moments all week, a bit of beige might be welcome. Did you catch that new detective series, ‘Shadows of the Moor’? The one with the brooding inspector? Oh, I did! Bit slow to start, I thought. The plot was a bit convoluted with all the family secrets, but it picked up. Quite enjoyed the gloomy atmosphere, though. Reminded me a bit of Edinburgh in November, actually. All grey skies and hidden resentments. I’m still on ‘Vera’. Brenda, you’d love it! She’s a wonderfully pragmatic detective, a bit rough around the edges, and lives in Northumberland. Much more my speed than those psychological thrillers everyone's obsessed with. They just give me a headache. I tried one of those last week. Utterly baffling. Too many twists for the sake of twists. Vera sounds more up my street. I need something…grounded. Speaking of grounded, I need to get back to reality eventually. This transcription job is paying the bills, but it’s draining. You should really consider doing more creative writing again, Brenda. You were so good at that short story course you did a few years back. Remember that one about the lighthouse keeper? Oh, that! That was a long time ago. Life got in the way, didn’t it? Bills, work… the garden gnome transcriptions. Nonsense, life is  always  getting in the way. You just have to carve out a little time for yourself. Have you used your Kindle much lately? I downloaded a load of poetry. Perfect for a quiet evening.

…and honestly, Doreen, I’m telling you, young Timothy next door, he’s got no respect. Absolutely none. Leaving his scooter right across the path again. Nearly tripped over the blooming thing this morning. Could’ve broken a hip, I could! Oh, Arthur, you and that scooter. He’s just a lad, isn't he? Probably doesn’t even  think  about it. You know how children are. All elbows and knees and no awareness. He  is  a bit of a nuisance, though. I saw him kicking a football against Mrs. Higgins’ fence yesterday. She wasn’t best pleased, I can assure you. Not best pleased? She came out shouting! Told him she’d report his parents. And rightly so! It's the parents I blame, you see. No discipline these days. Back in my day… Oh, here we go. “Back in your day…” Arthur, things change. It wasn’t all sunshine and roses back then, either. You just remember it differently. I used to have little David, bless him, building forts in the garden out of anything he could find – old pots, flower baskets… drove me mad sometimes! But he was just being a boy. Flower baskets? That's different, Doreen. Flower baskets aren’t a trip hazard. A scooter left carelessly is. And this isn’t about being a boy, it's about common courtesy. He knows perfectly well we’re older. He should show a little consideration. It's a generational thing, really. They don't quite grasp the… fragility. I had a student once, utterly oblivious. Kept talking about ‘influencers’ and ‘going viral’. Completely lost on me, of course. Oh, Harold, you and your students. You used to come home complaining about them all the time. Still, you were a brilliant lecturer, even if you didn’t understand TikTok. TikTok? What in the world is TikTok? Sounds like a clockmaker’s convention. It’s… a platform. For short videos. Never mind, Arthur. It’s not relevant. The point is, this boy… Timothy… perhaps a firm but polite word with his mother would do the trick? Polite? Harold, I’ve tried polite! I’ve said “Good morning, Timothy, perhaps you could move your scooter?” And he just looks at me like I’m speaking Martian! Well, you do have a way of… delivering things, Arthur. Very direct. Perhaps  I  could have a word? I’m quite good at getting through to mothers.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of biscuits is a bit alarming. I mean, do we  need  three different kinds of shortbread? Never, ever underestimate the British public’s need for shortbread, Liv. It's practically a national requirement. Though, yeah, maybe tone down the empire biscuit selection. People either  love  them or hate them, no in-between. I think it’s a good spread generally. Are we still on for the venue being the Eagle? It feels… appropriate. History and all that. The Eagle’s good. Plenty of space, and we can get a good look at people arriving.
