Just need to confirm the booking. I’ll chase them up again tomorrow morning. Did anyone manage to get a headcount beyond the initial invites? I’ve had a decent response from the international teams. About twenty confirmed so far, which is pretty good considering the time difference and everything. Though, several asked if there’d be vegan options… which reminds me, we definitely need a vegan cake. Oh,  please  don't let me be on cake duty again. Last time, I spent three hours wrestling with aquafaba and it still looked like a deflated volleyball. I’ll take the cake! I’m surprisingly good at vegan baking. My nan practically raised me on lentil loaf, so I’ve got a natural affinity for plant-based alternatives. Brilliant! That’s one thing ticked off. Speaking of… did anyone else see that poor bee struggling outside the loading bay earlier? It was flipped on its back. Oh aye, I did. Little fella was having a right time of it. I used a bit of cardboard to help it flip over. Hope it buzzed off okay. It’s awful seeing them like that. I tried to help, but I'm rubbish at delicate rescues. I nearly squished it. I felt awful! It just wouldn’t grip onto anything. You're not alone, Liv. I once spent ten minutes trying to rescue a moth from a spiderweb and ended up just making it more tangled. Sometimes, it’s best to just let nature take its course, as grim as that sounds. I always feel bad leaving them, though. Especially bees. They do so much. It reminds me of Old Man Hemmings back home. He used to rescue stray worms after a rain shower. Said every creature deserved a chance. Proper scouser, that one. That’s lovely.

…and then Mr. Harrison  actually  said, "Newton’s laws are like, totally relatable to TikTok trends." Like, what?! How are falling apples and gravity anything like dance challenges, honestly? It's just… ridiculous. No way! He said that? Mr. Harrison is trying  so  hard to be cool, it's painful. Remember when he tried to wear trainers to school and got told off by Mrs. Davies? Oh god, yes! The bright orange ones! It was a power move that spectacularly backfired. But seriously, physics is hard enough without him trying to link it to… social media. I just want to understand the formulas, not analyze the trajectory of a viral video. Tell me about it. I’m struggling with the momentum questions. I get the concept, kind of, but applying it to the problems in the textbook… my brain just glitches. Did you manage to finish the homework? The one with the colliding trolleys? Ugh, that horrifying one? I  think  I did. My dad helped a bit, though. Don’t tell anyone. It feels like cheating when he has a physics degree and I’m staring at it like it’s hieroglyphics. No judgement! My older brother practically did mine. He’s at uni studying engineering, so it’s different. He said the key is breaking it down into smaller parts, but then  that  feels complicated. That’s what Dad said too! But then breaking it down turned into more equations and I just… gave up. How are we even supposed to know which formula to use? There are like, a million! It’s overwhelming. Honestly, I think Mrs. Lee explains it better than Mr. Harrison. She actually makes it make sense, instead of just saying “it is what it is” and writing stuff on the board at a million miles an hour. Definitely. Mrs. Lee understands we’re not all tiny physics geniuses. Did you hear she’s applying for that Head of Department position? Yeah! Old Mr. Peterson’s retiring at the end of the term, right? She’d be amazing. Imagine having  her  running the science department. Things might actually feel… manageable. It would be! Less TikTok analogies, for a start. And maybe she’d actually invest in some decent lab equipment. Remember when the Bunsen burner nearly exploded last week? Don’t remind me! Honestly, it felt like something out of a really bad film. It was flickering, and then just  whoosh .

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had to wade through this morning was ridiculous. It’s like everyone decided Monday was the day to unleash all their accumulated problems onto the admin team. Tell me about it. My inbox was overflowing too. Though, mostly it was just people chasing updates on the Henderson project. Apparently, Mr. Henderson is breathing down everyone's necks about the delivery date. It’s only a week away! Sounds like a right kerfuffle. Reminds me of old Mr. Patterson at the mill. He’d have a face like thunder if a shipment was even  slightly  delayed. Used to say, “Time is money, lass, and Patterson’s ain’t givin’ any away!” Oh, Mum! You always have a story. Though Henderson doesn't quite have the same rustic charm as old Mr. Patterson, I suspect. No, definitely not. More… intense. He just wants everything  perfect . Which, fine, is his prerogative, I guess, but it's adding a lot of pressure. What about you, love? Is admin always this manic? Usually it's manageable. But this week is end-of-quarter reporting, so everything gets ramped up. Plus, Professor Davies decided  now  is the perfect time to revamp the entire departmental filing system. Honestly, it's like he wants chaos. A filing system revamp? At this time of year? The man’s clearly lost the plot. You know, when I was at University, our lecturer, Dr. Bell, he was a stickler for organisation. Everything had to be in alphabetical order, by author, then date…it was a nightmare. But at least he waited until after exam season! Sounds stressful. Right, let’s talk about something less… organisational. This lasagna is amazing, Mum. Honestly, you’ve outdone yourself. It really is. It’s been ages since I’ve had proper home cooking. Uni canteen food just doesn’t compare. Though, I'm trying to learn to cook more. I attempted a roast chicken last weekend… Oh? And how did that go? Let's just say the smoke alarm got a good workout. It was… slightly charred. Very slightly. Slightly? I bet the dog thought it was Christmas! He was very interested in the aftermath, yes. I think he secretly enjoys the drama. Well, practice makes perfect, love. Your grandma was a terrible cook when she first started. Burned everything to a crisp. But she persevered and eventually became legendary for her apple pie.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just a disaster. He insisted on making a ‘potion’ in the garden, using everything he could find. Apparently, it needed ‘essence of slug’ which, thankfully, he didn’t manage to acquire. Oh, teenagers! They’re all a bit mad, aren’t they? Mine did something similar with glitter and washing-up liquid when they were fourteen. The bathroom was sparkling for weeks, but scrubbing it up wasn’t fun. What was this potion  for  anyway? Apparently, it was to… enhance his gaming skills. He read something online. Honestly, I spend half my life apologising to the neighbours for his antics. He got detention last week, you know, for disrupting Mr. Henderson’s history lesson. Something about making fart noises with his armpit. Oh dear. Henderson’s a good teacher, a bit strict, but fair. Sounds like your Jamie’s got a bit of energy to burn. Is he still seeing much of Chloe? I haven't seen her cycling past lately. They’re… complicated. They had a big row last weekend about something involving TikTok and a boy called Ben. He's not speaking to her at the moment. Teenage drama is exhausting! It’s just… with everything else going on, it feels like a lot. Everything else? Is your mum alright? You sounded a bit down when I spoke to you last week. It’s… the biopsy results came back. It’s cancer. Breast cancer. They caught it early, thankfully, so the prognosis is good, but… the operation is next Thursday. I'm trying to be strong for her but truthfully, I’m terrified. Oh, Sarah. That’s awful. I’m so sorry to hear that. Truly. That must be… overwhelming. You’re a good daughter, always have been. She’s lucky to have you. Is there anything  I  can do? Honestly, anything at all? I could pop in more, help with shopping, whatever. That’s really kind of you, Carol. Honestly, just knowing you're here… it helps. Mum’s being incredibly stoic about it all, which is her way, but I know she's scared. I'm trying to sort out everything work-wise. I’ve got a huge client meeting on the Friday, and I’m trying to see if I can reschedule, but Mr. Davies is being a nightmare. He thinks everything revolves around him. Men! Always the same. Don’t let him push you around.

…and honestly, the bloke nearly tipped me a fiver for just  remembering  his order. A fiver! For a pint of lager and a packet of crisps. You wouldn’t get that in a fancy cocktail bar, would ya? It's all about knowing your regulars, innit? A fiver  is  good though, isn’t it? Especially for just being nice. Though, I’m picturing the type. Probably the same one who tries to tell you long, complicated stories about his prize-winning marrow. Oh, you’ve met ‘em. They’re  all  like that. Old man Henderson, he’s the worst. He’ll hold court at the bar all evening, detailing the growth cycle of his tomatoes. And then complain the beer’s not cold enough. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I need a degree in horticulture to serve him properly. Which, ironically, is more use than my Masters degree at the moment. Tell me about it. Philosophy degree and I’m…well, I’m applying for jobs stacking shelves at Tesco. It feels a bit…deflating. What  is  a Masters in Existentialism even good for, realistically? Don’t be like that! You’re clever, you’ll find something. It’s just… the job market's a right mess at the minute. At least you're thinking about what you  want  to do, even if it's not glamorous. I just fell into bartending after uni. Needed the money, and it was easy enough. Didn't exactly plan on spending my evenings smelling of stale beer and cleaning up spilled shots. Easy money is still money, though. And you're good at it. You’ve got that…natural charm. People warm to you. I tried a bar job over the summer, for like, two weeks, and I was awful. I just couldn’t remember what everyone ordered. Kept bringing people the wrong drinks. It was a disaster. Aye, you need a good memory. It’s like a mental filing system. And thick skin. You get all sorts. Last night, a hen do came in. Absolute chaos. One of ‘em tried to pay with a loyalty card from a different pub! Oh my god! That's brilliant! Honestly, working’s so weird. You never know what you're going to get. My mum keeps going on about me becoming a teacher. Says it’s a stable job with good benefits. Your mum’s got a point, but is it what  you  want?

…and honestly, the all-inclusive thing is the only way to go with the kids. Otherwise, it’s just constant requests for ice cream and complaints about sand. Did you get anywhere booked for August, Brenda? You were saying something about maybe Spain? Aye, well, Spain  was  the plan. But then I started lookin’ at prices and…oof. It’s gone mad, hasn’t it? Everything’s gone up. So, we’re thinkin’ Blackpool now. Blackpool? Oh, that’s grand! Don’t be knockin’ Blackpool. Good old seaside fun. Though it’s not quite the Costa del Sol, is it? I haven’t had a proper holiday in…oh, goodness me, it must be three years now. Just day trips to Chester, you know? Lovely city, Chester. Chester  is  nice. I did a training course down there a few years back. Though, I’m looking at something a bit more… adventurous. Thinking of hiking in the Dolomites. Dolomites? Cor, ambitious! You and your fancy holidays, David. Last time you went ‘adventurous’ you came back with a sprained ankle and a story about a rogue goat. A slight exaggeration, Mark. It was a particularly determined goat. And the view was worth it! Besides, I’m fitter now. I’ve been doing Pilates. Pilates, eh? Sounds…relaxin’. I need somethin’ a bit more lively. My grandson, little Tommy, he’s obsessed with pirates. So Blackpool it is, then. Pirate shows, arcades, the lot. It'll keep him entertained, at least. Oh, pirates! There’s a lovely little folk song about a pirate, I’ll have to remember the words for you. It's a bit bawdy, mind you, so maybe not for Tommy! It goes… Oh dear, it’s gone right out of my head. Age, you know. It’s a thief. Don't worry about it, Mary. My memory’s going the same way. I spent ten minutes this morning looking for my glasses… while wearing them. Classic. It happens to the best of us. I'm trying to combat it by learning Italian, for the Dolomites trip. Apparently, it’s good for your brain. “Ciao,” I’ve mastered. That’s about it thus far. Italian, eh? Well, good luck with that. I once tried learnin’ French for a holiday in Paris. All I managed to pick up was ‘Où est la toilette?’ Which, to be fair, was pretty useful. That’s a good one!

Honestly, this is painful to watch. Absolutely  painful . They’re playing like they’ve never even  seen  a football before. Come on, now. It’s only half-time. Plenty of time for them to pull it back. You’re being a bit harsh, aren't you? They’re up against a pretty solid defence. Harsh? Harsh?! They’ve had, like,  two  shots on target all game! And both were deflected! It’s…it’s just frustrating. You'd think with the money they spend… Money doesn't buy you skill, love. Though it certainly buys you a lot of questionable haircuts, looking at their striker. What  is  that? Did he do it himself? Probably. Typical. He thinks he's a superstar. Honestly, I miss the days when football was…grittier. Less about the celebrity, more about the actual playing. Remember when we used to go to Roker Park? Proper atmosphere. Oh, Roker Park! Now  that  was a football ground. You could feel the history practically seeping out of the stands. Packed like sardines, screaming your lungs out…much more authentic than these soulless, all-seater stadiums. Though, admittedly, my knees appreciate the seats these days. Old age, eh? Don't even start. You're not  old . Just…seasoned. Besides, the atmosphere at the Stadium of Light is decent enough. Though it’s not the same. It’s never going to be the same. Speaking of decent enough...are you ordering anything? I'm starving. This tension is seriously working up an appetite. I was thinking about it. Fancy a cheeky takeaway? Been craving a proper greasy burger all day. A  proper  greasy burger? From where? Not that pretentious burger place near the market, I hope. They charge fifteen quid for a tiny thing and it’s still lukewarm. No, no, definitely not there. I was thinking…Five Guys? Or maybe even a McDonald's. Sometimes you just  need  a McDonald's, you know? It's a comfort thing. Oh, you’re speaking my language now. McDonald’s. A McChicken Meal, large fries, and a Galaxy Caramel. Don’t judge me. Judge you? Never! That’s a solid order. A classic. Although, I’m leaning towards a Big Mac. It’s been  ages . And a McFlurry, definitely a McFlurry. Oreo, obviously. Oreo is the only acceptable McFlurry flavour. Anything else is just…wrong. You know, sometimes I think our shared love of terrible fast food is the foundation of this entire relationship.

…and honestly, the client just kept adding scope creep. It started as a simple website update, right? Now they want a fully integrated e-commerce platform with, get this, augmented reality features for browsing the products. Augmented reality! For garden gnomes. Garden gnomes with augmented reality, you say? Well, I never. In my day, a garden gnome was just a garden gnome. Painted concrete, maybe a little chipped paint. That was excitement enough. Oh, Mum, you and your stories. Honestly, it  is  a bit much, though, isn’t it, David? People want everything instantly, and they want it fancy. It’s the same in sales, you know. No one wants a sensible saloon anymore, it’s all SUVs and electric everything. Exactly! It's exhausting trying to manage expectations. And the budget hasn’t even  remotely  adjusted to accommodate all these 'essential' additions. I’m pulling my hair out. I swear, I’m considering a career change. Maybe become a gnome sculptor. Less tech, more concrete. You’d be good with your hands, lad. Your grandfather was a dab hand at fixing things. Though I remember the time he tried to build a bird table… looked more like a leaning tower of Wigan, it did. Oh, Grandad! He was a character. Remember the Morris Minor he had, Mum? That thing was constantly breaking down. He’d spend more time under the bonnet than driving it! My first car was a disaster, actually. An old Fiesta. The exhaust fell off on the M6. Had to pull over and wait for the AA. Humiliating. I’ve learned my lesson though - always get the extended warranty. Warranties are a good idea. Though nothing lasts like a good, solid bit of engineering. Everything's so disposable these days. Remember when things were  made  to last? Your Auntie Margaret's washing machine… that was still going strong when she moved into the bungalow! Speaking of Auntie Margaret, are we still going to her for Christmas dinner this year? I know she’s not been feeling too well. I spoke to her last week. She’s much brighter now, said she's determined to host. She was complaining about the price of turkey though! Said she’s thinking of doing a goose instead. A goose? Now  that's  a proper Christmas dinner. A nice, fat goose with roast potatoes and gravy... mmm. Though a bit messy, I remember.

…and honestly, Leo, another bite. Just  one  more. It’s not going anywhere. It’s a perfectly good pancake! But it looks like a face, Mummy! A grumpy face! It  is  a grumpy face! Look, the blueberry is its eye. Right. Well, grumpy pancakes need to be defeated, don’t they? By being eaten. Come on, tiny warrior. Just a little bit. How was assembly today, you two? Anything exciting? Miss Davies showed us the shiny globe! And said people live  all  over it! And Finley fell over trying to sing! He landed on Ben! Oh dear! Well, that sounds… memorable. Did anyone in your class bring in pancakes for show and tell? No. Thomas brought a rock. A  big  rock! He said his grandad found it. A rock, huh? Still, good for Thomas. We're going to the Science Museum on Saturday, remember? I booked tickets. So you can see  real  rocks – and lots of other amazing things. Yay! Can we go to the shop afterwards? We'll see. Depends on how good you two are at remembering to wash your hands after touching everything! Honestly, the germs… it’s a constant battle. I washed my hands after playing with the playdough! Good boy. You are a very conscientious germ-fighter. Speaking of battles… I had a really upsetting conversation with Mrs. Peterson today, at school. Who’s Mrs. Peterson? She’s a teaching assistant. And she was telling me about some of the children in her class… families who really struggle. Some of them don’t always have enough to eat. It just breaks your heart, doesn’t it? Especially when you're trying to get kids to eat a pancake and they're making faces! It feels silly to complain about a little bit of fussiness when… well, you know. Why don’t they have any food? It’s… complicated, darling. Sometimes grown-ups don't have enough money to buy food for their families. It's not their fault, and lots of people try to help. We're very lucky, aren't we? We have lots of pancakes! We do. And that’s something to be thankful for. Right, enough serious talk. So, Science Museum on Saturday. And then, I was thinking… maybe a trip to the beach on Sunday if the weather holds? The beach! Can we build a sandcastle? A really, really big one? With moats!

…and honestly, the sweet and sour pork is  nothing  like Mrs. Li’s used to make. It’s just… gloopy. Remember how she’d get that perfect crispy coating? This is just… sauce-logged. You’re being harsh, Elara. It’s decent enough takeaway. And after lugging all those soil samples back from the farm today, ‘decent enough’ is all I need. My back is screaming. He’s right, Elara. Stop comparing everything to Mrs. Li’s. She was a culinary genius, we all know. It’s a losing battle. Plus, this spring roll is actually really good. Did you order enough prawn crackers? Fine. But Mrs. Li’s was legendary. It’s just… everything feels a bit… muted lately. Even the food. Speaking of muted, did you see the news about Old Man Hemmings? Hemmings? From down the road? The one who always complained about my tractor noise? That’s the one. Apparently, he passed away peacefully in his sleep. The funeral’s next week. Oh, wow. That’s… sad. He was a grumpy sod, but you didn’t wish that on anyone. Remember when he threatened to report us to the council because he thought the sheep were plotting against his prize-winning marrows? Oh God, yes! And you, Leo, spent a good hour trying to explain to him that sheep aren’t strategically minded enough for vegetable warfare. They are surprisingly clever, actually. Don't underestimate ovine intelligence. But yes, that was a surreal conversation. Still, it’s a shame. Even grumpy people leave a hole. It is. Makes you think, doesn't it? Life’s just… fragile. I was talking to Sarah – my old housemate from uni – yesterday and she’s completely re-evaluated everything after her grandma passed. Thinking about moving to Australia. Australia? That’s a big leap. Is she okay? She always seemed pretty grounded. She's processing. Apparently, Grandma always said Australia held the secret to eternal happiness. It's a bit… Bob the Builder-esque, honestly. “Can we fix it? Yes we can!… in Australia!” Oh, Elara! You’re terrible! But seriously, that's tough. Losing a grandparent hits hard. It does. My Nan was my rock. Spend as much time with your family as you can, that's what I always say. Speaking of time… anyone fancy catching a film later? That new sci-fi one’s been getting good reviews.

…and honestly, Mrs. Higgins next door, she’s started putting little gnomes  everywhere . It’s becoming a bit of an obsession. She asked me yesterday if I thought they needed tiny little hats for the winter. Tiny hats! Gnomes, eh? Reminds me of Old Man Hemmings in Wolverhampton. He had a garden full of them, all facing the street, like a little army. Said they were guarding his prize-winning dahlias. Dahlias! He was a stickler for those. Oh, I love a good dahlia. Though I’m more of a rose person, myself. It’s amazing what people get passionate about, isn’t it? Though the gnomes sound…intense. Intense is putting it mildly! She’s talking about building them a miniature village. Honestly, it’s like living next door to a fairy tale. Did you hear from Uncle George about his trip to Italy? He was going on about the food. George and his food. Always has been. Remember when he tried to make paella at your Aunt Mildred's house? Nearly burnt the kitchen down. Used all the saffron she had – the woman barely used a spice in her life! Oh, yes! And then he swore it tasted “just like Barcelona”. Aunt Mildred was furious. She’d saved that saffron for a special occasion, apparently. A special occasion involving… bland English cooking, probably. He sent me pictures of all the pasta he ate. Mountains of it. He’s convinced Italian drivers are the worst he’s ever encountered, though. Says they ‘have no respect for lane discipline.’ Lane discipline! Hmph. Back in my day, lane discipline meant staying on the road at all. These new drivers… they’re all glued to their phones, I wager. Though I hear tell of these driverless cars now. Can you imagine? Letting a  machine  drive you? It's… a thought. Part of the psychological study I’m involved with actually touches on that. Public trust in AI and automated systems. They're showing us videos of driverless cars making ethical decisions in accident scenarios. It’s quite disturbing, actually. Ethical decisions? What, like choosing who to run over? That's terrifying! Essentially, yes. It forces you to confront some very uncomfortable questions. They’re hoping to gauge how people react to that kind of responsibility being outsourced. They asked me about air travel safety, surprisingly. Air travel! Don't even get me started.

…and honestly, the glitter is  everywhere . Honestly, Leo, you look like you’ve been hugging a unicorn. It  is  sparkly! I’m a dragon! A glittery dragon! Mine’s better! Mine has scales  and  wings! See? Oh, wow, Elsie, that  is  impressive. Very detailed scales. Are those… planets in the background? Uh-huh! Dragons fly to space! And they eat noodles! And dumplings! Grandpa makes the best dumplings. He does, doesn’t he? Right, dumplings are a must for Chinese New Year. We’re having a proper feast on Saturday, you two remember? Spring rolls, noodles, maybe even try to make some potstickers. Can we help make the spring rolls? I can fold them! You can definitely help. Though maybe not the frying part. That’s Mummy’s job. Speaking of which, has anyone practiced their piano today? I did a little bit. Mr. Henderson says I need to remember to keep my wrist straight. It’s  hard . It is hard, sweetheart. It takes practice. And Elsie, you promised me half an hour after lunch. But I want to finish my dragon! It needs fire! You can add fire  after  piano. It’s important to keep up with your lessons. Just like Leo and his drum lessons. Drumming's awesome! I can do a really loud boom now!  makes drumming noises  I believe it! Though perhaps save the ‘really loud booms’ for your lesson, eh? We don't want to scare the neighbours. You two have so much energy. It’s exhausting just watching you. Mummy, can we watch 'Barbie and the Great Adventure' tonight? The one with the dragons and the horses? Hmm, maybe. If you’ve both been good and finished your practicing. It's a bit long, though. Perhaps after Chinese New Year we can have a movie night specifically for it. I want to learn aerial hoop like Isla! She can do amazing things. Isla  is  very good, isn’t she? It looks a bit scary to me, to be honest. We'll see. It's expensive, and we need to think about it. It’s good you’re trying new things though. That’s what Chinese New Year is about, isn't it? New beginnings, fresh starts. What does Chinese New Year mean? Well, it’s a celebration of the Lunar New Year. It’s a bit like our new year, but it follows the moon.

… honestly, the gelato was worth the slightly dodgy directions. That little place near the Pantheon? Proper good. Better than anything you get back home, yeah? Absolutely! Though, Mum’s been trying to perfect her own gelato recipe since we got back from Italy last time. She’s convinced she can replicate it. It’s… ambitious. Your mum’s always ambitious, love. Remember that time she decided to breed alpacas? Oh god, don’t remind me. The smell… the spitting… It was a whole thing. Honestly, Rome’s already less chaotic than that was. You guys are killin’ me. Alpacas? Seriously? I’m still trying to wrap my head around the sheer  history  here. It’s just… everywhere. Like, walking down the street and thinking, ‘Someone important probably walked this exact same patch of cobblestone two thousand years ago.’ Freaky. It is, isn't it? Though, I'm starting to miss a proper cuppa. The coffee's amazing, don't get me wrong, but sometimes you just need a milky builder's brew. You’re telling me! I’ve been searching for a decent full English all week. Found a place that  claims  to do it, but it was more like… a vaguely British-themed breakfast. The black pudding was an insult. Well, you should have asked me! I did my research. There's a little place near our AirBnB, run by a bloke from Manchester. He does a proper fry-up. Bit pricey, but worth it for a taste of home. Speaking of the AirBnB, how are you two finding it? Mine's a bit of a trek from here, but it's got a gorgeous view of the Colosseum. Ours is lovely, actually. Bit smaller than the photos suggested, classic AirBnB, but really central. Though the host… a bit  too  enthusiastic about recommending local restaurants. Followed us down the street yesterday offering to make reservations. Ah, the overbearing Italian host. A time-honoured tradition. Mine’s thankfully left us to it. He just kept pointing at a map and saying “Bella! Bella!” and making hand gestures. Didn’t understand a word. Yeah, the language barrier's been interesting. I figured I’d pick up a few phrases, but it’s way more complex than I thought. They speak so fast! And every region has a different accent, right? I tried ordering a beer yesterday and I swear the barman thought I was asking him to marry his daughter.

…and honestly, the glitter  everywhere . I’m still finding it in the vacuum cleaner. It was worth it though, seeing Sarah's face when she opened the personalised sash. Though, next time, less glitter. Definitely less glitter. Oh god, glitter is the bane of my existence. My flat still hasn’t forgiven me for helping with Chloe’s banner. It was sparkly nautical themed, naturally. But seriously, Sarah’s hen do sounded amazing. You really went all out. It did. I saw the pictures online. The cupcake decorating looked particularly ambitious. Did you bake them all yourself, Ella? Largely! I mean, I got the basic sponge from a local bakery – sanity, you know? - but all the icing, the decorations, the little edible pearls… that was all me. It took a solid two days. I nearly lost my mind piping roses. I’m much better at spreadsheets, honestly. That's why I'm an administrator. You’re a saint, Ella. I admire your patience. I’m coordinating Amelia's hen, and I’m leaning more towards booking a weekend away, something less…craft intensive. I’m already stressed thinking about it! A weekend away is a good shout, Liv. Less pressure, more fun. Where were you thinking? I was looking at Brighton. It’s easy enough for everyone to get to, and there's loads going on. Plus, we could do that cocktail-making class Amelia’s been talking about for ages. Brighton sounds perfect! Loads of cute shops too, if anyone needs a little retail therapy. It's so hard to please everyone, though, isn’t it? Amelia's quite…specific with her tastes. Tell me about it. She’s already vetoed anything involving a bouncy castle  and  anything remotely embarrassing. Which basically rules out half the hen do options. Oh dear. That sounds…challenging. Sarah was the opposite. Up for anything, as long as there was cake involved. It makes things so much easier. Although, I did have to subtly dissuade her from thinking a full-on medieval reenactment was a good idea. A medieval reenactment?! Seriously? She’d been watching  Outlander . It was a phase. Luckily, a few strategically chosen images of pretty floral arrangements did the trick. Now, back to Amelia’s hen… Liv, have you asked Amy and Jess what they’d be up for? They’re Amelia’s oldest friends. I have, actually. Amy’s totally on board with Brighton.

… honestly, I reckon I’ve had better nights. This lurgy’s really knocked me for six, hasn’t it? Feel proper rough. You do look it, mate. Pale as a ghost. And you’ve been moaning since you woke up. Is it just a cold, or do you think it’s something worse? You were saying yesterday you felt achy all over. Achy’s an understatement. It felt like someone had been using my body as a punching bag. I think it’s just a really bad cold, yeah? But it felt like the flu for a minute there. I nearly cancelled coming round, but I promised I’d help you with this lasagne. Glad you did, actually. I’m absolutely rubbish in the kitchen without a second pair of hands. And honestly, lying in bed feeling sorry for yourself isn’t going to make it better. Chicken soup is, though. That's why we’re making lasagne – comfort food central! Plus, I’m testing out a new béchamel recipe. Important stuff. Important stuff indeed. Right, what do you want me to do? Chop more onions? Because if you say chop more onions, I might actually lie down and give up. No, no more onions for you, poor lamb. How about grating the cheese? That's low-effort, high-reward. Plus, you can just sit at the table. Speaking of rewards… remember that hotel we stayed in in Barcelona last year? The one with the breakfast buffet? Oh,  that  hotel. The one where you ate approximately your weight in croissants every morning? Vaguely. I was still recovering from the dodgy paella incident, remember? Okay, okay, fair point. But the cheese selection! It was incredible. Proper mature cheddar, brie, even some weird Spanish goat cheese I couldn’t pronounce. This cheese is… functional. It’ll melt, but it's not exactly a culinary experience. Look, I'm too ill to appreciate nuanced cheese profiles, alright? Just point me towards the grater. Honestly though, Barcelona was brilliant. We  need  another trip. Somewhere warmer preferably. Definitely no paella. Agreed on both counts. Maybe Italy? I've always wanted to go to Florence. We could do a cookery course while we’re there. Honestly, learning to make proper pasta from scratch is on my bucket list. Florence sounds… ambitious. Maybe something a bit more laid-back? Like, the Greek islands? Sun, sea, gyros… and you can practice your Greek on the locals.

…and honestly, Doreen, I’m starting to think I need a list just to  remember  what I need from the shops these days. It’s not like when we were girls and Mum just sent us with a pound and said ‘get what you need’. A pound! Goodness me, those were the days. You could get a proper bag of sweets for a pound then. Though I suppose we mostly spent it on comics. Speaking of lists, have you got a card for young Thomas’s birthday? He’s turning… well, how  old  is he turning now? Seven. Seven on Tuesday. And yes, I have a card, but I’m wrestling with what to write. It feels so silly putting ‘To Thomas, age 7’ on it. Like stating the obvious! Do you still do that? I did when my students were little, but then I thought, ‘they know how old they are, don’t they?’ It just feels a bit… patronising. I usually just write a lovely message. Though, you know, Mrs. Higgins always insisted on it. Said it was important for their record-keeping. Old habits die hard, I suppose. Mrs. Higgins! Oh lord. Remember how she used to make us do those awful felt tip pictures? All scratchy and uneven. I was hopeless at art. Hopeless? You were always quite good, actually. You had a better eye for colour than I did. I was all about the numbers, remember? Always adding up the sweets in our lunchboxes. Though, goodness, the things they do now at primary school. They had a pottery club at Leo’s last term, and he came home covered in clay every week. It’s a world away from stick men and colouring inside the lines, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking about getting those little calendar fobs, you know, the ones with pictures for each month? For the grandchildren. Oh, that’s a nice idea! Where did you have in mind getting them from? I saw some at that little craft fair last week. They had some lovely ones of animals. Reminded me of the wildlife club we had at school. Utter chaos, that was. Mr. Davies ended up chasing a escaped ferret around the playground! Oh, I'd forgotten about Mr. Davies and the ferret! The stories that man could tell! You know, talking about schools… it makes me think about Leo choosing his university courses.

…and honestly, the sheer  noise  of it all, after Southend. It's not the sea air, that's for sure. More like tractors and sheep. Though, I suppose, it's a good sort of noise, isn't it? A  living  sort of noise. It is different, Dad. Very different. But nice, generally. Old Man Hemmings next door is a bit…intense about his prize-winning marrows, though. He actually stopped me admiring them yesterday and launched into a twenty-minute lecture on slug pellets. Oh, Devon farmers. They’re a breed apart, aren’t they? We’ve got Mrs. Treloar the other side, lovely woman, always bringing round eggs. Real free-range, you can practically see them running around in her garden. Eggs! That’s the spirit! I was worried we'd be stuck with supermarket eggs forever. Though, I'm still trying to figure out the train situation. I thought Devon was supposed to be idyllic, but getting to Exeter is a  nightmare . Delayed signals, single tracks… reminds me of my commute back in the day, and that was supposed to be London! They are improving things slowly. There’s talk of dualling the line, but…well, talk is cheap. It’s okay if you’re going into the city for a bit of shopping, but if you need to be somewhere on time, it's best to drive. And even  that  can be slow on those little country lanes. Speaking of shopping, have you managed to find a good butcher yet, dear? I told you about Harries in Hatherleigh, didn't I? Proper Devon beef, they get it all locally. Not yet, haven't had a chance to properly explore. Been mostly occupied with trying to assemble that flat-pack bookcase. Honestly, for a management consultant, I'm appalling at DIY. Spent half an hour trying to put a shelf on upside down. Dad! Classic. I offered to help, remember? You insisted you could handle it. I’m a man of pride, Eleanor! Besides, I didn't want you to think I was completely useless in my retirement. This course I’m doing…well, it's keeping my brain ticking, but it doesn’t translate to bookcase construction, apparently. Honestly, it's on local history, fascinating stuff about Dartmoor myths and legends. They say there's a spectral hound that roams the moors… Oh, the Hound of the Baskervilles territory!

… honestly, I don't know  why  I bother looking anymore. Another application, another automated rejection email. It’s like they don’t even read 'em, ya know? Just…  ping … 'thanks but no thanks'. Sounds about right, Liam. It's brutal out there, even for people  trying  to work. Though, to be fair, applying for "Professional Biscuit Tester" probably wasn’t the most…strategic move. Alright, alright, laugh it up. It was a joke application! Gave me somethin’ to  do  for twenty minutes. Besides, who wouldn’t want to test biscuits? It’s a valuable skill! Valuable to who, Liam? The biscuit industry? Look, have you seen that new telly advert? The one with the dog doing parkour? It’s brilliant. Much more productive than dwelling on biscuit-related career paths. Parkour dog, eh? Sounds… distracting. I’ve been down a rabbit hole of online shopping, trying to feel productive, and it's just made me realise I have absolutely nowt I  need . Just a load of stuff I…  might  need. Oh, don’t tell me you’ve been looking at those ridiculous gaming chairs again? The ones that look like they belong on the bridge of the Starship Enterprise? Worse. Robotic vacuum cleaners. Apparently, they’re ‘life-changing’. I was seriously considering one. Imagine, no more hoovering! Then I remembered… we don’t have carpets. Just laminate. It would just push dust around. Oh, Liam. You’re a disaster. Seriously though, maybe you should try focusing on things you  can  do. Online stuff, like freelance writing or… I don't know. Something you used to enjoy at uni? Enjoy? Uni feels like a different lifetime. It was all essays and pretending to understand post-structuralism. Now it’s just… endless scrolling and applying for jobs I'm massively overqualified for, or woefully underqualified for. And frankly, I'm starting to forget how to  be  a person. You’re being dramatic. You're still very much a person. A slightly cynical, biscuit-obsessed, robot vacuum cleaner-contemplating person, but a person nonetheless. Thanks, that's… reassuringly insulting. What are you looking at on your phone anyway? More study notes? Still aiming for top marks in History, then? Yeah, trying to. Mock exams are looming. But also… I was just looking at flights. Cheap ones. For like… October. Flights? Where to? Don’t tell me you’re planning a secret getaway without me.

…and honestly, the central heating’s a bit temperamental, isn’t it? Keeps dropping out. I’ve been messing with the thermostat, but I reckon it needs a proper look at. Remember old Mr. Henderson from the estate? Said the whole system's ancient. Proper Victorian guts under modern casing, he reckoned. Oh dear. That doesn't sound good, especially with the weather turning. You'll be needing layers! I'm making a quick lunch, fancy a toasted sandwich? Got some lovely cheddar and ham. It’ll warm you up while you contemplate the heating crisis. Cheddar and ham sounds lovely, darling. Toasties are the perfect fuel for planning. Speaking of planning, are we still on for that walk on Saturday? I’ve been checking the tide times for Hartland Quay – you want to be careful there, that path gets awfully close to the edge. Definitely the walk. Need to stretch the legs after all this unpacking. And Hartland Quay sounds brilliant. Bit bracing, mind. Should I bring my old Barbour? It’s seen better days, but it’s still waterproof… mostly. It’s probably older than some of the houses around here, that jacket. My dad bought it in… oh, 1988, I think. Mum, you said that about your shoes last week! Everything's "older than the houses around here" with you. The Barbour's fine. I’ll wear my waterproofs too. We’ll be grand. Have you thought about what furniture you’re after for the living room? We need to make a list before we go to that place near Okehampton. Yes! A proper comfy sofa is top of the list. Something you can really sink into. And maybe a new coffee table? The one you’ve got at the moment is… functional. Let’s be kind. Functional is a polite word for ‘inherited from Aunt Mabel and slightly wobbly’, isn’t it? I’ve been browsing online, seeing what’s about. Everything seems ridiculously expensive these days. Feels like I’m back managing budgets, but without the paycheque! Tell me about it! Everything is… inflated. We saw a nice sofa at that place last month, but it was way over budget. Perhaps we should look at second-hand options? There are some good antique shops around here. That's a good idea. We might find something with character, and save a bit of money. Speaking of savings, have you remembered to book your Christmas haircut, darling?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of revisions they wanted on that grant proposal was ridiculous. It felt like they wanted a whole new project, not just tweaks! It’s just… exhausting. Three months of work basically chipped away at by someone who clearly wasn't even  reading  the methodology properly. Oh, no, really? That sounds awful, Tom. You put so much into those, I know you do. Was it Dr. Ainsworth again? She’s notoriously picky, isn’t she? Worse, actually. It was Dr. Harding. Ainsworth at least offers  constructive  criticism, even if it's brutal. Harding just… pointed out things that weren't true, then asked me to address them. It was maddening. I spent all evening yesterday re-writing the section on participant recruitment, because he claimed it didn't account for potential biases, when it explicitly did! Good grief. That's just… undermining. You'd think someone in his position would at least try to understand the work before demanding changes. How are you feeling about it now? Still submitting? I have to. It's too late to pull it. Rejection stings, but not submitting at all feels worse. Plus, if I don’t get  something  funded soon, the lab’s going to be in a tricky position. They’re relying on me to bring in the cash. Speaking of tricky positions, how was your day at work? Anything exciting happening in the world of GCSE assessments? Exciting is… a strong word. Mostly just parents emailing, convinced their darling child was  robbed  by the marking scheme. Apparently, a 7 isn’t good enough these days. Everyone wants a 9. It’s exhausting on a different scale, honestly. The emotional labour of dealing with all that… Right? It’s the same with research. People think it's all intellectual stimulation, but a huge part of it is just managing expectations and dealing with…well, people. Did you manage to get through to Mrs. Peterson? She was the one who emailed about her son, wasn't she? Eventually. Took three phone calls and a very carefully worded email explaining the moderation process. She was convinced he lost marks because of the handwriting, not the content. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if they think we just sit here making up grades. It's baffling. Still, you’re good at that stuff. You have a knack for diffusing situations. I’d be completely lost.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of Mr. Henderson’s cat, walking across Mrs. Peterson’s prize-winning begonias! She was absolutely fuming. Said it looked like a feline assault course. Old Mrs. Peterson. Everything's a drama with her. Though, cats  will  be cats, won't they? Reminds me of Buster, our terrier when we first got him. He dug up half the garden trying to get at a mole. Speaking of animals doing chaotic things, did you see that video online of the goat on the roof? It was brilliant. Just…completely unconcerned, munching on the shrubbery. Goats are mental, innit? Proper little mountain climbers, those things. Makes you wonder what goes on in their heads. More than can be said for some humans I know. Oh, leave ‘em alone, Dave! They’re just trying to get by. You were a bit of a handful yourself when you were younger, weren’t you? Remember that time you ‘re-decorated’ your mum’s wallpaper with felt tip? That was one time! And it was a very vibrant shade of blue. Artistic licence, I call it. Besides, it was awful wallpaper to begin with. Floral, can you believe it? Oh, you and your aversion to florals. It’s legendary. Though ironically, your Auntie Mabel  loved  floral wallpaper. Remember her sitting room? It was a riot of roses and chintz. And the smell of lavender potpourri! That woman could overpower a room just by walking into it. She was a character, though. Always had a story to tell. Speaking of stories, anyone heard from Emily lately? Haven't seen her post anything on Facebook in a week. I texted her yesterday, she's been swamped with work. Big deadline looming. Apparently, a client wants a complete re-write of their marketing campaign. Stressful stuff. She said she's living on coffee and biscuits. Poor thing. She needs to look after herself. Being a copywriter sounds glamorous but it must be draining. It’s like nursing, really. You give and give and give until you're completely depleted. It is. And the emotional toll. It really gets to you sometimes. Which reminds me, have we talked about the rota for next month yet? I'm hoping for fewer night shifts. My sleep schedule is completely messed up. I've had a look, Sarah. It’s a bit tight. But I’ve managed to swap one of your nights with David.

…and honestly, the parmo was  huge . Like, genuinely, I couldn’t finish it. It’s a Sunderland thing, you know? Breaded chicken or pork, covered in béchamel, then cheese. It’s…an experience. Parmo, you say? Sounds a bit… excessive, doesn’t it? We had things like steak and kidney pie when I were a lad. Proper hearty stuff. Not all this… coating. Sounds amazing, actually. A bit like a fancy chicken Kiev, maybe? I’ve been trying to branch out with my cooking lately, less ‘engineered nutrition’ and more… actual flavour. I made a proper roast the other weekend, Yorkshire puddings and everything. Took all day. It's nothing like a Kiev, Liam! It's on another level. You’d need a knife and fork to tackle one properly. And a lie-down afterwards. Dad, you’ve never had a parmo, have you? Never. Manchester wasn’t known for its… northern soul food, I suppose. More chips and gravy, if we were lucky. Though, my mother, God rest her, could whip up a trifle that would make you weep. Layers upon layers of sponge and custard. Trifle  is  a classic. My nan used to make a fantastic one, but she always used sherry. A bit much for a Tuesday afternoon, if you ask me. Oh, Dad! Tuesday afternoon sherry sounds perfectly reasonable! Anyway, you were telling me about your trip to Italy last year, weren't you? You were going on about the pasta. Italy. Lovely place. Went with Betty, before… well, before she got poorly. Florence, Rome, Venice. Beautiful. The pasta  was  good. Simple, you know? Just tomatoes, basil, a bit of olive oil. Nothing fancy. They don’t muck about with things over there. It wasn’t like some of the… creations you get served these days. I spent a month in Rome last year, actually, working on a structural assessment of some old buildings. It's incredible how much history is just  built  into the place. The food was… intense. I lived on pizza and gelato, pretty much. My waistline suffered slightly. You and me both, Liam. I went to Barcelona for a conference last spring. Tapas, paella, sangria… it was a culinary disaster zone, but a brilliant one. Have you ever been, Dad? Barcelona? Never made it to Barcelona. Not a travelling man, never have been. Betty and I went to Blackpool a few times. That was exotic enough for us!

…and honestly, the student feedback on the Wordsworth seminar was…brutal. They said it felt like I was just  performing  Wordsworth, not actually  teaching  him. Can you believe it? Performing! Ouch. Harsh. Though, knowing you, you probably  were  doing your dramatic reading voice. You do love a good dramatic reading. It’s… engaging! They need to appreciate the passion! But okay, maybe a little toned down. I think I got carried away. What about your Ming Dynasty class? Did they dissect your theories on porcelain as viciously? Relatively peaceful, actually. Though young Li Wei kept asking if the emperor really did have hundreds of concubines. Kept circling back to it. Eventually, I just said, "It’s complicated," and moved on. It's not exactly in the syllabus. “It’s complicated” is the historian’s go-to answer, isn’t it? Works every time. Right, so, plans for next semester. We need to solidify this. I’m thinking of completely restructuring the Romantic Poetry module. More group work, less me…performing. Good. Honestly, less performance, more facilitated discussion. That’s the key. And I think we should coordinate a bit more on our introductory lectures. Remember last year, when half the students showed up thinking history was all about kings and queens, and the other half already knew Foucault? Don’t remind me! It was a disaster. I spent the first three weeks undoing ingrained misconceptions. Okay, coordinated intros it is. Maybe a joint lecture? “History & Literature: The Interwoven Narrative”? Bit cheesy? A little. But it gets the point across. We could frame it around a case study – Anglo-Chinese Opium War, perhaps? Plenty of literary and historical angles there. And it'd force us to actually  talk  to each other about our approaches before standing in front of a hundred students. That’s a good idea. Difficult subject matter, though. We need to be sensitive. And prepare for the inevitable “whose fault was it?” debate. Absolutely. We can acknowledge the complexities without getting bogged down in blame. It’s a starting point for critical thinking, not a historical courtroom. Speaking of starting points…I'm starving. What are we having for dinner? I was thinking maybe that little dumpling place down the road? They do a fantastic pork and chive. Dumplings sound  amazing . I’ve been craving proper dumplings all week. Though, I did buy some aubergine and that Sichuan peppercorn paste...

…and honestly, the manual is written in what I suspect is ancient Sumerian. Honestly, for a coffee machine that cost nearly two hundred quid, you’d think they could manage a simple ‘press this button’. Two hundred quid for coffee? Sounds about right for modern life. Let me have a look, Mam. Maybe I can decipher it. I’m good at untangling messes – professionally, at least. Transcribing politicians is basically the same thing. Two hundred! That’s daylight robbery. We used to get perfectly good coffee from a cafetiere. No buttons, no fuss. Just hot water and ground beans. Simpler times, eh? Simpler, definitely. But I wanted a fancy one! A treat, after all those years of chalk dust and quadratic equations. Though, truthfully, the chalk dust was less stressful than this contraption. Speaking of stressful, have you two even started to look into removal storage costs? I got a quote today and nearly choked on my tea. Ugh, don't even  mention  it. I did a quick browse and it's… grim. Especially for long-term storage. We’re talking about needing a substantial chunk of change just to keep the furniture safe while we sort things out. I’m trying to be optimistic and think we can drastically downsize, but… well, Dad, you know how you are with your tools. My tools are  essential ! You never know when you might need a spanner, a screwdriver, or… a perfectly calibrated widget calibrator! Besides, they’re investments. They’ll be worth something someday. Calibrated widget calibrators? Right. Anyway, back to the money pit. I’m starting to think we should have just burned the house down and started again. Perhaps a little dramatic, but… Mam! Don’t say that! Dramatic is an understatement. We’re trying to be practical here. Though, I do agree, the costs are… eye-watering. It feels like everything's climbing. It's all this government, honestly. Oh, here we go. Politics at breakfast. It’s never a dull moment. Well, someone has to talk sense! This Labour leadership thing is a mess. Starmer...he lacks a spark. He's all strategy and no soul. I’m not completely convinced either, to be honest. He seems… cautious. Like he’s afraid to actually  say  anything. Which isn’t exactly inspiring, is it? He's a lawyer. Caution is kind of their stock-in-trade. You need a bit of bluster, don’t you?

… honestly, calling him ‘Baz’ just feels… wrong. It’s too much of a mouthful. He  looks  like a ‘Reg’. Proper old school, y’know? Like Reginald. You're terrible, Leo! He'll hear you! And Baz is fine. More approachable than Reginald, definitely. Though, thinking about names, did you know my nan used to insist on calling anyone with blonde hair ‘Shirley’? Didn’t matter their actual name. Oh, bless her. My grandma was obsessed with rivers. Every holiday had to involve a river. The Severn? Spent a week near there. The Thames? Two weeks. She’d read out every little fact about them. Apparently the Thames has, like, forty different names throughout history. Forty? Crikey. We just call ours… well, a river. Mostly. Though out in the bush, they have these little creek names that are proper tongue-twisters. You try saying ‘Warragamba River’ five times fast. Sounds… challenging. Speaking of waterways, I saw a  beautiful  canal boat down by Limehouse Basin yesterday. Painted all vibrant colours. Makes you wonder about living on one, doesn’t it? Total freedom. Freedom and damp, probably. And trying to navigate the towpaths with a full grocery shop. No thanks. Though, I did meet a couple living on a narrowboat who were strictly kosher. Apparently, keeping kosher on a boat is a  nightmare . All the different storage, needing separate cooking equipment… It was intense. Kosher on a boat? Wow. That  is  commitment. This place is empty, isn’t it? I thought more people would have wandered in. Good for us, I guess. More space for our gossip. Anyone fancy going to a club tonight? There’s that new place in Shoreditch, ‘The Static.’ Heard good things. Shoreditch? Sounds a bit… fancy for me. I’m happy just chilling, maybe finding a pub with a good pint. Though, I’m always up for people-watching. I’m in for The Static. Been meaning to check it out. What about you, Chloe? You finishing up early at the bakery today? I knocked off a couple of hours ago. Gotta use the quiet weekdays while I can. And yes, The Static sounds good. Though, I’m warning you, I’ll be judging everyone’s condiment choices. People and their ketchup distribution are a serious matter. Ketchup distribution? What are you on about? Honestly, the amount of people who just  drown  their chips. It's an affront to culinary sensibility!

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of lads on Tinder in Chester is… startling. It’s like everyone’s on there. Back in Donny, it was slim pickings, you know? Proper slim. Tell me about it! Chester's a student town, innit? It’s a breeding ground for questionable profile pics and bios that just say ‘banter’. I swear, if I see another one that says ‘banter’… Oh, you get that everywhere! I had a lad on Bumble – Bumble’s a bit better, I reckon, slightly less… chaotic – who literally just listed his favourite takeaways. Like, that’s your personality now? Domino’s and Chinese? Riveting. See, I’ve given up on the apps completely. Too much effort. And half of them are either taking pictures with a tiger, or desperately trying to look like they go to the gym. It's exhausting. I’m with Sarah on that one. I had one ask me if I ‘liked hiking’. I live in a student house, the closest I get to hiking is walking to lectures uphill! I told him straight, said my cardio consisted of running for the last slice of pizza. Good for you! You need to be honest. I swiped right on one, seemed alright, then his opening line was… “Do you like pineapple on pizza?” Honestly! Like, that’s a dealbreaker question? Oh my god, the  audacity . That's a personality test disguised as a conversation starter. I once matched with a lad who asked me what my 'spirit animal' was. That's mental! Right, I’m changing the subject. Housemates. How’s everyone finding theirs? Because my flat is… an experience. Chloe insists on burning incense constantly, and it smells like a head shop in there. Oh, no. Mine are alright, a bit messy, but generally harmless. We have a rota for cleaning, which helps. Though, Liam still leaves his dirty socks  everywhere . It’s a passive-aggressive war zone. Ours are…loud. Like, consistently loud. They’re all doing music, and apparently, 2 am is the perfect time to practice the drums. I’m contemplating investing in earplugs. My house is surprisingly civilised. Old Mrs. Higgins owns the house, and she pops in occasionally for a cup of tea and to ‘check things are alright’. It’s a bit weird, but also keeps everyone in check. No wild parties happening on her watch. That’s brilliant! You’ve won the housemate lottery.

…and honestly, Doreen, I’m telling you, this new housing scheme they’re pushing through near Old Catton – complete madness! Building on perfectly good farmland. Where's the common sense, eh? They talk about affordable housing, but affordable for  who ? Not for folks like us, that’s for sure. They’ve been saying that for years, Arthur. Affordable this, affordable that. It’s all just words. They don't care about us lot, do they? Never have. Remember when they shut down the shoe factory? Said it wasn’t ‘viable’. Viable for  who ? Left half the village struggling. Now, now, George, don’t get yourself all worked up. It’ll only raise your blood pressure. And Arthur, you know what they’re like. Promises, promises. It’s just the way of things. Though I agree, building on farmland is a bit much. Makes you wonder where all the good soil’s going to go, doesn't it? My Gerald used to say… Your Gerald always had a sensible head on his shoulders, Doreen. Unlike these politicians. They haven’t a clue what it’s like to struggle, not a clue. I was reading in the paper about the increase in Universal Credit. Pathetic, truly pathetic. They take with one hand and give back a pittance with the other. Universal Credit… a right mess, that is. Spent an hour on the phone with them last week trying to sort out a discrepancy. An hour! Speaking to someone in India who barely understood a word I was saying. I asked for a supervisor, and then I was on hold for another twenty minutes! It’s designed to confuse you, I reckon. Just wear you down until you give up. You poor thing, George. That sounds dreadful. I’m glad I’m not dealing with that anymore. Though I did have a right palaver with them when I was claiming for a bit after Gerald passed. All those forms… it’s degrading, really. Makes you feel like a criminal. It’s all part of the plan, Doreen. Keep us occupied, filling out forms, arguing with call centres, so we don’t notice what they’re  really  up to. It’s distraction tactics, I tell you. And have you seen that chap Farage popping up on the telly again? Oh, don't even mention him. Always stirring things up. A bit of a charlatan, if you ask me.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is just…criminal. They expect us to be proactive  and  document every single interaction, down to the minute. It's exhausting! Honestly, I barely had time to breathe today. How was your day, love? Anything exciting in the world of charitable giving? Exciting? Not exactly. More… persistent. Old Mrs. Higgins called again, bless her. Still convinced she never received the acknowledgement for her donation last October. I’ve sent her three letters now, and explained it went in the post, but she’s convinced it’s been ‘lost by the system.’ You know how she is. Oh, the Higgins! That woman could find fault in a perfectly brewed cup of tea. Did you manage to calm her down this time? Eventually. Promised to pop round tomorrow with a freshly printed one. It’s a small donation, really, but you can’t just dismiss people, can you? They're giving what they can. It’s just… draining. It’s always  something . Thankfully, young Mark in the office helped chase up a larger pledge from Bellweather Industries. That was a win. Good. You need a win. This shepherd’s pie is lovely, by the way. You’ve really outdone yourself. Is it a new recipe? Just a little tweak. Added a dash of Worcestershire sauce. Makes all the difference, doesn't it? You always appreciate a good dash of Worcestershire. How was your meeting with… what was his name again? Henderson? Henderson, yes. Utterly pointless. Two hours of talking about restructuring, and all I got was a headache. They’re clearly trying to streamline, which means fewer people doing more work. Classic. Honestly, I’m beginning to think I need a holiday. Somewhere with no paperwork and absolutely no ‘restructuring’. You deserve one. We both do. Remember that little cottage in the Cotswolds we looked at online? With the roses around the door? Mmm, I do. A bit… twee, perhaps? But the thought of just  being  somewhere quiet… It’s immensely appealing. Has Sophie said anything more about university applications? She's narrowed it down to three. Bristol, York and… surprisingly, Newcastle. Newcastle? That’s a long way. I know. She says she wants to "experience something different." Apparently, all her friends are applying to places closer to home. She wants to be independent. Honestly, she’s turning into a proper little rebel. Well, that’s Sophie.

…and honestly, the sheer  grey  of it all. Cambridge is grey sometimes, of course, but it’s a… refined grey? This is just oppressive. Feels like it’s seeping into my bones. I’ve been feeling utterly wretched since I got back from the airport, actually. Not full-blown flu, just…off. Ugh, I know the feeling. Tarnow does do grey  very  well. Though, to be fair, it’s not helping that it's currently spitting with rain. You sure you didn’t pick up something on the plane? That funeral must have really taken it out of you, though. Travelling all that way… It did. Poor Aunt Margaret. Not entirely unexpected, she was 92, but still…it’s the finality, isn’t it? And yes, the travelling. Especially the airport. A petri dish, the whole lot of it. I just feel a bit…hollow. And tired. Really,  really  tired. This is why I avoid going back, you know? It’s just… a reminder of everything I  don't  have there anymore. I can imagine. So, Cambridge doesn’t really feel like ‘home’ anymore then? Even though you grew up there? It’s complicated. It looks like home. The streets, the buildings… they’re familiar. But the ‘home’ bit feels… fractured. Like looking at a photograph of a life you once lived, but can’t quite step back into. I haven’t really  lived  anywhere long enough to have a proper sense of belonging, I suppose. Tarnow feels…easier. Less expectation. That makes sense. I still feel most at home up in Bury, with Mum and Dad. But even that’s changing, you know? It’s not  my  life anymore. Everything’s… quieter. I loved teaching in Vietnam, honestly. The chaos, the energy, the sheer vibrancy of it all. That was a proper adventure. Better than anything I've done since returning. Vietnam! Oh, I saw some of your pictures on… Instagram, was it? The food looked incredible. You always did throw yourself into things. Remember when you tried to learn pottery? Oh god, don’t remind me. It was a disaster. Everything I made looked like a wonky ashtray. But that’s kind of the point, isn't it? Trying things. I think that’s why I’m starting to think about going back abroad again. Maybe somewhere in South America? I’ve been scrolling through pictures of Colombia… Colombia?

…and honestly, the brief was  wild . “Evoke nostalgia for a washing machine.” Like, how do you even  do  that? Seriously, Martha, a washing machine! Oh, you're kidding! That’s… spectacularly awful. Is that a new client? I thought you were mostly doing stuff for that outdoor gear company these days. It's a one-off. Apparently, they’re rebranding. The outdoor gear is still there, thankfully. Pays the rent. Though, even  that's  got its moments. Last week I was researching the tensile strength of tent poles for approximately six hours. Six! Hours! Sounds thrilling. Still, better than washing machine nostalgia, I reckon. I’m drowning in code at the moment, honestly. This survey programming is… mind-numbing. It’s for a study on consumer attitudes towards sustainable packaging. Very important, very dull. At least it's important. My washing machine brief felt actively detrimental to the human spirit. Speaking of important, have you heard from Chloe recently? I tried messaging her about Saturday, but no reply. No, not since she went to visit her aunt in Bristol. She mentioned the signal was patchy out there. Probably just hasn’t seen it yet. Don’t worry, she'll get back to you. She booked that aunt visit ages ago. Remember, the one she was stressing about because her aunt keeps trying to set her up with vicar’s sons? Oh God, yes. The vicar’s son situation. A fate worse than writing copy for appliances. I was hoping we could all go to Borough Market on Saturday, that new cheese stall everyone’s talking about. Oh, the one with the truffle brie? Yes! That sounds  amazing . I'd be up for that. Maybe we should text her again later? After lunch? Good idea. Actually, Borough Market reminds me – I need to actually buy food. My fridge is looking… bleak. Mostly just condiments and a wilting lettuce leaf. Oh, classic. I'm the same. I tell myself I'll meal prep, then end up living on tea and biscuits. It's a postgraduate lifestyle, I think. Convenient, but deeply unhealthy. It's a universal student-adjacent lifestyle, I’d argue. Even though I  have  graduated, my cooking skills peaked at instant noodles during finals. Have you seen the price of avocados recently? It's criminal. Don't even  start  on avocados! It’s a conspiracy. They’re deliberately inflating the price.

…and honestly, the cat was using my face as a springboard. Honestly, Pip, a full-on assault. Did either of you sleep at all? A little bit. I had a dream I was a sparkly unicorn and I was flying over a giant ice cream cone. I kept hearing noises. Thought there were monsters under my bed. Monsters, eh? Well, the cat is probably closer to a monster this morning. Right, operation breakfast. Who wants pancakes? I found that American recipe with the buttermilk…it’s supposed to be ridiculously fluffy. Pancakes! With sprinkles? Sprinkles are  always  allowed with pancakes. Ben? Pancakes a good shout? Yeah! But can we have maple syrup? Real maple syrup, not that fake stuff. Deal. Real maple syrup it is. Right, let’s get these going. While I’m doing that, we need to finalise today. Remember, Mrs. Davies asked if we could bring some biscuit donations for the school bake sale? Oh yeah! We can get the chocolate digestives. They’re my favourite. And the custard creams! Everyone loves custard creams. Excellent thinking. Okay, biscuit run after pancakes. Then… what about this afternoon? I booked tickets for that Neon Moon event at the village hall. Remember, the one with all the vintage stalls and live music? Oh, the one with the glitter? I want to wear my sparkly shoes! Is it boring? Will there be anything for  me  to do? It won’t be boring, I promise. There’s supposed to be a face painter, and often someone does a little workshop. Last time they were teaching circus skills. Circus skills?! Like juggling? I want to learn to juggle! I want to learn to walk on my hands! We'll see what they're offering. Look, I was chatting to Sarah from next door yesterday, and she was telling me all about this new circus school she’s found in Cambridge. Apparently it’s brilliant. Cool! She was using the  strangest  phrases though. She kept saying things like “No worries, mate!” and "Chuck a U-ey". I had to ask if she'd been spending too much time watching Crocodile Dundee! Turns out her brother's been living in Australia for ten years and she’s picked up all the slang. "No worries, mate?" That sounds funny! It does, doesn’t it? It’s just… odd hearing it in Comberton! Right, pancakes are almost ready.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the postal vote changes just feels like another attempt to disenfranchise people. It’s subtle, isn’t it? Not a blatant ‘you can’t vote’ but making it  harder , particularly for the elderly, or people who work long hours. You’ve hit a nerve there, Eleanor. It’s always the same song and dance, isn’t it? A little tweak here, a bit of a complication there. They call it streamlining, we call it voter suppression. Though, honestly, after years of observing politics, I’m starting to think they’re just remarkably incompetent rather than maliciously clever. Dad, you always say that. You underestimate them. They  know  exactly what they're doing. It’s all about consolidating power. It’s just… frustrating. Feels like nothing ever really changes. Your father’s a perpetual optimist, Rhys. Bless him. Though I agree with you, there’s a method to the madness, even if it’s lacking in any sort of moral compass. It reminds me of Great-Aunt Maggie, actually. Maggie? What on earth has she got to do with electoral reform? Not reform, exactly. But she had a knack for getting what she wanted by appearing utterly harmless and then subtly manipulating situations. Remember, she convinced Grandad to plant that prize-winning rose garden because she “just wanted to see pretty flowers”? She’d been subtly complaining about the lack of colour in the garden for months beforehand. Oh, Maggie! A force of nature in a floral dress. She could charm the birds from the trees, that woman. And she firmly believed she was always right, of course. Just like… well, a lot of politicians, actually. Sounds terrifying. I only met her a couple of times. Was she always like that? Always. Born and bred in Bermondsey, you see. A proper Londoner through and through. Tough as nails, but with a velvet glove. She lived through the Blitz, you know. Lost her brother in the war. I think that hardened her a bit. Everything was a battle after that. That’s right. Poor Arthur. She never really got over that. And her father… he was a dockworker. A miner for a while, actually, before he moved to London. Hard life, that. Which explains his staunch Labour leanings, naturally. Quite the contrast to my side of the family. Speaking of leanings, are we nearly there yet? My back’s killing me.

…and then the badger, right, he’d built this  enormous  fortress out of jam jars and old wellington boots! It was brilliant. What do you think happened next, Elsie? He fought a dragon! A sparkly dragon! No! He fought a giant carrot! A really,  really  big carrot that wanted to take all his jam! Ooh, a giant carrot! That’s a good one, Leo. Very menacing. Better than a sparkly dragon, actually. Though sparkly dragons  are  quite impressive. So, the badger's fortress… facing this giant carrot… what did he do? He threw jam at it! Sticky jam! He used his wellington boots as catapults! And shot pebbles! Oh, you two are a fantastic writing team. Pebbles from wellington boot catapults! That's inspired. We should write this down. Right, after biscuits. Anyone want another biscuit? Me! A chocolate one! I want a plain one! Coming right up. You know, this reminds me… I was looking at the Linton Book Festival line-up. They’ve got loads of children’s authors this year. Remember Helen Moss? The author of the Flightpath books?  The  Helen Moss? The one with the falcon and the girl who saves the birds? That's the one! She's doing a workshop. It’s all about creating your own adventure stories, building characters, and… well, rather like we're doing now. Is it far? Can we go? It’s not  too  far, about an hour’s drive. We’d have to go on the Saturday, and it might be a bit busy. But we could make a day of it. Perhaps see a show in Cambridge afterwards? Ooh! Cambridge! Can we go on the punts? Perhaps. If the weather’s good and we have time. One thing at a time! First, let’s see if you’re both interested in the workshop. It's specifically for kids your age, and sounds really good. It's about world-building, which is what we're doing with the badger and the carrot. Will we get to meet Helen Moss? Yes! You'll get to ask her questions and she’ll help you with your stories. Think of all the ideas! You could tell her about the wellington boot catapults. She'd like that, wouldn't she? She writes about adventures! I’m sure she would. It's all about imagination, isn’t it? And you two have plenty of that.

…and honestly, the texture was  almost  right. It just needed a bit more… something. Maybe paprika? You think? It was supposed to be a ‘beef’ mince replacement, but it was just… bland. Paprika's a good shout, definitely. Was it one of those Beyond Meat things, or something else? Because the Beyond ones can be a bit… aggressively beefy, you know? Like,  too  much trying to mimic. Too much trying is their whole  thing , isn't it? It's the uncanny valley of sausages. I’m still on team ‘proper veg’ myself. This lentil shepherd’s pie is going to be glorious. Although, the prep… honestly, all that chopping. It was that Vivera one, actually. The one in the red packaging. It smelled promising! I just… I feel guilty even  trying  to replicate meat, you know? Like I’m perpetuating the idea that we  need  it. I get that. It’s a weird internal struggle, isn't it? But then I think about the environmental impact, and the sheer suffering… and honestly, if a bit of lab-grown ‘chicken’ saves a bird from a horrific life, I’m all in. I’ve been reading about cultured meat – they’re actually growing it from cells now, no animal involvement at all. Shmeat, basically? Sounds… terrifying. And also, suspiciously futuristic. Like something out of a Philip K. Dick novel. Shmeat! Exactly! It's just… I don't know. It feels… detached. Like we're even further removed from the reality of what we’re eating. At least with veggie alternatives, you know it’s plants. But isn't  all  meat detached these days? We don’t go hunting for our dinner, most of us. It all comes in plastic packaging from a supermarket. It’s already a sanitised experience. A hunter at least… participates in the taking of a life. Grim, but… honest. Abattoirs are just… efficiently awful. That’s a good point, actually. It’s easier to ignore the cruelty when it’s hidden. Though, I did do a bit of gamekeeping with my grandad when I was younger. It's… different bagging a deer yourself. A horrible, necessary difference. Still doesn't make me want a steak, though. Ugh, don’t even mention steak. I had a  dream  last night about a particularly sad-looking cow. It’s probably because I was reading that article about factory farming. It was horrific.

… honestly, I don't know  why  he keeps leaving his socks everywhere. It's like a trail, honestly. You’d think after thirty years, he’d have grasped the concept of a laundry basket. Your brother, eh? Still the same as ever, then. Remember when he tried to “help” Mum with the garden and accidentally weeded out all her prize-winning roses? Oh,  god , I’ve heard that story a million times! It's family legend. Though, to be fair, they  did  look a bit…wild? Wild?! They were beautiful, meticulously-cared-for hybrid teas! And he just ripped them out, saying they were “overgrown”. Honestly. Anyway, it's not just the socks. He called earlier, complaining the internet’s down at his place. Complaining! Like it’s  my  fault the internet isn’t working in Surrey. He always does rely on you for tech support, doesn't he? Figures. Still, at least he  called . My sister, Margaret, she just texts endless strings of emojis when she has a problem. It’s infuriating trying to troubleshoot over a string of crying laughing faces. Emojis are the bane of my existence. I’m a words person, obviously. Trying to explain nuanced advertising copy using only pictograms… it's a nightmare. Speaking of nightmares, have you guys sorted New Year's Eve yet? We’re still debating. I was leaning towards a quiet one at home, maybe a nice roast, watch something on telly. Though, honestly, there’s nothing  on  is there? Everything is a repeat, or some dreadful reality show. I was thinking we could go to The Plough. They’re doing a live band, apparently. It’ll be proper lively. The Plough sounds good! A bit of dancing would be fun. Although, I wouldn’t put money on either of you lasting past midnight. Bold statement, young lady! I've got stamina, you know. Just because I complain about my feet after a particularly long shift at the hospital… It’s true. She’s a secret party animal. Though, speaking of shifts, how was work today, love? Busy. We had old Mr. Henderson in with a chest infection – he’s convinced it’s the draught coming from his new front door. Honestly, some of the things people come up with. And then Mrs. Davies was in, again, convinced she’s allergic to the hospital soap. Oh, bless them. You have the patience of a saint, you really do.

… honestly, I still don’t understand  why  you needed a butterfly fork. It's for peas, Leo! A normal fork does perfectly well. But Mum, it’s  elegant . It keeps the peas from escaping! Honestly, you wouldn’t understand. It’s a sophisticated eating experience. He’s been practicing his ‘sophisticated eating experience’ all afternoon. Nearly launched a pea at the cat. Right. Well, just try not to weaponize your cutlery, please. We’re having guests tomorrow, remember? Old Mr. and Mrs. Davies. And yes, that does mean two minutes of silence after supper. Ugh, the silence. Why do we  have  to do that? It's so awkward. Because Mrs. Davies finds it… reflective. She says it lets the supper ‘settle’. Honestly, I think she just likes the feeling of control. Anyway, it’s polite. And it’s her birthday tomorrow. Eighty-seven, can you believe it? Eighty-seven! Wow. Does she still talk about Russia? Does she ever! Apparently, her grandfather was a tea merchant in St. Petersburg before the revolution. She has  stories . Mostly about how much better the tea was then. And how cold it was. And the bears. There are always bears involved. Bears? In St. Petersburg? Apparently. It's all a bit embellished, I suspect. She’s a wonderful woman, but her memory is… selective. I remember last year she told us she’d personally taught the Tsar how to waltz. That’s… unlikely. Massively. Though she presented it as a completely factual account. Anyway, back to the fork situation. Why a butterfly fork, Leo? Honestly, where did you even  see  one? At that fancy French restaurant with Uncle Ben and Aunt Carol. You know, the one where everything was tiny and cost a fortune. They had them. It made me feel very grown-up. Oh,  that  restaurant. The one where you complained about the portion sizes? I was hungry! And it’s a statement piece. It's a fork, Leo. He’s got a point. Look, it's fine. You can use it for peas. Just… be careful with it. It probably cost more than my shoes. Speaking of, did you two finish your homework? It's your cousin’s birthday next week, and I need a head start on the present wrapping. Nearly. Just the history essay. It's about the Crimean War.
