Pretty boring, actually. I finished mine! It was about… engineering. Bridges, mostly.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Year 6 SATS papers is  criminal . I’ve marked approximately one million reading comprehension answers this weekend. One. Million. Mummy, is a million bigger than a billion? Yes, darling, a billion is even bigger. A  lot  bigger. It’s… well, it’s enough to buy Adventure Island, probably. Adventure Island! Can we go this summer? Please? I want to go on the Scorpion Express again! We’ll see, Leo. We’re still trying to figure out what we’re doing for summer holidays. Your dad was mentioning Cornwall again. Cornwall sounds boring. There’s no rides. Cornwall has beaches! And you can build sandcastles! And find crabs! He’s got a point, Maisie. Cornwall is lovely. We haven’t been since you two were tiny. Remember that little cove near Newquay? I remember building a massive castle! It got washed away by a big wave! I remember being really cross! Yes, you both were. Your dad’s thinking about renting a cottage, somewhere near Padstow maybe. We could do some coastal walks, try some proper Cornish pasties… Pasties are good! Can we have ice cream every day? Woah there, hold your horses. Every day might be pushing it. Although… your dad did say something about letting us have a ‘holiday treat fund’ this year. What's a treat fund? Is it money for Adventure Island? It  could  be money for Adventure Island, or for ice cream, or for little souvenirs. It’s for special things on holiday. Speaking of special things, I’ve booked us tickets for that V&A exhibition. The one on Alice in Wonderland. Alice in Wonderland? Is it scary? Not scary, silly. It’s full of amazing costumes and… well, it’s  Wonderland ! It’s going to be brilliant. It’s during the week we’re back from wherever we end up going. Can we wear sparkly dresses? Absolutely. You can wear your most sparkly dress. Right, let's talk logistics. Dad's being a bit vague about dates. He's also muttering about needing to check if his gluten intolerance will be catered for everywhere we go. Honestly, it's a whole operation just trying to find a suitable pasty! What’s gluten? Is it yucky? It’s a thing in some foods, darling, that makes Daddy’s tummy a bit poorly. That’s why he has to be careful. We need to find places that do gluten-free options.

…and then Mr. Harrison  actually  said my essay was “lacking in… nuance.” Nuance! It’s a history essay about the Battle of Hastings, not a blooming poem! What nuance does William the Conqueror  need ? Harsh, mate. Harrison’s always been a bit of a pedant, isn't he? I got a ‘could do better’ on my practical for physics, and honestly, I think it was just because I didn’t compliment his tie. Seriously! He’s got, like, fifteen different paisley ties. It’s unsettling. Did you finish the maths coursework? I’m completely stuck on question four. It’s that whole simultaneous equations thing again. Nearly. Got to check my answers, but I think I’ve cracked it. Want me to have a look later? We can go to my place, Mum’s making lasagne. Unless… you're avoiding lasagne again because of the dairy? Thanks, that’d be amazing. And yeah, the lasagne thing. It’s not  avoiding  exactly… more like preemptively minimising potential discomfort. My stomach just… doesn’t always agree with cheese. Remember what happened at Leo’s birthday last year? Oh god,  don’t  remind me. You went practically green! Ruined the whole bouncy castle situation. Honestly, you'd think after fifteen years, your mum would just stop trying to sneak cheese into everything. She thinks a little cheese builds strong bones! It's a maternal instinct, apparently. Speaking of Leo, have you heard about his party next weekend? Apparently, he’s hired a DJ. Yeah, everyone’s talking about it. Sounds decent, though I heard old man Hemmings, one of the prefects, is determined to shut it down. Apparently, Leo didn’t get permission to have it past ten. Hemmings? That’s just… expected. He’s on a power trip. Always has been. He thinks being a prefect gives him the right to ruin everyone’s life. Remember when he gave Ben a detention for… whistling? Whistling! It's a  whistle ! It's not like he was full-on belting out opera during double maths. Honestly, the guy's a menace. Though, to be fair, Ben  was  deliberately trying to annoy Miss Davies. True. Ben is a professional irritant. Have you seen the new Marvel film yet?  Quantum Realm  or whatever it’s called? Not yet. Been swamped with work. I’m trying to convince my little sister to watch  Everything Everywhere All at Once  with me though.

…and honestly, the roundabout at the A19 and the A1018 is just  asking  for an accident. It’s chaos. People just barge on, thinking they have right of way. You wouldn't get that up south, would you? Everything’s so…orderly down there. Orderly? That's debatable. M25 says hi. But yeah, roundabouts can be tricky. I think it’s more a ‘driver education’ issue, rather than a regional one. People just aren’t confident enough merging. Though, I’ll admit, some of the North East roads are…enthusiastically designed. Enthusiastically designed is a polite way of putting it! It's like they were built by someone who’d never actually  driven  a car. Seriously, the hills! You're either going straight up or straight down, no in-between. Makes cycling a nightmare too, mind. Speaking of cycling, are you still doing that charity ride next month? The one to Whitby? Aye, still on for it. Though I'm starting to seriously regret volunteering. My legs are feeling it already just  thinking  about those hills. You’re coming to cheer us on, right? Promised you would. Of course! I wouldn't miss it. Though I might cycle part of the way with you, just for a bit of moral support…and maybe a better view of the carnage when your legs give out. Just kidding! Mostly. Ha, very funny. You and your fancy road bike. You think you’re the bee's knees just because you’ve got gears for days. I’m doing it on Bessie. My trusty, slightly rusty, single-speed. Bessie? Seriously? You're tackling the North Yorkshire Moors on a single-speed? You're a legend, you know that? Honestly, though, I admire your stubbornness. It’s… very Northern. Stubborn? I prefer ‘determined’! And Bessie and I have a bond. She's seen me through worse. Remember that time I tried to cycle to Durham after one too many pints? How could I forget? You were convinced you were drafting behind a tractor. And nearly ended up  in  a field. It was a very convincing tractor! Anyway, enough about my questionable life choices. Did you catch any of the cricket yesterday? England were looking a bit shaky there for a bit. I did, actually. Got a bit of streaming done during a lull in a project. Root looked good, but the bowling was a bit… inconsistent.

…No, no, that’s definitely not what I meant. I just… I don't understand  why  they keep changing the number. It was 01733-567890 last time, I swear! Relax, Elsie. It’s just Chinese. It’s not like national security depends on getting sweet and sour chicken. Did you try directory enquiries? Honestly, you two. It  is  frustrating when they change the number, Elsie, especially when you've got a favourite. I remember trying to order from ‘Golden Wok’ last year and spending twenty minutes trying to track down the updated number. Nightmare. Exactly! And this is ‘Lucky Dragon’. They do the best salt and chilli ribs in Peterborough, change my mind. It’s vital we get ribs tonight. It's been a week. A  week  without Lucky Dragon ribs! Dramatic much? Okay, okay. Let me try. I’m better at deciphering these things. It’s ringing… It’s ringing… Nope. Engaged. Great. Engaged? On a Saturday night? That's not promising. Everyone and their dog wants a takeaway tonight. This is a disaster. I was really craving it. I even cleared space in the fridge! Right, Plan B. Google it. Maybe they’ve got a website now. Or a Facebook page. Everyone has a Facebook page these days, even Chinese takeaways. Good shout, Liam. I’ll have a look on Just Eat as well, just in case. Sometimes they update the numbers there quicker. Oh. Oh dear. What? What is it? Don’t leave me in suspense! Are they closed? Did they run out of ribs? Worse. They’ve been…rebranded. It’s now ‘Eastern Delight’. Same address, same phone number as  last  time you looked up, Elsie, but it’s not Lucky Dragon anymore. Rebranded?! No! This is an outrage! What happened to the dragon? Was he…fired? Did he retire? Elsie, it's a takeaway. They don’t have staff mascots. You never know! Maybe Lucky Dragon was a real person! A culinary genius! And now he’s gone, and we’re left with ‘Eastern Delight’. It sounds…generic. Apparently, the reviews are…mixed. Someone said the ribs are 'okay, but not Lucky Dragon okay'. ‘Not Lucky Dragon okay’ is not okay! This is a tragedy! We  have  to try it, though, right? For the ribs. It's our duty. You’re taking this way too seriously. But yeah, for the ribs. We owe it to the memory of…Lucky Dragon.

… honestly, the waiting lists are just getting ridiculous, aren’t they? Old Mrs. Higgins down the street, needs a hip replacement, been on the list for eighteen months. Eighteen! And she’s in constant pain. It's just… demoralising for everyone involved, isn’t it? For her, for the doctors, for the nurses… Tell me about it. It’s the same at the clinic. We’re seeing people with conditions that should have been caught and treated months, sometimes years ago. Preventative care is just… vanishing. Funding cuts, staffing shortages, it’s a perfect storm. I spent half of yesterday reassuring a man who’d finally gotten a referral for a chest scan - after  nine  months complaining of a cough, mind you - that he wasn’t being deliberately ignored. It’s heartbreaking. It's a political choice, isn't it? They talk about supporting the NHS, but the actions… they don’t match the rhetoric. Makes you wonder if they even  use  the NHS themselves. Don't even go there. My sister works in administration at the Royal. She’s saying they’re constantly shifting goalposts, implementing new “efficiency measures” which essentially just mean more workload for fewer people. It’s relentless. And they’re even talking about… well, I probably shouldn't repeat gossip, but there’s talk of further bed closures. Oh, brilliant. That’s just what we need. More beds disappearing. It’s not that long ago I was in A&E with my lad, Leo, and you wouldn’t believe the state of it. People crammed into corridors. It felt like a… a holding pen. Not a hospital. It  is  a holding pen some days. And then people complain about the delays. Where do they expect us to put everyone? It's not like we’re intentionally trying to make people wait! Speaking of kids, how’s Leo doing now? Last I saw him he was obsessed with… was it coding? He is, still! He's brilliant. Applying to uni next year, wants to study computer science. It's a relief, actually. Something solid. I always worried about the humanities, being a lecturer and all. It feels… precarious these days, doesn't it? Academia. Less and less funding, more emphasis on impact metrics… Precarious is a good word for it. At least nursing is, sadly, always in demand. Though the  demand  is wearing us all out! Have you had any trouble with the new neighbours yet?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I’ve got this week is criminal. Essays on  Beowulf  – you wouldn’t believe the interpretations some of them come up with! It’s like they’ve never even  read  the thing. Anyway, you were telling me about young Michael and his trouble with the Jobcentre? Aye, that lad. Bless ‘im. They’re givin’ ‘im grief again, they are. Says he hasn’t applied for enough jobs. Enough jobs! In this city? There’s nothin’  to  apply for, lad. Not nothin’ decent anyway. Just zero-hour contracts and places lookin’ for folk to clean floors for buttons. He’s tryin’, he is, but they treat ‘im like dirt. It's appalling, isn't it? It sounds like the system is deliberately designed to…discourage people. I mean, I lecture at the university, a relatively secure position, and I still feel the pressure of constant assessment and proving my worth. Imagine what it's like for someone genuinely seeking work. Tell me about it. My Arthur, God rest his soul, he spent years lookin’ after he left the Merchant Navy. Always a good worker, Arthur was. Always. But things changed, didn’t they? Docks closed, factories shut down…they didn’t care then, did they? Just left ‘em high and dry. Now, they expect everyone to be a computer whiz or somethin’. Exactly! And it’s not just the skills gap. It’s the whole attitude. Everything is so…temporary. No long-term security. Remember when people  stayed  with a company for life? It feels like a different world now. Different world indeed. Though, talkin’ about different worlds, did you hear about what happened down on Lodge Lane last week? Police raided that little cafe, the one that does the amazing samosas. I did hear something…something about immigration papers? Aye. Said they were checkin’ for illegal workers. Turns out, old Mr. Patel had all his paperwork in order. Perfectly legal. But they turned the place upside down, frightened the customers half to death. All for a bit of a show. It’s scaremongering, pure and simple. It feels…targeted. And the rhetoric gets more and more hostile. It's unsettling. My mother, she came here from Germany after the war. She wouldn't have been able to build a life here now, not with the way things are. People forget how much this country benefits from immigration.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data we’re getting through is mental. Like, I’m wading through transcripts of people talking about… toast. Seriously, toast! For five hours a day, some of them. It’s for this dialect levelling project, right? But toast?! Toast is surprisingly revealing, actually. The way people describe it - “golden brown,” “slightly burnt,” “needs more butter” - gives you insights into socio-economic background, regional preferences… It's fascinating, really. Though five hours  is  dedication to the subject matter. You are being far too generous giving toast that much credit, Alice. It’s a bread-based control, isn't it? Something universally relatable so you can strip away the context and focus purely on linguistic features? Aye, that’s what they say. But I’m starting to dream in sourdough. And the accents! Trying to transcribe someone from, like, deepest Cornwall when you’re from Sunderland is just… a challenge. They’re practically speaking another language. That’s the beauty of the UK, isn't it? The linguistic diversity is incredible. From where I sit – having bounced between the US and the UK for a while now – it’s endlessly interesting. It's easy to forget, working with ELT materials, that the ‘standard’ English we often teach isn’t really representative. Exactly! I was talking to my aunt in Bradford the other day and she was telling me a story, and I literally had to ask her to repeat herself like, three times. And she's my  aunt ! She just uses so much Yorkshire slang, it goes right over my head. And I did my undergrad in Leeds! It’s all about intonation too, isn’t it? I’ve been looking at some recordings from Norfolk, and the rising inflection on almost everything… it sounds like they’re constantly asking a question, even when they’re making a statement. It's hypnotic. Oh, don't get me started on rising intonation! I had a phone call yesterday with a woman from Essex and I genuinely thought she was questioning  everything  I said. It was exhausting. It's not that I mind the differences, it's just... the sheer volume of them. It does make you realise how much our own accent shapes our perception of others. I’m used to a fairly neutral Lincolnshire accent, but even  I  find myself making judgements about people based on how they sound.

…and honestly, the buffering was  criminal . I was right at the climax of ‘Slow Horses’ – you know, the Gary Oldman spy thing? – and it just froze. Froze solid! Three times! It's infuriating, isn't it? Especially when you're paying for 'superfast' broadband. More like ‘super-slow’ if you ask me. Oh, I know the feeling. BT are robbing us blind. I’ve been threatening to switch for months. Though, to be fair, I’ve been mostly distracted by trying to mark these blasted essays. Honestly, the things students think are acceptable arguments… It’s a wonder. Essays, right. Still at the university then? Still dealing with the…enthusiasm of youth? Still at it. Researcher now, thankfully less direct teaching. Though I occasionally give a guest lecture. This term it’s on linguistic relativity – the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis. You know, the idea that language shapes thought. Fascinating stuff! I remember dabbling in that during my undergrad. Always felt a bit…fuzzy though. Like, how much is  actually  down to language and how much is just cultural differences manifesting themselves  through  language? That’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it? I was just reading about a study done in Namibia, with the Himba people. They don't have words for blue, or really distinguish it as a colour. Show them a selection of green squares, one slightly bluer than the others, and they struggle to pick it out. But give them the same task with greens and they’re spot on. Apparently, it’s not just vocabulary, it affects perception. Wow. That’s…profound. Makes you think about how limited our own perspectives are, doesn’t it? I've been trying to learn a bit of Mandarin, though I’m making painfully slow progress. It’s so tonal. I can say something that  sounds  exactly right to me, but means something completely different. Mandarin is notoriously difficult. I tried a bit when I was travelling in China. Gave up after about three weeks. I concentrated on pointing and miming instead. Surprisingly effective. Although, I did accidentally order a plate of chicken feet once. Thought I was asking for chicken with vegetables! Oh dear! That’s a culinary miscommunication for the ages. Speaking of cultures, I was chatting with a chap at the library the other day – he's a visiting scholar from Japan - and he was saying how impressed he is with the British obsession with queuing.

…and honestly, lad, I don’t know  why  they keep changing the mark schemes. It’s a nightmare! Last year it was all about ‘showing working’, this year it’s ‘elegant solutions’. What  is  an elegant solution to a simultaneous equation for a fifteen-year-old, eh? It’s just maths, not a blooming art competition! Sounds stressful, Mum. I’m just glad I’m nearly done with GCSEs. Though Physics is… well, Physics is still Physics. Aye, Physics. Always a tricky one. Your Grandad here barely scraped through it, didn't you, Arthur? More interested in tinkering with engines than triangles, he was. She’s not wrong. Triangles never fixed a Ford Anglia, let me tell you. Though I reckon I could build you a mark scheme for that, Doreen. Plenty of steps involved! Oh, you would, wouldn’t you? You always were a practical man. Now, are you two comfortable enough? Can I get you another cuppa? I made Brenda’s shortbread, you know, your favourite, Arthur. Don't mind if I do, lass! Brenda always made a cracking shortbread. Better than anything you get in the shops. And comfortable as can be, thank you. This armchair is a godsend for these old bones. Me too, dear. Lovely and warm in here. Not like that draughty old house we had in Hull, eh Arthur? Remember the winter of ‘63? Frozen pipes for weeks! Don’t remind me. Had to melt the ice with a camping stove! Nearly burned the kitchen down. That was a bit of a panic, that was. Wow, really? Sounds…intense. Intense is one word for it! Your Gran was a force of nature then, she was. Always had a plan, even if it involved a camping stove and a potential house fire. Speaking of plans, I was thinking, Michael – that’s you, love – maybe you could give your Grandad a hand with the garden next weekend? He’s been moaning about the weeds. Ugh, weeds? Mum! Now, now, be polite. It’d be lovely for both of them. And a bit of fresh air would do you good, glued to that computer screen all the time. He’s a good lad, Michael. Always willing to help. Unlike some! Now, now, Doreen. I  helped  with the garden. I pointed out where the weeds were. That's a crucial contribution, you know. Strategic weed identification. Strategic weed identification?

…and honestly, the dumplings were incredible. I mean,  incredible . Not like anything we get back home, even in London’s Chinatown. They just… melt. You and your dumplings. You've been talking about those dumplings for a week. Though I agree, they were a step up. Speaking of food, did you manage to get a decent picture of Old Man Wei making them? I wanted to show the history students. It’s such a living tradition. I tried! He was moving so fast, a blur of flour and pork. I got one… vaguely resembling a hand shaping dough. It’s on my phone somewhere. Let me see… Ah, here. What do you think? Artistic impression, perhaps? Artistic is… generous. It mostly looks like a grey smudge. But the  intention  is there. Good effort. You're much better at photographing landscapes, aren't you? Remember Skye? Those photos were stunning. Skye was different. Static beauty. This is… dynamic. And hot. It was  hot  in that kitchen. Honestly, it made me miss proper air conditioning. Remember complaining about the drafty pubs in Norwich? Now  that  feels like a luxury. Oh God, Norwich pubs. And your perpetual complaints about the lack of central heating. We were so young. So naïve. Though I do still maintain a proper pub needs a draft. Builds character. Character and pneumonia! No thank you. This weather is definitely testing my British resilience, though. I miss a grey, drizzly day, actually. Sounds mad, doesn’t it? Not at all. It’s the familiar. It’s… home. It’s funny, isn’t it? After all this time, living here, you still get pangs for things you thought you hated. I was just thinking about Liam and Sarah the other day. Wondering what they're up to. Oh, really? The Liam and Sarah who tried to convince us to join their commune in Wales? The very same. Actually, I saw a picture of them online. They’ve got a kid now. And a flock of sheep. Predictable. I wonder if they ever regret ditching wifi. Probably not. They were always… committed. It’s just… it feels like a lifetime ago. Everyone’s lives have just… diverged. It's strange. Do you ever think about going back permanently? I do. Sometimes. But then I think about the opportunities here, the students, the research…and the dumplings! And frankly, the thought of navigating the London housing market again fills me with dread.

… honestly, I still feel wrecked. Like, properly wrecked. Did you see Chloe trying to order chips at 3am? She asked for ‘potato sticks with sauce’. Potato  sticks ! Oh my god, no way! Chloe after three vodka lemonades is a whole different species. I was trying to keep her from attempting a TikTok dance on top of a bin. It was…a situation. A situation is putting it mildly. I thought security were going to have to get involved. You were doing alright though, weren’t you? Relatively composed. Relatively? I spent twenty minutes explaining the nuances of Premier League football to a bloke who thought Harry Kane played for Man U. It was exhausting. And he kept calling me ‘love’. Ugh, the ‘love’ thing. Always with the ‘love’. Makes you want to just…not. Did you manage to get home okay? My flatmate, bless her, was asleep on the sofa surrounded by empty takeaway boxes. It was a horrifying sight. My brother, Kai, picked me up. He was actually…surprisingly sober. Said he had a big presentation today. Typical Kai, always responsible. He made me promise not to tell Mum and Dad we were out 'til that time though. Apparently they were already giving him grief about  my  behaviour last week. Oh no! What did you do last week? Don't tell me you were scaling lampposts again? Worse, apparently. Apparently, I was singing karaoke…badly…to a security guard. And offering him a biscuit. It's all a blur, honestly. I vaguely remember a biscuit. You and biscuits. It's a dangerous combo. I need to start exercising properly. This feeling of being hungover until Tuesday is not a vibe. I saw Ella posting pictures from the gym this morning. Looking all toned and radiant. Ugh, don’t even. Ella lives at the gym. Honestly, she probably has a protein shake intravenously. I tried going once, felt like everyone was judging my attempts at a plank. They're probably just concentrating on their own form, babe. It’s intimidating at first, but once you get into it… Easier said than done. Speaking of intimidating…Did you see Leo at the club last night? He was chatting up Maisie.  Maisie ! No! Seriously?! I thought he was still…you know…into Freya. Apparently not. Maisie was practically batting her eyelashes off. It was a whole performance. Honestly, the drama. It's exhausting just  watching  it.

…and honestly, the peas are a bit undercooked, aren’t they? Not disastrous, mind you, but a good two minutes more would have done them the world of good. Though, I suppose, having chips with them distracts from it. They’re fine, Mum. Honestly. You always critique the peas. It’s a tradition. And they  are  good chips, Dad. Crispy. They are, they are. Proper chips. Remind me of the chippy back in Walsall. Though, nothing  quite  beats a proper chip shop, does it? Even the best homemade…it’s just not the same. Oh, don't even get me started on chip shop chips. Pure indulgence. But we were talking about your mother, weren’t we? Has she confirmed the visit yet, Helen? I’m starting to worry she’s changed her mind. She texted this morning. Train’s booked for next Friday. Says she’s bringing that ridiculous knitted shawl she’s been working on for…well, I’ve lost count. She thinks it’ll keep the Cumbrian chill at bay. Your mother. Always prepared for arctic conditions, even in July. Good on her for making the effort, though. It’s a long trek for her. It is. And I do feel bad, asking her to come all this way after… well, after everything. But I need her here. I need someone to talk to. This quiet is driving me mad since retiring. You know you can talk to us, Mum. It’s not the same, love. You two have your own lives, your work. I don’t want to burden you with my… my existential dread about no longer having quadratic equations to solve. Existential dread? That’s a bit dramatic, isn’t it? You always said you were looking forward to retirement, Agnes. All that gardening you planned… I  thought  I was! But gardening just feels…pointless without a timetable. And besides, the slugs are winning. Honestly, they're ruthless. It’s a battle I’m losing. Anyway, change of subject. Helen, did you watch that Manchester United game last night? Bits and pieces. I was mostly editing transcripts. But saw the highlights. Honestly, the refereeing was appalling. Absolute shambles. Appalling is an understatement. That penalty decision was daylight robbery. Sheer daylight robbery. I nearly threw the remote at the television. Oh, don't be so dramatic, Arthur. It was a bad call, yes, but hardly the end of the world.

…and honestly, the sound it made when it finally gave up the ghost was like a strangled seagull. Completely bricked. I think I was trying to run too many things at once – editing a lesson plan, streaming music, and having about a million browser tabs open. Classic me. Oh, you’re such a digital hoarder, Liam! Seriously. You need to learn to close tabs. It’s a wonder anything  works  on that poor laptop. Did you back everything up, at least? Thankfully, yes. Cloud’s a lifesaver. Though now I’m debating whether to get it repaired… or just bite the bullet and get a new one. It's just… expensive. Repair, definitely repair. Wasteful otherwise. Back in my day, things  were  made to last. You’d get a good telly, and it’d see you out! This throwaway culture… He’s right, George. Though, to be fair, everything’s just… faster now. More complicated. My Sarah’s phone packed in last week, and she was beside herself. Took me ages to set up her new Blackberry. Honestly, it felt like learning a new language! Blackberry? Really, Mum? Who even uses Blackberry anymore? Well, she liked the keyboard! Said it was easier for her contact lenses to focus on the physical buttons. Honestly, it's a nightmare trying to explain technology to her sometimes. And then she wants me to figure out voice recognition software… Sounds familiar. I’ve had students like that. Trying to explain the difference between 'there', 'their' and 'they're' is often harder than explaining quantum physics. Speaking of things being difficult, has anyone else noticed the water tasting…odd lately? Odd? It tastes like water, doesn't it? What flavour were you expecting? No, Dad, he means like… chemically. I think Southern Water are doing something again. Remember last summer and all the protests? Exactly! I was reading they're diverting water from somewhere else, and it’s affecting the mineral content. I'm seriously considering just buying bottled water. Though that's another expense… Oh, don't start on expenses! The bin strikes are bad enough. The whole street smells of rotting rubbish. It's just lovely, isn't it? Plus, with Auntie Maureen coming next week, the flat  has  to be spotless. Oh dear god, Maureen. Prepare for scrutiny. Every cushion will be fluffed, every surface polished. She means well. She just... expresses it intensely.

… honestly, I still can’t believe how much a decent umbrella costs here. Fifteen quid for something that’ll probably blow inside out with the first gust of wind! Back home, you can get one from Tesco for a fiver and it’ll last you a season. You’re comparing Tesco prices to Poland, Auntie Carol! Everything’s… different. And honestly, the Polish wind  is  pretty fierce. You need something sturdy. Did you see the rain this morning? Absolute deluge. Though, this coffee  is  good, isn’t it? Much better than that lukewarm stuff we had yesterday. It is lovely. Properly strong. Helps keep the gloom at bay. I’m starting to feel that winter thing creeping in again, you know? The SAD. It’s not just the lack of sunlight, it’s… everything. Missing Cambridge, missing proper shops, missing a proper Sunday roast. I get it. I’ve been feeling a bit…off, too. It’s just, everything feels  grey  right now. And everyone's talking about the football. Did you manage to check the scores? Did United actually win? Oh, don’t even  start  me on football. I glanced at something on my phone, but honestly, it all blurs into one miserable mess after a while. They lost, didn’t they? Expect the usual outrage on social media. It's all anyone talks about. I’ve been trying to read more, actually. Escapism, you know? Just finished a really good historical fiction. That's a good idea. I haven't picked up a book in ages. Been too busy prepping my students for their exams. Honestly, I feel so responsible for them. This one boy, Marek, he’s such a bright spark, but he gets so anxious about speaking. It breaks my heart. I spend half my time reassuring him. Oh, you always were a softie. That’s a lovely quality, though. But you can’t carry their anxieties, darling. They need to learn to cope themselves. It’s hard, I know, being a teacher. It’s not just about the grammar, it’s about building confidence. Exactly! I feel like I’m parenting sometimes. One of them asked me the other day if I thought he’d ever be able to live in England. It was so sweet, but also… daunting. I want to prepare them, tell them it's amazing, but also be realistic about the challenges.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of beige at that corporate away-day was criminal. Beige carpets, beige walls, beige… everything! You’d think a company holding a ‘team building’ retreat could splash out on  some  colour. It felt like being inside a digestive biscuit. Right? Sounds proper depressing. I spent all day yesterday shiftin’ bricks in the rain. Beige wouldn't bother me much after that, just grateful for a roof over me ‘ead. Did you at least get a decent free lunch out of it? Decent? They had a ‘build your own sandwich’ station. Which consisted of white bread, processed cheese slices, and ham that looked like it’d seen better decades. I think I stuck to the water. Though, even the water tasted a bit… beige. Oh, Chloe, you always find the drama. Though, yeah, corporate events can be soul-destroying. I had a supplier try to convince me last week that pastel pink was 'on-brand' for a tech conference.  Tech . Pink. Honestly. See! It’s a plague! Honestly, I'm starting to think everyone in event planning secretly hates colour. Speaking of things that are depressing, how’s the dating scene been, Liam? Still swiping endlessly? Still swiping. It's a right mess. Everyone's got the same pictures, doin’ the same stuff. Loads of ‘hiking enthusiast’ profiles, you know? Like it's the only hobby people have now. And everything’s so… curated. It is. Everyone's projecting this perfect life. It's exhausting, even just  looking  at it. I had a date last week who spent the entire time talking about his 'side hustle' – selling artisanal dog biscuits online. Artisanal dog biscuits? That's… a choice. Was he at least handsome? Perfectly presentable. But the biscuit obsession was… a lot. I think I subtly steered the conversation towards the impending climate crisis just to change the subject. Didn’t work. He started explaining organic sourcing. Sounds like a winner. You deserve better, Jess. You’re always workin’ flat out, doin' a proper job. Anyone'd be lucky to have you. He’s not wrong, you know. You’re always on, Jess. Which reminds me, how's that new project going? The one with the pharmaceutical company? It’s… intense. Massive budget, ridiculous expectations. They want a ‘cutting-edge, immersive experience’ that basically needs to resemble a sci-fi film set. My team’s pulling all-nighters.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of chuggers around Russell Square is becoming ridiculous. It's like running a gauntlet just to get to the coffee shop. You'd think with all the students around here, they’d leave us alone, wouldn't you? Tell me about it. I had one practically clinging to my arm yesterday, going on about water filters. It’s exhausting. Though, this square’s nicer, isn’t it? More open. And look at those lime trees – proper London, that. It is. Though I'm still mapping it out in my head, trying to figure out the best route for a proper circuit for my lunchtime walk. You get turned around so easily. Makes me think of the layout of parks in China… utterly different. China, eh? Thinking about that trip again? Still fancy teaching over there after the PhD? It's a thought. A colleague, Mei, was telling me about the demand for good TEFL teachers. Apparently, the emphasis is shifting away from rote learning. She said they’re desperate for people who can actually make it  fun . She was explaining how her sister had a group of Chinese guests visiting, all wanting to improve their English. Sounds busy. She work with pandas or something? I remember you saying she was involved in some wildlife project. No, that’s her brother. He's researching bear populations in Sichuan. Apparently, it’s surprisingly complex because of habitat loss and, well, the… let’s just say the somewhat delicate relationship between humans and bears in those areas. It's a world away from Devon, that's for sure. Devon, that reminds me. We should try and get down there this summer. Proper countryside, good for a drive. Although driving in rural areas is…an adventure, isn't it? Narrow lanes, tractors blocking the road... An understatement! Though anything’s better than trying to navigate getting to the Isle of Wight. Honestly, all the ferries and roads… my head spins. You and I need a proper, unplugged holiday. Though, Mei was also telling me about how even  within  China, travelling to remote areas is getting easier. Improved infrastructure and all that. Still, the food… that’s always a talking point. I’ve heard some interesting things. Apparently, they use an awful lot of salt. They do! It’s almost in everything. Though I've had some amazing coconut cake over there, washed down with proper coffee.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is mental. Like, we’re talking terabytes of transcribed interviews. Terabytes! It’s all for this study on dialectal variations in Northern English vowel sounds, which is fascinating, don't get me wrong, but… organizing it all feels like trying to herd cats. Sounds… involved. More involved than I anticipated when you said ‘corpus administrator’ at dinner with your mum last month. I thought you just, you know, filed things. Filed things?! Oh, you sweet summer child. Filing is the  smallest  part. It’s tagging, annotating, cleaning up dodgy transcriptions where someone’s confused ‘aye’ with ‘I’. It's making sure the metadata is consistent across all the different recording devices. It’s… it's a whole thing. Honestly, sometimes I just want to scream into the void. Well, scream into the void  after  you’ve told me about your weekend. You were mysteriously vague on the phone yesterday. Said something about a ‘catastrophe’ involving a biscuit tin? Oh, don't even  start  me on the biscuit tin. It wasn’t just  a  biscuit tin, it was Gran’s biscuit tin. The floral one? The one she’s had since… well, since before I was born, probably. And Buster, bless his fluffy little soul, decided it was a climbing frame. Buster? Your neighbour’s Maine Coon? He's a monster. A majestic monster, but a monster nonetheless. He somehow managed to topple the entire thing, sending digestive biscuits scattering across Mrs. Henderson’s prize-winning begonias. Mrs. Henderson was  not  pleased. Oh dear. That does sound like a catastrophe. Did you have to… compensate for the begonias? We’re still negotiating. I’ve offered to weed her garden for a month. She's currently considering painting a portrait of Buster as penance. I think she’s leaning towards the portrait. That’s… remarkably reasonable, actually. Although Buster would probably look deeply unimpressed. Listen, about Saturday… are we still on for that hike in the Peak District? I’ve booked us a table at that pub in Castleton, The Castle. Oh, brilliant! Yes, definitely. I desperately need to escape Sunderland for a bit. The biscuit tin incident has raised my stress levels exponentially. And to be honest, I need a break from vowels. Just… silence. And hills. Perfect. I’m checking the weather forecast again tonight, but it’s looking good. We should get some decent views.

…and honestly, the catering at that conference last week was  criminal . Seriously, stale sandwiches and lukewarm coffee. You’d think for the money they were charging, they could at least manage that! It’s a wonder anyone focused on the presentations. Anyway, how's yer mam doin’, Ben? Last I heard she wasn’t too good. Aye, she's still a bit rough, Sarah. Doctor thinks it’s just a really nasty bug, but she’s been exhausted. Just sleeps most of the day. It’s worrying, you know? She's never been one for being ill. Makes me feel useless, not being able to do much 'cept make her tea and toast. Oh, bless her. That sounds awful. It’s the not knowing, isn't it? That's the worst part. My grandmother was the same last winter, just completely wiped out. Turns out it was pneumonia, but it took ages to diagnose. Aw, no way. That’s scary. Poor woman! It’s a right pain when family’s poorly. Distracts you something fierce. Speaking of distractions… how’s things with Chloe, Ben? You’ve been a bit quiet about her lately. It’s… complicated. “Complicated” rarely means good, does it? Spill. We’re your friends, you can tell us. Well, she’s been spending a lot of time with this bloke from her pottery class. Says he’s just a friend, but… I don’t know. She’s been on her phone loads, and kinda distant. I tried asking her about it, but she just gets defensive. Ooh, that  never  bodes well. Defensive is relationship code for “something's definitely going on.” You gotta be direct, Ben. Bottling it up’ll only make it worse. Don’t let her walk all over you, lad. Sarah’s right. Gently, of course. But you need to know where you stand. Maybe suggest a proper date night, just the two of you? Really focus on reconnecting. See how she reacts? I did try. Last week. Took her to that new Italian place, the one with the fairy lights. She barely touched her food, and spent the whole time texting. Said it was her mum, but… “It’s me mum” is the oldest excuse in the book, Ben. Honestly. She’s testing the waters, seeing how much she can get away with. My cousin went through the same thing last year. Nearly lost her fella to a ‘yoga instructor’.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of emails already this morning is making me question all my life choices. It’s like everyone decided 8:30am was the perfect time to collectively lose their minds. Ugh, mornings. The enemy of productivity. What’s kicking off the chaos today? Same old project hiccups, or is it a full-blown meltdown? It's mostly Mark. Mark from Accounts. He’s emailed three times already about a spreadsheet.  A spreadsheet , Liv! It's literally just a colour-coded list of expenses. I explained it to him on Monday. Twice. Oh, Mark. Bless him. He's… a lot. Remember when he tried to print a 50-page document double-sided and ended up jamming the printer for an entire afternoon? How could I forget? I had to call IT. It delayed the entire marketing report schedule. Honestly, I sometimes wonder how he manages to dress himself in the morning. But it's not just him. Sarah in Sales is being… passive-aggressive again. Leaving little notes on my desk about ‘teamwork’ when all I did was ask her for an update on the client proposal. Sounds exhausting. You need a holiday. Seriously. You’ve barely had a day off since you started this project coordinator role. I  know . But the deadlines are relentless. Plus, I feel bad leaving Ben to pick up the slack. Speaking of which… have you heard back from Dan? About Friday? Oh. Right. No, not yet. I texted him earlier, just a casual “Hey, still up for Friday?” Nothing. Radio silence. That’s… not good. Is he deliberately avoiding me? It's been two weeks since… well, you know. Since he and Chloe called it quits. I don’t know, babe. Dan can be a bit… emotionally avoidant when things get tricky. Remember when his nan passed away? He disappeared for a week and communicated entirely through his mum. Yeah, but this is different. Chloe was  everything  to him. I thought he'd want to talk, you know? Lean on someone. And I genuinely thought... I thought maybe now, without Chloe, he might be more open to... us. Oh, sweetie. Don't do that to yourself. He's fresh out of a serious relationship. He needs space to process. It's not a rejection of  you . It's just… him. And honestly, after watching Chloe treat him, he needs a long period of self-discovery before he can even  think  about another relationship.

…and that’s why the Green Man is always depicted with leaves growing  from  his face, not just  around  it. It's a symbol of constant rebirth, you see? Even when things look…dark, like winter, there's always the promise of spring hidden within. But what about the baddies? Like, the really scary ones? Grandma told me about Black Shuck! He’s  massive  and has red eyes! And he breathes fire! Leo at school said his grandad saw him on the roads near Thetford Forest. Well, legends are funny things, aren't they? They often start as ways to explain things people didn’t understand – storms, unexplained noises in the night, even just…fear. Black Shuck, for example, is likely based on sightings of large, black dogs, maybe even a particularly imposing Newfoundland. People then  added  to the story over the years, making him scarier and more dramatic. But he  is  scary, though! He’s a ghost dog! He's a legend of a ghost dog, darling. It's important to remember the difference. Legends aren’t necessarily  true , but they tell us something about what people worried about, or what they found exciting. It’s about the stories, not just the… the monster at the end. So, good stories need baddies? Even if they're not real? That’s a very good question, Thomas. Often, yes. A good story needs conflict. And very often, that conflict comes from something, or someone, representing “evil”. But “evil” isn’t always a person who wants to hurt people. Sometimes it’s just…force of nature, or temptation, or even just making a bad choice. Think about the stories of dragons guarding treasure. The dragon isn’t necessarily  evil , it’s just protecting what it believes is rightfully its. Like when I protect my Lego castle from you, Thomas? Hey! I wasn’t going to  break  it, I just wanted to borrow some bricks for my spaceship! See? Conflict! Protection! A little bit of 'good versus bad' right here in the kitchen. Now, speaking of protecting things…did you two finish those posters for the Comberton village fete? The ‘Local Legends’ display needs them by Friday. Almost! I’ve drawn the Green Man and I’m colouring him green. It takes ages to make all the leaves. Mine’s Black Shuck! I made his eyes really glowy red. But I keep accidentally colouring outside the lines.

…and honestly, the whole thing sounded a bit chaotic. Apparently, they filmed a scene in the Co-op. The  Co-op , Sarah! Can you imagine? Blocking off the biscuit aisle for dramatic effect? Oh, classic school filmmaking. They always aim high, don't they? ANON, did you get to be an extra in the biscuit aisle? Were you wielding a custard cream like a weapon? No! I was… I was a townsperson! I had to walk past really slowly and look important. But Leo bumped into me. It wasn’t my fault! She walked  into  me! And then I tripped over the pretend cobblestones. Pretend cobblestones? They went to that much effort? Right, so was it worth it? Did they get good footage? Apparently, they got a lot of footage of Leo falling over. Mrs. Davison was mortified. She spent ten minutes apologising to his mum. It  was  funny though! Sounds like it. Right, back to reality. It felt surprisingly chilly last night, didn’t it? I had the heating on for a bit. It did. I’m glad we’ve got those extra duvets. I was thinking of getting the winter duvet out altogether, actually. Do you think it's going to get colder? Hard to say. It's October, it's always a bit unpredictable. Speaking of unpredictable, how’s your leg, ANON? Still sore from yesterday? It’s a little bit better, but it still hurts when I run. She tried to do a cartwheel and landed funny. Right, no more cartwheels for a while, young lady. You need to let it heal. Honestly, she's a little daredevil. You get that from your mother. Remember that time you tried to climb the oak tree in Gran’s garden? I did  not  try to climb it! I got… stuck. There's a difference. And it was a perfectly reasonable tree to attempt. What were  you  doing at the gym today, Dad? Trying to avoid looking like a complete idiot while attempting to use the running machines. Honestly, they’re terrifying. All those blinking lights and digital readouts. They make it sound like you're launching a spaceship, not just going for a jog. Oh, don't be dramatic. They’re just trying to motivate you. Motivate me by telling me how unfit I am? Thanks. I saw a guy today who looked like he was running a marathon  on  the machine.

…and honestly, the rheumatologist just shrugged. Said it’s ‘age-related wear and tear’. Wear and tear! Like I’m a bloody machine, not a man who spent thirty years hunched over essays. Sounds about right, Arthur. Doctors these days. Quick to label and slow to actually  do  anything. Mine told me my dodgy knee was just ‘part of getting older’ when I was complaining about it for six months. Ended up getting a second opinion and a decent physio sorted it right out. See? That's what I’m thinking. I might have to go back to Dr. Davies, my old GP. He actually  listened . This new one…well, she's a lovely girl, but she seems awfully rushed. Speaking of rushed, have you seen the news about the Green Party’s proposals for the city centre? Bits and pieces. Something about pedestrianising more streets, wasn’t it? And cycling lanes? That’s the gist of it. They want to turn North Street into a completely traffic-free zone. Can you imagine? Absolute chaos. How will deliveries get through? And what about people with mobility issues? It’s all very well for the young and fit, but… Hold on a minute, Arthur. I think it’s a good idea, actually. Brighton needs to breathe. It’s choking on traffic. And frankly, getting a parking space is a nightmare. My old delivery driver, Billy, retired last year. Said the stress of navigating these roads was killing him. Couldn't find anyone to replace him willing to put up with it, paid good money too. Billy, bless him. He always had a kind word. But still, the economic impact! Think of the shops. People won’t bother coming into town if they can’t park nearby. My daughter, Sarah, she owns that little bookshop on Bond Street, she's already worried sick. Sarah’s a smart woman. She’ll adapt. She always does. Perhaps she can focus on deliveries, and build up an online presence. That's what I did with the antiques business. Had to, really, when the high streets started… well, you know. Remember when boot sales were  the  place to find a bargain? Oh, do I! Stanmer Park on a Sunday. Glorious. Remember old Mr. Henderson, always selling chipped teacups and calling them ‘vintage’? And his wife, constantly fussing over him! Good times. They're all gone now, aren’t they?

…and honestly, the audacity of that woman, telling me mustard yellow wasn’t “a neutral”! A  neutral ! Like, have you  seen  Scandinavian interiors? It's all ochre and burnt sienna. It’s perfectly acceptable. Right, because obviously the entire design aesthetic of a whole region hinges on your outfit choice for a Tuesday. You're taking this very seriously, aren't you? Seriously enough to defend my perfectly coordinated outfit, thank you very much. It’s a statement! Besides, it’s more about principle. People are so quick to judge. It’s the same with… well, everything, isn’t it? Like Trump. Oh, here we go. Don't tell me you're still dwelling on Trump. We're in Cambridge, enjoying a perfectly good afternoon. Let's not ruin it with American politics. I’m not  dwelling ! It just… the sheer confidence he had, saying utterly ridiculous things and people  believing  him. It's the same energy as someone telling me my jumper clashes with my trousers. It's a denial of reality! Okay, that’s… a stretch, even for you, love. A bad fashion opinion and a geopolitical disaster are not comparable. Though, I will admit, the man had a knack for saying things that made you question everything. Remember that press conference where he talked about disinfectant? Don't remind me! It was horrific. Honestly, it made my brain hurt. It's just… I read this article this morning about the impact of his tax cuts, and it's still rippling through the economy. It’s frightening. It makes me think about our savings, actually. Are we still on track for that house deposit? We are. Mostly. I ran the numbers again last week. The interest rates are still a bit bonkers, though. We might need to adjust our expectations slightly. Maybe not a four-bedroom semi with a garden, but a very nice two-bedroom terrace? A terrace? In Milton? No thank you. I want somewhere with space for plants! I'm planning a whole jungle, you know. Monstera, fiddle-leaf figs, maybe even a bird of paradise if I'm feeling ambitious. A jungle. Of course. You and your plants. You spend more time talking to them than you do to me sometimes. They're more appreciative. They don’t question my fashion choices. Speaking of which, remember that time Uncle Barry tried to tell me pasties were a sophisticated meal?

…and honestly, the student just blinked at me. Blinked! After I’d spent fifteen minutes explaining the nuance of post-structuralist feminism in relation to Virginia Woolf. You'd have thought I was speaking Klingon. Sounds about right. They don’t prepare you for the sheer…blankness, do they? I had one ask me yesterday if Plato was a DJ. A  DJ , darling. Oh, stop! That’s brilliant. Though, slightly terrifying. It makes you question everything, doesn’t it? Is any of this actually going in? It does. It really does. I’m starting to think my lectures are just ambient noise at this point. Speaking of noise though, have you seen that documentary about killer whales? The ones mimicking human speech? Oh! The BBC one? I started it, got distracted by marking, and then completely forgot about it. Is it good? Astounding. They’re learning specific calls to blend in with different pods, almost like accents. It’s incredible. Makes you wonder what depths of intelligence we’re overlooking in other species. It’s miles more interesting than debating the merits of reality TV, which is what my sister was droning on about earlier. Oh, don’t even  start  on reality TV. She was trying to convince me  Love Island  is a profound commentary on modern relationships. Honestly! And it’s all so…violent, isn’t it? Even the seemingly innocuous ones. All that manufactured drama. Aggression disguised as entertainment. It's subtly conditioning, I think. Little bits of conflict normalised. Remember when there was that massive fuss about cartoon violence? That feels almost quaint now. It does. Though I do remember being utterly traumatised by  Count Duckula . That bat was terrifying. It's funny, though, thinking about childhood TV. Do you remember trying to collect Blue Peter badges? Vaguely. Mum kept losing all my application forms. The injustice! I was  convinced  I deserved one for that terrible papier-mâché volcano I made. I think I sent in a drawing of a particularly impressive dust bunny once too. You and your dust bunnies! I only ever got a half badge. For sending in a poem. It was dreadful, honestly. All about my cat, Winston, and his dislike of Tuesdays. Charmingly awful. Actually, speaking of awful things and things people occupy…did you read about that squat in that old mill near Wymondham? Apparently, it's been going on for months.

…and honestly, Doreen, the state of that hostel was a disgrace. Damp patches the size of tablecloths, and young lads sleeping three to a room. Three! Used to be decent places, you know. Managed by the council proper. Now it's all… contractors. Cutting corners everywhere. Oh, Arthur, you get yourself all worked up. It's awful, of course, but what  can  you do? It's not like you're going to volunteer to run it. Remember Mr. Henderson? He tried running the youth club for a bit, nearly had a breakdown. It's a systemic issue, really. Underfunding, lack of oversight… I see it at school. Fewer resources, bigger classes, kids falling through the cracks. It's the same principle. You strip away the support and expect everything to magically hold together. Magic won’t fix it, Richard. Hard work will. My father, now  he  worked. Had that butcher’s shop in Costessey for fifty years. Up at dawn, every single day. Proper cuts of meat, not like that pre-packed rubbish you get now. And my mother, running the greengrocer’s next door. Always fresh produce. They didn’t believe in handouts, they believed in elbow grease. They were a different generation, Arthur. They  had  to work. There wasn't much choice. Your father wouldn't have had a social worker offering him ‘options’ back then, would he? It was just… get on with it. No, and good riddance to these options! All this talk of 'wellbeing' and 'mental health'... It's codswallop. A bit of graft builds character. Though, mind you, that abattoir down the road from my father’s shop…  that  was a grim business. Always the smell, even on a windless day. It’s fascinating, actually, the physics of air currents and how scent travels. We were talking about it in science class today. Bernoulli’s principle… the speed of the air, the pressure differential… Oh, don’t start with the science, Richard! I’m trying to enjoy my tea. Remember Brenda from Bingo? She’s in hospital again. Poor love. Her knees are just gone. Says the doctors are talking about a replacement, but she’s terrified. Brenda’s a good sort. Always a smile, even when her numbers weren't coming up. Shame. Is her son, Kevin, looking after her alright? He was always a bit of a scamp at school, wasn’t he?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of applications was just  relentless . I mean, I understood  why  it was like that, of course. Everyone and their dog seemed to be applying for everything. But sifting through them, the cover letters alone… it was soul-destroying. Right? Sounds brutal. So, you were in recruitment before lecturing, then? I didn’t realise that, actually. I always just assumed everyone landed here directly from a PhD. Oh, no. Definitely not a direct route. I did it for about four years. After my Masters, needed to pay off some debt, and it seemed…practical. Paid well enough. Just… not fulfilling. It’s a world away from dissecting Milton, let me tell you. The pressure to fill roles, to meet targets…it was all very… transactional. I can imagine. A completely different skillset, I guess. Although, assessing people  is  a common thread. Which, actually, brings me to something. I’m a bit stuck on the formative assessment for my ‘Introduction to Academic Writing’ module. Oh, the first years? How’s that going? They always need a lot of hand-holding, don’t they? That’s putting it mildly! It’s…interesting. I'm finding their baseline academic literacy is all over the shop. I’ve students who can write perfectly coherent arguments, properly referenced, and then others who…well, struggle with paragraph structure, let alone referencing. I’m trying to figure out a good way to gauge that  before  the big essay. Have you thought about a short, structured analytical piece? Something where they have to respond to a relatively simple academic text, but needs clear argument and evidence? Keeps it contained, limits the scope for just… rambling. I was thinking a response essay, yeah, but I’m worried it'll just highlight the gap too much, and demoralise them. I want something diagnostic, but not crushing. I considered a mini-research proposal, but that felt a bit much for an introductory module. Hmm. A proposal is maybe a bit ambitious, you're right. Thinking back to my recruitment days, actually, ironically, we used little 'situation judgement' tests. Not exactly the same, obviously, but they were good at quickly identifying people who could process information and apply logic. Maybe something similar, tailored towards academic concepts? Like, give them a weak argument and ask them to identify the flaws. That’s…actually a really interesting idea. A sort of ‘spot the fallacy’ exercise.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of reading for this dissertation is  criminal . Like, who needs this much academic torture in their life? It's a wonder anyone graduates. Tell me about it. I’m just trying to survive shifts at the phone shop, let alone contemplate existential dread through academic papers. Though, to be fair, explaining mobile phone contracts  is  a special kind of hell. Oh, no way! That sounds…intense. I’m used to slightly different kinds of customer service from my part-time job, but frustrating people are frustrating people, I suppose. I work at that little cafe near campus, "Brew & Bites". Oh, I’ve been! Their lattes are the only thing keeping me functioning some days. You're the girl with the bright pink hair, right? Guilty as charged! It helps ward off the dissertation gloom. I'm Aisha, by the way. Liam. And yeah, pink hair is…distinctive. Good distinctive, mind. I’m Chloe. We've definitely seen each other around campus, Aisha. Small world, Salford Uni. This is… oh, you haven’t met Priya yet, have we? Hi everyone! No, I’m new to this study group, Chloe mentioned it and said it was a good way to… well, survive. I’m Priya. Welcome to the chaos, Priya. We mostly complain and occasionally achieve something vaguely academic. Sounds perfect, actually. I’m doing my Masters in Environmental Science, so the reading list is equally terrifying. Although, it's more about impending doom for the planet rather than personal academic doom, which feels…slightly different. Oh, Environmental Science! That’s brilliant. Seriously needed. I’m doing English Literature, so it’s all tragically beautiful prose about things that happened centuries ago. Useful, yeah? In a ‘understanding the human condition’ kind of way, absolutely. What are you writing your dissertation on, Chloe? The portrayal of working-class women in Northern Victorian novels. It’s… a lot. Mostly about grime, poverty and quiet defiance. It’s grim, no pun intended. What about you, Aisha? I'm examining the impact of social media on political discourse. Which basically means scrolling through Twitter all day and confirming my worst fears about humanity. It’s research, I swear! Sounds academic enough. My research involves trying to convince people that unlimited data is a worthwhile investment. It’s equally depressing. Anyone got any good jokes? I need a distraction from the sheer monotony of my existence.

…and honestly, the gravy was  nowt  like Mam makes. Too thin, all watery. You could see straight through it! It's the principle, innit? When you’re having roast beef, you need a proper gravy you can stand a spoon up in. You’re such a Yorkshire purist, Chloe. It was nice gravy, honestly. A little… refined, maybe, for your tastes. It’s Cambridge, not Doncaster, you know? Things are a bit different. Refined? It were weak! Honestly, it’s like people down here don’t understand the basics. Anyway, never mind the gravy. I was reading this magazine – one of yours, actually, left it here last time – and it had this article about women in the military. Really made me think. Oh, the ‘Vanguard’ one? Yeah, they often have good pieces on that. What about it specifically? Well, it got me thinking about Dad, really. He always used to talk about his time in the Royal Signals. Never  much  detail, mind you, very tight-lipped about it all, but he always said it made him the man he was. Proper discipline and all that. But the article was talking about the challenges women face, the… subtle biases and things. I hadn’t really considered that before. It’s huge, isn’t it? The expectation to be ‘one of the lads’, to prove yourself constantly, and then the extra hurdles around maternity leave and childcare. My cousin Sarah’s in the Navy. She loves it, genuinely, but she’s had to work twice as hard to be taken seriously. It's mental to think about, really. That’s what I mean! Dad never mentioned anything like that, obviously. Probably wouldn’t have  known  to. Times were different. He joined straight out of school. Speaking of different times… did you see that new sci-fi film, ‘Nexus Point’? The special effects are insane. Proper mind-bending. Oh, is that the one everyone’s raving about? I haven’t had a chance. I’ve been buried under conference planning. That tech conference next month is a nightmare. The AV guy keeps saying the projector won’t work with their bespoke software. Bespoke! Like they can’t just… adapt something. Tech people. Don’t get me started. It's always some last-minute thing. As a production controller, I deal with similar headaches all the time. It’s the principle again, isn’t it?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of him to suggest I wasn’t ‘serious’ about my career just because I also enjoy going out for a drink. Like, excuse me? I design buildings, mate. Buildings! Right? Men are consistently… baffling. Was this the one from the gallery opening, the one who kept talking about his ‘process’? The very same. Thought he was some sort of tortured artist just because he splatters paint on canvas. Honestly, a five-year-old with finger paints could probably achieve the same thing. Anyway, rant over. How was the game, Leo? You were pretty quiet during the last quarter. Just thinking, actually. About this potential documentary I'm trying to pitch. It’s about… gentrification, specifically how it impacts smaller northern towns. Wirlpoole's changing so fast, it's almost unrecognisable. Oh, that sounds really interesting, Leo. Really important, actually. Winchester’s seen its share of it, but nothing on the scale of what I imagine you're seeing up north. All those fancy Londoners buying up properties as weekend retreats… it’s awful for locals. Speaking of Londoners, Mum and Dad are descending this weekend. Brace yourselves. Dad’s already started on the ‘when are you going to settle down and give us grandchildren’ routine in our group chat. Oh god, the pressure. I’ll hide in the shed. Seriously though, doesn’t he realise you're building a future, literally? It’s not like you’re aimlessly wandering the earth. Tell him that! Apparently, having a ‘secure’ job with a pension is the only valid life choice. He doesn’t understand the freelance world at all. He thinks I’m just… playing at being an architect. It’s the same with my parents. They keep asking about finding a ‘nice young man’ and settling down in a detached house with a garden. Like, that’s the ultimate goal? I’m happy with my flat and my career. Why does everyone assume you need a husband and 2.4 children to be complete? It’s ingrained, isn’t it? Generations of societal expectation. I was reading an article about how that pressure actually impacts women’s career choices… steers them towards ‘safer’ options. Which is rubbish, obviously. Absolutely rubbish. It’s just… exhausting. It's also exhausting dealing with microaggressions at work. Last week, a client literally patted me on the head and asked if I was ‘sure I understood the structural calculations’.

…and honestly, the window cleaner just  looked  at me like I’d asked him to paint the ceiling. He said he’d ‘never seen a window so… enthusiastic’ with bird droppings. Apparently, Sussex birds have strong opinions. “Enthusiastic” is a good word for it, Ben! You should have seen the state of Mum’s face when she first looked out. She nearly choked on her scone. Which, by the way, is pronounced ‘scone’ as in ‘gone,’ not ‘scone’ as in ‘cone,’ Dad. Now listen here, young lady. I’ve been eating scones my entire life, and it’s  always  been ‘scone’ as in ‘cone.’ It just sounds… right. It's a proper scone, innit? Oh, leave him to it, dear. It’s a regional thing. Ben’s right, down here they say ‘scone’ like ‘gone.’ Though frankly, after that cream tea, I’m not sure I  want  another scone for a month. Far too rich. Still, lovely, lovely. So, about that richness… Dad, how’s the cholesterol been? You didn’t sneak a second helping of clotted cream, did you? Don't you worry your head about my cholesterol. I'm a robust seventy-two, I'll outlive the lot of you. Heard about old Maggie Peterson? Hit 103 last week. Still sharp as a tack, apparently. Though she does require everything pureed. That's amazing! Although, pureed everything doesn’t sound very appealing. It's funny to think about getting  that  old. What do you think the secret is? I reckon it’s not worrying so much. Your generation stresses about everything. And proper cooking. None of this microwave nonsense. Speaking of nonsense, anyone fancy helping me tackle the mountain of plastic bags under the sink? It’s officially become a biohazard. Oh god, don’t remind me. I swore I’d get reusable bags, but I always forget. I’m terrible. Plastic bags are a plague. Used to be you got a proper paper bag from the shops. You could actually  carry  something in them. Now everything’s flimsy plastic. Like the state of modern politics, frankly. Don't start on politics, George. We're trying to enjoy ourselves. Although, it is a bit much, isn’t it? All the… fuss. So, about the flat… Mum, are you comfortable with everything? Is the kitchen alright? I know it’s not huge. Darling, it's lovely. Much brighter than your old place in Brighton.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data we’re dealing with now is mental. It's not just transcribing, it's annotating for sentiment, for dialect features, for everything. It's exhausting. How's the bridge building going, anyway? Still battling with physics and concrete? You have no idea. It’s less battling physics, more battling planning permission and NIMBYs at the moment, to be honest. Spent most of yesterday justifying why a slightly wider access road  isn’t  going to ruin the aesthetic of a village green. Seriously. You’d think people would be pleased about improved infrastructure. Oh, Cambridge villagers. They’re a special breed. Bet they all drive Range Rovers anyway. Speaking of ridiculous things… did you see that new article about house prices? Apparently, the average house here is now… wait for it… nearly £550,000. No way! That's insane. I was looking at places in Kent last year, thinking I could maybe get a small flat for around £200k. Cambridge is just…another planet. Honestly, I don’t know how anyone my age manages to buy anything around here. Exactly! My mam keeps sending me Rightmove links, saying "You should think about investing, love!" As if I’ve got a spare half a million lying around. I’m lucky I got a flat back in Sunderland before I left for uni. Even  that’s  gone up considerably, but not… Cambridge levels of bonkers. Sunderland’s still relatively affordable, isn't it? My German cousins were asking about moving to the UK, and I actually suggested Newcastle. Said it had a good vibe and was way more sensible price-wise. Aye, Newcastle’s canny. Sunderland’s getting there, slowly. It's building up a proper tech scene though, which is good. Less reliance on shipbuilding, thankfully. Still, feels a world away from all this… academic wealth. What about your work? Is it at least  interesting  even if the paperwork is infuriating? It is, when I actually get to  do  engineering. We're working on a sustainable drainage system for a new development, using bio-retention ponds and stuff. It’s actually pretty cool. It's the endless meetings and justifying things to people who don’t understand the first thing about load-bearing capacity that’s draining. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I spend more time explaining things than actually designing them. Tell me about it.

…and honestly, the state of the night shift is just  dire . We’re down two nurses again. Old Mr. Henderson called in sick – again – says it’s his back, but I wouldn't put it past him to be enjoying a long weekend. Honestly, it's always something. Oh, no way! Seriously? Still? That's awful, Mum. You’d think after, what, three ‘back episodes’ this month they’d start questioning it. Doesn’t the ward manager do anything? Brenda’s alright, she’s just… overwhelmed. She’s brilliant with the patients, absolutely lovely woman, but paperwork and people-managing? Not her forte. She’s spending more time filling in forms about staff shortages than actually  solving  the staff shortages. It’s a vicious cycle. Tell me about it. Down at the residential home, it’s the same. We’re constantly covering shifts. Mrs. Peterson fell yesterday, thankfully only a minor bruise, but it highlighted just how stretched we are. Thankfully, young Chloe – that's Speaker_4, by the way, she's just popped to the loo – was quick thinking and cushioned her fall. Cushioning falls is practically a job requirement these days! Honestly, it’s exhausting. I love the residents, genuinely, but some days I feel like I’m running a marathon, not providing care. You both sound completely frazzled. Copywriting is stressful, deadlines and client revisions, but it sounds…different. Less physically draining, at least. Though, dealing with some clients  is  a contact sport. Speaking of stressful, did I tell you about Auntie Maureen’s 60th? Oh, don’t even get me started on Maureen. What’s she planning this time? A full-scale themed extravaganza, I presume? Last year's Hawaiian luau was… memorable. Worse, actually. She’s decided on a ‘Roaring Twenties’ party. And she’s insisted  everyone  dresses up. Which, fine, I can handle that. But she’s hiring a jazz band… and a Charleston dance instructor. For a party full of people who last danced at their school disco. Oh, bless her. Maureen always goes big. My Arthur will probably hide in the garden. He hates being the centre of attention. Sounds… chaotic. I think I’d rather be on a night shift, to be honest. At least there’s a quiet sort of exhaustion. You’d think after all these years, I'd be used to the unpredictability of the ward. But it still gets to me.
